history.title: King of Kong Island
history.text: King of Kong Island is one hour and twenty – four minutes and release in theatres on September 29, 1968. The basic story line is that a mad scientist in the jungles of Kenya is experimenting with mind control devices and implanting them in the brains of gorillas. The rest of the movie is never quite explained and there are a lot of plot holes in the movie. King of Kong Island and Kong Island are the basically the same movies with King of Kong Island being a minute longer. The original Italian version is one hour and ninety – two minutes and contains the nude scenes. Also with the Kong Island packaging you get the Most Dangerous Game as an extra movie. This DVD contains no extras. King of Kong Island gets a D- for lack of story.

history.title: The Monster and the Girl
history.text: The Monster and the Girl is one hour and four minutes and was released in theaters on February 28, 1941. The main storyline is a guy is sentenced to death for a crime he did not commit. A doctor visits him in death row and asks for the use of his brain after he dies. The man’s brain goes into the body of a gorilla. The gorilla with the man’s brain inside of it goes on a revenge killing spree for the people who framed and save his sister and that boys and girls is your movie in a nutshell. The movie sort of reminds me your cheesy seventies movies short on plot, action and budget. The Monster and the Girl gets a C+.

history.title: Starcrash (Roger Corman Cult Classics)
history.text: Starcrash is one hour and thirty – one minutes and was released in the United States on March 7, 1979. The main story is that Stella Star, Akton and Elle, under the orders of the Emperor, set off to find Count Zarth Arn secret weapon on a hidden planet and to find the Emperor only son. That is the movie in a nutshell. The main thing this movie has going for it are two things. First the artwork and remember no computer graphic imaging in the Seventies so a lot of this was painted. A lot of the space scenes were paint and some background as well. Also the stop-motion model animation is not bad also. Second the music of John Barry which was scored in just four days is good. In the United States version the original film was trimmed by five minutes to keep in going. This film marks Europe first foray into the science fiction movie franchise. Starcrash gets an A. history.title: Tower of London
history.text: The Tower of London is one hour and thirty – two minutes and was released in theaters on November 17, 1939. The main story is that Richard, Duke of Gloucester is sixth in line to the throne and plots to eliminate those ahead of him. The story is closely related to the real Richard III of England. An interesting note here is that Vincent Price who plays Duke of Clarence would go on to play Richard the III in a 1962 remake with the same title. Basil Rathbone does a superb job as playing the evil Richard, Duke of Gloucester. The Tower of London gets an AA++.

history.title: The Phantom of the Opera (1962) [DVD]
history.review_title: You feel sorry for this one
history.text: The Phantom of the Opera is one hour and twenty – five minutes and was released in theaters on June 25, 1962. This was the third Phantom of the Opera movie and the first one made in the United Kingdom. This one has a different twist then the other two. In the first two the Phantom worked solo and in this one he as an assistant who unknowingly or knowingly does his dirty work for him. The one follows closely to the 1943 Claude Rains version. The main difference is Claude Rains was a violinist and Herbert Lom is voice trainer. Professor Petrie takes is unpublished music to Lord Ambrose D'Arcy in the hopes that he would publish his music. Instead Lord Ambrose D'Arcy publish the music under his own name and when Professor Petrie finds out he goes to the printing place to destroy the printing plates and all the printed music. However a fire erupts and in his attempts to put out the fire he accidently throw nitric acid on the fire and some of it splashes back on his face and he runs out screaming and falls into the river where a dwarf saves him. Now of the three Phantoms this one has the most horrific face even though it is shown very briefly at the end of the movie. Even his hands looks badly burned. Though with this one you feel the most sorrow for. The first two Phantoms wanted Christine all to themselves whereas this Phantom wanted to help her become a better opera singer to perform in his play. Even when he dies at the end of the movie saving Christine you still feel remorseful about the guy. This Phantom of the Opera gets an AAAA++++. DVD Options A. Play B. Subtitles a. On b. Off

history.title: Hollywood Legends of Horror Collection
history.text: Hollywood Legends of Horror Collection is six hours and one minutes, not including bonus materials, and was released on DVD on September 27, 2017. All six movies are good in their own right with the exception of The Return of Doctor X. In my opinion not the best movie in the set. A few interesting trivia about this sent are: Lionel Atwill appears in Doctor X and Mark of the Vampire and Lionel Barrymore appears in Mark of the Vampire and The Devil Doll and only the Devil does not come with a commentary. Also the Mask of Fu Manchu does not come with a theatrical trailer. Below I gave a brief cliff note about the movies and with some of them a few interesting facts. Hollywood Legends of Horror Collection gets an AAAA++++. Doctor X is one hour and fifteen minutes and was released in theaters on August 3, 1932. The movie is basically about a person who is dubbed by the newspapers as the Moon Killer Murders. The Moon Killer has killed four people in the past several months. The police suspect one of the doctors at a nearby medical academy because a certain type of scalpel is used and it is only used at the academy. Dr. Jerry Xavier does not want any bad press on the school so he begs the police to allow him to do an internal investigation and the police gives him 48 hours to find the killer. Doctor X was made in two-color Technicolor which looks a little like a colorize black and white film. Doctor X hints at murder, rape, cannibalism and prostitution during the film but none of that is actually shown. The Return of Doctor X in one hour and two minutes and was released in theaters on December 2, 1939. The movie tells the story of Dr. Maurice Xavier and how he is bought back to life after he is executed for his crime. Dr. Francis Flegg brings back Dr. Maurice Xavier using synthetic blood. However synthetic blood cannot reproduced itself and Dr. Maurice Xavier goes on a murder spree looking for rare Type One blood type so he can stay alive. This film marks Humphrey Bogart first and only science fiction\horror movie and later in his career he would talk little about it because he thought it to be his worst film of his career along with Swing Your Lady. This film is not a sequel to Doctor X. Mark of the Vampire in one hour and was released in theaters on April 26, 1935. This is a remake of the 1927 classic London After Midnight. Basically a group of people try to figure out who murder Sir Karell Borotyn and their main suspect is Baron Otto von Zinden. Since twenty minutes were cut from the original film there are some unexplained gaps in the film. There was to be a subplot of Count Mora of having an incestuous relationship with his daughter Luna. Thus he committed suicide by shooting himself in the head. In the movie there is an unexplained bullet hole in his right temple throughout the movie. Since Tod Browning previous film Freaks was a flop, he could not object to the cuts. The Mask of Fu Manchu is one hour and eight minutes long and was released in theaters on November 5, 1932. The movie is about Fu Manchu trying to get a hold of the sword and mask of Genghis Khan. With the mask and sword Fu Manchu wants to proclaim himself the reincarnation of Genghis Khan so he can rule Asia and the Middle East. It is up to Sir Denis Nayland Smith of the British Secret Service to stop him. Some fun facts about this movie are this was Boris Karloff first speaking role. Also this would be the last time Myrna Low would play an oriental female. She would have to wait another two years before her breakout role as Nora Charles in the Thin Man. This movie may have been longer because in later years scenes were cut due to racial overtones of Asians. Mad Love is one hour and eight minutes long and was released in theaters on July 12, 1935. The story is about Dr. Gogol who is obsessed with the actress Yvonne Orlac. When Yvonne tells Dr. Gogol that she is retiring from the theatre to be with her pianist husband Stephen Orlac. This drives Dr. Gogol into a mad love, hence the name of the movie. Mad Love was Peter Lorre first movie in the United States. The Devil Doll is one hour and eighteen minutes and was released in theaters on July 10, 1936. The movie is about a wrongly convicted man who has escaped from Devil’s Island and want revenge on the three men who wrongly convicted him. In doing so he uses a formula to make people small, no more than three inches tall to aide him in his quest for revenge and justice. This was Maureen O'Sullivan first horror movie. Disc 1 Doctor X 1. history.title: House of Wax [DVD]
history.text: House of Wax is one hour and twenty – eight minutes long and was released in theaters on April 10, 1953. The main story is that wax sculptor Henry Jarrod creates wax sculptors for his museum, but his partner Matthew Burke is unhappy with the museum and believes it could generate more money is it displays horror wax figures. Henry does frowns on doing horror wax sculptors. Matthew has an insurance policy and wants to cash in on it since the museum is not making that much money. Matthew sets the museum on fire and he and Jarrod gets into a fight all while the museum is burning. Matthew knocks Jarrod out and escapes. Jarrod awakens and tries to save his wax figures but is unable to do so. Jarrod jumps throw or is blown through a glass window. It is several years later and a new Chambers of Horror is about to open. Henry Jarrod somehow survived the fire, but is bound to a wheelchair and his hands and fingers are of no use to him. Sorry will not give the ending away. The differences between the House of Wax and the Mystery of the Wax Museum are: House of Wax is eleven minutes longer, House of Wax was made using stereoscopic 3-D color and Mystery of the Wax Museum was made using two-color Technicolor. The man in the House of Wax that tells the police that the museum is a wax morgue is an alcoholic and in the Mystery of the Wax Museum he is a drug addict. Overall House of Wax is an excellent remake of the Mystery of the Wax Museum and gets an AAAAA+++++. DVD Extras House of Wax I. Play Movie II. Scene Selections III. Special Features a. history.title: King Kong (1976)
history.review_title: The original is still the best
history.text: King Kong is two hours and fourteen minutes and was released in theatres on December 17, 1976. Basically it is almost has the same story outline as the original King Kong. Pretty blonde girl gets capture by big gorilla, big gorilla falls head over heels for blond girl and big gorilla gets killed. Now here are the differences from the original and remake. Original movie Carl Denham is taking the crew to film an unknown creature on Skull Island. New version, Fred Wilson of Petrox Oil Company is heading to an unknown island in the Indian Ocean to look for oil. Old version Carl Denham finds a female to film a movie for him. New movie, they find a female in a raft floating in the ocean. In the original version there is no stowaway except Son of Kong, new version stowaway. Original version King Kong is a stop-motion animation gorilla and new version a guy in a gorilla suit. Original version King Kong climbs the Empire State Building and falls to his death and in the new version King Kong climbs the World Trade Centers and dies. Also at the end of the original version a police officer remarks to Carl Denham that the planes got him and Carl Denham replies back "Oh, no, it wasn't the airplanes. It was Beauty killed the Beast." There is no famous last line in the new version. Also in the original version King Kong battle a Tyrannosaurus, Elasmosaurus and Pteranodon and in the remake the only creature King Kong battles is a snake. Finally the remake is forty – four minutes longer than the original. Overall in my opinion the original was much better than remake. To me if it aint broke than why fix it. King Kong 1976 gets a C+ for not bringing anything new to the movie. DVD Extras A. Play B. Set Up a. Audio Options i. English Dolby Surround ii. English 5.1 Surround iii. French b. history.title: Interstellar (Blu-ray + DVD Combo Pack)
history.review_title: competently produced science fiction film but not the 2001 of this generation. (This review has spoilers)
history.text: I wanted to be blown away by this film but it simply wasn't to be. Perhaps I simply allowed myself to get caught up in the hype and overblown expectations. It has plenty going for it theoretically. big name director, well known physicist as a science consultant, decent enough actors, big budget and yet... It has impressive visuals but it feels like the story doesn't quite know where to go. Is the point that man must evolve to go off world or evolve to find other planets upon which to live? were the 5th dimensionals aliens or future humans? Other parts of the story also didn't make much sense. For somebody that grew up when the space race was still 'a thing' I was hoping to see a story about mankind's resourcefulness and desire to explore. I wanted a film that showed the development of practical interstellar travel by present human ingenuity and the first such voyage to another star and the adventure that would ensue. Instead, in this future, it turns out that mankind has abandoned the desire to pursue science and engineering due to an environmental collapse and the politically-correct socialistic group-think types have taken over and believe that the moon landing was capitalist propaganda.wonderful. To top it off the instellar part is thanks to a deus ex machina wormhole that shows up with no apparent explanation - and nobody really cares to ask why. But here is the part of the film that ultimately sunk it in my eyes: So here we are (once again) with the typical American trope of a kid growing up resenting their parent because said parent promised them something that they ultimately failed to deliver. It doesn't matter that any reasonable person once becoming an adult would realize that the promise their parent made was completely beyond their ability to guarantee. It doesn't matter that this parent was knowingly risking life and limb on a mission that might save not only the future of the entire race but the child's own personal future as well - pretty much the definition of the word 'hero'. oh no. we have to be mad at daddy because he couldn't buy you a pony for christmas or whatever. The worst part is that after all that heartache he comes back decades in the future and gets laughed at by the medics because he thought they named the space station after him. Hello. The guy just traversed time and space. Back from a suicide mission. Decades in the future. He didn't age. And they treat him like he's some dumb no-nothing shmuck from the boonies. Seriously? To top it off he finally gets to see his now aged daughter...and she totally blows him off...and all of these descendants of his that are around her - have absolutely no reaction to the guy! Anyway, like the title states, it's competently made even if the story isn't quite there and it's still enjoyable such that i would recommend someone watch it, if they hadn't already seen it. The banter with the robots was enjoyable - in some ways they were the most interesting and most developed characters in the film.

history.review_title: A mediocre Spacemonster movie with a twist ending that you can see from a mile away.
history.text: This is not a bad film, but it isn't an especially great one either. This is essentially an updated version of a 1950's 'monster from space' B-Movie ; one with modern A-grade effects work. Many have compared it to Alien which I suppose is valid but it doesn't provide the tension of that earlier film. Sadly there is nothing really unique here and even the 'twist' ending was easily intuited. Much of the plot is driven by character decisions and reactions that make no sense for a presumably highly trained crew entrusted with investigating the first known sample of extraterrestrial life. Examples include: There is no proper isolation of the organism. There is no emergency sterilization equipment for potentially infectious or hazardous organisms. Some characters at first care about quarantine and exposure and then alternately don't care about it. The ability to jettison such an organism out into space relies on a soyuz capsule that needs to be launched only after an emergency situation arises. Hopefully NASA and ESA are better than this in real life. All that said, if you just enjoy it as a popcorn monster movie then this film is can be enjoyable as a Saturday afternoon diversion.

history.title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars (Two-Disc Special Edition)
history.review_title: Pilot film for the animated Clone Wars series
history.text: As a fan of Star Wars overall, I've read many of the books from the now non Canon expanded universe, and the prequel films were ok, the main trilogy remains a classic and I kinda dig the new Rebels series and was amazed by Force Awakens. The Clone Wars series was something I watched occasionally but never had time to watch it. I have the box set now and making my way through it. This film sets the stage for the series and while it's not perfect it's still very entertaining and it holds your attention with the action as well as the character dynamics and politics. Not bad for a cartoon show for kids. I love how this film and each episode of the series kicks things off with a montage of images with a voiceover bringing people up to speed on what is going on, much like a wartime newsreel. You are invested in the characters even though in the back of your mind you already know that things are going to end badly for a lot of them given what we know from Episode 3 and so on. The sight of seeing our heroes onboard star destroyers with an army of storm troopers is a bit weird a tad unsettling. But it is still awesome seeing Anakin in his element as someone who clearly cares about the lives of his men and about living on the edge in the heat of battle. The relationship he forges with Ahsoka is a bit prickly at first, the disrespectful little know it all snot that is teamed up with a brash and somewhat overconfident warrior. Its a great pilot film, and as a lead in to the rest of the series it sets up what the series is all about... Showcasing the wider scope of the war and the various people involved. Its an epic space opera, which is exactly what star wars is meant to be but this series takes that concept and pushes it further. Highly recommended

history.title: Ben 10: The Complete Season 1
history.review_title: No ordinary kid, no ordinary cartoon
history.text: I came across this series when it was on Netflix and was hooked. As a fan of cartoons, I was blown away by how well crafted this series is, along with it's subsequent sequel series Alien Force and Ultimate Alien (not counting omniverse or the reboot series). This series is very well written and constructed overall, as it taps into that essential element for young kids that dream of being superheroes, here is ben Tennyson getting that chance largely by accident. I love how as the series progresses the mythology of the universe od this series builds and builds as we learn more about Grandpa max and his time as a 'plumber'. Ans also see Ben still be your typical 10 year old but also learn about doing the right thing and about his responsibilities, even when he isn't constantly bickering with his cousin Gwen. That was one thingbthatnalways kinda bothered me watching many of these epusodes back to back , hearing the sniping and bickering and gwen calling ben a dweeb a doofus a dork all the freaking time got really tiresome. Im grateful that by the time Alien Force was made they made the characters older and pretty much had the antagonism between Ben and Gwen replaced with genuine familial affection. Anyway, I loved how the people taht made this aeries were clearly comic book fans cu with the omnitrix and its abilities, it reminds one of tue Dial h for Hero, where the special dial allows the user to transform into different types of heroes for different types of situations. I especially love how Ben tries to go for one alien hero and ends up with a different one by mistake, which is funny but also Aids in teaching ben to think on his feet and make use of powers and abilities at his disposal. Also the fact that the omnitrix is green and even the symbol on the chest of each alien, and even the corps of plumbers being galactic defenders.and policemen, brings to mind the green lantern Corps. This first season sets the tone and also sets things in motion rather nicely.

history.title: RuPaul's Drag Race: Season 4
history.text: I have enjoyed this series largely because I am a fan of drag, even though I am a straight man, I have nothing but respect and admiration for these very talented men who express their artistry, creativity and femininity through the art and illusion of drag. I've watched each season since the beginning and have been pretty impressed by the challenges, the drama, the hilarity, the ingenuity, and so on demonstrated by each queen. Season four is without a doubt where this show began to hit its stride by demonstrating true diversity in the world of drag, particularly with who eventually won this season. The challenges this season were pretty awesome and showcased some great branching out, building upon what they were doing in previous seasons. One thing that is usually still very cringe inducing for me is watching the preparations for the filmed acting challenges, cuz you do have a tendency to see the whole warts and all elements with them either screwing up their lines, complaining about how they screwed up, or showcasing that they just really suck at acting. Now, there are moments that occur in this season that are infamous and still remain in Drag pop culture, like the first appearance of Sharon Needles, in all her gothic glory! I loved Sharon Needles even before the season started, and the fact that she went on to win the season was fantastic. Sharon Needles is essentially the Marlyn Manson of Drag, a true entertainer that is more than just a spooky and shocking exterior, and holds within the heart, soul, and brains of a fearless and inventive performer that takes calculated risks as opposed to some that take risks without putting any thought behind those risks. Her rivalry with Phi Phi O'Hara is a major source of drama (but not only source) this season, as Phi Phi showcased right off the bat when she entered the competition a sense of arrogance and superiority (overshadowed only by Willam's supreme arrogance), and looked down on Sharon, and even underestimated her abilities and more often than not made no secret about how she felt about what she thought were Sharon's limitations as a Drag Queen (even though Phi Phi at times showed herself to be just as weak in certain areas, like her performance as Gaga in Snatch Game or that ridiculously annoying Sarah Palinesque caricature during the Frock the Vote challenge). And that whole 'Party City' insult she threw at Sharon, it pretty much exemplified Phi Phi's whole attitude during that season, plus how quick Phi Phi is to tell people to kiss her ass, telling people to 'shut up before I smack you', showcases how thin skinned she can be. I have been told and have seen evidence that Phi Phi is actually really nice, and as a child suffered from a great deal of abuse for being gay, and she has my sympathy, but being abused as a child is not an excuse for having a stank ass attitude to all and sundry, and treating nearly all and sundry with derision and contempt (I'm still not convinced her giving Chad Michaels her phonecall home during 'Sntach Game' wasn't just a ploy). Willam was just.... irritating. Willam is a professional actor but brought that Hollywood arrogance into the show, and it showed. Willam was certainly clever in certain areas, but her arrogance and snobbish superiority complex was not cool. So it's no surprise that her sorry ass got disqualified when she decided to break the rules (which apparently involved having her significant other visit her at the undisclosed location where the queens are sequestered to during their time on the show). Milan, I did no care for Milan. Milan was just not interesting and had a tendency to make some really dumb mistakes, and also had a tendency to not take direction and not really listen to criticism. Milan is a fierce performer, no doubt, but not one that I would go out of my way to see. Kenya Michaels, I have a soft spot for her, given that is Puerto Rican, just like me. She did have some flaws in her abilities as a performer, but I was still sad when she was eliminated. Latrice Royale, large and in charge, chunky yet funky. Latrice definitely elevated the presence for plus sized queens on the show, and was definitely one of my picks for top three, since most plus sized queens tended not to last beyond the middle of the season. I love Latrice, she was awesome. Chad Michaels, phenomenal! Its Cher Bitch! Jiggly Caliente, sweet but insecure. LaShawn Beyond.... unremarkable. Madame LaQueer.... okay. The Princess... sweet and zen, and possessing of untapped potential that I was sad that I didn't get to see. Dida Ritz... okay. Very sweet, and very likeable, but at times was just... there Alissa Summers... wonderful queen from Florida (where I live), and definitely gone too soon. Sharon's win showcased that Drag Superstars come in all shapes, sizes, personalities, and abilities, and Sharon's win also opened the door for other unconventional queens to enter the competition in the seasons that came afterwards (for better or worse).

history.title: RuPaul's Drag Race: Season 3 (4 Discs)
history.text: I remember when this season came out, and this season is still pretty solid for me because of the various queens, the various challenges and whatnot. Many of the queens that were on this season were awesome but there were some I wasn't too keen on, but that's usually the same with each season. The surprise twist at the start of the season with the return of Shangela was pretty neat, but it also did cause an imbalance in the competition and allow me to explain. I am all for giving people a second chance, and Shangela was someone that got eliminated in season two in the first episode cuz she was unpolished, but had a ton of personality that was just begging to be showcased. And it was cool to see that play out as the season progressed, but I did not like that having Shangela back meant that someone else had to be sacrificed, and that unfortunate person was Venus Dee Lite. Venus was someone I was looking forward to seeing compete, and if Shangela had not been brought back, my feeling was that the bottom two that would Lip Sync would've been Venus and Phoenix, and I think that Venus would've been saved and Phoenix sent home. The fact that Phoenix got sent home in the next challenge just showcased how unimpressive she was as a performer while Venus a lot more to show and would've grown in the competition. but Shangela once again was unpolished, but Ru did not want to send her home in the first episode AGAIN, and so Venus was sacrificed just so Shangela could have her chance to compete. I've got nothing against Shangela, and I'm sure she has learned a lot over the years since season three, but here is something I just have to know. In the time Shangela got eliminated from season two to the time she came back for season three, couldn't that bitch have taken a damn sewing class!?! Because another aspect of Shangela highlighted in season three was that she couldn't sew and needed help from others in order to make stuff. The acting and the creative challenges were awesome as they always are, the Christmas challenge, the money dress challenge, the Sci Fi movie challenge, the Snatch Game, the Totally Leotarded episode with Susan Powter, the QNN challenge with Debbie Matanopolous, and I could go on and on. it was just a fun season. Now, the queens featured this season: Alexis Mateo, one of my favorites cuz Alexis is from Florida, like me, and I was already familiar with Alexis' style of drag and performing and knew she would be a top contender, and the fact that she was in the top three was great, but I was sad Alexis didn't win. Carmen Carrerra, she could be kinda polarizing, because on the one hand she was absolutely gorgeous and was creative, and was clearly smart, but also seemed a bit vain and kinda clueless. Manila Luzon, one of my personal favorites, gorgeous, witty, funny and just an absolute delight, was also a favorite of mine to win. Raja... FAN-TAS-TIC!! Smart, beautiful, charming, witty, and talented, and I was very happy when Raja won. Mariah.... she was ok. Very pretty, but also kinda vain and a shallow. Phoenix.... blah. Yara Sofia... another favorite cuz she's a fellow Puerto Rican. Gorgeous and hilarious, struggled a bit cuz of the language barrier, but fought through it, although that breakdown she had on the runway during the lip sync on the money challenge broke my heart. still, her Amy Winehouse was freaking hilarious. Mimi Imfurst... tried waaaaaaay too hard to be the Pandora Boxx of season three. she was clearly talented as a performer and a comic queen, but seemed to go so far over the top that she ended up crashing into a satellite and burning up in the atmosphere. and what she did during her lip sync did her no favors. Venus... lovely and talented and gone way too soon. Shangela,.. hilarious, charming, and talented, and utilized her second chance well. Delta Work... lovely and talented, but seemed very standoffish at times, especially when she joined up with the 'Heathers' clique, which I will talk about soon. Stacey Lane Matthews.... such a lovely southern creature, and many is the time I just wanted to hug her. she has talent, but also self-esteem and confidence issues. Her Monique on Snatch Game was amazing. India Farrah... was just kinda... there. Now, the Heathers Clique.... much as I love the queens who were part of the clique individually, it created this unnecessary schoolyard mentality and this ridiculous class system of an 'us vs. them', that we are so much better because we are prettier than everyone else. What really annoys the crap outta me about the Heathers thing was the fact that all of these queens probably at one time or another have suffered from being humiliated and ridiculed and were probably bullied and abused for being gay, and yet here these bitches go excluding themselves and being all snobby and snooty in their mentality, essentially making the other bitches feel humiliated and ridiculed, essentially doing to others what they have experienced in their lives, and for what?!? And another thing that annoyed me was Delta's comment in that stand up comedy challenge, she got eliminated in the lip sync cuz she lip synced against Manila and Manila won. Delta's parting words were like 'I'm glad that I lost to a Heather rather than one of the Boogers', what the hell!?!? and then her bullcrap explanation during the reunited episode was exactly that, bullcrap, and Delta didn't even apologize to Stacy or any of the other queens, it was Raja that had the balls to try and make amends. despite these gripes, its still a wonderful season that I really loved.

history.title: Angie Tribeca: Season 1
history.review_title: It's kinda like Sledhge Hammer! But more on par with Police Squad for the modern era.
history.text: I came across this show on TBS and was very intrigued. I have been more or less disappointed with most comedic programs that tend to think that awkwardness is a reasonable substitute for humor. This show brings humor back to where it belongs, at least in my opinion. Everything is done very straight laced and po-faced, and the humor is essentially derived from the fact that there are all of these insane things going around and none of the characters comment on it, they just go with it or just accept it as normal. The Carrels I think are more than likely influenced by the likes of the Zucker brothers, who created the Airplane films, Police Squad, the Naked Gun films, and so on. Its all there in the dialogue as well as in the multitude of sight gags on display. Its utterly brilliant, and long may it continue.

I really enjoyed watching the show, but then when season three came around they did so really unthinkable things... New York, the seat of government for this post apocalyptic world is destroyed... the human family that was part and parcel of the town of Defiance... ALL WIPED OUT!! I couldn't bring myself to continue watching because so much of what I liked was changing far too drastically to the point of being completely unrecognizable. I mean, i can understand sometimes when people kill off certain characters in order to emphasize the dangers of certain circumstances, but it didn't feel this way at all, it just felt like a cheap ploy to be shocking and daring in the short term without really thinking about how this would shape out in the long term, because if all you do is make things bleak without any sign of hope, it doesn't make your show daring and envelope pushing, it makes it downbeat and depressing because you suck out all of the things that made it enjoyable and entertaining in the first place. its a real shame cuz i really enjoyed watching this show considering there aren't that many shows with such a lived in universe filled with alien species interacting with humans and each other like its no big deal. any TV show that deals with living in space nowadays have ALL HUMAN CASTS! The current hit on SyFy now is Expanse, and there aren't any aliens in it! its a great show, but it just seems to continue to emphasize this ridiculous notion of humanity essentially being the center of the universe, because if they go out there and all they find is a whole lot of nothing and humanity spreads out and encounters no other life aside from themselves, it makes the universe rather lonely if there is nothing else out there aside from us. sorry, i got off track, but i really enjoyed Defiance in the first two seasons, but by season three i couldn't bring myself to even watch the rest of the season despite it having some really interesting story arcs because i couldn't get over the bleakness and the downbeat nature set down by the season three premiere.

history.review_title: Enjoyably entertaining mashup of sci fi action, police procedural and domestic family dramedy
history.text: The 1990s was definitely filled to bursting with a wide variety of genre programs sold into first run syndication, some obviously having longer runs than others like Star Trek and it's numerous spinoffs, and of course the absolutely epic Babylon 5. Space Precinct was one of those shows that unfortunately slipped through the cracks and ended up lasting only a season, largely due to poor scheduling (many US markets scheduled this show either really late at night, 12 am or 1am, or really early in the morning, like 4 or 5am, on weekends). It's a shame because this is a quite enjoyable and entertaining. Although the storytelling does try to walk a fine line between gritty, hard edged sci fi action with the police action and lighthearted humor usually brought about by the domestic stuff centering on the Brogan family, or Lt. Haldane's numerous attempts to woo Lt. Castle (which invariably fail until... well you'll see). This is probably what got station affiliates.confused, as they were uncertain how it should be marketed, cuz it was at times too hard edged for kids, but also a little too silly at times for adults. This series was the last production by genre icon Garry Anderson to feature live actors mixed with his impressive model work often associated with his puppet programs. I rather enjoyed the mix of sci fi action, police procedural and domestic stuff, it gave things a rather unique flavor and an identity all of its own. While the series did not have a proper first episode to set up the show and it's plot, the series has a good lived in universe with some nice background details sprinkled throughout with dialogue that feels natural. Credit where it's due, the actors involved do a great job with the material. And while Ted Shackleford will probably be forever known as the lesser Ewing brother, Gary Ewing, from.Dallas/Knots Landing, he does quite well as Patrick Brogan, an NYPD cop now serving and protecting tarns and creons, and dealing with humans and other species of ne'er do wells, all while coming to grips with having uprooted his family from Earth to live out amongst the final frontier. Haven't seen Rob Youngblood in much else aside from this, but his character of Haldane is awesome, cocksure swagger, wisecracking, a ladies man, and always flirting with Castle (and always getting shot down... most of the time). Simone Bendix I haven't seen in much else either, but she is great as Jane Castle. Beautiful, smart, tough, but compassionate. Her banter with Haldane is awesome, and over the course of this series, you do see her softening towards him until it reaches it's natural conclusion in the series finale Deathwatch. It's sad this only lasted a single season. It should've gone on for at least three or four seasons. But it's great stuff and worth watching if you are a sci fi fan, and a Gerry Anderson completist.

history.title: Contamination
history.text: This film certainly had potential to be something pretty good and a lot of fun, especially as it was directed by Luigi Cozzi, same guy that created the awesomely cheesy and fun Star Wars knock off Starcrash, but this film does not possess Cozzi's signature style. Things seem fairly pedestrian in its pacing, and I swear there is one scene of the female lead speaking with a former astronaut, played by Ian McCulloch, about a previous failed mission that reminded me of a similar dialogue exchange featured in an episode from Space: 1999 called 'Dragon's Domain'. What suffers the most has to be the fact that the film front loaded its best stuff at the beginning of the film, with the eggs exploding causing chest bursting for some reason. Other than that, the film itself is fairly unremarkable. As a knock off of Aliens, it's also not worth your time as there are many other films that are better executed.

targets.title: Only When I laugh (The Ultimate Collection 5 dvd set)
Transformers Beast Machines: The Complete Series

history.text: Well, having seen the great Shaka Zulu epic miniseries, I thought I would check out this film on Amazon Prime. Well, to sum it up, it is terrible. As a historical drama it fails, as it is history goes Hollywood. The script is totally laughable and nonsensical. The only good thing about the film, is that the late great South African actor, Henry Cele, is once again cast in the role of Shaka, to reprise his memorable portrayal of this Zulu warrior and king in the mini-series. The role of Lt. Francis Fairwell, originally played by Edward Fox in the mini-series, is, instead, played by his brother, James Fox. There, the resemblance to the miniseries stops. As for David Hasselhoff, who ever told this guy he could act? Karen Allen, who is usually solid, sports an on-again, off-again British accent. Moreover, the romance between them strikes this viewer as false as a three dollar bill. The film is totally tedious. The only reason I gave it two stars, rather than the one star this turkey deserves, is entirely due to Henry Cele's performance as Shaka. Do yourself a favor and take a pass on this film. It is not worthy.

This Poldark is the original 1970s mini series, which I actually saw on video tape about 20 years ago. At the time, I loved it. Seeing it again, after watching the new Poldark series, the bloom has come off the rose. It simply does not compare to the new Poldark series, as it looks almost amateurish due to the vast difference in production values and enhancements brought about by new technology. It also has more of a stage production feel to it, as does the acting, rather than that of a film. Still, I enjoyed it a great deal, once I got over the lackluster production values and the graininess of the film. Having read all twelve of the Poldark books, only seven or eight of them had been published at the time that this series had been filmed. It is a reasonable adaptation, only slightly different from the new Poldark mini-series, which I find to be somewhat more faithful. Nonetheless, it remains an engrossing family saga featuring the character of Ross Poldark, his wife Demelza, his first love, Elizabeth, and his sworn enemy, George Warleggan. Set in 18th Century Cornwall, it showcases the life of the gentry, as well as that of the villagers and the mining community in which they live.

This is a crime drama with supernatural elements, excellent cinematography, and good production values. Michael Palin is outstanding in the role of elderly Tom Parfitt, an elderly man who stages a fall in his home so that he can be placed in a senior residential facility. It is not immediately clear why anyone would want to do that, but as the story unfolds, light is shed on this issue. As the supernatural elements rise to the fore, some of which are truly spooky, the story starts devoloping. While some portions of the storyline become clear, other threads are left dangling with questions unanswered with a resultant sort of mish mosh. As to the acting, other than Michael Pailin, the actresses who play the ayah and the neighbor, who give excellent performances, the rest of the cast are just adequate in their roles, nothing memorable. Still, there was enough in this three part mini-series to maintain my interest. So, overall, I enjoyed it. It is a shame that the story was not better written, as its premise is intriguing, and that some of the performances fell flat. It could have been a contender. Still, there is enough working for it to make this atmospheric mini-series worth watching.

In 1930s Cornwall, the solitude and peace of a coastal Cornish village is disrupted when two elderly sisters discover a young man washed ashore, more dead than alive. They manage to get him to their cottage, where they begin nursing him back to health. It turns out that the young man, Andrea, was on an ocean liner on his way to America, when he was swept overboard, somehow making his way to that Cornish coast. The two sister, Janet (Maggie Smith), the elder, and Ursula (Judi Dench), the younger, are drawn to Andrea like a month to a light, though there is a bit of a language barrier. It turns out Andrea is polish. The sisters have lived together for some time. Janet is a widow, having lost her husband in World War I, while Ursula has never married, there having been a dearth of available men after the war. Andrea brings out a lot of mothering in these two sisters, but it also brings out something else in Ursula, something bittersweet, perhaps the promise of what might have been in her youth. In any case, Andrea, realizing he cannot stay there with them forever, makes a bold move with a new connection who recognizes his artistry and has the wherewithal to help make his dreams come true. in a split decision, he cuts the umbilical cord tethering him to the two sisters but later gives them an unforgettable experience, one they will all cherish. This is a beautifully acted, gem of a film with glorious music. Fans of Maggie Smith and Judi Dench will be over the top at having these two powerhouses in the same film. I loved this tender, funny, bittersweet film!

history.title: Poldark
history.text: This is an engrossing family saga featuring the characters of Ross Poldark, his wife, Demelza, his first love, Elizabeth, and his sworn enemy, George Warleggan. Set in 18th-century Cornwall, it showcases the life of the gentry, as well as that of the villagers and the mining community in which they live. This version Poldark is the original 1970s mini-series, which I first saw on videotape about 20 years ago. At the time, I loved it. Seeing it again, after watching the new Poldark series, the bloom has come off the rose. It simply does not compare to the new Poldark series, as it looks almost amateurish due to the vast differences in production values and enhancements brought about by new technology. It also has more of a stage production feel to it, rather than that of film. Having read all twelve of the books in the Poldark saga, only seven or eight had been published at the time that this series had been filmed. It is a reasonable adaptation, only slightly different from the new Poldark mini-series thus far, which I find to be somewhat more faithful to the storyline. Still, I enjoyed it a great deal, once I got over the lackluster production values and the graininess of the film. I was sorry to see it end. Those who have read and enjoyed the Poldark family saga, will most certainly enjoy this series, especially if one is a fan of period drama.

I loved the book of the same name upon which this movie was based. So, I was delighted to find that Amazon decided to make a film about Percy Fawcett's exploration in the Amazon jungle in the early twentieth century. What actually started as a surveyance of the area became an obsession for Fawcett, convinced that there was a lost, once highly civilized city to be found in the Amazon. He eventually returned to the Amazon jungle one last time with his son and was never heard from again. The film does an excellent job of depicting the interest that the British had in exploration and the feeling that, at the time, the British were, indeed, masters of the universe. The portions of the film that take place in the Amazon jungle are gripping and give the viewer a sense of the determination necessary to endure the trials and tribulations of what was then the unknown. The acting is excellent throughout the film, as is the cinematography. There is also an authenticity of time and place that is transporting. While the pace of the film is slow and deliberate, one should keep in mind that this is not an action film. Its tempo is in keeping with its subject matter. I really enjoyed it.

history.review_title: A WASTE OF TIME AND MONEY...
history.text: The script for this World War II film was predictable. Its depiction of the era was almost campy. I did not get a real feel of authenticity of time and/or place. I was also surprised at how bad Brad Pitt's acting was in this film. The pace of the film was slow, and, quite frankly, I could not wait for this film to end. I did not enjoy it and cannot recommend it.

history.title: American Experience: The Big Burn
history.text: If one is a history buff, one will love this fantastic documentary of the raging, runaway woodland fires that that devastated the Northwest in 1910, resulting in over three million acres of forest burned away. The fires resulted in great loss of property and lives. It also honed in on how little the national psyche knew about fighting this type of fire. It changed the way that the National Forest Service would fight these fires in the future and brought about congressional funding. With archival footage and photographs, coupled with excellent narration, the devastating forest fires of 1910 are brought to life for the viewer. The documentary also highlights the role of the buffalo soldiers in fighting these fires. All who fought to stop these fires were, indeed, the bravest of the brave, as they did so with primitive tools and only with the most rudimentary knowledge of firefighting. This is a gripping narrative that history buffs will enjoy. It is simply first rate!

history.review_title: A PERIOD DRAMA TURNED GOTHIC THRILLER...
history.text: This is a loose adaptation of two novellas by Frances Hodgson Burnett. A young, well-educated woman named Emily Fox-Seton is living in genteel poverty, making for a hardscrabble existence. While working temporarily for Lady Maria Byrne, she meets her nephew, Lord Walderhurst, an attractive widower. He is looking for a wife, and despite the machinations of his aunt to find him a suitable wife, he makes Emily an offer she can't refuse, and she accepts. After all, she has nothing to lose. Lord Walderhurst will get a wife and the heir he desires, and Emily will get a wealthy husband. They sojourn to Lord Walderhurst's isolated country manor, and their burgeoning relationship exceeds both their expectations. Then, he is called back to India with his regiment, and Emily is left alone in the house with the servants. Uninvited relatives of her husband drop in on Emily, and with her trusting nature she welcomes them into her home. Then the mood turns gothic and all hell breaks loose. While some of it quite melodramatic, it is always entertaining. I have viewed this period drama twice and really enjoyed it. The cast is likewise excellent. If one likes gothic thrillers, one will certainly enjoy this one.

This is a well-acted historical drama with a stellar cast. It tells two truncated stories. One story is of the reign of Mary, Queen of Scots. The second story is of Queen Mary's son, King James VI of England, also known as King James I of Scotland.. Both stories are fraught with historical inaccuracies. Still, as it is a historical drama, not a documentary, artistic license is to be expected. Nonetheless, the story presented is not as coherent as it could have been. Making the film a mother/son story is an interesting idea gone awry. Consequently, the film is moderately entertaining, at best.

history.title: The Wizard of Lies
history.review_title: I THOUGHT I HEARD ENOUGH ABOUT BERNIE MADOFF --- but
history.text: For me, once I started watching this I could not stop. Robert DeNiro IS Bernie Madoff---- but then --- so was Richard Dreyfous. They were both great. Richard Dreyfous' portrayal -- I was convinced he was Madoff. Robert DeNiro --- convinced in a different way. Maybe Richard Dreyfous being Jewish had a leg up on DeNiro. Michelle Pfeiffer was the PERFECT RUTH MADOFF --- in style, speech, demeanor, looks, hair style, her face, her lips, her clothes, her inflections ----- Michelle Pfeiffer NAILED THE PART OF RUTH MADDOFF. This movie felt like it took you right there with all the characters involved. It is definitely worth the watch !

history.title: Apocalypto [Import belge]
history.review_title: IT's ONE OF THOSE MOVIES THAT ONCE YOU START WATCHING --- YOU CAN'T STOP !!!!!!
history.text: This movie is incredibly fantastic. I felt like I was there living there through the entire movie ---- on the edge of my seat. The scenery is gorgeous, the acting superb. Everything about this movie is 5 STARS. This definitely deserved BEST MOVIE OSCAR and a whole slew of other Oscars. After watching this ---- I realized that Mel Gibson is a genius.

history.review_title: Spoiler Alert !!! I would highly recommend this movie
history.text: Spoiler Alert !!!!!!First time I started watching this, I thought it was a great movie until ----- the turn of events that I found so depressing. Elizabeth Taylor, of course, beautiful and upbeat. Montgomery Clift --- well ----- I could watch him on the screen if he was just staring into the camera for 3 hours. ---- and Shelley Winters --- so morose, dull and downtrodden. She played that part to a perfection. Put yourself in George's shoes (Montgomery Clift) ----- a message for us all ---- but how could he have foreseen the future. What a life he could have had if he had not used poor judgement. That one initial decision ruined his life. You never know what can come into your life in an instant changing it for the better ----- or the worse. As depressing as it is I would highly recommend this movie. I can't help myself from watching it periodically. ----- hoping for a different ending.

history.review_title: THIS IS AN UNDERATED COOL MOVIE !! THERE NEEDS TO BE A SEQUEL.
history.text: I thought this was going to be a stupid B movie. It's not. It really held my interest. Movie starts off with a real twist rather than ending with one. "I admit --- I did not see that coming" . Luke Evans is a very good actor. And if this was one of the worst movies ---- he is great to look at. He reminds me of a very good looking Leonardo DiCaprio. All of the cast acted well. Great ending soundtrack that is perfectly in sync with the scene.

history.review_title: I WOULD GIVE THIS A ZERO IF I COULD !!!!!
history.text: Simply ---- this is the worst movie that I've ever seen. It is so depressing and boring with zero substance. Not the least bit entertaining. A total waste of my time. Totally stupid.

history.title: The Best of Everything
history.review_title: Worth the watch if just to see Suzy Parker in that RED DRESS.
history.text: I leaned ALOT from this movie. I was a very young 12 yr old when I first saw it --- but it had a lasting impression on me. I guess the most important thing I learned from this movie was to not be naive and let any guy take advantage of me ---because grief and personal regret was right around the corner. I stuck to that philosophy and it served me well. I love looking at the street scenes of New York City from the late '50s. All the women were beautiful --- especially Suzy Parker ---- and oh that RED DRESS. You don't see that kind of class and good taste any more. The plot of the movie is not rocket science but a simple enjoyable story with a simple but worthwhile message.

history.title: Good Ol' Freda
history.review_title: IF YOU LIVED THROUGH AND LOVED THE BEATLES IN THE '60s, YOU ARE GOING TO LOVE THIS FILM !
history.text: Yep. This took me on a wonderful trip down memory lane. It is very hard to describe the feelings experienced at that time in the early '60s. Anything wonderful was possible. The Beatles were so different than anything we had before. It was a thrilling time to be around. Freda Kelley had the job to die for being a part of this wonderful world phenomena. It was hard to even blink while watching the film for fear of missing ANYTHING. Highly recommend it.

history.title: The Boy (2016)
history.review_title: IF YOU ENJOY WATCHING PAINT DRY --- YOU WILL LOVE THIS MOVIE.
history.text: I should have done with this movie what I do with programs on the ID channel. Watch the first 7 minutes (if it remotely holds my interest) and then the last 3. Saves me 50 minutes.

history.review_title: IT IS A LITTLE HARD TO WATCH BUT IT WILL HOLD YOUR INTEREST.
history.text: Rebecca de Morney played the "matriarch" to a tee. Very good acting on her part. The movie did hold my interest till the end.

history.title: Hell Or High Water
history.review_title: WATCHING PAINT DRY IS MUCH MORE HIGHLY ENTERTAINING !!
history.text: I'm into this right now for over a tortuous hour. "What about Bob" is coming on now on another channel. I have no choice. I'd rather watch Bob Wiley for the 45th time than sit through this for another 60 seconds. ---- and is Jeff Bridges ever going to talk normal again without that old man raspy voice? Are we ever going to see the handsome Jeff Bridges again or is it always going to be this long hair, bearded, scraggly, (the have not shaved in over a week) dirty looking guy as of years late? I mean --- can't he scrub up for at least one more decent movie? Anyway, this is one boring ass movie. Can't possibly imagine why anyone would give it more than one star. And even THAT is a stretch.

history.title: Silk Stockings
history.review_title: The last of the big MGM musicals...They almost got it right.
history.text: MGM's production of "Silk Stockings" was vastly superior to the second rate Cole Porter Broadway musical on which it was based, to a great extent because the leading lady, Hildegarde Neff, could neither sing nor dance. Of course, Charisse is dubbed, as she always was, though her very infrequent stage appearances proved that the voice was on key, but too faint unless she was miked heavily. But the lady could sure dance. 'Dancing in the Dark' in :"The Bandwagon" also with Astaire, and the best musical ever made, is the most romantic moment on film, bar none. But the title song, as danced here by Charisse is as beautiful a number as she has ever filmed. (I have to block out 'One Alone' from "Deep in My Heart" as James Mitchell, finally given a chance to dance in an MGM musical, actually steals the number from her no matter how good she is.) Janis Paige is a hoot as a 'dumb' Esther Williams - Williams was not dumb. But Paige is great. And who would have thought that Peter Lorre would make such a good comedian? Astaire and Charisse are perfection together - they always were. But Astaire's final solo should have been dumped before filming. It is the only clunker in the movie's score - the worst of the Broadway show was long gone. He does what he can with it, but it is a losing cause as the song, 'The Ritz Rock and Roll' was dated when it was filmed and has become a pathetic piece of film now. Otherwise, they are magic- but not 'Dancing in the Dark' magic, which surpassed anything Astaire performed with any of his other leading ladies. Yes, including Ginger. For fun, watch Charisse's skirt become a skort, and then a skirt and then.....with really no reason except that the censor board must have hovered over the set making sure that neither the title song nor Paige's 'Silk and Satin' went beyond their limited line. They both did. Never underestimate Arthur Freed when he was determined to get around them. So if this is not in your collection, add it. You won't regret it, though you may fastforward it through the 'Ritz".

history.title: Cover Girl
history.text: "Cover Girl" is a film that almost never was made. Hayworth had made two films with Astaire that she treasured. He was not available and the part was then to be cast with a non-dancer. That didn't balance the film. MGM said 'no' to loaning out Gene Kelly and offered another dancer who was considered too young for Hayworth. Back to the drawing boards. But Kelly began to push LBM and got his way as long as he agreed to two films that MGM wanted him to make, one a nonmusical. Now, the technical aspects started to get in the way. Columbia wanted colour. Columbia could get it, but it meant time and money, neither of which Columbia liked to lose. Convenient illnesses held up the start of production. Then the stars were in alignment, and the movie began, though costumes were still a problem. Looking for something 'different', they finally decided upon ridiculous hats, which Hayworth refused to wear, but Eve Arden looked fabulous in them. And shooting began. Then it stopped while everyone tried to figure out just how to film the solo that Gene Kelly wanted to do, knew how to do, told them how to do, and drew a few days of blank stares. And from that point on, all went smoothly. Musicals should all have such problems if the results are to be this good. What is here is hard to criticize unless one gets truly petty - like how big a stage would a Broadway theatre have to have in order to stage the title number? Yep, Madison Square Garden size, doubled. But it is so gorgeous that one tosses aside logic and lets it wash over you. What is Gloria DeHaven doing in this film when she had already signed with MGM and had far bigger roles? And here, is she even billed? But to heck with all that. Sit back and enjoy one of the few great musicals that MGM did not produce, and in Wartime, too. Just remember, without Hayworth, gloriously talented Hayworth (Watch her in "Separate Tables" to see the full range of that talent) this film would never, problems or not, have been made. If you don't own it - and this is my second CD of the film - buy it now. You'll have to hate musicals not to fall in love with this one.

history.title: Halt and Catch Fire: Season 1 [Blu-ray]
history.text: "Halt and Catch Fire" is so well done that you almost believe it is factual. Part of that is due to the cast, especially Lee Pace who has to walk a fine line between being a louse and a decent human being; and he pulls it off. The insecurities of the character are the giveaways of the real personality and the driving force of this series. Against the lies told, more for his own necessary illusions about himself, they inform us of the other characters true natures. One, Mackenzie Davis, believes only what she chooses, and her choices are usually right, but occasionally spectacularly wrong.This makes her role another difficult one to grasp. The third main character, Scoot McNairy as Joe, is so wrapped up in his work and fears that he sees little as it is, but acts as the anchor that holds it all together. Like real people, it takes a long haul to really get to know them, and even longer to understand them. Be patient; it is worth it. Also, don't watch this series just for amusement; keep your mind alert for all the subtle machiavellian moves. Don't fear the technical side. Most of it is plausible, but unnecessary to the characters - it is the highway that allows us to travel with them and learn a good deal about them and the early years of computer research. All in all, a series that is caviar. It will take about three episodes to grab you, but then it will not let go. Technically, of course, this is a well written, acted, shot piece of the drama of life, with just enough humour to keep us going.

history.title: Les Girls [DVD]
history.review_title: Wait for TCM to show it.
history.text: "Les Girls" might have been a great musical if it had been made ten years earlier. Quite clearly, MGM was no longer willing to spend the money and the time on musicals any longer. The photography is sloppy, as it is in "It's Always Fair Weather", lacking the sharpness and intelligent use of angles and keeping clutter from the dancers' feet. And what could have possessed Mitzi Gaynor to take a role in a film where she doesn't get to sing a solo and her one major number is as a foil for Gene Kelly? Perhaps she should have had a good talk with Cyd Charisse who commented that dancing with Astaire was heaven, with Kelly, hell. The Cole Porter score is functional but there is nothing there to whistle or hum to, and most must have been remnants from his trunk full of discarded songs, what few there are. And the book - oh, where does one start with that mess? With a few good writers, a lot of care, and ruthless rewriting, it might have worked. But it is a slap-dash affair, unworthy to be compared with any of the MGM magical musical of the past. "Lili", for instance, had few songs, but one smash hit, and was presented with such style and charm that it became one of the first MGM musicals to be transferred to Broadway. Buy this if you are a Gaynor fan. Buy it if you loved Kay Kendall, but don't expect her to have much to do of value in this script. Buy this if you want to see an opening number that is so over the top that ego trumps skill every second the song goes on, and on, and on.

history.title: The Bitter Tea of General Yen [Blu-ray]
history.text: Barbara Stanwyck is one of my favorite actresses - she can do just about anything and I'll watch it. Here she plays a young missionary recently arrived in China to marry her childhood sweetheart. While her betrothed and she postpone their wedding to rescue orphans in a war zone, she is rescued by General Yen, who has fallen in love with her. This was a strange film. Megan can't help but be attracted to General Yen, but, at the same time, she finds his cruelty revolting. She tries to convert the General (who bears resemblance to Mephistopheles), but ends up being converted by submitting to him. Is she acting out of guilt? Does she feel naive for believing in Mah-Li and causing the General's downfall? I was surprised at Mah-Li's treachery despite being saved by General Yen and Megan. So much for loyalty. It's all a muddle at the end and General Yen's decision to commit suicide is his answer to get out of the whole mess. There's no happy ending here like the other Capra films I've seen, but only complications that ensue from two people of different races and cultures who have fallen for each other. The B&W cinematography was sumptuous and the Blu-Ray quality excellent. However, despite Stanwyck's presence and the exotic settings and props, the film was just okay. I'd recommend it for Stanwyck and Capra fans only, but it's not a must-see.

history.title: THE MIRACLE WOMAN
history.text: Barbara Stanwyck plays the daughter of a minister who seeks revenge on the hypocritical people of her parish. She teams up with a con artist and becomes a filthy-rich megachurch evangelist. Problems arise when she falls in love with a blind musician who believes in her message of faith. She also learns how hard it is to become honest after partnering with a devious man. This was the second collaboration between Stanwyck and Frank Capra. I loved the scenes between Sister Fallon and John and the dummy, Al. The scene at the beach with crashing waves was also memorable and tender. Stanwyck is wonderful playing a young woman who is naive as well as tough. The only problem I had was the ending; it felt like a deus ex machina. Hornsby, infatuated with Sister Fallon, seemed to set her free after the fire. What happened to all his threats? How was she able to join the Salvation Army with all that Hornsby held over her? Despite the ending, this was a great film. I wonder what the people who get suckered by the megachurch televangelists would think after watching this?

history.title: Landscape in the Mist
history.text: What did I just watch for two hours? Two children embark on a road trip to search for their father in Germany. It's a MacGuffin since we learn from the uncle that there is no father and that it was just a lie. The children refuse to believe it and continue on their quest. Along the way, they meet someone who helps them and someone who rapes the young girl in a terribly disturbing scene. I read that the director was influenced by Orson Welles' long take at the beginning of Touch of Evil. Here, Angelopolous makes virtually every shot in the movie using the long take. Granted, it must've taken a great deal of time and patience to get every shot right, but after awhile, I stopped being impressed and started to wonder where this was going. A giant hand emerges from the water and is carted off by a helicoptor. A tree emerges out of the mist. It was unclear to me what any of this was supposed to mean. Would it have made any difference if a tree had emerged from the water and a giant hand had emerged out of the mist? My conclusion? I thought this was a pretentious movie.

history.title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers [DVD]
history.text: The acting talent seemed wasted in this rather dull film about a murder that took place 18 years ago. I toyed around with the idea of each of the actors switching roles. What, for example, would the film have been if Barbara Stanwyck had taken Toni's role and Kirk Douglas had played Sam? Douglas should've been cast as Sam, but this was his first movie role and no one seemed to know how best to use his talents. Also, I thought Van Heflin was more suited to the meek, devoted Walter O'Connor role. Another idea I had was to begin the film with the ending and show the rest of the film as a flashback. Not sure if those ideas would've helped, though.

history.title: The Deceivers - The Merchant Ivory Collection
history.review_title: Handsome Production and Lead Actor Is Not Enough
history.text: Before I watched this film, I considered Pierce Brosnan to be a wooden actor straight out of GQ magazine. I didn't like him as the suave Remington Steele or as James Bond. His performance in this film, to my surprise, was a step above his usual acting. Here, he plays a British officer in British-controlled India who goes undercover to infiltrate a murderous cult called the Thuggee. Their method is to strangle their victims, rob them, and bury the bodies. Brosnan slowly loses his identity and starts to get off on the killing. It's what he learns about himself that is the most disturbing part of the story. By the end, when he throws away his crucifix, you know that his old beliefs and his wife's love can't help him any longer. The production design including the costumes and period details was excellent. Unfortunately, the film never really took off. Brosnan, despite acting in maybe his best role, did not have the emotional presence to make the film moving to me. The plot also felt thin and stretched out to nearly two hours with repetitive killings and chase scenes through vegetation.

history.title: Sherlock
history.text: After Sir Arthur Conan Doyle brought Sherlock back to life in The Empty House, there were a few more good stories left but a noticeable drop in quality. It was as if the author was tired of the character or, possibly, just ran out of good ideas. The same unraveling started to occur in Season 3 of Sherlock and continued with an unpleasant and sloppy Season 4. The series jumped the shark when Charles Augustus Magnussen's would-be assassin turned out to be Mary Morstan. With the introduction of a psychopathic sister, Eurus, and her disguises as therapist, handicapped daughter, and love interest, the implausibility stretched so far that it snapped. Moreover, the horror story at Sherrinford was not entertaining like the cat-and-mouse games between Sherlock and Moriarty or Irene Adler, it was just unpleasant to watch. I was looking forward to a Season 5, but after this, it may be a good time to put the series to rest. Overall, I enjoyed the first two Seasons with the exception of "The Blind Banker". A Scandal in Belgravia was the highlight of the entire series for me.

history.title: Paths of Glory
history.text: The film does a good job showing the insanity of war and a little of what it must've been like to be in a trench during WW I. Kirk Douglas, always watchable, plays a colonel in the French army who's ordered to lead a suicide mission. As the soldiers scramble across the barbed wire and rocky terrain, I was reminded of ants. Then, I remembered their objective was to take Anthill - we're all insects here. As if to drive the point home, a soldier squashes a cockroach. The main problem is that Kirk Douglas alone wears a white hat while all the surrounding officers wear black hats. There seems to be no in-betweens. The two officers in charge are depicted as slimy and less-than-human. At one point, Douglas accuses Adolphe Menjou of being a sadistic, old man. The kangaroo court doesn't fare well either. We're meant to hate these people in power, who eat nice dinners and go off to their luxurious parties. Yes, there probably were officers like these, but were all of them? For this reason, the film, while making a strong statement about the absurdity and cruelty of war, falls short because of its simplistic characterizations.

history.title: Sleep My Love
history.text: It's hard to see what attracted Sirk to this project. Maybe it was assigned to him? It's about a rich woman, Claudette Colbert, whose husband, Don Ameche, plots to make her believe that she's mad. He plans for her to commit suicide and, after she's dead, continue living with his mistress. Plans go awry when Colbert meets and falls in love with her friend's friend, played by an amusing Robert Cummings. The cinematography is nice, but absent is Sirk's style and themes. It's pretty straightforward and runs a little too long. In Jon Halliday's book of interviews with Sirk, the director didn't have too much to say about it except that he remembered the Chinatown wedding. He also said that he wanted to emphasize Colbert's split character and believed that was the most interesting part of the story. I'm not sure what he meant by this -- her doubts about her madness? Or, her unwillingness to believe that her husband was trying to make her insane? Whatever the case, Sirk's lack of interest in the project showed.

history.title: Stay Hungry [DVD]
history.text: I watched this film because I'm a big fan of Sally Field. She plays the love interest of Jeff Bridges, who works for a real estate company intent on buying a gym to make way for an expensive high rise. The cast has a likable charm. I especially liked the chemistry between Jeff and Sally. The film is set in Alabama and retains a lot of local color including a fiddling band where Arnold Schwarzenegger (!) plays. Unfortunately, the second half isn't good. Jeff Bridges acts like a jerk at a country club party for some inexplicable reason. He's supposed to be ashamed of his friends, Sally and Arnold, because they aren't sophisticated enough, but there was no setup for this turn of character; it just came out of the blue. The plot became disjointed and tedious and I just wanted it to end. It was worth watching, especially for Sally Field and Jeff Bridges, but it's too bad the second half fell apart. Arnold is also likable although his acting range and role is limited.

Richard Pasco does an excellent job playing Brutus in this adaptation of Julius Caesar. I found him convincing as a person who agonizes over doing what he thinks is right against betraying his friend. Also, the very qualities which make him so honorable prove to be his undoing; he projects his own values and beliefs on the crowd and on Mark Antony, imagining that they'll understand why the assassins had to do what they did. Of course, Brutus should've heeded Cassius' warnings, but, just like every other piece of advice Cassius offered, didn't listen. The scenes which moved me the most were the intimate conversations between husband and wife, both Brutus' wife, Portia, and Caesar's wife, Calpurnia. I also liked the short exchanges between Brutus and his young servant, Lucius, and Brutus' tender regard for him. My sympathies, curiously, were with Brutus even though he perpetrated such a dastardly deed. I wondered why? Mark Antony and Octavius weren't likable, although they seemed to be on the right side. The only thing I didn't like about this production was that it seemed to drag in places, especially Mark Antony's funeral oration. Whether it was the fault of the production, the choice of actor, or the play itself, I'm not sure. Finally, my favorite line in all the play was said by Titinius when he discovers Cassius has killed himself. "Alas, thou hast misconstrued everything."

history.review_title: A genuine classic, and it looks great in HD!
history.text: This film impresses me for what it was able to accomplish given the era when it was made. Like another of Wells' story-to-movie, The Invisible Man, this is an enjoyable translation and an absolute classic. Rod Taylor's performance as The Traveller was as well done as fans of his work might expect. It's much different from the Guy Pearce film, but seeing this should explain some of the influences it has over the remake. This is a better adaptation of the original story, and still a treat to watch so many years after it was made.

In terms of a remake, this is a far departure from the original. In terms of something new, it's well-imagined and adds some ethereal quality to the horror genre. It would've been interesting to explore the characters further, but for what this film was, it was worth the price of a rental.
