history.text: Go to your nearest home improvement store. Buy a sheet of plywood, paint, and a paint brush. Paint one side of the plywood sheet. Pull up a chair and watch the paint dry. Congratulations! You've just done something more productive with your time than watch this movie. Seriously, I've seen all kinds of movies, but if a movie doesn't end the way you want it, you should at least have a modicum of satisfaction at the end. This is the most unsatisfying movie I've ever seen. If you must watch it, rent it, don't buy it. But if you need not watch it, don't. You'd be better off painting the other side of the plywood.

history.title: The Middle: Season 1
history.text: To be honest, I bought this show for one reason: Neil Flynn. And if we're all being honest, he was the funniest character on Scrubs. While that type of character doesn't completely translate in this series, I have, nonetheless, enjoyed his acting. Like most brand-new shows, the first few episodes are a little uneven. But as the series progresses through the first season, the quality greatly improves. And I like the idea that I have eight more seasons to enjoy the show, though it was recently announced that the ninth season will be the last.

history.title: The Lost City of Z
history.text: Like so many other contemporary films, The Lost City of Z has potential, but ultimately ends in an unsatisfying and disappointing way. Save your time, save your money, and skip this one.

history.title: xXx: Return Of Xander Cage
history.text: I don't know where to start. To say this movie was horribly clichéd would be a compliment. I can't even articulate how bad it was. Is it just me, or are movies these days that are funded by the Chinese particularly bad? I like Vin Diesel, which is why I bought the film in the first place, but man, this is so bad. Did you really need a paycheck this badly, Vin? If you like Vin Diesel, I'd suggest any of the Chronicles of Riddick films.

history.title: Kong: Skull Island (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: Could have been a straight-to-DVD film
history.text: Yet another bad movie funded by the Chinese. Kong proves, once again, that throwing a bunch of big names into a movie does not a good film make. This film is completely directionless, introducing characters and plot lines that lead absolutely nowhere. The *only* thing that kept this movie from being a complete washout was John C. Reilly. No, I really mean that. There's also an Asian woman in the film who has about five lines, and was apparently only added to appeal to Asian audiences. She has no memorable presence in the film. And for goodness sakes, please stop throwing Samuel L. Jackson into every fourth movie created these days. You're killing the guy, and we need him for the Avengers movies. Someone wake me up when they start making good movies again for American audiences.

history.title: Brooklyn Nine-Nine: Season Four [DVD]
history.review_title: It was good while it lasted.
history.text: This show has definitely lost steam fast. I thoroughly enjoyed the first three seasons, but...what happened? I can deal with the mild gay references, but after one of the characters suggested that one of the other characters needed to "bone" his husband, I'm done. If you're reading this and you enjoy boning another man, whether you are also a man, hey, whatever. But I don't watch TV (and I certainly don't pay) to hear this kind of stuff. Permanently dropping this show would be more difficult, if this season weren't so bad. And I didn't get back the first disk.

history.title: Fences [BD/Digital HD Combo] [Blu-ray]
history.text: Maybe I take some movies too personally, but I don't like to see actors I generally favor (Denzel) portraying jerks. I did find some interesting similarities between Denzel's character in this movie and his character in Training Day: both were abusive, both cheated on their wives, and both died at the end. Of course, in his movie, Denzel's character doesn't die in a hailstorm of bullets, but if he had, I would have been okay with that. I'm honestly not sure why I watched this to the end. In some movies which portray a difficult character, the writers give you an out, explaining why the character is so unlikable. Not so here. Considering the course the movie takes, the photo on the cover is completely misleading. Bottom line, Denzel's (and he is the reason I watched it in the first place) character is a reprobate with genuinely no redeeming characteristics of which to speak. Skip this one. But if you are looking for a good Denzel movie, I recommend The Equalizer.

history.title: Going in Style (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: Oh, Zach Braff directed it? That explains it...
history.text: I loved Scrubs, but I would have been okay if Zach Braff hadn't been in every season of the show. But this isn't about Braff's bad acting, it's about his bad directing. You would think with this level of star power, this movie would be pretty amazing, but instead, it shows once again that great actors can only do so much with a weak story and script. Just before the bank robbery, one of the supporting male actors says that, "There is always another way." Why? What was the point of this line? The characters were going to rob the bank, no matter what. And I'm supposed to be happy about the movies happy ending? They still stole millions of dollars from innocent people. This movie could have been so much more, and had it not had the actors it did, I would have given it a one or two star rating. This isn't worth the money.

history.title: Fixer Upper Season 1

But they also get the job done, turning plain (or nearly condemned) houses into lovely homes. I only wish Season Two and forward were available on DVD.

The audience is left with the question of whether the lady who said she was Anatasia Romanov, was actually the Grand Duchess Anastasia, daughter of Tsar Nicholas II. I don't know?

history.text: Worked great in my Pioneer Blu-ray player. Picture quality is amazing. Also sound is perfect. An excellent movie that I thoroughly enjoyed. There is another, longer version of this movie that shows the young Hitler youth boy picking up a P-38 pistol and shooting a Russian soldier with it. After he does so he regrets doing it and returns home to his Father. This scene, for some unknown reason, has been edited from the movie. So I must change my review from 5 stars to one star. history.title: Fury [Blu-ray]
history.text: The movie was pretty good. But I have a few negatives that prevent it from being 5 star. #1 While the color is magnificent, the movie is letterboxed. What the heck, this is Blu-ray made for hi-def TVs in 2015, not 1980s square glass picture tubes. C'mon Sony, you can do better than this. #2 The movie has some propaganda aspects and Hollywood silliness to it. For instance, Brad Pitt's character carries around a nickel-plated pimp revolver instead of the issue 1911A1 Semi-auto. Even back then I think his Commanding Officer would have told him to lose it, or at least hide it. Either Brad Pitt or the Director thought it would look "more macho", I guess. It looks ridiculous. #3 The Waffen-SS troops marching in the open and singing songs. Really? In 1945 the allies had air superiority and they would have been wiped out very quickly. Plus the morale of ALL German troops by then was very low. Even the Waffen-SS knew it was over, although they kept on fighting bravely and loyally. So showing them marching merrily along like they were in downtown Berlin during a 1938 parade was ridiculous. Plus they made the CO of the SS look more like a Russian officer than a German one. The officers in the Waffen-SS fought right alongside their men. They didn't just stay back and encourage them.

history.title: Guardians Of The Galaxy
history.text: I'm only gonna review the technical aspects of the movie, as you either like it or don't. I bought the Blu-ray 3D movie, which included a standard Blu-ray version. The 3D is just plain spectacular and really ads a lot to the movie. Audio is sharp and clear, and the music really sounds great. Be advised that even though this movie is Blu-ray, when you watch it on a wide screen HD TV, it WILL be letterboxed. That is because of the 2.40-1 aspect ratio. I had the same thing with the movie "Fury". The 3D version also changes aspect ratios, but it is SUPPOSED to do that because of the way it was filmed. Other movies in 3D do the exact same thing. Anyway, my opinion it is definitely worth the money. Buy it. Enjoy it. I AM GROOT! :-)

history.title: Lord Of Illusions (Collector's Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I already have the DVD Director's Cut, so the content was no surprise to me. I am a major fan of this movie, so I wanted to see if there was any improvement in the picture with Blu-ray. I can happily report that there IS a major improvement through the great majority of the movie. The only part that doesn't look any different from DVD is the opening with the credits. There is a tiny bit of speckling on the print that is still visible with Blu-ray. But as soon as you move forward to Harry in his apartment, the picture makes a major improvement. And all through the rest of the movie the clarity and colors look spectacular, When you see the construction guy climbing out of the hole he is working in when Harry is visiting the mental hospital, you can actually count the blades of grass on the ground!!! It's that sharp in detail. Audio is also quite good. There are two possibilities with the slight film flaws in the beginning of the film. Either this was the best print they could find for the beginning of the film, or it was done intentionally to give the appearance of it being earlier in time. I haven't watched the movie yet with any commentary, so I don't know if Mr. Barker mentions it. All in all I would say the Blu-ray is definitely worth getting. The Director's Cut is the ONLY way to watch this movie. I find it interesting that cable channels are still airing this movie in the theatrical version, but in HD. Whatever they are showing doesn't come close to the picture on Blu-ray. I still watch it on cable, but more as an avid fan and tradition than anything else.

history.title: Halloween (Two-Disc Unrated Collector's Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I am not going to waste anyone's time reviewing the movie. If you have seen it already, you know what it's about. Me telling people how good or bad it is won't change their idea about buying it. I AM going to describe the transfer and any extras on the disc. First off, the Blu-ray transfer is fantastic. It is incredibly sharp and clear. Clearer than any other Blu-Ray I own, and I have a bunch. And clearer than what you see on an HD channel on TV. It is that clear and bright. It does have bars on top and bottom, but that is because it is in 2.40:1. That is the original size of the movie and the only way they can fit ALL of it on a TV screen. I have a large screen (52 inch) plasma TV so it looked just fine that way. The audio gave a choice of two types. Either one was clear and crisp.Not sure exactly what the difference between the two is, but I experienced no problems using either. The deleted scenes on the disc were interesting, but I am not sure all of them are present. I have seen some scenes on YouTube from the movie that were NOT on the disc. One being a group of security guards who were assigned to move Michael Meyers from the original hospital to a less secure hospital. Michael made short and gruesome work of them. That scene is missing from the movie and deleted scenes. It IS nice that the deleted scenes all have subtitles as an option. The second Halloween by Zombie didn't have that, and some of the the dialogue is hard to understand on his Halloween II. The second disc includes a 4 hour "made for" by Rob Zombie. Haven't watched it yet. All in all the Blu-Ry version is worth every penny I paid.

history.title: Francis the Talking Mule Complete Collection
history.text: I bought the 4 movie collection earlier and was happy for the old fashioned non violent themes. So when I saw the complete series at a great price I jumped on it. Everything would have been fairytale but I run into the occasional glitch in the sales process. See the unscrupulous venders will create a shipping label and tell the overlord that it's on its way, pay me. But in reality the item takes weeks to send, either through outright fraud or they'd rather ship once weekly instead of daily. Meantime the overseer takes your money and pays the huckster. This happens every day but most don't realize the scam perpetrated on them and wait and wait and wait for their purchase. It would be caught by normal business practices and reported as fraud. But the overlord has a vested interest in keeping status quo so there is faith in the system. Wouldn't want a panic in the masses causing loss of sales and/or profit. Much better to screw the occasional buyer and give free money to the scoundrel. Eventually the product gets to the customer. Why bother with keeping sellers honest.

history.title: A Fish Called Wanda
history.review_title: Better than expected blu-ray transfer for this 27 year old classic (except for the opening shots)
history.text: I avoided this blu-ray transfer for quite awhile, with quality concerns based on several o the review here on Amazon. Not to fear - it was perfectly adequate, in fact, OK (one you got past the opening scenes on the first "reel") The transfer was actually on par for other low-budget films of the 80s. The audio track, despite its DTS transfer, remains fair. It's all front end loaded with poor differentiation between speakers. Volume had to be turned up for speaking, then turned down for those synth outbursts in the soundtrack. As noted, the film contains no extras - these would have necessitated a DVD to accompany the blu-ray. I didn't feel the need to make any additional adjustments on either my player or projector. The picture quality, contrast, saturation (surprisingly) were all good. No one will ever mistake this for a transfer on par with, say, Finding Nemo, but then again - anyone who is expecting that is a bit naive. Hmm…what does Nemo go well with? AAaahhhh…..chips!

history.title: Paul Simon & Friends
history.review_title: A WONDERFULLY ENJOYABLE EVENING OF SONG, WITH A PAINFULLY DIFFICULT FINAL PERFORAMANCE
history.text: This is a wonderful film, of a truly great night for American song craft - Paul Simon's receipt of the Gershwin Prize for popular music, at the Library Of Congress. Excellent video, and great DTS soundtrack. This one excels on all fronts (Allison Krauss is simply amazing!) But alas - it ends with Glass. Glass' composed music does not go over my head (as suggested by another commentator) in fact I own many recordings of his music. But ending the concert with his tortured, hamstrung, heavy handed performance of Sounds Of Silence is simply awful. Dreadful. Glass has had some wonderful collaborative efforts with Simon - most notably in composing the coda for Simon's "The Late Great Johnny Ace". But Glass the composer is a basher of a pianist. He bludgeons this keystone song of Simon's career into an unrecognizable pile of rubble. (If you want to hear some of Glass' piano music performed with great delicacy and beauty I suggest listening to Bruce Levingstone's recording of a suite of music from Glass' soundtrack to Dracula - extraordinarily beautiful [[ASIN:B005OZDXSW Nightbreak]] Adding to this disappointment was the penultimate performance that lead into it - Stevie Wonder missed his cue on a verse of Loves Me Like A Rock and stops the entire song dead in its tracks as Simon - ever the perfectionist - looks on aghast ("Sorry - I couldn't read my cue cards!" jokes Wonder) The song starts all over again, but the aging Dixie Hummingbirds are running out of steam and this dynamic song never truly takes flight. This is the performance that sets the stage for the shards of Glass, er, Sounds Of Silence. Up until this point, the concert, as noted by other reviewers, is phenomenal. Well, not to be too much of a curmudgeon, but Bridge Over Troubled Water with Artie has some rough spots too. The pianist loses her way at one point, and then indelicately plays an awkward key modulation down about a third in order to allow Artie to hit those final notes that he can no longer hit. The good news - is that he was still in decent vocal condition when this concert was filmed. It's fun to see and hear the boys together again. ("My good friend, and partner in arguments…" jokes Simon) My only other disappointment is that Simon didn't perform Wartime Prayers, which was saluted in the introductory remarks to the program. A truly remarkable song. Simon - more than any other American songwriter - deserved this first Gershwin prize. A truly remarkable artist. Little did they know, that Simon was about to record several of the finest songs of his career on his most recent recording: So Beautiful Or So What. The song "Love And Hard Times" is simply, as Duke Ellington used to say, "beyond category". The same can be said of Paul Simon. A class act - beyond category.

history.text: As far as bio-pics go, Lust For Life is one of the best. Kirk Douglas was superb in his portrayal (and guttural groaning) of the tormented Dutch artist. history.review_title: A truly sad epilogue to a career studded with moments of genius
history.text: Horrible. SImply horrible. And I used to wait on line at the Cinema I & II on the East Side for the opening midnight showings of new Allen movies back in the 70s. Allen was quoted for months as saying this project terrified him, and he had no idea what he was going to do. And now, the end result of that process makes it painfully obvious that he was right. We spend much of the time watching two legendary comedians from the 50s and 60s (Allen and Elaine May) attempt to re-create their half-century-gone-by personas painfully. Very, very painfully. It is difficult to understand what May is saying at times - it appears that the poor woman had a stroke at some point, but apparently hasn't. The slurred speech has resulted from too much plastic surgery. The material is old Woody shtick. But now, his delivery is slower and the lines sound labored and forced. While it's nice to see him paired with an actress his age, it was inevitable that he'd create a part for a younger muse. In this case, Miley Cyrus. I must say, the kids pulls it off. But unfortunately in doing so, she underscores the truly sad, pathetic due she plays against. Groucho Marx said (and I'm paraphrasing here) that he couldn't imagine running around with the cigar chasing women in films when he was 50, it was getting ridiculous. So, he and his brothers disbanded. Woody Allen should have heeded Groucho's advice. He's way beyond his Amazon Prime.

history.title: The Marx Brothers Silver Screen Collection (The Cocoanuts / Animal Crackers / Monkey Business / Horse Feathers / Duck Soup) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Love, love, love this collection! The comedy is timeless, but the celluloid was not. This is the clearest, cleanest transfer that I have seen of these films, and overall, I am quite pleased. Others have been hypercritical of the quality of the nearly 90 year old (!) optical soundtracks recorded on a small soundstage in Queens, NY - but really...digital transfers have only been a fairly recent option, and I am just grateful and thankful that these cinema treasures are in as good condition as they are. I project them using a Ben-Q projector onto a 6' diagonal screen and find it hard to believe that their original audiences had it much better than this. Hooray for Captain Spaulding!

history.review_title: TRANSPARENT JUMPS THE SHARK AND BECOMES OPAQUE
history.text: What happened to Transparent? From the opening scenes and episodes it was very, very obvious that something has gone very, very wrong. Not only with the Pfeffermans whose various eccentricities and neuroses have blossomed into psychosis, and also with the writers who seem to have lost their voice, their style, and their sense of sublime (and not so sublime) the season seemed gratuitous, unnecessary, and a desparate ploy to get some "new stuff" into an otherwise unwatchable season. Same with the whole trip to Israel These characters - with the exceptional of Jeffrey Tambor who remains a national treasure - have morphed into thoroughly unlikable, disagreeable, ethnically stereotyped, I don't know - dare I say - dotards. The Pfeffermans? Feh!

history.review_title: I never thought I would ever say "boring action" but here it is.
history.text: The best way to summarize our experience with this movie is "overly action packed". Not that it had lots of different action sequences, or the action was interesting, but it was super redundant - the same childish action fighting over and over. It was so much action that after a short while it became annoyingly numbing and diluted the good parts of what could have been a great movie. There was really good dialogue, story, and acting across the entire cast to interest us however, but lost in the incessant distraction of all the cookie cutter overflowing action. They made a movie to appeal to both intellect and extreme childish comic figure action- just way too much childish action. When the acting is very good as it was in this movie, you just don't expect it to be "ruined" by too much ridiculous action. But that is how to sell movies across all age groups, even though without all the repetitive boring action I would have really enjoyed this movie and given it at least four stars.

history.title: Haunted Honeymoon (1986) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: We turned it off after 30 minutes. We never hated a movie so much. This desperately needed Mel Brooks as the director!
history.text: After five minutes we looked at each other like, "Wow this is really bad!" But we gave it a chance. And another. And yet another. The so called jokes and gags were just...so empty, immature and ridiculously boring (and stupid). For example, the disproportionately amplified musical accent crescendo when one particular character knocked on the castle door was annoying and lame. Then the "looks" that character gave to others (and them back) which I suppose was supposed to funny, wasn't. Not even close. Even the worst comedy movie I ever saw was ten times better than this and I am not exaggerating. This would be funny for a six year old. And we love our comedies! We've seen them all! After 30 minutes and bad boring silly gag after bad boring silly gag, we said, Gene Wilder should have stuck to acting and never attempt directing- this was really that hard to watch. What a waste. And a wasted 14 bucks for this blu-ray since it was not available to just rent on Amazon Video. Can't give it a s a gift (it's opened and I would never insult anyone's intelligence.) Oh well. Don't trust reviews. You know that famous Socrates quote, If you want to be wrong then follow the masses? Well this movie is the "poster child" for that!

history.title: The Original Keystone Comedies, Vol. 4: Mabel's Wilful Way, That Little Band of Gold, and Mabel and Fatty's Married Life [VHS]
history.review_title: Cute Silent. But if you are hoping to see a lot of Idora Amusement Park, you might be disappointed.
history.text: OK. I've just seen Mabel's Wilful Way on TCM. It was really cute, and the comedy is timeless. What else can say about a movie that was literally ad libbed with no script at all? (None of the stunts were big or dangerous?) Greg Proops said that in his introduction. A very small crew and group of actors would go to a place and use whatever was around to create a little story as they went along. There aren't even hardly any cards to let you know what they were saying in this Silent. But none of that was important to me. Here is what was... If you're hoping to see much of Idora Park that WAS in Oakland, CA from 1904 to 1929, you might be very disappointed. In this little Silent Movie you only get to see: One bear One Ice Cream Stand Two Carnival Games One Slide One Merry Go Round And some landscaping You never get to see even a glimpse of even one of the roller coasters, or the dark ride, or anything else. That was very disappointing.

And the telling of their story is LONG over due, and imperative to increasing the understanding that there are MANY black people who are SMARTER and MORE IMPORTANT than many WHITE People. history.title: Double Indemnity
history.text: I have always considered Double Indemnity to be the "Daddy" of all crime dramas, then, now and probably forever. Although it seems to be considered a "film noir" by almost all, it was made (1944) some time before anyone ever heard of that term and strictly speaking, it isn't one but it matters not, it can be considered film noir even if it doesn't strictly fit the definition of noir. The story line is classic (femme-fatale) and has been remade in variants at least twice, "Body Heat" and "Body Language." Body Heat is also one of the great "noirs" and very close and almost equal in quality and entertainment / suspense value as D.I. I need add nothing to the voluminous great reviews other than to mention that if Billy Wilder was involved it deserves our attention.

history.title: Body Language [DVD]
history.review_title: A PRETTY GOOD AND INTRIGUING "B" MOVIE A LA BODY HEAT
history.text: Body Language has been called by some reviewers "depressing," "The pits," etc. I can't agree. it's essentially a well crafted "B" movie, a variant of the classic and great "Body Heat" which was a variant of the classic and superb "Double Indemnity" (1944). It is well cast and performed (especially Nancy Travis) and worth a look by fans of the genre. it's certainly not a "smiley face" movie and is rather grim in spots but it will hold your interest up to the twister ending.

history.title: Body Heat (Deluxe Edition)
history.text: A remake of 1944's superb Double Indemnity and almost, if not actually, its equal. These two films are (for me) the greatest crime dramas ever made. They hold up consistently under many repeated viewings. The makers of Body Heat have managed an amazing feat, conveying the humidity, heat and atmosphere of the locations so well that if you were watching in an ice locker there would be perspiration rolling off your body. Plus, the great music score conveys the same conditions. A truly great film and a perfect example of how to make movies.

history.title: The Artist [DVD]
history.text: I saw this film for the first time earlier tonight on TCM. Bless them for that!! I first became aware of it a few years ago via a friend who'd just seen it and told me it was excellent. When I learned it was a silent I tuned out and promptly completely forgot about it . MY LOSS! The only silents that ever really interested me were the Chaplin gems and his full-length feature "City lights" which i've long considered to be one of the three greatest films of all-time and which I see as the very likely inspiration for this film as the plots bear a close relationship. Had "City Lights" been a "talkie" or shot in color it would mot have the impact it has in its original state. In that vein, 'The Artist" may very well be a near equal or actually equal to "City Lights" in quality, artistry and impact on the viewer. Only one thing about this film mystifies me, part of he music score. At approximately 88 minutes running time the music becomes quite dramatic and romantic and VERY familiar. It is very similar to, if not actually note for note identical in parts to what I would call the Love Theme" in Vertigo by composer Bernard Herrmann. I'm sure that's not the title of that music cue but it's an apt description of the Vertigo music which i haven't the time or inclination to look up at the moment. But trust me, as a musician, if that music cue were played for me sans picture I would bet it all that it was Vertigo. (See my addenda concerning this mystery below) This detracts nothing from the film but the similarity really struck and amazed me. The film is absolutely magnificent and the casting of the five leads (including the Jack-Russel terrier which I suspect is related to Fraiser's pooch, Eddie) is beyond perfect). I am about to order the DVD having been totally enthralled by this superb film and especially the two stars. ADDENDA: It's a couple of days since I composed this review and I;'ve just learned from Wikipedia's page on the film that the music in question is indeed Bernard Herrmann's "Scene D'amour" from Vertigo. Unless I overlooked it there was no mention of this in the film's credits. Now I feel better.

history.review_title: YOU WILL SEE BETTER FILM ON TEETH!
history.text: I am about half-way through it and will have to force myself to see this turkey through to its conclusion if there ever is one. it is impenetrable and amateurish and (as per the DVD) seems to have been shot in the dark. I often wonder what has happened to people's minds that they can give such high praise to such boring and (to repeat) impenetrable efforts. I realize that most will think it unfair to judge a film before seeing it through to the end and they are probably justified but at this point the film should have offered something, no matter how minuscule to pique my interest even slightly. Maybe that was the intent of the unforgettable opening scene, so far the only aspect worthy of praise. I purchased the disc new from one of Amazon's third party vendors for only two cents (bless Amazon for their third party vendors. Thanks to them and the great prices I'm greatly increasing the size of my collection) but even at that price this film is a rip. You will see better film on teeth.

history.title: Rehearsal for Murder DVD
history.text: I first saw this gem on commercial TV years ago and was immediately captivated. I later found it in a 3 DVD set titled INVITATION TO MURDER (long gone) and purchased it. As the video quality was a bit wanting, I ordered this one in the hope that there would be an improvement. There is. It's not perfect (it could be a bit more sharp) but decent enough, especially considering that it's from an old TV movie. This is a truly excellent and brilliantly conceived mystery. Comparisons to Colombo by other reviewers are ludicrous and sadly uninformed. Colombo was fine but this is an entirely different animal worthy of comparison to Agatha Christie. If she'd been listed as the author I think few people would know the difference. Further, I suspect that only the most capable mystery writers or buffs will be able to figure out who the culprit is. It's a real twister and a most refreshing delight. Add Robert Preston who was one of our greatest actors supported by an excellent cast and you have a film that should be far better known. DO NOT take seriously the poor boobs who panned this film. They wouldn't know a high quality creation if they ate it for lunch. it's for them that the old saw about TV being a vast wasteland or brain shrinker applies. There is great stuff out there for those capable of appreciating it and who know where to find it. Miss this one at your own peril.

history.title: Amazing Stories: Season 1
history.text: The "MUMMY DADDY" episode in this fine series is, alone, worth the price of admission. It is hysterically finny and brilliantly clever almost beyond description and the performances are first-rate. It never fails to bring a huge smile to my face and great laughs whenever it comes to mind. it should have won an Oscar or at the very least been nominated. Any viewer who can't appreciate this brilliant marvel is very likely already a mummy and has my sympathy for missing one of the important things in life. Also worthy of mention is an earlier episode in the series, "THE MAIN ATTRACTION." It too is brilliant and very funny but not quite up to the level of "MUMMY DADDY". Few things are! Miss these at your own peril. JD

history.title: The Empire of the Wolves
history.text: Jean Reno is pretty fun if not on the edge of crazy and dark, although his part is more of a supporting role. The movie suffers from too many sub plot points all trying to rule the empire of being the major plot point. A little horror nightmarish, a little Jason Bourne, a little Fringe. If they stuck to one of these, the movie could have been better. Unfortunately it doesn't. If you're looking for Jean Reno films, this one is a "maybe-catch-it-on-TV-sometime" viewing. Won't miss too much. Also, in terms of family friendliness, it is rated R and for good reason. Some grisly dark violent scenes, as well as nudity and language.

history.title: Mrs. Soffel
history.text: Well acted, well filmed and based on a true story. The studio likes to promote this one by saying both Mel's character and Diane's are seeking and finding freedom. In reality and figuratively, though, throughout the film it show's Mel's character's struggle to escape prison, while Diane's--deceived into thinking she needs freedom--is spiritually deceived into finding a prison in her sins, as well as one to physically sit in. Movie features some nice Biblical allegory and Scripture for discussion and a nice score by Mark Isham. For family friendliness there is a scene or two to fast-forward.

history.title: The Fight Before Christmas
history.text: The Trinity boys back for Christmas! You can never really have enough Christmas westerns. John Wayne's "3 Godfathers" is a great one. Chuck Norris did a version for "Walker: Texas Ranger". And if you like the Trinity movies and the Hill/Spencer collaborations, you'll enjoy this! Though different characters, they live up to their Trinity western personas with some new gags and nods to previous ones. Filmed in the early '90s, they bring about an emphasis on family (much like the recent Indiana Jones movie).

history.title: Suicide Squad (Extended Cut / Blu-ray)
history.text: Wow, so maybe a studio shouldn't hire as many people as they apparently did to write positive reviews of a movie that sucks rotten eggs like this one. Especially when trying to dupe Amazon customers. It becomes way too obvious. Some claim to have known the Joker's part was small; however, that could only be true if they worked for the studio and knew ahead of time, or were told by peers who were giving them reasons why they thought the movie was one of the worst ones they had ever seen and that Uncle Rico's football movie was Award worthy in comparison. Margot Robbie's acting is the only decent piece of this mess of a puzzle. However, her origin part (of the 13 or so origin stories quickly told in this movie) is horribly written and doesn't make sense. Will Smith's acting wasn't believable--he tried to force his bad guy image. The Batman cameos were basically shown in the trailer...and Bruce Wayne gets easily duped again, this time by Amanda Waller's character. The directing and editing was a mess: they should have taken notes from Mos Def's and Jack Black's characters in "Be Kind Rewind" (Granted that is possibly the studio's fault for trying to step in and fix the complaints of BvS on this film...hopefully not that of David Ayers). Oh and the music soundtrack? Clearly trying to copy "Guardians of the Galaxy" except it's almost like a spoof here. Way too many hits (more than likely to try and sell a CD soundtrack hoping to generate more dough than this film would provide), and very forced, not even making sense in the scenes they're played in. Think 10-15 seconds of the top 50 classic songs played every 30 seconds apart, no matter the scene. For a real sense of the movie, please look up The Honest Trailer.

history.title: David and Bathsheba
history.text: If you are looking for a Biblical truth in this movie you won't really find too many. This is a fantasy written about David the king. The design of Uriah's death is only planned after he finds out about Bathsheba being with child according to Scripture. Only after was Uriah sent for by King David. The proposed death of Bathsheba by the prophet Nathan and the people is completely false. Nathan came to King David and told him what the Lord said would happen to him. Not the townspeople. There is nothing in Scripture about David pleading for the life of Bathsheba. that is fabricated David placing his hands on the Ark and not dying is against Scriptural teaching and not found in II Samuel. After watching the movie I decided to read II Samuel again. Chapter 112 states Joab went out to fight Rabbah and David remained in Jerusalem. Therefore he would not be fighting at Rabbah and having a conversation with Uriah. The movie was slow moving, just this side of boring. But a true fantasy. This is truly only a movie for entertainment and not Biblical teaching.

history.title: Parental Guidance
history.text: I am very disappointed after seeing this film. I have always enjoyed Bette Midler's work, and thought with her teamed up with Billy Crystal, the film would have to be funny. I was so wrong. The film is about three kids that are catered to 24/7, and all the adults in their world that spend their lives catering to them. The children are rude and disrespectful, and allowed to throw one tantrum after another because Artie, played by Crystal, DARED to try to impose any limits on their behavior, or to tell them NO. The youngest little cretin ruined a symphony performance, in only one example of his behavior, and still Artie was chastised for even implying that discipline would result. All the adults spent all their time apologizing to the children, when the children, specifically the youngest, were the ones that had done wrong, and should have been taught that they were doing wrong. Sadly, this kind of "non parenting" has become prevalent, where the children are in charge of the adults and the household, and it's doing no one any favors, least of all the children. I don't know how Crystal's character could have told Tomei's character that she was a "good mother," with a straight face. Non parenting, and allowing horrible behavior, is being the worst kid of parent. Bribing the children with cake and money was pretty bad grandparenting as well, and I didn't like how Midler's character kept ragging on Crystal for trying to discipline the children, and ruining her chance to be the "fun" grandmother. I did feel for the oldest child, who was being pushed into devoting her entire life to playing the violin. It is ironic, that the film was about "parents making sure that children are heard" yet no one heard that child. I guess that some people thought the movie was funny, if they like seeing horrible monster children being as horrible as possible while their mother looks on lovingly, and seeing zero respect for any adults exhibited or expected, and seeing all the adults crawling around catering to and placating the children. I didn't think it was funny. I gave the film one star because I can't give it less.

I find all the glowing reviews for a 'wonderful family film" disturbing, when it shows the kids having gross disrespect for the adults, especially Vin's character at least, and causing a woman to fall down the stairs at most, with no one saying a word about it. We have a little girl following Lt Wolfe around asking him personal questions, and then when he tries to send her off, she screams "disrespectful" and says she is "no longer interested" in him. Sadly I think that scene nails what is wrong with the film. The kids are in charge and feel that their feelings and wants are the only things that matter, and feel free to do and say whatever they want to, even when they hurt people. That is not a good message for a "marvelous family film," nor is it funny.

history.title: The Girl Who Spelled Freedom [VHS]
history.text: Just saw this film again on VHS, after seeing it so many years ago, and it is still such a good film. I too wonder why it is not on DVD. I also think that it is very important for American kids to see this, now more than ever, as kids' feelings of entitlement have gone through the roof. Linn is just heartbreaking, with her courage, spirit and amazing intelligence! The two things that bothered me, and I have seen this also in accounts of international adoptions from the 1970s, were that it didn't occur to the Thrashes to learn ONE word of Cambodian, in order to make even the most basic communication possible. There was a scene in the film where Mr. Thrash is learning the names of some body parts in Cambodian, but they had been there for many weeks by then, with no way to communicate, and it was done more as a game than as a basis for actual communication. People used to feel that English was the only language, and that those coming here had to learn it or lump it. I sincerely hope that people adopting internationally now have a more humane and accepting approach. The other thing that bugged was the Thrashes' daughter, who was absolutely spoiled rotten. She spoiled the movie for me the first time I saw it too. Even though she knew the level of deprivation and loss the Yanns had suffered, even though she knew of the courage and strength it took for them to come to a new world and try to survive, all she did was whine and complain about not getting new sneakers or because her mama wasn't there to see her cheerleading tryouts one time, as she continued to live in her comfortable home with everything she wanted around her. Poor baby!!! I wanted her parents to have a "come to Jesus" meeting with her but they never did, just went on coddling and apologizing to her. Otherwise, great film, and after Googling, I have learned that all the Yann kids went on to successful lives! YAY!

history.title: Ocean's Twelve
history.text: I think this is just a really fun film, and better than the other two. I think all the actors just had so much fun doing it as well, which makes it even more enjoyable. You can tell that the actors just really like working together. I have a couple of questions though, even though I have seen the film several times, there are things I apparently miss, and thought maybe someone could help me out. First, in regard to Linus' mother being the head of whatever international security organization she was with, how could she know that Linus was part of Ocean's gang, and not only not do anything about it but get them all out of jail? How could she aid and abet her son? Was she lying about being the Section Chief? The other question is similar, in regard to Isabel. She forged the arrest warrant for all of them, and got caught, yet there were no legal repercussions for her. Since I haven't seen "Lost in Translation," what did Matsui do to Linus? How in the world did Yen breathe in that bag for two days, and didn't he ever have to relieve himself? I also missed the reason he had to be sent in the bag in the first place. I really have seen the film, but I miss this stuff. The look on Danny's face when he walks into the hotel room and Yen is literally bouncing off the walls in his freedom, food everywhere, and Danny can't say anything, is a great moment.

history.title: Downton Abbey: Season 4
history.text: I was very anxious to see this new season on dvd, and have just finished it. There is some that is pretty good, some that is really good, and sadly, some that is not so good, but even with frustration with some of the plot lines, the acting is for the most part, excellent. SPOILERS..........................SPOILERS.......................SPOILERS......................SPOILERS.............................. There seemed to be some reversion to character traits of earlier seasons, which was unfortunate, since we had seen some development. I don't think it was just being with Matthew that "changed" Mary," but I had hoped, some maturing through the war, etc. All that is gone, and Mary is completely cold and self absorbed again. Even though Anna was expected to, and did, help her carry Pamuk's dead body to his room so that Mary's secret might be kept, and even though Bates left his job, his security, his happiness, to return to psychowoman, so that Mary's secret might be kept, when Mary was faced with the choice to keep his or not, what did she tell Mrs. Hughes? "it's a man's life, it's WRONG." She had no proof that Bates was the killer but was that ready to sell him out. ONLY when Bates yet AGAIN saved her family and the monarchy from another embarrassing scandal did Mary change her mind. Mary is loyal only to her position. Period. It broke my heart, and Carson's, when she was cruel to him. I am glad he got in the last shot. Nor did she tell Anna or Bates what she had done with the ticket, so Bates has to live in worry. I thought there were some layers of human complexity in Thomas last season, but that too is all gone. He is back to being "one note" evil, causing trouble for everyone for no apparent reason. Additionally, the thing with the Nanny was clunky. He was trying to get her in trouble, but she cooked her own goose when Cora heard what she said to Sybbie, which had nothing to do with Thomas. In contrast, the guy who plays him, from what I have seen in the extra features, seems to be a nice guy. He is good at being bad! I wonder what if it had been Tom who heard Nanny, and what he would have done to her. Sadly, there were probably many many children of "privilege" who were at the mercy of nannies and governesses like Nanny West, and even still. I thought it was too bad that both Robert and Cora seemed to suffer from extreme amnesia this season, to the point of seeming demented. First, when Thomas and Braithwaite were pointing fingers at Anna, saying she was being mean, they believe them, even though they know Anna is the sweetest person ever, and is never mean to anyone! They even speak to Bates about her. Totally wrong. It was the same in the scene where Thomas is complaining to Robert about the other staff and Robert said, "are you not liked downstairs?" Never mind that there were incidents of theft and attempts to frame Bates in earlier seasons, and what kind of person Thomas is, which Robert well knows. Amnesia, I say. Robert and Cora should have laughed Thomas out of the room. Why is he still working there? I was glad Braithwaite got kicked out early on, and loved her smackdown by Mrs. Hughes. Additionally, when Violet was questioning Robert about his wanting total control of the estate, I too was thinking, yeah, because you have done so well with that up til now!" Now Edith. She seems to present as a sympathetic character for alot of people, but she isn't to me. While Mary is not a nice person, she never did anything to really hurt Edith in the first season, yet what Edith did to her by telling the Turkish guy what happened to Pamuk, would have ruined Mary's entire life, if she had not married Matthew. She would have never married and even worse, have been shut out of the society she lived for. I thought it perfect karmic justice that Edith was jilted at the altar, losing her chance to marry, and now experiencing what would cause equal scandal for her. I wanted her to remember what she did to Mary, but the show didn't go there. I have to say that Cora and Mary were pretty blind to not know Edith was pregnant, since they knew she had a boyfriend,had to have started to show, and suddenly off to Switzerland for months. Stevie Wonder would know. I thought Violet's reaction was great.." I see I will have to take the slow path" but not judgmental, nor was she of Sybil and Tom. For all her clinging to the old ways, she was pretty down to earth with her granddaughters and matters of love and sex. It was funny how Robert chastised Dr Clarkson for saying the word "urine" in front of her! Tis a mystery what happened to Gregson. If the Nazis killed him, they would have found a body? They didn't have camps yet in 1922 I don't think. has he faked his death? Why would he give Edith his power of attorney? I didn't like Rose at all. She was a spoiled little rich girl who didn't give a thought to anyone else, but wanted what she wanted. No replacement at all for Sybil, who was a real person, with brains and a heart. I SO miss Sybil. Matthew was a nice guy but I loved Sybil. I wish that Cora's mother had been there when Sybil was dying. She would have thrown Sir I Know it All out the window, got Sybil to the hospital, and saved her. I absolutely think Dr Clarkson was right and would have saved her, had they listened to him. I agree with Cora, and didn't want her to reconcile with Robert, even though Violet pushed her to. It was completely Robert's and Sir Know it All's fault. I thought the Daisy/Ivy/Alfred/Jimmy adolescent posturings went on interminably, but Daisy and Mrs Patmore's relationship matured, which was nice to see. I got really tired of seeing Molesley whining and feeling sorry for himself. I liked how he stood up for Baxter though, helping her to feel better about herself, and hopefully telling Thomas to go jump in the lake. I see a relationship developing there, no matter what she's done. The pig stuff was dumb. When DID Mary learn to make eggs? Cora's mother and brother stuff was dumb and unnecessary. Also the cloak and dagger spy stuff in trying to get the letter back. If it was that important, maybe girlfriend shouldn't have had it in her bag and then left her bag unattended! What was REALLY good... Anna's storyline, and her acting. She brought it!!! I hope they have British Emmys, she should definitely win. I really wanted her to go to the police after she knew Bates knew though. I thought that she was selling him a bit short for being so sure that he would kill Green, and ruin their lives together. I LOVE Mrs Hughes, she is such a badass! I thought she was going to kill Green with her bare hands, and I bet she could have. Such great scenes with Anna, with Green, with Braithwaite, with Carson. ALL of them. It's such a shock to see her on the show and then how she looks in real life, a decade younger, like Mrs. Patmore. I also love Carson. He is absolutely old school, and is judgmental and rigid and everything else, but it is his job to make sure everything goes right. It was all on his shoulders. He does have a caring heart though. He adores Mary, though I am with Mrs Hughes on that, and I loved the scene with he and Sybbie. One of my favorite scenes was when he had just found out Mrs Hughes was okay, and he was singing and laughing while he polished the platter, so unlike him, but so sweet. The final scene of this season is right up there too, with Carson in BARE feet, wading, and holding Mrs. Hughes' hand for security! Others think they should be married, I don't know, but even if not, their friendship is wonderful to see. I don't think Bates is the killer. It would take alot of things to fall into place to take the train to another town, rent a car, find where the guy lives, follow him to where you would be able to hit him, with no one seeing it, or you, then returning the car and getting back on the train. It is possible he had someone else do it, but they would have the same problems. He was hit by a car right? I think it was an accident. I wanted someone to kill him, but slowly. I can only imagine how many victims he had. As vulnerable as women have always been to sexual assault, I feel sure that women and girls in service positions were especially easy to victimize. Tom matured this season, I thought. I didn't like him when he was with Sybil. He was controlling, willing to let her sacrifice everything in her life for him but gave up nothing for her,not wanting her to "disappoint him" I hated that, or to have ideas about their child that disagreed with his, and not even treating her family with the slightest respect, when they were sheltering him and even keeping his ass out of prison. I understood and agree with where he was coming from but he could have given Sybil that much.He was a jerk but did start to grow up after Sybil's death. I think maturity involves the ability to not only see your corner, but the other guy's as well, including the English, and he was getting there. It was such irony to see him dancing at the ball with monarchy. I wonder if the "troubles" are going to rear their head again next season, since one of the guys after Mary has a castle and holdings in Ulster, which I believe is in Northern Ireland. How would Tom deal with Mary becoming an occupier? I LOVE LOVE LOVE Dame Maggie Smith. I love her snarkiness and her wisdom. Her scenes with Isobel were gold. It was well done how Isobel could have gladly strangled her, yet when Violet was ill, wouldn't leave her side. Even sick, Violet had good lines! The scene where they are playing cards and having fun together is great. I had a sad moment though, in seeing her ill scenes, to realize she is nearly eighty years old. She is a treasure, and always will be. This show is a treasure as well, even with all its faults. It has stellar performances and often excellent writing. I don't compare it in any way with Upstairs Downstairs. This is its own entity, and it is awesome to see how many people around the world love this show.

history.title: The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel
history.text: This is such a good film. Others have spoken much on the issues presented of getting older, feeling obsolete, a bit frightened, as well as the feelings toward spouses, deceased and living, that went unspoken. It was awesome to see the courage of this group, who for the most part, as Evelyn said, not only survived, but thrived. I love love LOVE Maggie Smith and Judi Dench, and they were excellent here, though they seem to have a bit of pattern by now to many of their roles, Smith as sharp tongued and witty, Dench as motherly and warm. As a total Downton Abbey fan, Maggie Smith was not far here from Dowager Countess Crawley, but my goodness, Penelope Wilton, as a shrewish, bitter woman here, was worlds away from the strong and compassionate Isobel Crawley. At least with distant familial intermarrying, you don't have to change the monograms! I think it's a little unfortunate that the only character that refused to embrace her new surroundings was Wilton's character. We can plainly see that her prison is of her own making, yet I am sure it is true that a place like Jaipur might be too difficult, in many ways, for many people, and that wouldn't make them bad. To see Maggie Smith's character sitting on her hospital bed, exhausted, in pain, when she says, "I want to go home," hurt my heart. I loved her emotional and physical recovery. Another scene that broke my heart is when she is pouring out her heart to the woman who isn't understanding a word she is saying, and to see the emotional connection on the face of the woman "who no one else will even acknowledge." I had to put aside my American sensibilities with the scenes with Sunaina and her brother, when he was telling her what to do and listening on her phone. I know it's a male dominant culture but I still wish she had stood up to him and told him to bug off. It surprised me though that Sonny's mother was as controlling of him as she was. It would have seemed more accurate with a daughter. The tiny little things that bugged a little bit were when Evelyn saw Graham in the swing and just walked away. There was no blood or wounds, and you can't tell by looking a someone from feet away, whether they are living. He could have been asleep, he could have been unconscious and in need of medical help. Not the medical help from Sonny, who had problems telling living from dead. Sonny was awesome. The other thing that I wasn't sure felt very accurate was Graham's telling practically everyone that he was gay, even as a reply to "where are you going?" which seemed very odd, and not one person had a moment's problem with it, even though he had only known these people a couple of weeks. It was great to see that acceptance but not something anyone can count on, especially I would think, amongst older people. I also wondered, since Graham apparently planned to die in India, why it didn't bother him to make friends with these people, knowing he might drop dead in front of them, and not care at all about they might feel about that? Also Manoj's, whose life he just dropped back into out of the blue, unannounced and uninvited, and then drops dead. I suppose one could also argue that the pursuit of Evelyn by the other guy, I forget his name, was rather rushed, seeing as his wife wasn't even at the airport yet, but on the other hand, sometimes there isn't all the time in the world. But these are little picks. This is truly an excellent movie and has much to say about the human condition, caring about others and living life, no matter the age, or what your mother wants.

history.title: Captain Phillips
history.text: This was a gripping, chilling film, and Tom Hanks does a great job. The actors playing the Somalians kept the intensity on high throughout as well. I didn't remember hearing about this event so I did not know what was going to happen in the film. I agree with the posts asking commenters not to reveal full plots without using spoiler tags. I often will skim a few reviews prior to seeing a film to see if most people liked it,though with a Tom Hanks film, that's a safe bet, and therefore the comment that people shouldn't come here until after, is just rude and thoughtless. As angry as the hijacking all the way through made me, the most frightening scene in the film was the one in which the ship's crew of 19 have to hide for their lives, and Hanks as the captain, standing alone, watching in fear as four, only FOUR soulless cretins come tooling up in a boat the size of a bathtub, and take over the ship the comparable size of a mountain, terrorizing everyone on board. How can this happen and be allowed to happen? I don't know anything about maritime law but it's inconceivable to me that ships are sent into areas with high pirating activity, with no way to or right to protect themselves. The actual captain said piracy is a fact of life on the high seas and that may be, but having to face murderous thugs, unarmed and defenseless should not be. In my opinion, hostile forces should be permanently neutralized if they get within a mile of a ship. There was not the least bit of equity of force or power and there is no way these pirates should have been able to take over or even get close to the ship. The movie's synopsis states that both Phillips and the Somali captain undertake an emotional journey throughout the hijacking and kidnapping, but I didn't see this to be true. Muse was as much a terrorist at the end as he was in the beginning. I did see Phillips try to get the kid to give himself up and save his own life, which indicates a journey of sorts, and the kind of person Phillips was and is. I also didn't feel one bit sorry for Muse or any of the Somali adults. I know they have an impoverished country but a little money would have gone a long way to better their lives, and Muse refuses to take the money, then bragging about receiving millions for previous hijackings. Phillips asks him what he is doing there then, and to me the answer was that Muse and the others had no humanity, but lived only to hurt and kill others. I don't usually cry when watching films, but I was having a hard time when Phillips was in the medical bay, all right. Another powerful film for Hanks.

history.title: Watsons Go to Birmingham
history.text: I am surprised that some reviewers think the book is so much better than the film, since the book had, in my opinion, huge gaps in the story. For example, in the book, Byron, who is making a habit of getting into trouble and has zero respect for his parents, completely reforms on the very doorstep of his grandmother, with never a single word said again about him. Seriously, he says "yes Ma'am" and that is it. There is nothing at all about his or the family's experiences in Birmingham throughout the summer, or why he returned home with the family, when they had planned to have him spend the school year in Birmingham, or how or if his behavior changed. The book goes from the family's arrival in June, to the church bombing, to everyone, including Byron, back home in Michigan, in just that way. The film indicates that the bombing was in September, not during the summer, which in the book is confusing, and that tragic event should have been made clear, and the film indicates why the family was still there in September, which is also confusing in the book, since the younger two should have been back in Michigan for school. The book also contained far too much about the "wool pooh," which to me made no sense to begin with. I thought the film made cohesive sense. You see how Byron starts to mature and think about something more important than himself. I liked the part where his cousins are talking about fighting for equality at the costs of being jailed and injured, and you see the light bulb start to go on in Byron's head. You see how prejudice and segregation affected the family, which is not at all present in the book. You see Byron's and Kenny's growth when they are back home. The film is also gripping as it shows actual footage of the turmoil. The things I didn't like about the film are, for one, the casting of Byron. Byron was 14 or 15 in the book. There was no way that Byron of the film was 15. He looked 20, and his friend older than that, and both looked menacing, especially when they were roughing Kenny up. They looked like adults beating a child up. It made no sense to me in book and film that Byron's parents would choose to take a troubled boy who wouldn't listen to anyone, already committing small crimes, and heading for bigger trouble, to the rabidly prejudiced South, where the slightest misstep could get him seriously hurt or killed. Emmett Till was only 14 when he was brutalized and murdered for allegedly just whistling at a white woman. The other thing was Mrs. Watson's trying to keep her kids in a protective bubble while putting them in a middle of a war, where not knowing what to do could get them hurt. That seemed kind of insane to me. By the same token, Byron saw the conflicts on tv, and should have known about the segregation. I absolutely feel that the film is excellent, and much better than the book. Though, however, the four little girls were mentioned in the dedication, but I wish there had been an accompanying feature on them and on the church bombing.

history.title: Call the Midwife: Season Five [DVD]
history.text: I have just come to the series, and while I wasn't sure originally how much I liked it, I have now finished season 5 and I love it. LOVE it. It is so interesting and beautiful and aggravating to see how people lived in times that are so different from the one we live in now, and the births of more than babies, but also of viewpoints and practices that turned out to have such profound impact on people's lives. Whether to feed with breast or bottle, whether what is new is automatically best, the ongoing issue of desperately poor people having one child after another that they can't feed or adequately shelter, illiteracy, hatred of people who are different, regardless of in what way, are still issues we grapple with today. It is also so interesting to see how things were then that are so different today, the ignorant but well meaning prescribing of or irresponsible taking of medication in pregnancy, the lack of technology, doctors making house calls, the constant smoking!!!!!!! I am not one to demonize smokers who do it responsibly, and i know back in the day they were just starting to know it wasn't healthy, and people did smoke everywhere, but to see people smoking in the hospital rooms, around sick babies, in the bedrooms, during birth scenes, everywhere, just is really revolting. You would think that people with medical experience would know that it wouldn't be helpful to anyone but they all puffed like chimneys. I give the series four stars instead of five because of the writers' tendencies to make some of the characters too saintly and perfect. Perfect people are boring. Shelagh is the perfect wife, mother, and office manager, and Dr Turner and Peter Noakes are the perfect husbands, even though wives and mothers working for fulfillment instead of economic need was not widely done at that time. Sister Mary Cynthia is so saintly, she has no personality at all. There was a bit this season in which she showed some emotion, for about three minutes. I do not care for the characters of Jenny and Trixie, since it seems very unlikely to me that two young, very attractive girls would choose to live in a convent with a bunch of nuns. The character of Sr Monica Joan is basically one note. Since the first season, all she has done is go for the sweets, quote poetry and moan about her physical infirmities. The additions of Nurse Crane, who is a loveable curmudgeon, and Patsy, who hides much pain, are much more believable. Sr Julienne often comes across as the all knowing, all wise, all gentle mother of the house, but we see her struggle privately, and Jenny Agutter portrays her with excellence. The other characters and performances that absolutely shine are Sr Evangelina, who says it like it is, often too harshly, but never intending malice, and knows what she is about. SPOILER............................. HER DEATH at the end of season 5 was heartbreaking. She was the best character, hilarious and genuine. Pam Ferris is stellar in this role. If there had to be a loss among the sisters, it should have been Sr Monica Joan. I also love Chummy. She also is humorous, incredibly poignant, and her coming to terms with her mother, and her feelings about how she was treated by her mother are such good scenes. Patsy and Delia's trying to live and love authentically when no one in the world wanted to allow them to do so also hurts my heart, and I love their scenes together. I am watching the dvds of the seasons, so is there deleted material of their scenes? I don't know.

history.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul
history.text: THIS blu-ray come with the UV code for this film as well as the original 2010 movie. Good continuation of a really funny kids franchise. This movie was different from the first three in that it didn't take place at The Wimp's home town. It was a road trip movie. So that makes it stand apart as far as plotline. I think the story was very funny. Lot's of good comedy. A decently endearing story of a typical pre-teen boy trying to meet a youtuber. So that makes it a little more modern than the original trilogy. There was definitely some humor hidden in there for the adults watching it, including a hilarious reference to the classic film Psycho. As far as the cast. I think the New Wimp (Jason Drucker) did a very good job in the lead role. His timing and facial expressions, as well as physical acting was right on. The parents where parents, probably nothing special there. If they could have gotten the original parents back that would have been nice. Rowley was only in one or two scenes, so not much to mention there. The actor who plays the New Rodrick (Charlie Wright) did a good job being the low-IQ clueless older brother. His casting did cause controversy with fans, because he doesn't look that much like Drucker. However, if memory serves (the original Rodrick) Devon Bostick (who is now 25 and aged out of the role) did not look much like Zachary Gordon (the original Greg). Speaking of Zachary Gordon. Fans were also (strangely) upset that he did not reprise his role as the WIMPY KID regardless of the facts that he is now 19 years old, has a very husky deep adult voice, is in college, and clearly hits the gym on a regular basis and does a lot of weight lifting. Overall this movie was very funny and very fun, and has a lot of redeeming qualities. The story is fun. The acting is solid. The direction is as well. 9/10
