The Palladinos did it again! I don't give five stars, I just don't, except for classics like Citizen Kane and the like. But this is a five-star show. The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel is indeed marvelous. Rachel Brosnahan lights up the screen like a Klieg light. I can't wait to see the next season.

I see a couple of people have compared this to The Office. I hated The Office, too. I am not interested in watching a bunch of spoiled millennials move back home and mooch off their parents. I made it ten minutes into the first episode and that was it. If any of the losers were my kid, the welcome mat would say "GO Home," not "Welcome Home."

history.review_title: Low budget but very good movie
history.text: I have always loved Katie Holmes (except during her Tom Cruise years; we'll not speak of that) and she does a great job, along with Patricia Clarkson and Oliver Platt, in this low-budget but overall very good movie about a prodigal daughter who wants to make peace with her family, and particularly her mother, since her mother has cancer and this could very well be her last Thanksgiving. There are enough comic moments to keep the movie from getting too maudlin and enough poignant moments to bring a tear to the viewer's eyes. It's not something I would watch as a feel-good Thanksgiving movie. In fact, April would actually be a good time to watch it. Just about as far from Thanksgiving as you can get.
Sutton Foster. Need I say more? Watch this!

history.review_title: Two people can keep a secret...if one of them is dead
history.text: If ever there was a case to illustrate the immaturity of a teenager's mind, this is it. It's not the fact that the sisters decided to kill their mother, although I'm sure they could have found a better solution to their problems. Their mother was an alcoholic who'd had multiple boyfriends who abused and tried to molest the girls (it isn't clear whether any of them actually did). She was a horrible mother and social services wasn't any help. They did at least try to get help before deciding to kill her. Their mistake was telling all their friends about it. I mean, there was practically a "Murder Your Mother" club at the school! Of course, all but their closest friends thought it was either a joke or it was just big talk they would never act on. But what did the girls think would happen after they did it? Not only were there people at school who knew about the plan beforehand, the one sister, Sandra, who actually did the murder, went around boasting that she did it after the fact. That's where the immaturity comes in. Surely at some point they had to realize that someone was going to be responsible enough to tell the police. Sandra was also stupid enough to "forget" to get rid of a laptop where they made all their plans. Both the sisters are out of prison now. I wonder if they see each other. I wonder what they think of each other now. If this movie represents even a small amount of the truth, I can't imagine either of them would want to have anything to do with the other any more. *shrug* But then, I could be wrong

Well, that's 81 minutes of my life that I'll never get back. There are a number of theories you could apply to the story. WARNING: POTENTIAL SPOILERS. First, the original tenant's ghost is haunting the apartment and takes over any woman who moves in and causes her to re-enact the original tragedy. Second, the apartment itself is haunted somehow (I won't pretend to explain how, I didn't write this garbage) and so the apartment makes the tenants act the way they do. Third, this is an incredibly stupid movie made by incompetent people and there is no explanation for what happens. Whatever the explanation is, postpartum depression it ain't, so whoever suggested that - forget it. I won't get into a long explanation as to why, just trust me, it that's what the filmmakers are intending to portray, they are more psychotic than I thought.

Any movie in which Tori Spelling gets bumped off gets my vote. Yes, I know that is terribly cynical but I can't stand her. The movie was typical made-for-TV, Lifetime movie quality. Kellie Martin's acting was wooden and unconvincing. Tori Spelling was, as she is in every movie or TV shows she's in, Tori Spelling, rich girl popular simply because she is rich, not because she has any charisma or because she's a decent human being. If you like this type of movie, you will probably like this one. It's watchable. That's the best I can say about it.

I read the book this movie was based on so perhaps I have a different perspective than those who haven't read it. Also, I am old enough that I grew up without the internet. I think that makes a HUGE difference in the way people view this movie. Millennials and Gen Xers who barely remember a time when there wasn't internet and social media really don't have a true concept of privacy. Their photos, stories of their every day lives, are splashed all over the internet. They don't know how to live without it. And maybe that's the way it's going to be from now on. I'm glad I lived in a time where what went on behind closed doors stayed behind closed doors. Because you know what? Despite all the "transparency" of social media as it exists today, crime hasn't decreased, parents still beat their children, terrorists still kill people. I think the whole point of the movie was when Mae challenged Bailey and Eamon to go totally transparent. As Bailey said, "We're effed." (Sorry, Amazon won't let me put the actual word, even with asterisks.) They weren't any better than the politicians they criticized. And Mae's naivete and idealism simply don't work in the real world. So all of you out there who gave this movie just one or two stars - READ THE BOOK!

history.review_title: Watch paint dry. It's a better use of your time.
history.text: What do you say about a film without a single truly likeable character that goes nowhere, just goes on and on without much story to it except for the cheating - like father, like daughter. There is no reason for this film to exist. It is a total and complete waste of time and I am SO glad I didn't pay money for it, although maybe I should ask for a refund of $2.99 on my Prime membership because I feel Amazon owes that much to me for sitting here and watching the entire stinking film waiting for something to happen but NOTHING HAPPENS. NOTHING.

I first saw this when it came out in theaters in 1980. It still holds up. Timothy Hutton's performance in particular is amazing, considering how young he was. I think my dislike of the character Mary Tyler Moore plays colors my attitude toward her performance. She certainly shows a range that she never did as perky Mary Richards on the MTM Show. Donald Sutherland, as always, lost himself in the part. It was nice seeing Elizabeth McGovern and Dinah Manoff in roles fairly early in their careers. I just finished reading the novel this was based on and I have to say this is an excellent adaptation.

history.title: One Magic Christmas
history.review_title: “Write and tell me if you are really real.”
history.text: Incredibly disheartening, this secularized vision of Christmas as hell on earth, presents Ginny Grainger (Mary Steenburgen), a crabby disillusioned mother of two who of course HATES Christmas. At every opportunity she tries to ruin the event for her Christmas believing daughter Abbie. Pushing the boundaries of good parenting to the point where she is prepared to tell her daughter that there is no Santa!!! Ginny is cheerless and tyrannical and rides roughshod over everyone including her poor husband who has a dream of owning his own bike shop. Enter an extremely creepy “angel” (Harry Dean Stanton as Gideon) who stalks little Abbie while the family is about to lose their home. He tells the little girl that angels are dead people. He was, in fact, a cowboy. “I got myself drowned.” Death and destruction tramples its way through this depressing story that the late Roger Ebert called “a tactical miscalculation from beginning to end.” Why are so many Christmas movies completely devoid of joy!?

history.title: Snow Bride
history.text: This Christmas romance is about a gossipmonger (Katrina Law as Greta Kaine), who makes her living off of disparaging stories she writes about the rich and famous. She has no scruples, she doesn’t care if the stories are real or not. “These people don’t deserve our sympathy.” Her editor wants the dirt on a famous political family and encourages a competition between her and another sleaze merchant. Whoever gets the best dirt first gets to be the editor of the tabloid’s online magazine. Happily, Greta not only gets her foot in the door, she’s housed with the family in question, just waiting for an exposé to fall into her lap, no work required. Unfortunately, she is not the only ‘sneak’ in the house. An ex-girlfriend has shown up, switching from one brother to the other, intent on becoming a member of this family, or else! As presented, every character in this movie lies out of convenience. To soften what might be problematic, they’ve tried to present this as a screwball comedy. In which case, it works great if you don’t consider the fact that no one in this movie is virtuous.

history.title: A December Bride
history.review_title: “You have a good eye, it’s just not enough.”
history.text: Interior designer wannabe Layla (Jessica Lowndes) loses her fiancé when he’s introduced to her cousin, who promptly marries him. Said cousin whines to her mother that Layla won’t forgive her, so Auntie manipulates poor Layla at every turn, including coercing her into attending the marriage of her ex to her cousin! Apparently, Auntie believes backstabbing family members is permissible as long as they get something out of the deal. Who came up with this plot!? Fortunately, Layla gets fired from her crappy job and has a chance at a better boyfriend (Daniel Lissing as Seth Murphy) and a better job. If she will only stop pouting and look to the future instead.

history.title: Santa's Apprentice/Magic Snowflake Double Feature
history.review_title: “Christmas crackers, it’s worse than I thought!”
history.text: Two movies, two disks. The first movie introduces the dilemma. Santa has reached the age where he must start training an apprentice. The problem is, Santa doesn’t want to give up the job, doesn’t want to retire. All the ex-Santas convene, insisting that Santa pick a replacement. The requirements are: the boy must be named Nicholas, he must be an orphan, and he must be pure of heart. And in this case, he’s at the other end of the world, bullied by a monstrous oaf named Grincroch. The training doesn’t go well because young Nicholas is plagued with self-doubts and Santa isn’t that enthusiastic about the boy taking over. The sequel has Santa and his wife Beatrice leaving Nicholas on his own with just a bunch of elves, his pet, and a little girl from the orphanage, also conveniently named Beatrice. Without any adult supervision, Nicholas decides he needs to grow up fast and become responsible. Unfortunately, part of being Santa means remaining young at heart. With this new disaster, the magic snowflake in the basement starts to melt. In a state of panic, the Council of Retired Santas show up to rectify the matter, without knowing how. Bricks are involved! Both films are fun. I thoroughly enjoyed them. I hate to use this word, but they are cute. It was a happy find.

history.title: Christmas Melody
history.text: Mariah Carey’s footprints are all over this clunky Hallmark movie. She directed this less than sterling effort, snagged a bit part for herself, then insisted on rewriting the song that poor Fina Strazza had to sing. If she had been a real director she would have had enough sense to recast the role of Melissa. The woman misplaying that role was almost lifelike. The plot was rudimentary at best, a widow (Lacey Chabert as Kristin) takes her daughter home to Ohio after her business fails in L.A. She meets more than her fair share of ghosts from Christmases past. Apparently, most of her former classmates never made it out of that small town. The place is mishandled by Melissa, a woman who will brook no dissent from anyone, at any time, over any matter, without consulting her first, in which case the answer is always no. Melissa is played by a waxwork doll; her features never move. I believe she was animatronic. I almost liked this movie because of Lacey Chabert. Otherwise, it was remarkably bad. I blame that on the director.

history.title: Debbie Macomber's Mr. Miracle
history.review_title: “I like to play gin rummy and read.”
history.text: An amateur angel gets his first assignment on Earth, to help an indecisive student find her way in life. Unfortunately, this particular angel (misplayed by Rob Morrow) is a bit unorthodox, as in slightly demented. He is erratic and profoundly unstable. He blunders through his assignment with all the verve of a two-year-old. To say Morrow overacts limits the bizarre expressions he exhibits throughout this film. What’s worse, he’s supposed to be a teacher! Yet he acts like a halfwit. Morrow’s performance is shocking when juxtaposed with the normal characters that populate this simple tale of insecurity and self-doubt. And a lame romance was tossed in as well...as an afterthought. This is a complete misfire.

history.title: Lifetime Holiday Triple Feature [DVD]
history.text: Three so-called Christmas movies crammed together on one DVD. The first movie deals with a music hating mother who tries to stifle her daughter’s dream of becoming a singer. A contest is involved but actually has very little to do with this family melodrama. Dolly Parton almost sings Jingle Bells. The ending negates the reason for the plot in the first place. The second film also involves a faux contest. Twelve trees are decorated for Christmas. In this case no winner is announced, and no actual judging takes place. The contest is simply a ploy to save a building that a spoiled brat wants to tear down. The third film is about a party girl who travels back in time to visit her teen-self, so she can dispense useless advice to herself that she won’t follow. Again, another pointless exercise in futility. None of these movies are very Christmassy. A disappointing collection. Lifetime is no Hallmark.

history.title: Dragons: Gift of the Night Fury [DVD]
history.text: This brief “winter tale” concerns Berk and its population of dragons who inexplicably leave en masse. This migration excludes Toothless, incapable of flying without his rider, and Meatlug, held prisoner in secret. It is quickly revealed where the dragons went and why. Naturally, they return, if they didn’t it wouldn’t be much of a franchise. At best, this harmless tale is cute, but hardly Christmassy.

history.title: Piranha
history.text: Not quite a remake, this version of the classic film Piranha only has one thing in common with the original―the title. Otherwise, this is just another wild raunchy romp that relies too much on sleaze and base humor to get by. The plot is simplistic: spring break happens at the same time as a seismic event occurs, releasing a ton of prehistoric piranha into the lake they’re frolicking in. This movie made enough money to support a sequel that did not fair as well. If you’re expecting more than killer fish, plenty of gore, and bare breasts, you will be greatly disappointed. This is not the Citizen Kane of piranha films.

history.title: Piranha [Roger Corman's Cult Classics]
history.text: Signs, what good are they if no one pays attention to them. In this case, two hikers ignore the obvious NO TRESPASSING warning on a fence and go for a dip in something that clearly isn’t a swimming pool. They don't live to regret their mistake. And a classic was born. Enter skip-tracer extraordinaire Maggie (Heather Menzies), obligated to find the hikers, or what’s left of them. Instead, she unknowingly unleashes the voracious piranha, allowing them to snack their way to a summer camp filled with kids. Farther downstream is a resort, a smorgasbord of unwilling foodstuffs. The military gets involved, but not to help, to hinder. Perhaps the pesky piranha won’t make it that far. A sly rip-off of Jaws, it may take more of the little buggers to get you but get you they will. What’s one shark compared to these toothy devils? “People eat fish. Fish don’t eat people!”

history.title: The 1939 New York World's Fair -A Collection of Amazing Films
history.review_title: Inferior to Jason Robards' "World of Tomorrow"
history.text: This film about the 1939 New York World's Fair is not up to the standard of "The World of Tomorrow," a film narrated by Jason Robards and his trip to the NY World's Fair with his family when he was eleven or twelve years old. His narration gives us a feeling for those times: "We glimpsed the world of tomorrow poised on a needle point between the Depression and the War." This film consists of official films issued by the World's Fair organizers, many dignitaries such as FDR, Fiorello Laguardia, Albert Einstein, the King and Queen of England, Universal sound newsreels, color home movies taken by Robards' father, an official sound and color film issued by General Motors of its Futurama exhibit, the Westinghouse film about the Middletons visiting the fair and a film shown at the fair called "The City" showing the misery of the conditions during the Depression and how we could pull ourselves out of it. Actually we didn't have to. The Second World War accomplished that for us. The film being reviewed here shows little of all this. Sadly, "The World of Tomorrow" is no longer available. Apparently I got my copy just in time.

history.title: The Producers (Widescreen Edition)
history.text: A completely inept remake of the original 1968 film. This film and the Broadway musical on which it was based had none of the edge of the original film. Those who found this funny either didn't see or failed to "get" the original satire. The Hitler tryout scene and the "Springtime for Hitler" production number just lay there. One joke of Nathan Lane saying his whole life flashed before his eyes, "and it was the wrong life! It was some other life!" was stolen from a standup routine of Woody Allen's.

history.title: America's 58 National Parks 3 pk.
history.review_title: BEWARE: Packaging MIsleading as Being in HD when it is Standard DVD
history.text: This product's packaging title (ALL 58 PARKS IN HD) is, in my opinion, misleading to purchasers as being a high definition product. The three discs are standard DVD's which means they are not of the high definition television system known as Blu-ray. The manufacturer defends this as being material that was shot in HD (high definition) though not released on high definition (Blu-ray) discs but rather on standard DVD discs. My understanding is that the DVD disc conforms to the original NTSC television system and is, therefore, not of the High Definition disc system known as Blu-ray. Customers should be aware of this before purchasing.

history.title: Mississippi Burning [Blu-ray]
history.text: Excellent film of a true case of three freedom fighters, two white and one black disappearing in a small Mississippi town. The FBI is ordered to investigate. The two lead characters portrayed by Willem Dafoe and Gene Hackman as leading the investigation are fictional. The film does hit all the right notes. Brad Dourif as the deputy and his wife played by a very young Frances McDormand are outstanding. Hackman finally convinces his superior Defoe to resort to the tactics of the opposition. The film looks spectacular in blu-ray.

Tragically, only two of the original actors are still alive at this writing. Blue-ray disc shows a fair amount of grain in some shots.

history.title: Spotlight [DVD]
history.review_title: Excellent - - Well Deserving of Academy Award
history.text: Given its genre, I consider “Spotlight” to be as close to being a perfect movie as any recently made that I’ve seen. The film has no action scenes and is entirely dialog driven. With a running time of 2 hours and nine minutes, one might think that such a picture would be considered unlikely for public acceptance. In fact, after three viewings, I find that this engrossing film seems to flash by, totally lacking in any slow moments thanks to exceptionally adept writing, acting and editing. The film is based on a true story based of the efforts of an investigative team of the Boston Globe newspaper in exposing a Catholic priest suspected of sexually abusing children. The incident is initially believed to be uncommon in nature but additional information from various sources leads the team to suspect that this sort of offense had been happening more frequently and over a much greater period of time than initially believed. As one of the attorneys involved in the case advises a member of the investigating team: “The Church thinks in centuries, Mr. Rezendes. Do you think your paper has the resources to take that on?” It is suspected that common practice has been to prevent these incidents from becoming public knowledge and to reassign the offending priests from one parish to another in the attempt to avoid outside disclosure. This story from the Boston Globe was instrumental in the world-wide exposure of such offenses. This excellent though disturbing film won the Academy Award for Best Picture and Best Original Screenplay making it the first Best Picture winner to receive less than three Academy Awards since “The Greatest Show on Earth” of 1953. “Spotlight” won many other awards and accolades for 2015.

Some years ago, in 2003, Warner Bros. began to release a series of multiple DVD sets called "Looney Tunes Golden Collection" each set containing around 60 cartoons in what appeared to be beautifully restored and in unaltered, complete condition. As I remember each set (there were six of them) came out each year in October. They were't cheap but the quality was excellent. Each set contained four discs. The sets had many extras about the history of Looney Tunes and the talented people involved in producing them. The best period of Looney Tunes, in my opinion, were those released to theaters between 1940 and 1953. The earlier ones weren't very good (funny) with many of those were produced in color and those after 1953 were, with a few exceptions, looking increasing crude. The video and sound quality are all to notch in these collections which I treasure. I guess the old adage applies here: "You get what you pay for".

history.title: You Can't Take It with You
history.text: Best picture award of 1938 -- hard to believe. Two hours and six minutes of talky, noisy Capra corn and not very funny by any standards. Also hard to believe its being a play by George S. Kaufman, considering his penchant for wit. Lionel Barrymore -- so much better in David Copperfield and Grand Hotel. Likewise James Stewart -- better in "The Spirit of St. Louis" or any Hitchcock film in which he appeared.

history.title: Hollywood Revue Of 1929
history.review_title: Nice But Not of the Original Aspect Ratio
history.text: This film is of historical interest being among the earliest of optical synchronized sound films. The presentation of this DVD is, however, not that of the original aspect ratio of 1.20:1 of early optical sound films and of which this is an example, but is of the TV standard of 1.33:1 making the cropping of the top and bottom of the image rather obvious. Silent 35mm films were made with Edison’s original ratio of 1.33:1 (4 units wide by 3 units high), the same ratio that would later be decided upon for American NTSC television in 1941. The first optical sound films of the 1920s were those of Fox Movietone News and, as it was necessary to provide space for the new optical soundtrack, the width of the image had to be reduced thus changing the image aspect ratio from 1.33:1 to 1.20:1 thus allowing the continued use of 35 mm film. Examples of other early optical sound films having this aspect ratio were the first Marx Brothers movie “The Cocoanuts” (1929) and Fritz Lang’s “M” (1931) the latter of which the Criterion DVD provides in the original aspect ratio. I suspect that if “Hollywood Revue” had been presented in this format there would have been numerous customer complaints about the big black spaces on either side of the picture. Warner Bros. “The Jazz Singer” (1927) had the original 1.33:1 ratio since the sound was not printed on the film but was provided by phonograph disc recordings synchronized with the projector which was known as “Vitaphone” and which didn’t last very long. The 1.20:1 aspect ratio remained the standard for optical sound movies for about 3 years. Audiences didn't like this aspect ratio which looked nearly like a square and theater owners didn’t like it as they had installed large wide screens for silent movies. In 1932 the Academy of Motion Picture Standards made the decision to change the aspect ratio to 1.37:1 by cropping the top and bottom of the frame and providing a new aperture plate to be inserted into all movie projectors which was known as the “Academy Aperture”. Film cameras likewise compensated for this change for all subsequent films. This maintained the original spacing between frames in order to avoid obsoleting all existing cameras and projectors. This aspect ratio remained the standard until 1953 when wider images became the thing thus resulting in the current standards for movies of 1.85:1 to 1.66:1. In the late 90s American HD television adopted a 1.78:1 aspect ratio which it remains to this day. Except for this, the DVD of “Hollywood Revue of 1929” is much appreciated and, considering its age, is of surprisingly good quality. Amazingly, Jack Benny looks the same in 1929 as he did in his television shows the 1950s. No wonder his ongoing jokes about being 39. Since it was then necessary for the singing and dance numbers to be done live before the cameras and microphones, the difficulties in producing this film must have been enormous. Prerecording the singing and lip syncing to it on the set and sound mixing were in the near future and would soon become the standard method of producing nearly all musical films.

history.title: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
history.text: No question this outing in the franchise is worthy of all the praise heaped upon it in these posts, and I agree with most so I will only comment here on something technical that was very annoying. I took this BR disc to more than one player and display thinking that the problem might be my system, but no, it followed the disc. I found that the convergence of the subtitles was way off; my eyes/brain couldn't converge them properly and it was so bad that I wound up having to close one eye when the subtitles appeared so I could read them. I had no problem with the 3D with the movie itself, just the subtitles. In fact, the 3D depth was so realistic that at one scene I remember saying outloud to the others in the room, "Damn, THIS is why I love 3D!" Subtitles are a separate file on BluRay so it could just be that they were not authored correctly, I don't know, but it does get minus marks in the technical department for this glitch. I have no idea if this was just a bad disc that I got or if anyone else has experienced the anomoly. Let me know if you have. That said, it was a small negative that barely impacted the great affection I have for everything about this film -- (oops, not "film;" digital).

history.title: The Martian [Blu-ray 3D + Blu-ray + Digital HD] [3D Blu-ray]
history.text: Matt Damon meets MacGyver -- or how to survive by hook or crook. Much less science fiction than it is a page out of Science Mechanic. The fact is, this could have taken place in the middle of the Mojave desert or the Sahara and it would have been just as entertaining, only difference there being that in either of those places, a helicopter and a rescue team would have come by in the first 20 minutes and plucked our hero out in a simple rescue -- end of the movie. On Mars, it's a bit more complicated, and everything wouldn't have had that omnipresent red tinge over-cast to it. Sure, we are routing for our hero because he's got a great sense of humor and that unstoppable American pluck, but in the end, his survival pretty much depends on luck, which he seems to have a carload full -- some of which REALLY stretches credulity. The 3D has plenty of depth and adds that sense of involvement that I happen to enjoy big-time but which always seems to be a matter of subjective taste...some love it, some find 3D adds little. I saw it in the RealD 3D format and found that so dull and lifeless as to be a constant distraction -- my brain saying, "Hey...someone turn on a few more lights!!" I can understand how watching THAT kind of poor 3D would put anyone off the 3D version, but then I want back with friends to see it in IMAX when they added for a week after THE WALK was pulled. IMAX uses dual digital projectors to double the light on the screen and there it was a totally different film -- the 3D was spectacular; it was bright and immerse -- a totally different, MUCH better experience (an IMAX experience if you want to use their marketing jargon). All I can say is, IMAX does it 3D right and the RealD 3D presentation is a much more inferior version. Here's hoping the 3D Blu-ray will be much closer to the IMAX 3D version.

history.review_title: There are MUCH better Dracula movie versions...pick any one OTHER than this one.
history.text: So let's see...as if Amazon charging 3 bucks for a nearly 25yr old movie is not enough, insult is added to injury when your are roped into this mishmash of film by the big name actors and of course the uber-well-respected Francis Ford Coppola's name. But that is where your being impressed in any way about this film will abruptly end -- that and possibly the superb cinematography, but there is not much else. Pretty (or pretty gruesome) photography on its own can't hold a movie together, and this one starts falling apart amazingly fast. Of most terrible note -- Anthony Hopkins' bizarre interpretation of the Van Helsing character; it is just so incongruous and out of place with the entire tone and Gothic feel of the rest of the movie. Well, wait, I take that back -- when did you ever see a Texan with a Texas drawl wearing a 10-gallon hat and touting a shotgun in ANY of the many Dracula incarnations up to now? Well, one is thrown in this version for no apparent reason whatsoever. What relationship any of this has to Van Helsing in poor Bram Stoker's novel is beyond comprehension. On top of that, Hopkins doesn't seem to know what accent he is trying to master -- sometimes it's British, sometimes it has a German twang, sometimes maybe Ygoslavian?? ("Yah") and worse, if he is supposed to be playing the very serious Van Helsing, that vampire expert and killer, and a man who has the responsibility of saving all of human kind from this evil, then why at times does it seem like he's mimicking Jerry Lewis in THE NUTTY PROFESSOR? This, unfortunate out-of-tune character blunder has to be laid at the feet of Coppola himself and probably with a nod of scowling disapproval at the screenwriter as well, because his dialogue at times is laughable. And not to take anything away from Gary Oldman's acting ability, but as Dracula, he is really miscast here. He has neither the mystery nor seductive good looks need for the sexual underpinning that Dracula must have. Mina pants "he's irresistible," and everyone in our home theatre said, "Who is she talking about?" Oldman simply can't pull that off look of irresistible perverted evil. In fact, he seems like he is actually bored with the role and just walking thru his lines, waiting to pick up his paycheck; and then there's his silly dark granny glasses and geeky long stringy black hair which makes him look oddly like Captain Hook in Disney's Peter Pan. When he is transformed into the decrepit old version of himself, he does the tongue quiver that Hopkins made famous in SILENCE OF THE LAMBS (sans the "..fava beans and a nice Chianti" line ). Watch this DRACULA trailer and catch that iconic Hopkins bit of business at 1:05. To sum up.....how can I put this kindly...hmmm...OK, you hear that loud barking? It's this awful DOG of a movie!

history.title: The Black Stallion [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: PURE CINEMA...imagery that is a beauty to behold.
history.text: Total, whole-hearted agreement here with the rest of the 5 star praises, but let me just add, when you watch this magnificent film, take special attention to the horse taming sequence where Alec (Kelly) and Black gain each other's trust and friendship. The sequence is, brilliantly played so naturally and genuinely by Reno and the horse (named Cass-Ole), was as good as any human actor -- kudos to its wrangler. This sequence is PURE cinema...a concept is fully conveyed only with visuals, not a word spoken, much like what needed to be done in silent movies. The spectacular images accompanied by Francis F. Coppola's dad's (Carmine's) powerful score couldn't be a more perfect marriage. Turn the music up LOUD for that sequence; throw anyone who talks during it out of the room!

history.title: Metalstorm: The Destruction Of Jared-Syn (3D Bluray / Bluray) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Enough has been said about the silly story, the stilted dialog made worse by the terrible acting -- if Hollywood has a C list of actors, they are all assembled in this film. And of course the direction is stiff and unsure. That aside, and believe me, it is bad enough to be laughable, I really want to comment on the 3D. I happen to be a 3D fanatic; loved it from the very first time I saw it as a kid in a movie theatre in NY (the then Century Fresh Meadows -- flagship of the chain in Queens) when I watched HOUSE OF WAX. I was hooked; forced my poor mum to sit thru it a second time). Saw every 3D film that came out after that, including the real clunkers, and back then, there weren't many that rose to Academy Award winning quality, but I loved the process, the feeling of depth and space in the image I was watching. To me it was stereo for the eyes. Imagine my delight when technology today allows me to show my kids that same HOUSE OF WAX in my living room on a curved, 65" OLED 3D TV. It's come full circle. BUT as much as I will watch almost anything in 3D that they release on BluRay, the 3D in THIS particular title is so bad that I actually had to stop watching it only a third of the way through. This was shot in SpaceVision 3D, a process that uses literally half the 35mm frame, one half for each eye. That limited film geography on the negative reduces the effective resolution and increases the film grain size to the point that even on a relatively small tv screen (compared to the theatre screen) gives the image a weird, textured look. The fact that the grain is not part of the 3D perspective, it sort of just sit there at the screen frame making the picture seem like it is superimposed on a bed of rice. But that is just the quality of the original source...you know, OLD film. BUT -- and this is where it crashes and burns -- many of the shots are soooo badly converged in the original negative that they are just impossible for your eyes/brain to resolve and you get this terrible feeling like you are seeing double. This happened to be the case with the SpaceVision process which, possibly because of physical spacing of the lenses in what they called the Trioptiscope attachment on the camera, the depth that the viewer experiences is very severe and very unnatural, not like the films shot and shown in dual strip 35mm (all the 50's so call "golden age" of 3D). The severity of the SpaceVision system to start with, then any shot where the cinematographer increases that convergence quota, can make the image unwatchable. This same problem is present in the other SpaceVision 3D film I saw -- Andy_Warhol's_Frankenstein. Many shot are impossible to converge and you see double. LOTS of shots in METALSTORM give that same "Damn, I am going blind" feeling, starting with the very opening credits where the starfield behind the Universal logo is impossible to converge and you say, "Geez, this is not a good sign!". Next you are treated to a "futuristic" vehicle, i.e., a Jeep that has been outfitted with a painted plywood shell over it, driving aimlessly over hill and dale for no apparent reason for what seems like 20 minutes, with half the shots having that very difficult convergence problem, and you ask yourself, "Why am I watching this plywood covered Jeep riding over dirt roads?" Everyone in the room complained. I even went into the 3D settings on the TV menu where the 3D "depth" can be adjusted (really just overall image spacing control) which was set at 50% and I reduced it to down zero (the mildest depth adjustment) in the hopes that would make the images easier for the eyes to converge, but everyone in the room complained that they STILL couldn't deal with some of the images. So as far as the 3D imagery, this gets the extra star only because I love 3D,but really, combined with the awful story and acting, it really deserves 1 star, sorry to say. Others have pretty much reviewed the rest of the quality of the film, which in my mind they are a little to forgiving, but it's obvious this is low budget so pretty much with low expectations so I will leave it at that, but I will add just on additional observation, that the two lead actors, Jeffrey Byron and Kelly Preston are particularly weird -- Preston because his singular expression is that of someone who just gotten tazzed; his eyes are fixed wide-open and bulging. Then there is dear Kelly who must have fell asleep under a hair drier for an hour -- her hair is so frayed and frizzed that it looks like she has one hand on a Tesla coil; Preston on the other hand looks like his hair was dipped in liquid plastic. Add to that the silly dialogue these actors are forced to say and you've got another reason to hit the EJECT button. My advice -- get this thing for free at your local Library or wait until you find it at a flee market or for a couple a bucks used because guaranteed, you won't watch it more than once (and if like me, not even once), but certainly don't be sucked in as I was and shell out list price for this dog of a 3D title.

history.title: Luna (1979) La Luna
history.review_title: A Bertolucci masterpiece finally available, but the Bluray has a serious technical flaw.
history.text: This probably is one very unjustly maligned Bertolucci film that back in 1977 was considered quite controversial but quite honestly, today it really is pretty tame except for the taboo subject matter (Oedipus has been around long enough that we should be over it by now). But this is to report on a very serious technical flaw in this Bluray release by Kino Lorber. For those purchasing this incredible Bertolucci masterpiece in this current release (finally!) be aware that the audio is seriously defective. All the sections that have music are so distorted that it's painful to listen to. Luckily the film has very few moments where music is actually playing, so at least that is a blessing -- dialog is fine, but where the opera music is mixed in, it is atrocious -- full on distortion. How it could be remastered this badly and no one noticed is beyond comprehension. Even the front menu audio is totally distorted. Didn't anyone at KL check this before it was mastered? Anyway, that is just a technical mishap -- KL should remaster this very worthy title and offer to replace the defective discs already sold. That said, this technical flaw shouldn't dissuade anyone foregoing this visual and psychological feast. It is a stunning film that grips you and will keep you intrigued for the full 2 hours. Not to mention it is probably Jill Clayburgh's best work.

history.title: It Came From Outer Space (2-D / 3-D Blu-Ray)
history.review_title: Historically interesting film, with less a less than intelligent storyline.
history.text: More of an historically significant film than it is anything special in the way of story-line (filled with plot holes and cliches) or serious content. It was, along with CREATURE FROM THE BLACK LAGOON Universal's foray into dual projection, polaroid 3D. The "alien creature," such as it, was pretty hokey, and certainly watching this film, you are very much aware of the technical limitations of what could be done with special effects in the 50s. That said, also in that same year (1953) came a major leap forward in much more realistic special effects (and quite frankly, much more of a coherent story line too) with the release of George Pal's WAR OF THE WORLDS (Paramount) which raised the special effects barre by light-years in the same way Kubrick's 2001 did in the 60s. IT CAME FROM OUTER SPACE still is what today we would consider a "B" movie, although at the time it did very good business for Universal. More interesting than the movie itself is the very informative commentary that is part of the added features with this BluRay release. BTW, THE WAR OF THE WORLDS and IT CAME FROM OUTER SPACE both start with a metior hitting the earth, out of which both spew aliens, nasty and benign (sort of) respectively.

history.title: American Mummy [Limited Edition Blu-ray 3D + 2D Versions]
history.review_title: How many ways can you say EFFIN AWFUL?
history.text: Don't be snuckered in by the professional looking DVD cover-art. It makes it look like it's a real movie, doesn't it? It's not. Or by the fact that it's a mummy movie, maybe like me, it a favorite genre of yours; with one new one about to hit movie screens as a potential blockbuster - this certainly is NOT THAT! There used to be such things as "B" pictures; this would be an "F" picture. Terrible acting by fairly unattractive people with a disturbing sexual undertone that constantly there to creep you out, this actually would be considered sexual harassment to women by any standard. Then there's NO story line, NO direction whatsoever; for the first half hour, you don't even know who the characters are, why they are there or what they are doing other than some gibberish about Aztecs and sacrifice . There no exposition, so you have no idea what the relationship is between any of them. The sets, if you could call them that, consists of a few tents and a rocky hill in Cougar Buttes California. And there in the rocky hills (filmed BTW, in almost monotone sepia -- the whole film has the look of faded 35mm stock) these half clad women are running around in short-shorts, legs totally exposed with no protection from snakes or scorpions, for no logical reason other than the director is tuck back in the 50s thinking bare legs in rocky terrain are titillating -- its not, it's just stupid and sexist. Also the gratuitously exposed breasts thrown in are wildly sexy to the point that they will distract from the gawd-awful acting -- THEY DON'T. By the way, those exposed tits are, for some inexplicable reason, immediately smeared and covered with what looks like road tar -- I ask you, how sexy is that?!. Believe me, this piece of garbage shouldn't have even been released directly to DVD, as that would have been a waste of plastic, but it seems it actually was released to cinema screens. Really... a theatre somewhere actually played this thing?! The only reason I bought it was because it was in 3D and I am a big 3D fan, but and even that couldn't save this dog of a movie. The 3D, btw, is nothing to write home about, those old hackneyed, in-you-face, cliche effects, like a shot of a spear coming at you is done with no subtlety whatsoever, with the camera lingering on it way too long as if the director is saying..."Do you get it? We're filming in 3D...see that spear sticking out of the mannequin and into your face? See....3D." I thought adding another 3D title to my 3D library would be a good thing because I am almost sure they are going to stop releasing 3D titles sooner or later now that LG and Samsung are no longer making 3D TVs. Buying this was NOT a good thing; don't make my mistake.

history.title: Brigadoon [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: This is no MY FAIR LADY
history.text: Lerner and Loewe at their not so good. Gene Kelly as a choreographer at his, well, let's just say, he dances better than he choreographs, and even his dancing we've all seen before. There are even some retread moves stolen right out of the SINGIN IN THE RAIN rain sequence. And Mr. Minnelli spent way too much time on set minutia...he seems to have forgotten that he needs to direct his actors...keep them from looking silly. And silly this whole 2 & half hours certainly does look. Thing is, I remember kind a liking this movie years ago -- used to book it in our retrospective art theatre and thought is was sweet. I don't know, maybe I am getting jaded in my old age, but damn, it certainly doesn't woo me now. Now it just seems cloyingly saccharin, with a much too short dose of witty sarcasm for relief that Van Johnson supplies. Yah, the signature Minnelli sumptuous sets are spectacular, but in that effort he has created a world that instead of looking "other-worldly and magical," it look like exactly what it is, a big MGM sound stage set. Everything looks too fake, even for Brigadoon. When I ran it in the theatre, I caught something I couldn't believe got by the editor -- in the big dance scene, there on what is supposed to be dirt ground, were yellow X marks to help cameras and actors land on their marks. I couldn't believe what I saw so I grabbed the binoculars that are in the projection booth to assist in focusing and I watched the sequence carefully and very "close," and yes, there were the stage cue marks. Not that this is a big deal, but it just added to the overall suspension of the "suspension of disbelief" that I get now from this ill-advised musical. I looked for them in the BluRay and either the frame was cut just a little more than the 35mm film frame, or they were digitally removed in the transfer, but there is no doubt that I saw them on the film. You hear people who don't understand musicals (or opera for that matter) say, "it makes no sense...people all of a sudden busting into song with a full orchestra." And I always respond, but you have no problem accepting Transformers and zombies and Klingons and freaking galaxy guardians, even SPIDER effin MAN? Either you go with the genre or just stay home when you see the word "musical" and leave the rest of us alone. But in this film, I found myself saying exactly the same thing about the dancing -- it all seemed so out of sync...just thrown in because, well, it's a musical and you need dance numbers. The dance sequences come abruptly out of nowhere and seemingly without motivation...AND they go on for WAY TOO LONG; the worst thing about them -- they don't move the story along at all, it's just --"Hey, stop the story, here's a dance number...Gene's gotta show off." And show off he does...it's embarrassing. I understand, Kelly at the time was a humungus big star and evidently Freed pinned the movie on his name and popularity. Thing is, he's totally wrong for the part. He's too old, he's much too slick, and nary a hair on his head ever moves or gets tousled. He certainly doesn't look or even sound like the idealistic, tousled-hair young romantic that the part calls for. And while we are on Kelly, let's take a look at the lack-luster choreography, sadly there is nothing new here. It's repetitive, it's all been done before, he steals almost identical movements from Agnes DeMille's CAROUSEL choreography (watch Louise's dance sequence -- ballet, actually -- with the Starlight Carousel barker) and then he steals Astaire's tap moves as well, and for good measure, he retreads a lot of his moves from SINGIN IN THE RAIN, but without the rain or the freshness. Move along...nothing to new to see here other than Gene Kelly designing dance sequences for himself that are too long and so obviously vanity vehicles for himself. Evidently Minnelli was too afraid to reign in the superstar. Then there is Ms Charisse -- yes, the woman is statuesque, and in this film, that's about it. Oh yah, the statue had with WAY to much rouge (who was her makeup artist? Should have been fired it's so badly done). Either it was Minnelli who just wasn't giving her any direction or the woman simply can't act, but thru the entire movie she either over-acts to the point of comedy or she does nothing but stare into space looking like a dear caught in headlights. There is one sequence where for what seems like a good 10 minutes, that's exactly what she does -- sits there, motionless staring off-set, looking at nothing...perhaps searching for motivation? She also walks with her arms unnaturally far out from her sides as if she's trying to avoid touching her dress; perhaps it was just pinned up by wardrobe and she's afraid it will come apart? I got the feeling she had no idea what she was doing and unfortunately Minnelli didn't clue her in. Oh, yah, let's not forget to mention how absurd this "Scottish" dialog starts to sound after about 5 minutes, all these Californians trying to get "Now dunna, ye worry the wee lassie" to sound authentic. And of course the songs; for me they are not very memorable, none followed me around for days after viewing like so many other good musicals songs do except maybe "Heather on the Hill." And I might add, like the dance numbers, the songs also didn't come naturally to the story line and worse, did they move the story along. Like I said, this is no MY FAIR LADY or CAMELOT. The only bright spot for me in this whole mishmash is the Van Johnson character's dialogue. There were some lines where I laughed aloud and heard the old super clever Alan Jay Lerner dialogue breaking thru. But that's countered with the forced attempt at mystical magical romantic sweet-talk he gives Kelly...just give me a barb bag along along with the BluRay. This sappy stuff was drawn out and so unpleasant that I actually grabbed the remote to see if I could skip ahead. Hey, it was a big hit for MGM so who can argue with success and it seems to get plenty of 5 stars here. But what seems painfully obvious to me is just a studio trying to hold the decline caused by TV at bay, recycling their aging, big musical stars and bigger, more lavish productions. There certainly was that over-the top effort to provide a sumptuous "look" that only Hollywood was capable of and that TV back then would never be able to give an audience. But in this instance, it was so overdone that it simply looks too fake...in Ansco Color? Ansco Color is a poor man's Technicolor and an even poorer man's Eastman Color. You can see how much the studios were trying to best TV -- the wide screen process name (CinemaScope) is put BEFORE the picture title or even the stars' names! Problem for me is, it just doesn't work for me any more. My suggestion, like in Brigadoon, see it once, then put it on a shelf for the next 100 years.

history.text: (1. Jax was business as usual mere days after Taras death (even WHILE still in prison for those 10 days) (2. Jax seemingly has zero reaction to Tara besides looking at an empty side of the bed, looking at kitchen floor and one single tear (all at S7 Ep2) he NEVER even visits Tara's tombstone (even though he practically lived at his dads and Opies for 6 seasons) poor character continuity. Not only does he not cry or show that he is ever thinking about her or his loss, looking at him in every scene (he is not "killing out of rage") you would have no idea that anything major JUST happened in his life. The Jax we all know would be an absolute train wreck. He has so much depth and love for Tara. Its as if the writers did not watch the first 6 seasons. (3. The mother and son storyline (priest family) all filler no killer. (4. Chib's and Bobby going along with this nonsense even though they were always the voices of reason. Poor continuity. (5. Unser of all people couldnt put 2 and 2 together with this murder? HE WAS THERE when Gemma left high and drunk the night Tara was killed! (6. Jax sleeps with a prostitute before Tara is even cold in the ground? (maybe dead for 20 days?) Paris claims that Jax cheated on Tara so why wouldn't get do this. He cheated on her once to make her leave this life. Then again when they were emotionally disconnected on the surface. The depths of his love were never realized in season 7. Fooling around while youre here and the ability to make love after you JUST DIED are two diff things. (7. Jax is suddenly neglectful and crappy father. Yes he was barely around but this was ridiculous. (8. The lack of August Marks...yikes. You hear about him but he is too busy on other shows to be there. His lack of presence really hurt overall. (9. Chib's and Jarry repetitive scenes over and over. Ultimately leading nowhere at the last episode with no character arcs. (10. A season long build up to Boroski being the rat, you never even see him for half the year and when you do it's over in a second. Completely anticlimactic sub plot with zero pay off. Woulda made sense if Chibs or Chucky was the rat. Chibs (mad Jax was giving gun to black due to his IRA ties) or Chucky (used to work for Lynn and thrown out for being a rat). Or Tig (who coulda made a deal with Marks the day Jax told Marks where to go to kill Tig in season 6). (11. The episode where Gemma was taken to the cabin because she thought she was gonna be killed and the big pay off what that she found out it was for the priest family? WE ALREADY KNEW THAT, where was our pay off? Woulda been way better if she killed a major character like Happy, out of fear and panic. (14. The pointless cameo of the Glee star at the diner. When she told her that it was her fault (Tara) was dead, waitress coulda told Unser that she rambled about being to blame for someones death (when Gemma left Unser there instead of giving him a ride back). Instead again it lead nowhere. (15. The cheat ending with Juice and Gemma, cliffhanger to nowhere. (16. The big build up to when the Crew finally catches up with Juice led to NOTHING! We never even got to see the confrontation! They took him away and had a whole conversation OFF SCREEN! WTF? (17. Jax has sex with Wendy after killing his mother? Was already weird when he had sex with her the night Dona died, now this? (18. Best ending for Gemma would have been a lonely miserable life away from her family. Instead Sutter gives us a typical ending with no depth or surprise. Everyone figured Jax would kill Gemma and he did. (19. Nero survives the show? For 2-3 years he says he is gonna "buy the farm" and instead he literally buys the farm. Woulda been a heart breaking death... but nope.. nothing. (20. I will end it with the demise of our main character... All we went through, the whole mythology and all of it led up to Jax killing a SOA prez in self defense and being voted to meet Mr Mayhem? history.review_title: Couldn't Wait for It to End.
history.text: I had never seen this Halloween movie and the price was right. I don't have any idea why this Halloween movie is popular. Yes, it has very famous stars in it, but the acting is abysmal. The best part is Bette Midler's costume and make-up.

history.title: A Royal Christmas
history.review_title: A Christmas movie you can watch again and again!
history.text: This is a perfectly delightful Christmas movie. It's endearing, a little suspenseful and wholly predictable. The love story of Leo and Emily proceeds uneventfully until Leo reveals (after a year of dating Emily) that he is a prince and heir to a kingdom. Leo's controlling mother, Queen Isadora, works to thwart their love story once the young couple visit the kingdom. Jane Seymour is just wicked enough.

history.title: DANCE That WALK – 5000 Steps in One Easy Low Impact Walking Workout DVD
history.review_title: This work-out is fun, but not overly challenging.
history.text: I have two left feet and no discernible rhythm yet I love this work-out video! The change of musical style every couple minutes makes this work-out fly by. There are four moves per "dance." Gina Buber is low-key and encouraging. I am a huge fan of Leslie Sansone work-out DVDs, but I enjoy this welcome change of pace.

history.title: Disney's A Christmas Carol
history.review_title: Highly recommended to lovers of "A Christmas Carol."
history.text: I've seen so many movie versions of Charles Dickens' immortal story of "A Christmas Carol." Somehow this version had escaped me. The animation was beautiful and intriguing. There was a few times when the movie maker grew too enamored of the animation and lost the trail of the story line. I loved that the dialogue stayed so true to the book.

history.title: Crown for Christmas
history.review_title: Super cute and engaging Christmas-time love story!
history.text: You must suspend all disbelief since a bright, artistic and selfless hotel maid becomes the love interest of an emotionally-repressed European prince within one week. That being said, I really enjoyed this movie and look forward to watching it many times. The actors and actresses are well-cast. The castle is splendid. You can't help but root for Allie, Princess Teddy and King Ryland.

history.title: Wizard of Oz: 75th Anniversary [4K UHD]
history.review_title: Truly a classic that deserves to be enjoyed again and again!
history.text: My husband and I hadn't seen "The Wizard of Oz" in decades. It was such a pleasure to watch it again. Everything about it is enchanting. It never ages. When you watch it, you feel like a wide-eyed child again. The music, the costumes, the fairy tale -- every generation should discover it or rediscover it as we did.

history.title: A Christmas Carol
history.review_title: I look forward to watching it every year at Christmas!
history.text: I have seen so many movie versions based on Dickens' immortal "A Christmas Carol." This one is my favorite. Patrick Stewart is Scrooge. The dialogue is very close to that of the book.

history.title: DANCE That WALK - CARDIO PARTY - Low Impact Walking Workout Pack with Two Easy 5000 Step DVDs (NTSC)
history.text: This is a fun workout that will give you a challenge. Gina is very bubbly. The moves take a bit of practice. The short segments go by quickly.

history.title: NCIS: Season 11
history.text: My only complaint with the Season 11 DVD, is with the Ep.1 Commentary. While it is fair to assume that people listening to the commentary have watched the episode in question, it is not fair to assume that DVD purchasers have necessarily seen the entire season. It is highly irritating & annoying to us enjoying this excellent series for the first time on DVD, never having watched it on TV, for it to be revealed in an Ep. 1 Commentary that a certain character is killed mid-season! It is like the A-hole who goes to a movie a second time and starts revealing upcoming scenes in a loud voice to the audience, or plot points upcoming in a book you are reading. If you wouldn't say or show it in previews of upcoming shows on the TV broadcast, don't put it in a Commentary! Just common sense really. Up to this point, in prior seasons, the Commentaries have been very good with sticking to talking about the show in question. Otherwise, the writing, acting and direction are all still excellent.

history.title: 13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi
history.text: How can a movie about the Benghazi travesty not mention the name "Hillary Clinton?" Nothing about the numerous requests for more security, down-play of the requests for help during the attack and the numerous orders to "stand down." Nothing about the real story of Benghazi, the immediate cover-up by Obama and Hillary Clinton (yes the internet video is mentioned but not who was selling the lie of the video being the reason for the attack.) Luckily, the movie was made within recent memory of people who know what actually happened (from the interviews of the heroes involved and seeing Susan Rice and Hillary Clinton with their own eyes lie about the video) so that the complete story of the failure to order the rescue and the subsequent cover-up is known by at least some voters. Ask yourself, if the only thing you knew about Benghazi was from this movie, would you know that Hillary Clinton had any involvement at all in the Benghazi incident, before, during, or after? Simply a whitewash that lets her off the hook. (Pretty well done otherwise, thus the 3 stars.)

history.title: The Last Ship: Season 1
history.text: Makes you wonder how TNT can afford the production cost of making a series that looks as good as any major motion picture. Very much a showcase of U.S. military capability. Bought the first season at a Black Friday sale, never having seen the show. Finally watched it and was glad I bought it (and just ordered Season two.) Great cast, great writing, plausible plot. Lots of action and good guys making tough decisions, always striving to do the right thing. Reminds me of the many ex-military men who I have been trained by, unabashed patriots and heroes all. Probably has the worst possible time-slot on TV, Sunday night at the same time as AMC's Fear the Walking Dead, but that is what a second cable hookup, TV and VCR or DVR are for. You certainly do not have to dislike The Walking Dead to like this show. They are both top-quality shows, worth watching and buying. This one is based more in real, scientific possibility, but both are about what happens to humanity when social order breaks down, however it happens, which is always interesting to think about. If it happens, just be sure you are armed with plenty of ammo!

history.title: Matt Helm Lounge: The Silencers / Murderers' Row / The Ambushers / The Wrecking Crew [DVD]
history.text: Worst adaptation of a book series ever. Donald Hamilton's Matt Helm is a serious bad ass in the books, not in any way a clown. Only the first film, The Silencers, was done half-way seriously, and even it did not live up to the book. The rest of the films were simply farces and makes The Silencers look good by comparison, when it really isn't. Believe me, each film gets progressively worse after The Silencers. Read the books instead, starting with Death of a Citizen, and you will see what I mean. I saw all of the films in the theater when they came out, so would not waste 10 cents on this set, much less the outrageous asking price for some of the worst films ever made. (The Matt Helm book series deserves a real adaptation of the books, done with a serious Director and leading actor, remaining true to the books. If done right, they would make very good films, more in the nature of the Parker films.) Zero stars is the real rating, but apparently one star is the lowest you can go.

history.title: Banshee: Season 3
history.review_title: Annoying Commentary Spoilers, but Great Show
history.text: No complaints with the show itself. This season features two brutally realistic fights and a number of interesting new characters. My only complaint is that in the Episode 1 Commentary there are spoilers of two different deaths of characters later in the season. There is even less reason to believe that people buying a series on DVD that comes from a premium cable show have seen the entire season on TV than shows from network TV. I usually like to watch everything on a disc at one time, while the episodes are still fresh in my mind, so foretelling future plot points and character deaths in an early commentary is extremely annoying. It's called drama people! Let the story develop! Since the season is only 10 episodes, the best way to watch it and the commentaries, is to watch all the episodes and then go back and watch the commentaries. Yes, I do like the commentaries, but a comprehensive commentary discussing the specifics of the entire season goes on the last episode of a season, not the first.

history.title: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. - The Complete Series (Repackage/DVD)
history.text: This series is definitely a mixed bag. The first season is one of the best seasons of a spy series of all time: good writing, real danger, well acted, great guest stars. Napoleon Solo was truly cool under pressure. The writers proceeded to ruin the show after that season, (think the first Lethal Weapon movie vs Lethal Weapon 3 or 4 or Twin Peaks Season One vs. Twin Peaks Season Two) It is probably still worth getting the full series set to see everything, but you can see how they destroyed a show with an excellent beginning. If you just bought Season One and saw how good it was, you would likely want to buy Season Two anyway, so you might as well get the whole series at a pretty reasonable price. (Had this show ended after Season One, this show would have had the same, or better, cult following as The Prisoner; just an excellent show that inexplicably ended, leaving everyone wanting more.) As it is, it very much wore out its welcome by the end.

history.title: Bone Tomahawk
history.text: One of the better recent Westerns once it got going.. Probably because the first-time Director was the writer, there was a clear attempt to put in whatever was written, instead of increasing the pace and trimming a lot of early, unnecessarily long setup. It looks great, extremely well acted. Sad but satisfying outcome. With a little editing, would have been even better.

history.title: Melancholia
history.text: Slow, tedious, boring. Take a fairly simple Science Fiction idea of the earth under threat of being destroyed and make it into an uninteresting bore-fest. If a point can be made in 5 minutes, let's take 15 or 20 minutes to make it, and on and on. The entire first half of the movie (of 2 hours and 15 minutes) was unnecessary to the rest of the film. No explanation of what happened to her husband, in the second half of the film, after going on and on, and on and on, with the wedding party in the first half. The only redeeming part of the film is Kirsten Dunst finally getting topless in two scenes, and the last 30 seconds of the film, but, beyond that, this movie is a total waste of time. Very good actors are simply wasted by the Writer/Director of this mess.

history.title: Ash vs Evil Dead - The Complete First Season
history.text: The show is very funny, extremely bloody in a tongue-in-cheek sort of way, and a lot of fun; but don't miss the commentaries. Some of them are as funny as the show. You would definitely want to hang out with Bruce Campbell. Pablo and Kelly are excellent sidekicks and funny in the commentaries especially. Good stunts and effects. Am looking forward to Season Two.

history.title: Bubba Ho-Tep (Limited Collector's Edition)
history.text: Chance to see Bruce Campbell act. Bruce is very convincing as elderly Elvis and young Elvis in flashback. Nice easy build-up to a neat idea. Very satisfying film, although with pretty blunt language. Just bought the novella based upon the Extra of Joe R. Lansdale's reading of chapter 1. Everyone is very good in this movie, but in particular, Bruce Campbell and Ossie Davis. True Bruce Campbell fans should be pleased with this performance, even though it is very different from the Evil Dead trilogy.

targets.title: The Strain: The Complete First Season

history.title: Wagon Train, The Complete Color Season
history.text: What I really wanted was the Wagon Train episodes from start to finish. This is not what I got. The DVDs start somewhere with the color episodes. At the end are some of the earlier ones, but apparently not in any particular order. I remembered this being a really good show. Now the episodes seem somewhat silly.

history.title: Garrow's Law: Series One
history.text: Drama is too schetchy. Not enough meat to the story lines. As with a lot of American TV, there is a contest to see how much female breast can be shown. This means there is a lack of confidence in the story line, the direction and the acting.

history.title: Vera, Set 3
history.text: Every thing about this series suits me just right - with the possible exception of occasional accents being difficult to understand. The stories are well thought out and easier to follow than some of the other British mysteries. There are usually several suspects to consider. Vera has her team checking the many leads that surface. The detective work is realistic. Each story includes moments of humor that are done just right. Too bad there were only four episodes in set 3. I hope the sets keep on coming.

history.title: William & Mary: Complete Collection
history.review_title: A real downer after Doc Martin
history.text: We watched only the first episode. That was enough. Perhaps if we had not seen Doc Martin, this would have been more acceptable. However, too much emphasis is placed on revealing as much of women's private parts as possible. The story line is weak, perhaps that is why more skin is revealed. For instance, his daughter keeps asking to spent the night at a friend's house and he says no. There is no argument, just good natured acceptance. Really, what family is like that? Of course, the daughter is granted such permission after the father gets lucky. The story lines are not even that funny. Maybe I should have given it two stars.

history.title: Kavanagh Q.C. Complete
history.text: John Thaw is such an excellent actor. This biggest problem with this series is that it is too short. With story lines that may at first seem black and white, the shows throw in lots of gray. As for the British judicial system, this series is a great follow on from Rumpole in that Kavanagh does not have that base of humor that Rumpole built upon but rather exhibits a great deal of seriousness.

history.title: Last Tango in Halifax: Season 2 [DVD]
history.review_title: This is a great series! There are so many real people with ...
history.text: This is a great series! There are so many real people with real vulnerabilities. None of them is perfect, but there is no (that I remember) back stabbing. Sometimes they just don't get alone with each other. They do try to get along without sacrificing too much of themselves. This series makes it without relying on sex or vulgarities. Be sure to see season 1 first.

history.title: Scott & Bailey: Season 2
history.text: I find this to be a great British cop series. The two stars have different personal problems which add to the interest. Their boss is one of my two favorites for this type of series (the other being Thursday in Endeavour). A lot gets packed into each show. So far, the powers that be have not resorted to female nudity to detract from the series.

history.title: The Brokenwood Mysteries, Series 1
history.text: Have watched three of four so far. We really enjoy this series. Humor is mixed in with emotions and detective work. So far, no female nudity observed, which is a rarity these days. We would rather have the story told by the writing, direction and acting than by female body parts. The accents are sometimes cute - "dead" is pronounced "deed". We will definitely get the next series, if there is one.

history.title: McClain's Law: The Complete Series
history.review_title: After all, he is Marshal Dillon
history.text: Three stars for James Arness. He is still a presence on the screen. The other actors all need improvement. We stopped watching when the show increased its sleaze factor with Markie Post doing some sort of Hooker/undercover function. If that does not bother you and you will watch almost anything to see Marshal Dillon again, go for it.

history.title: Midsomer Murders, Series 17
history.text: Have watched two so far and they are as good as the earlier ones. Amazon made the series difficult to find by switching from SET numbers to SERIES numbers. I had SET #25 and kept looking for SET #26. The season after SET #25 is SERIES #17. Go figure. It took a lot of digging and scratching to figure this out. Amazon lists SERIES 17 far below SET 25 leading one to conclude that SERIES 17 is older. There is now SERIES 18 and part of SERIES 19. I discovered this by using the Acorn site.

I bought seasons 1 & 2 as soon as Amazon offered them, and was disappointed to see that Season 3 was "Currently Unavailable". Now there is an offering of the entire collection including season 3 as a package. But I already have seasons 1 & 2 and I'm not a big fan of redundancy, so until Season 3 comes out as a standalone product in a format I can use in the U.S., I guess I'll just save my cash and do without.

history.text: I now have all three versions of this movie (DeCaprio/Winslet) 1997, (Webb/Stanwyck) 1953, and the Titanic mini series (George C. Scott) from 2012. This is the second best of the three. Being a "Historic Purist", I prefer the 1953 edition with Clifton Webb and Barbara Stanwyck.

Overall, a good TV series, a bit of a disappointment here due to the inability to view the entire series.
