history.title: A Boyfriend for Christmas [DVD]
history.review_title: Never thought much of it, but I was pleasantly surprised after watching it this year
history.text: Never payed much attention to this movie, but I decided to give it a chance this year (2016). I think this was done before Hallmark started their 'Countdown to Christmas' movies. Even so, this movie was a good surprise. It has a good and funny story. It is a bit predictable like many of the Hallmark movies, but it is still funny. I have enjoyed seeing Patrick Muldoon in movies since he was in Starship Troopers. I like Kelli Williams in this also. Martin Mull also delivers a few scenes that are very funny. I have not purchased it yet, but it will be added to our Christmas movies collection this year.

history.title: I'll Be Home For Christmas
history.review_title: Just when you thought that Jonathan Taylor Thomas couldn't be more irritating
history.text: Jonathan Taylor Thomas was annoying in Home Improvement. He thought he would just quit a successful TV show and get a big movie career starting with this one. Well, it was just the first of many horrible movies this idiot did. The story in this movie was extremely weak and just as far from a Christmas movie as it could be. What's interesting is all the liberal preaching that Thomas wanted put in Home Improvement about evil of capitalism and other ramblings. And then he does a movie that is themed around just that. His character wants to get home to get a Porsche? Wow. Greed at its best. So, this movie is irritating, Thomas is irritating and the whole experience is like a colonoscopy without medication...... Just skip this travesty.

history.title: Looney Tunes: Golden Collection Volume 3 (DVD)
history.review_title: A collection just not that great and one HUGE flaw Warner Brothers put in this collection
history.text: The collection on this one is not that great. Disc #2 has a lot of the really old cartoons that I am just not that crazy about. Why the one star? Two words - Whoopi Goldberg. Why did they have to put her on this collection at the beginning of the disc giving a 15 minute lecture on how these cartoons are hate-filled and racist. She is the true definition of hate and racism. She has no business being on this collection and totally ruined it for me. I hope Warner Brothers doesn't use her again, or there will be no more collections purchased by me.

history.review_title: Still pretty good even after these years
history.text: I first watched this many years ago and recently watched it on Amazon Prime. It still stands up pretty well. A few of the jokes are a bit dated, but it it is still funny. Having the original cast do the cameos that they did was a nice touch. The girls who played Marcia and Jan were excellent. I think putting the aspect of the one girl in who was after Marcia was in bad taste and was not funny. Gary Cole really nailed the 'Mike Brady value speeches'. Overall, I still enjoy watching this!

history.title: Agent Carter: The Complete Second Season (Marvel)
history.review_title: Season 1 was great - was this really this best follow-up they could come up with?
history.text: Season 1 of Agent Carter was awesome. It was a good continuation of the story of Captain America in WWII. The stories were interesting with good acting and action. And Hayley Atwell - hey, she always is pleasing to the eye. So, ABC announces Season 2. We watched it with anticipation of a continuation of Season 1. Instead, they plop Peggy Carter down in California (huh?). The stories were weird and boring. I think they were trying to go for something that really belonged (sort of) in Agents of Shield. After the second show, we couldn't stay away for anything else. It is really a shame that this show went down the route that it did. They could have taken this up to the late 1980's and helped explain how Peggy was there with Howard Stark and Henry Pymm at Shield headquarters. Instead, they managed to put a gun to Peggy's head and pull the trigger.

history.title: Zootopia
history.review_title: Avoid this piece of propaganda crap
history.text: This movie is so full of subliminal garbage and liberal agenda. If you don't see it, you need to check out a few of the videos on YouTube that tear this movie apart and the attempted brainwashing of children this movie does. There are satanic symbols throughout the movie - and I am an agnostic with a strong belief in the existence of evil. Disney tries to paint this picture as a cute-sie, cuddly movie about animals, but the liberal agenda is very transparent. If you are a parent or grandparent who has seen the travel down the toilet which Hollywood has taken and is concerned about it, this movie only sent them a few more miles down the pipes. This movie generally flopped at the theaters and is already being marked down on DVD at major retailers - that should tell you as well to avoid it.

history.title: The Incredible Dr. Pol Season 3
history.review_title: Not a review of the show - simply the DVD - please read the review for the 1 star rational
history.text: This is a review of the DVD only. It is NOT about the show. We love Dr. Pol's show and really regret that we won't have this season in our collection. The first disc set we received would not play. The DVD had no main menu or chapter menu on it. It would not rewind or fast forward - just play forward. I tested it in a computer with a DVD drive. The discs would play the opening NatGeo intro but would not play at all or display any menus. I returned the discs and received replacements promptly from Amazon. The second set did EXACTLY the same thing that the first set did. I called National Geographic's DVD / movie customer service. They were unaware of any issues with this season. I am returning the second set for a refund. Season 2 discs did not give us any problems, so I will try the other seasons and see if they have the same problem. Again, we LOVE Dr. Pol's show and deserves Five Stars.

history.title: Up the Academy (1980)
history.review_title: Restored to its original version with Mad Magazine references
history.text: This is one of those silly, nonsense movies of the 1980's which is actually truly a classic This version has the Mad Magazine scenes and references restored which had been eliminated in initial releases of this movie. The characters are silly. The humor is raunchy in a few scenes. Barbara Bach is in her prime and definite eye candy in the movie. One of the collection if you are a collector of 1980's movies.

history.title: Marvel's Jessica Jones: The Complete Season 1
history.review_title: Not for children - worth watching but not sure it is belongs in the my Marvel DVD / BluRay collection
history.text: This series reminds me a lot of the first portion of the first season of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. in it having little to nothing to do with superheroes or the Marvel universe in general. I was hoping for a superhero movie with some super powers, but there are vague references to Jessica's super powers. Jessica is only seen severely punching or throwing people. She also has a leaping scene to a second or third floor of the building. They do make some references to occurrences to other Marvel events ( The Incredible Hulk, The Avengers movie ). I will have to admit that it is an intense show that keeps my attention for the investigation, intrigue and suspense. However, this is not what I was looking for in this show. I was also disgusted with the whole character portrayed by Carrie-Anne Moss with her "love" triangle. It was in bad taste and unnecessary to the show. I guess when your career goes down the toilet after The Matrix movies, this is the only horrible role you can get. I will complete the series on NetFlix, but I will probably pass on buying it as I am sure that I will not watch it again like I do my Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and other Marvel DVD's.

history.title: Snatched
history.review_title: Shumer is not funny - just obnoxious and nauseating Hawn - how your career has fallen
history.text: Amy Shumer is not funny. She is vile, disgusting and repulsive to look at. Seeing her on the big screen makes it all that worse. She needs to think about a career in basket weaving where nobody has to look at her (and throw up in their mouth) and she just keeps her mouth shut. Goldie Hawn demonstrates just how far down the toilet her career has went having to pair up with a loser like Shumer. It is a real shame. Save your money and buy something actually worth watching like an actual comedy.

history.title: The Getaway [DVD]
history.review_title: Good story, but the cast ruins it.
history.text: I liked this much better when I saw it in the theater in '72. Watching it now kind of makes me wince a little at the truly awful acting and all the really noticeable errors in continuity. By the standards of the 1970s, this wasn't a particularly well made film. It was a very good story but the cast pretty well ruined it. McQueen could never act, and neither could Ali Macgraw. Al Lettieri was terrible, as usual, and Bo Hopkins was still a novice who hadn't developed any skills. Slim Pickens delivered the one good performance in the whole movie, during the closing minutes. Another big failure is that the musical score is particularly annoying. Even with its faults it's still much better than the 1994 remake, which was just godawful.

history.title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine (Single-Disc Edition)
history.text: After seeing the recent Xmen sequel with the wolverine character, I bought this one. This earlier installment is just plain silly in comparison. The action sequences are particularly annoying, with fantasyland actions by the characters. This at least had a little backstory crammed into the first few minutes, but the rest is pure adolescent fantasy.

history.title: The Revenant
history.review_title: There's a better telling of this legend available.
history.text: Needlessly bleak retelling of the Hugh Glass legend, this version has Glass following the band of trappers in an improbable series of events in which he recovers enough to be able to kill the man who killed his son. A more credible version of the myth is "Man in the Wilderness". That version is worth watching again, while this one is such a slog that rewatching it is even less bearable than your first viewing.
Very aptly named. It's so tedious that it seems to last for 6 days instead of 88 minutes.

history.title: The Walking Dead: Season 3
history.text: The 3rd season is much darker than the two earlier seasons. To me, it's depressing that they find a prison to hole up in, but that isn't the worst of it. This season brings a psychotic leader of another community to deal with. Naturally, Andrea falls for him. She fell for Shane, the psycho, and now the Governor. If she keeps this up, she'll fall for a walker next. To me, this is the bleakest season in the series. So many characters are killed off and such gore and nastiness is wallowed in that I had to force myself to get through it just for the continuity. Maybe it's just me, but the Rick character is insufferable. He seems unable to make a sensible decision but his group seems to love him for some reason. I just hope he doesn't get everyone killed before this season ends.

history.title: The Leftovers: Season 2 [DVD]
history.text: This second season is "beyond the book" as the director says, and it shows. The storylines ( yes, there are several) are a little unhinged and two episodes are beyond boring, "No Room at the Inn" and "International Assassin". The second series stories just aren't up to the level of the book-based first season.

This didn't do it for me. It's a very clumsily done CIA hero flick with two decrepit old former stars playing forgettable roles. All the current memes are dragged into the plot so it can be called a "ripped from the headlines" story. The trouble is that the headlines are false and so is the premise of this goofy tale.

history.title: The Leftovers: The Complete Third Season
history.text: The first season hooks you, the second kind of brings you along in hope, then the third season leaves you hanging. I suppose the series creators tired of trying to tie things up, and just quit. One thing you'll notice about this third season is the annoying music that takes the place of dialog for no apparent reason. Some interesting things are depicted in this season, but not enough is settled.

history.review_title: Very poor casting in this flick.
history.text: This film, with its relatively high budget, is ruined by the casting director. Michael Keaton is somewhat well cast, but the other leads are very poorly chosen. The Rapp character is played by Dylan O'Brian, with his patchy beard, hobbit-like features and small stature that make him totally unbelievable. Sanaah Lathan is miscast as a Deputy Director of the CIA, and is given an absurd wig to wear throughout, and is also unbelievable as the character she's trying to play. The story is pretty ludicrous, also. It's based on an unreadable novel by Vince Flynn, that reinforcer of fake MSM memes. Fans of his novels might enjoy this farce if they can get past the casting errors, but I just couldn't manage even the basic storyline, let alone the bad cast.

history.title: Sliders - The Complete Series
history.review_title: A good show with an awful final season and no extras
history.text: I remember really liking this series when it first aired on Fox because I've always liked parallel dimension stories. I also liked the characters and the actors who portrayed them. I do recall the series getting weaker in its fourth and final season on Fox, which was part of why John Rhys-Davies left. I never followed the show to the then-called SciFi Network. Just as well--the fifth season was practically unwatchable. There are no extras with this set, not even subtitles. I picked up a used earlier version of the first three seasons but kept this one because there were more episodes per disc and less space taken up; I recall Cleavant Derricks remarking the series was less fun to work on after Rhys-Davies left in the interviews from the other set. Given how awful the fourth and fifth seasons were, I now wish I'd kept the earlier versions.

history.title: September 11 - The New Pearl Harbor
history.review_title: A very solid documentary with two glaring omissions and one glaring error
history.text: I was very impressed with how well the case for conspiracy was laid out in this documentary. While borrowing from a number of sources, including [[ASIN:B00HO13ER4 9/11: Explosive Evidence - Experts Speak Out]], Mazzucco's film was clear and direct. If anything, the section on how the collapse of WTC1 and WTC2 was made more clear with the explanations supplied with the excerpted footage from Explosive Evidence than Explosive Evidence itself. Where this documentary fell down was in the omission of Silverstein's PBS interview where he freely admitted that WTC7 was deliberately imploded, which was one of the few actual pieces of evidence given in [[ASIN:B000VRF4C6 9/11: The Myth and The Reality - 2 DVD Set]]. The other glaring issue was the allegation that pulmonary fibrosis and mesothelioma were running rampant in the wake of the destruction of WTC1 and WTC2. Problem: asbestos-induced interstitial fibrosis and mesothelioma have very clear latency times of 20 years after the date of first exposure. If such an epidemic is to happen, it will not happen for another 45 months from the time this review is written. Also, mesothelioma already occurs in 1/1,000,000 people each year WITHOUT prior asbestos exposure. If these diagnoses in past cases are correct, there are some equally disturbing causes: either a) there was prior exposure well ahead of 9/11, or b) there are additional toxic materials not previously identified to the public used in the construction of WTC1 and WTC2. EDITED TO ADD: On a repeat viewing something I failed to note jumped out at me. The two Italian debunkers routinely cited in this documentary are members of CICAP. When this organization is first mentioned, there was a picture of a number of its most notable members. Chief among these, I recognized James Randi, AKA The Amazing Randi. In looking up CICAP on Wikipedia (hardly the best source, but CICAP's site is written in Italian), I learned CICAP is an organization devoted to the debunking of psychic phenomena and pseudo-science. On that basis, it would seem clear that CICAP is in no position to argue the scientific problems raised by 9/11 skeptics. Really, where are CICAP's architects and engineers?

history.title: 9/11: The Myth and The Reality Set
history.review_title: A supposedly "dispassionate" expose without much evidence
history.text: I immediately began to turn off when the speaker was introduced on the first DVD as a religious "scholar," which is about as impressive a title to me as an expert on (insert your favorite here) comic book universe. Worse, he states his specialty is in separating myth from truth, but religion and theism contain only myth. These lectures are made worse by the lack of evidence. Presumably the speaker showed a slide show at the lectures, both delivered in California to leftist audiences. The videos were edited to add pictures of various people and objects. As he speaks, he keeps talking about how dispassionate his analysis is, but his hatred of Bush and Cheney is evident in his speech, and every time Cheney is mentioned, the infamous "sneer" picture is displayed. However, such pictures don't constitute evidence. For instance, he claims a Bush brother and cousin owned the company responsible for security at the WTC (which had a 72-hour period where security was absent the weekend prior to 9/11), but his only evidence is a picture of the two of them jogging with Bush the Younger, not, say, a picture of the corporate ownership documents. The only real evidence he presents is a PBS interview with Silverstein where Silverstein admitted deliberately demolishing WTC7.

history.title: Cop 1988
history.review_title: A great movie comes to Blu-Ray
history.text: I've loved this movie since I first saw it on cable in the 1980s. The Blu-Ray transfer is decent but not great, I think owing to sub-par film stock used since this was a low-budget film. The commentary largely focuses on the director's career overall, rather than this movie. It was interesting to know that Harris and Woods worked for scale, intending to make their money on the back end, only to have the studio go bankrupt and the film be released with little publicity. It was also interesting to learn that Woods mainly convinced his friends to join the cast. Harris's commentary about Woods's character relating to Lesley Ann Warren's character focuses on the truth of male-female relationships rather than the uselessness of political correctness, and is great for a laugh.

history.title: The Prisoner (Miniseries)
history.review_title: What good is a remake of The Prisoner that explains everything?
history.text: I was leery of this miniseries when I first heard about it, since I was a huge fan of the 1967 series ever since my local PBS station did its only real public service by running it in 1978. I loved the abstract nature of the series and how it lent itself to multiple interpretations. Moreover, McGoohan himself encouraged this. That said, I bought this for Hayley Atwell, who impressed me in Captain America and in The Pillars of the Earth. Unfortunately the series teases the viewer with glimpses of her until the fourth episode. While she appears throughout, it's her last appearance in the series. Ian McKellen's performance seems forced and inauthentic. Jim Caviezel's performance has echoes of McGoohan's rebellion without any of the real substance, and Lennie James is wasted as one of the other Villagers. The end of the series is truly unsatisfying. Fans of Person of Interest might be interested in this as a dovetail to the surveillance culture of that series and for Caviezel, but as lame as the final season ended up being, this Prisoner remake is far worse.

history.title: The Perfect Weapon [Blu-ray]

history.text: I truly wish there had been an option for the "TBS cut" of this movie, which is vastly different from the theatrical release. The "TBS cut" shows that Mariska Hargitay had more to do than just stand around looking pretty, and was a more interesting movie. As stated in the header, the transfer is quite good despite the low budget of this film.

history.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A very good Marvel outing, but the SJW nonsense drags it down
history.text: There has always been a lot of hype about various Hollywood projects. When Civil War was coming out, the hype was that Tom Holland had finally nailed the Spider-Man/Peter Parker character. When I saw Civil War, I had to agree the hype was bang-on accurate. Holland continues his excellent work in this film, and the special effects are good but not great. I found the final fight somewhat lacking. It was also nice to have Downey along to bridge this film to the MCU with Iron Man, the MCU's linchpin. I also liked the choice to include a lot of 1980s music despite how out-of-place it is for the time. I fail to see how A Flock of Seagulls's "Space Age Love Song," which barely charted, could have much resonance with teenagers today. Unfortunately the film suffers from Marvel's SJW kick, so Peter, May, and Stan Lee are practically the only Caucasians in Queens. The ostensibly most beautiful girl in school barely rates a 3/10 (the actress who plays her mother is much better looking--perhaps the lesson is not to breed with Michael Keaton?), and despite being a senior, consents to date Peter, who's only a sophomore. "Flash" Thompson has gone from a bullying football player to an obnoxious kid of Indian extraction, and "MJ 2.0," while smart and funny, doesn't even rate a 1/10 on the attractiveness scale. Finally, I realize Happy Hogan's character has been somewhat the comic relief since Iron Man 2, but I don't see why he had to be written as such a half-assed loser. Given his dismissive handling of the cargo flight to the Avengers' upstate headquarters, one would think Stark would have fired him years ago.

history.title: Legit: Season 1
history.review_title: I wanted to like this show and just couldn't
history.text: Even with stand-up comics as good as Jefferies, TV shows featuring them have a distinct weakness: they're heavily larded with material you've already seen. Worse, Jefferies is an outstanding storyteller, and part of how effective he is on stage is how he makes you picture the events of the stories. Seeing them acted out diminishes them somehow, especially since they needed to be made "acceptable" for a cable audience, which further lessened the impact.

history.title: Legit: The Complete Season 2
history.review_title: Season 1 was weak; there should never have been a season 2
history.text: All the complaints I had about season 1 of Legit are magnified in the second season. From hearing Jefferies on the Jay Mohr podcast, his stories about working with George Lazenby were far better than Lazenby's actual work. I couldn't even finish watching the entire season before I had to give up and just get rid of the set.

history.title: Rapid Fire
history.review_title: A very good if derivative action film
history.text: Brandon Lee's only worthwhile starring turn in a martial arts film (Laser Mission just doesn't cut it, and Showdown in Little Tokyo was a buddy pic with Lee second-billed) highlights his athleticism and sarcasm. Unfortunately he never got the chance to develop into a better actor. The movie is well-cast. Somewhat sadly, the last time I got the urge to watch this movie, as soon as I turned it off I learned Powers Boothe had just died. I even liked the nod to Bruce Lee's use of the nunchaku in the laundry scene, where Brandon Lee faces a bad guy with a nunchaku and fouls it by throwing some of the laundry at it. This used to be a 5 star film for me, but ever since I saw Jackie Chan's first Police Story and saw how many stunts were taken directly from it, it ceased to be as enjoyable. I can say Pat Johnson's choreography improved since Showdown in Little Tokyo, although he kept the move where the bad guy catches Lee's leg in mid-kick, only to have Lee flip over and kick him with the other leg.

history.title: Love & Friendship
history.review_title: Soon to be a Jane Austen Classic
history.text: Kate Beckinsale, as the beautiful young widow, Lady Susan Vernon, makes you love her and despise her as she weaves her intrigues into the lives of the Manwarings, the DeCourcy's, the Charles Vernon's (her brother-in-law's family), and finally stops trying to get her daughter to marry "a blockhead". Beckinsale is formidable in this role, and the other actors do not disappoint. Jemma Redgrave and James Fleet are very believable, as always, and other actors less familiar to us were credible in their roles. We appreciated that there were no bedroom scenes -- only innuendo -- so that the viewing experience was very enjoyable and fittingly portrayed as a Jane Austen classic.

Fellowes is a gem, both as an actor (Monarch of the Glen) and his wonderful work in Downton Abbey, this work, From Time to Time, and more to come. As for Trollope, I can't think of a person who has the ability to produce both strong women and strong men at the same time and make both believable. Enjoy!!

history.title: Out of the Furnace
history.text: There were so many good actors in this movie I thought for sure it was foolproof and would be awesome. I really anticipated a great action movie. It was just okay for me. I think most of the movie was a little slow-paced, and it didn't really pick up until the end. Sadly, not soon enough though. The idea of it being loosely based on the old adage, an eye for an eye, wasn't for me either. It's been done too many times to count, so in order for it to stand out it needs to be impeccably done. The ending as I said was different and what I liked most about the film. Don't think it was because it was finally ending, though honestly, that helped too. I was over it at that point. The last of the movie was really gritty, and if you read my blog regularly, that's kinda what I'm into. I don't want fluff, I want blood and gore. What can I say?! My mom claims I should have been a boy. Will I recommend it? Probably not. I probably won't think about it again.

history.title: Birdman
history.review_title: I'm the one who didn't like it!
history.text: It's me. I just didn't enjoy it or get it, frankly. I also don't get how this film stole all the awards' (nominations - left out this word initially... sorry to the people who couldn't figure that out.) at the Oscars. I get it was a sophisticated story, but maybe too sophisticated for me. I felt the degrees of separation were just too far for my tastes. It was so hard to decipher what was real and what was fantasy. Was he crazy, suicidal or both? I feel like I will never know. In the end, I feel like this is two hours of my life I can't get back.

history.title: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
history.text: The hubby and I have both read the book. I also read Hollow City, the second book, so I have a great understanding for what the film should be about. I said after reading Miss Peregrine's that Tim Burton would be the guy to make this book come alive, and I was right! He did such a great job at creating what I had in mind for the film version of the story. The kids were so well cast, they literally blew me away. I wasn't a fan of the actress that played Miss Peregrine, but that is because, in my mind, Miss Peregrine was much older than her. Still, she played her well. I did think a couple of the scenes ended rather abruptly... and even the hubby was like, "What the hay?!" The film was a great adaption though, blending both the first and second book in the series. If you read the book, or books, then you will enjoy the movie. If you haven't, you may find it too peculiar for you. I suggest reading the book. Even if you think you won't like it. I love when people are surprised.... Then watch the movie.

history.title: Masterminds
history.text: The hubby and I had so many laughs watching this one. Based on a true story of one of the biggest heists in history, the director pulls you right in with hilarity. It took real finesse choosing how to make a serious event into a riot of laughs, but this guy did it well! A great cast of characters also helped make this film great! Zach Galifianakis is so funny, I could actually watch this one again. I was surprised by how much I enjoyed Mike McKinney too, played by Jason Sudeikis. This guy kinda stole the show for me! His part was jokes! I highly recommend watching the bloopers at the end too. Hilarious!!!

history.title: X-MEN: APOCALYPSE
history.text: Out of all the XMen movies I have seen, and I have seen most of them if not all, this was one of the best. Staying true to the comic in every way, blended with an exciting, edge-of-the-seat story line, I was hooked from the beginning. I watched it with the hubby and even he was blown away. He also thought it was better than some of the others. I can't wait to see more now! At least, provided they make them, which I'm sure they will. 4.5/5

history.title: Assassin's Creed
history.text: The hubby and I watched this together. I had seen him play the game a few times, but my knowledge of the game is slim-to-none. I didn't know the story or the characters, other than the role he played as the assassin. This is where the hubby could fill me in, knowing the game inside and out. The first thing he noticed was how much story they added to an already existing story, though that was minimal to begin with. There were a couple of moments that he was lost at what was happening, since it didn't happen in the game. It made the movie better though. The story got quite exciting, full of action, and pulled us in deep. The actors were well cast in this film too. They played the scenes well, which were also very vivid and brought it all to life. It was so interesting, even if you had no knowledge of the game or its existence. For those that know the game will agree some of the scenes are spot on! It was such a good movie!

history.title: Immortal Life of HenriettaLacks(DHD/DVD)
history.text: I wish I had read the book first, but the story in the movie was pretty epic. Henrietta is singlehandedly the reason why so many people have lived on. Her cells have been used in so many diseases, trying to combat or prevent them, that she should be cannonized. Oprah was the perfect choice as Henrietta's daughter, the reason the story is told in the first place. Her studios also paid for the film, so it is well made. Rose Bryne played a good part. She got to tell Henrietta's story. I'm so glad I've seen this. Learned her story and I still wamt to read the book too. Remember there is some emotional scenes but they make the story. 4.5/5

It was not what I was thinking at all, but in retrospect, I'm not surprised either seeing where Max comes from. It hits hard at the end. Bring some tissues for that one. Seriously. Can't wait for season 2 now!

history.text: A lame story with slow, plodding directing. Even Clive Owen could not save this sad attempt at a scary story. John Farrow's (played by Owen) young daughter, Mia, begins writing a scary story for school. At night she is being visited by a presence without a face who is trying to capture her to steal hers. (I've been a fan of his throughout his career, but this time he looked like he was phoning it in.) history.title: Sicario
history.review_title: Interesting story, great action, heart-pounding pacing! I highly recommend it!
history.text: Difficult to watch in places because of the violence but necessary to tell this story of our understaffed, under-funded FBI (with law tying their hands behind their back) fighting Mexican drug cartels. The story makes you question how far can you morally push the boundaries in the name of saving the most lives. Emily Blunt stands in for our belief that we should obey the law at all cost. Josh Brolin is tired of playing by every-changing laws limiting his ability to fight violent drug dealers who have no rules. Great story, great action and great pacing make this a movie that keeps you on the edge of your seat.

history.title: Jessabelle [DVD + Digital]
history.review_title: A FUN RIDE with creepy clues along the way, dark & dreary settings, great story & a fantastic twist at the end!
history.text: (4 1/2 stars!) Fantastic twists at the end of well-told stories are always the cherry on top for me! This was a gem (you know how difficult it is to find a really scary movie!) with appropriately dark and dreary settings and creepy clues found along the way that this story isn't just a "bumps-in-the-night" horror movie. This has very good acting, edge-of-your-seat pacing, good tense musical score, You know you are hooked when you care about the characters. I highly recommend it.

history.title: Splinter
history.review_title: A Really FUN Scary Movie…Surprisingly Well Done with Interesting Characters and an Awesome Creature!
history.text: Isn't it really hard to find a good scary movie? This little gem came out of nowhere. No well known actors or director or publicity, but is great! It starts off with a good scene, then slows, but HANG IN THERE until they get to the gas station, and you will see experience what really great character development, directing, the perfect claustrophobic setting, acting and pacing can do! This is a F-U-N, scary movie where you care about the characters, and it has an awesome monster! It's even better that it was done on a budget, and we get to see some unknown actors in a good movie for a change.

history.title: Tucker & Dale vs. Evil
history.review_title: Witty writing with hilarious situations & misunderstandings make this comedy laugh-out-loud FUNNY!
history.text: It felt SO GOOD to laugh this hard!!! Very witty writing with hilarious situations and misunderstandings make this comedy one of our FAVORITE! Tucker and Dale are two good ol' country boys who are completely misunderstood (serial killers even?) by some college kids on an outing. The kids begin to die one-by-one making the kids more certain that Tucker & Dale are pure evil. There are lines that we are repeating that can crack us up in any situation now! We highly recommend this tongue-in-cheek movie! Pure fun!

history.title: Fortitude
history.review_title: This is the most well-written, original, surprising, unpredictable, FUN show in a long time! Love it!
history.text: This is the most surprising, unpredictable, fun, adrenaline-rush of a show! It has you on the edge of your seat from the first episode of Season 1 to the very last second of Season 2. You will never be able to guess what is going to happen next. We loved the completely original writing and the well-developed characters who you either grow to love or to hate. It being set in Norway, the scenery is absolutely beautiful (wherever it was actually filmed). You might believe it to be a simple murder mystery at first but will soon find out it is so much more complicated. The story-telling is rich, the acting is first-class, and there simply HAS to be more of "Fortitude"! Warning: there are some scenes that may gross-out people who haven't seen it all before.

history.title: Megan Leavey
history.review_title: Best Movie I Have Seen in a Long, Long Time! SO well-written & acted! Gives a view of war we don't see!
history.text: This movie stuck with me long after I had seen it. It was so much more than about a bomb-sniffing dog and his trainer. There are so many of us, I think, that can relate to & understand animals better than we can with people. Megan instinctively understood Rex's needs and how to relate to him. He had been labeled as "aggressive" by the veterinarian (who would have been extremely believable as one of the more cruel Nazis in WWII). Megan came from a broken family and a narcissistic mother, so she had issues of her own. This movie showed VERY CLEARLY the fear you feel fighting in a war, how the Marines have each other's backs, what it feels like to be tossed through the air by a bomb and what the noise and compression does to you and teaches you that the heroes who save thousands of lives by sniffing out bombs for their handlers can also suffer PTSD. Well written, directed, filmed, edited and GREAT acting that captured you and didn't let go. Highly recommended.

history.title: The Grandmaster [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The films of Wong Kar-Wai, Filmmaker --
history.text: are a whole other universe. Zhang Yimou is consciously a visualist in film. Wong Kar-Wai is consciously a visualist in film. Zhang Yimou is entirely normal in substance. Wong Kar-Wai is untethered from norms, usualities, expectations, in substance. He is anomalous, progenitor of the distinctively anonymous. This is a grand film visually; a grand film substantively. A film which predicts nothing, but from which one perhaps can be expected to learn, even if that is opposed to one's hynotization to entertainment. There is an "Eastern" "philosophical" "maxim" along the lines of: The wheel is composed of an outer rim, and spokes which array the power from and to hub to rim, rim to hub. But at the center of the hub is emptiness, nothing, around which the wheel revolves. The wheel works because of nothingness. Western philosophy is outward aggression -- proof and fact. Eastern "philosophy" is a knowledge of the unknowable -- "knowing" and intuition tensioned against each other. He said, "What!?" "Nothing." This is not an action film. This is a contemplation for those who know that thought-understanding is a limitation. And all of that is speculative nonsense called (in the West) "philosophy". In prosaic terms, this film is stunning, visually, and in inferences, or impartations, from dialog. Watch and listen without getting one's analytic thinking in the way. _____ Addendum: The above is from several viewings of the 130-minute HK release bought in a brick-and-mortar. The "Martin Scorcese Presents" Blu-Ray -- that which is illustrated -- is (if the information on the box can be trusted) the 108-minute release. history.review_title: Orson Welles was an amazing man. Good horror adventure & dark occult mystery film for most ages
history.text: Orson Welles had to have been one of the finest actors alive to play the role of a movie villain. He was one of the greatest actors of his time. This character he plays way back in the 1970's is certainly one of his better dark portrayals. This movie is indeed very bizarre, still to this day in 2017, & it has been quite a lost gem over time. Basic plot: Young woman had a miscarrage, and both she and her husband find themselves in the company of what turns out to be a bizarre group of twenty and thirty somethings who form a weird witch like cult led by an even more macabe and strange but highly intelligent much older man in one Orson Welles. They soon realize at first these folks are both a neo-pagan counter culture group, and a sex cult who follow their own bizarre religion similar to that of real life whacko Englishman mystic Allister Crowley. This group is totally weird, but also it appears they are benign at first. But then the girl has mysterious dreams, nightmares, and ghoulish encounters until finally she discovers the weird frightening truth. I had generally really very much enjoyed this movie, and found Welles's performance so astonishing as this villain I would place him up there acting wise with other amazing past movie-tv show villain actors such as James Earl Jones's "Darth Vader" & "Thulsa Doom", Heath Ledger & Jack Nicholson's "Joker", Ricardo Montoban's "Khan", Robert England's "Freddy Krueger", Ian McDermand's "Palpatine", or Gary Oldman's "Dracula". This late man's performance in this very dated old film had really stuck out for me, it is that good even if the rest of the film isn't a masterpiece. The movie does have some sexual scenery, a few adult themes, a lot of nudity, and some very powerful frightening horror imagery with some mild violence but not once did this film ever cross the line into any gory or sadistic bloodletting to the R rated level of past movies such as "Halloween" or "Nightmare on Elm Street" so for me, unlike other folks who would be offended by anything, the PG rating was correct. Back in the 70's adults had rated movies, & Hollywood had no problem making both kid films and adult films unlike today where most movies are super hero CGI fests aimed only at teenagers. The film is not for very young kids but I say it would be a fun horror witch themed adventure thriller for older kids from 10 up along with teens and adults. If you enjoyed other horror thrillers which were not total monster or slasher fest films, but had good satanic and demonic imagery similar to vampire or warlock movies you might really enjoy this one like I did. A- for "Necromancy: The Witching".

history.review_title: Michael Keaton on a warpath in the action-adventure-spy thriller "American Assassin"
history.text: "American Assassin", staring one of my favorite actors Michael Keaton. And the verdict is in, its a true hit just as I imaged. The author of the books behind this new movie series had just passed away after a long ugly battle with cancer, as I had heard listening to Rush Limbaugh's radio program. The book franchise, along with the new movie series makes similar films in this action-adventure jingoistic spy genre such as the "Jason Bourne" film litterly look like pre-school material. Apparently this movie pulled the usual Hollywood stunt of barely following the book, but it still had worked for me. This is boldly a true and honest rated R movie through and through, thus I was proud to see this level of film making after many years of politically correct softened "PG-13" trash movies we have seen so much of in the 2010's. The movie is pure pro-American action-adventure "ass kicking-take NO prisoners" machinary 101 in every scene, it made me almost shout in the theater with morally patriotic glory. I had savored every minute of Keaton's team hunting down these sinister Isis bastards, & bringing them to an early grave. Plot: A renegade young guy trains his body, mind, and spirit to hunt down the Isis agents responsible for the cold blooded murder of his girlfriend. He physically trains the way I believe many American men should train. He masters the martial arts, he excells at physical fitness, learns numerous other skills, and he also becomes an expert with many firearms showing his proficancy in marksmanship. He rejects the lies of lame PC slogans such as "peace at all costs", "celebrate diversity", "guns are bad", "look out for micro agresstions", or "mutlitculturalism is the new norm", by truly understanding whom his most cruel & visicious enemy is on today's 21st Century battlefield (Holy Jihad & modern Terrorism). He celebrates multiculturalism with placing two rounds into his target's chest, and one round in it's head. The movie has NO political message but one thing is very clear, there is ZERO Left Wing crybaby rubbish in this film, which I found to be so darn refreshing. Believing the young man is insane, former old Sailor gone renegade turned into a CIA assassin Michael Keaton, is reluctant to recruit this kid but his boss believes he can be an asset for difficult spy missions hunting down the world's worst criminals & Terrorists. For this movie is truly not a usual Michael Keaton movie, we do not get the charm, the fun & humorous working class guy motiff we usually get from his much older movies like "Night Shift", "BeetleJuice", "Clean & Sober", or "Batman", no folks this Michael Keaton is a cold blooded fighting and death bringing machine with ZERO mercey whose only goal is victory over his enemies. He passes his knowledge of spy craft, and selected target acquirement onto this new lad with help from a beautiful young Middle Eastern woman. There is one minor plot hole, such as the logic behind the motivation of whom is revealed to be the true bad guy, but we do not get the lame PC message of "American Government just as evil as Isis" trash lies we usually get from Hollywood such as the "Bourne" movies. Nor do we get any superhero formula like we get with "007 James Bond". No this series is much more down to Earth, organizations such as the American Navy are properly portrayed as true heroes, the movie is much more gritty & real, and it's message is positive stating the TRUTH that there are some men in this world who are such vicious psychopaths that sometimes they must be hunted like animals in the 21st Century's "War on Terrorism", thus that war despite 17 plus years now of being waged is honestly STILL worth fighting. So I give this movie thumbs up, and a solid A-. It is one of the best I have seen this 2017 year.

history.review_title: One of DC's Masterpieces, & among the best Superhero movies ever
history.text: Fantastic action adventure superhero film. Finally we get to see Wonder Woman's origin in stunning ways, and the movie is so good it unlike other recent superhero movies which have some intense violence for realistic purposes to their plots, this movie can be seen basically by all audiences. I would rated this movie G (lame Hollywood rated the movie PG-13 , but I recommend ignoring them again, not a fan of the MPAA), even though there are a couple of viciously intese WW1 scenes of soldiers getting gased or shot, just like "Wizard of Oz" - the original "Planet of the Apes" - the orginal "Clash of the Titans", & "Star Wars" this film really is that well made that kids and adults will all enjoy it. Wonder Woman-Dianna's boyfriend and her other comrades in the film were portrayed excellently, and so are the ruthless villains along with this one character whom is acted very well based on Britain's Prime Minister Lyod George of the 1910's. Now DC really shines slowly indroducing us to a new group of amazing fantasy heroes who will compete well with Marvel's Avengers and X-men. Bring on the glory of the Justice League, for Batman and Wonder Woman are among the best super heroes ever created. I rank this movie right up there with the gold standard best next to the Caine-Nolen-Bale 2000's "Dark Knight" trilogy, Michael Keaton & Tim Burton's 1989 "Batman", 1982's "Swamp Thing", & also with 2016's phenominal adventure duel "Batman Vs Superman". I truly enjoyed the Hell out of this movie, and I think it is among 2017's absolute best films next to "American Assassin", & "Blade Runner 2049". Gal Gadot is amazing. Thumbs way up and A-.

history.title: Blade Runner 2049 (Blu-ray) (BD)
history.review_title: Better than the first film. Phenomenal Sci Fi Adventure sequel- Grade of A
history.text: It is official, the extremely long awaited sequal to "Blade Runner" is in & yes folks it is an astonishingly good movie- a true hit out of the park. "Blade Runner 2049" this year's true masterpiece movie in an entire decade of garbage Hollywood films. The special effects in this film are so amazing they blow franchises like "Jurassic Park" away, not one flaw did I observe for these effects are the most realistic I can think of in any movie or show I have seen. We also have some fine fight scenes intermixed with the drama. Over the weeks I had heard this movie was not well received here in the States, and that is ashame because it is one of 2017's best and a worthy sequal. Maybe the problem is the very long run time, and dealing with a modern American tv-movie pop culture public who has a very short "Transformers" level of an attention span. I had watched the first movie at the super young age of five, & thought it was weird back then, only to watch it again in my late 30's many years later only coming to the conclusion that the film was much more weird than I had remembered. This movie has a brand new plot element, but continues on in a major & helpful way the guidelines & plot of the original film down to every scene in fine detail. Not even "Star Wars" or "Star Trek" pays as much respect to continuity as this film does. If you are a fellow fan of tv or movies like "Aliens", "Star Wars", "Star Trek", "Batman", "Game of Thrones", "The Hobbit", & "Conan the Barbarian" you will probably like this movie franchise too thought it is much deeper. A new younger police detective (Ryan Gosling as K) is tasked with bringing down the new fugitive andriods, only to make a very odd & important discovery. A secret so powerful it could disrupt the entire planet. Later on we see this new cop eventually seek out old Detective Decker, Harrison Ford, who has been on the lame in hiding for over thirty years in a post apocolyptic Las Vegas. It appears the mysterious bad guys also want to hunt down the lost Decker, thus the old man and the new younger cop have to team up in order to survive to see if they can uncover this secret & make some form of a extreme good out of it all. It is awesome these last ten years seeing old Harrison Ford reprise what in my opinion were his three signature & best roles of his entire acting career, "Star Wars", "Indiana Jones", and "Blade Runner" three of the best movies of the 80's decade only recently getting their long awaited sequel treatment. We have a dynamic & young lovely Cuban actress who plays the role of the AI holographic girlfriend (Ana De Armas), whose performance is so strong it feels as if her character is a real emotional compelling human being. Her love for the new good guy Bladerunner is very genuine in outcome. She is an absolute credit to her island country. What is different from this new one to the old one? Besides better special effects actually not too much, the film makers stay right to the story line, tone, & themes of the original that I felt I was back watching that same exact fantasy world of a dystopian Los Angeles all over again. The old WW2 themed "film noir" feel (along with the passion intense love romance) is not as strong in the sequel, but the plot really allows for smooth transition, for you really believe as a fan that this new story does take place 40 years after the first film's world based on Phillip K Dick's " Do Andriods Dream of Electric Sheep?" sci fi novel. I rarely ever agree with the MPAA's lame rating system, this movie does have some rough violent karate-fight scenes, some dreary dark images, realistic gun battles, & a few scenes which require much more deep thought than a "Star Wars" film, but I would have rated it PG not R, because it is intense but not too bad. But the Hollywood disagreed. You be the judge folks. So again thumbs way up and the grade of an A, it is fantastic.

history.title: Victoria & Abdul [DVD]
history.review_title: Beautiful depiction of the UK's wisest, altruistic, loving, ruthless, fierce, strong, highly compassionate, & adored monarch
history.text: 2017's "Victoria & Abdul", a pop cultural melodramatic movie about real life historial characters, is a real winner for my tastes. The plot: 1880s-90's. A young Indian Muslim clerk who happens to be tall is selected to travel to the UK, with a shorter friend, to play the dress up role of the presenter of a coinage gift to the mighty high court of the UK's greatest, and longest serving, monarch Queen Victoria. She takes notice of him & enters her private world, impressing her with his extensive knowlegde, class, and charm much to the dismay of the Queen's court subjects and his fellow friend from India. A strong and deep friendship developes between this young man, and the elderly Imperial ruler that angers many in the royal court including Victoria's playboy & pompous son Edward the VII "Bertie", whom the Queen mainly blaims for the loss of her beloved famous husband Albert whom had died many decades earlier, ending the golden beloved romantic years of her marriage to that of morning and dread. Bertie along with the court's subjects including Britain's Prime Minister plot numerous schemes, in their own racial superiority & distain for the young Indian scholar, to rid him of her pressance & off the palace grounds. Judi Dench is phenominal in this role that was truly meant for her, depicting the glorious monarch in her painful last years of a reign of rule that had lasted longer than mostly any other head of state in the history of the world. And her reign had seen Britian as the largest, most powerful empire on the Earth even surpassing Rome, only coming to it's end at the end of horrific carnage of WW2. With her death, the begining of the end of world stability, civility, and chivalry had came to a bloody brutal end with her relatives losing their rock and instead plotting hostile war against each other for control of a large bulk of the world plunging humanity into slaughter house of The Great War (only followed by a conflict even more devastating with history's greatest monsters as major players). This film was at many times comical, light hearted, warm, and inviting depicting a common man in over his head among the world's elite, reminding me of movies of many years back such as 1990's "King Ralph", "The King's Speech", 1983's "Trading Places", & 2006's "The Queen". I loved the period costumes, the elogance, and the accurate depictions of grandiosity, it made me think I was back in the late 1800's. The movie was a breath of fresh air, despite many reviewers in Britain bashing the film just to push their own political agendas which in their minds seemed to not fit their ideologies. That is too bad, because we do have here in this picture high quality art. The American MPAA rating system again I find to be absolutely atrocious, for despite a couple of swear words and a few minor sexual slang words, I would have rated this film G instead of the catch all PG-13. I give this heart warming movie an A, & despite the ugliness of modern world politics, as an American it gave me much more appriciation for Great Britain as a country, and her glorious history.

history.review_title: A giant confusing mess with a great protagonist character- missed opportunity

The Brussels Detective finds himself surrounded in a "whom have done it" murder mystery plot while onboard a 1930's train traveling from the East to Western Europe during a cold winter. The film is packed with high caliber stars, yet for many reasons with the soul exception of Branagh's Poirot, which is a fine & convincing performance, the movie at least for myself in dramatic tone falls totally flat. The costumes are first rate, as are the performances along with the special effects imagery but not once had I been impressed at all with the unmoving plot, the very confusing elements portrayed as the film progresses to link the so called crime to suspects in the forms of a flash back story from years earlier just turned the movie into a mirky mess. What's worse than a great performance by the protagonist "A level" character, emerged into a screenplay plot that is as foggy as a Turkish snow storm? Well how about a really weird, pathetic, and very flat as a pancake ending to it all. I had also felt images of, my favorite horror monster of the 2010's yet again, political correctness were portrayed on screen featuring characters who would have in actual history never been placed in the roles or situations they were featured in. Another Hollywood cliche, so thumbs down for this one and D+.

history.review_title: Christmas-Holiday Delight: Drama of how it was made, just as fun as the original
history.text: The hard charging acting legend Christopher Plummer, Jonathan Pryce, & Dan Stevens star in "The Man Who Invented Christmas" a mix of a biographical story & fictional fantasy showing the emotional insperations for historical English author Charles Dickens when he wrote the one of the greatest novels of all time, "A Christmas Carol". I guess not only was the acting and dramatic effect impressive, the costume pieces, and the set elements really made you feel as if you were immersed back in Victorian - early industrial England of the 1800's. We see this Dickens more personally, his private inner demons which drive him to blend his vocabularic mastery of the English languge, together with the fantasy magically themed characters inside the mind of creativity. We are shown one of many reasons Dickens held so much personal sympothy with England's massive poor population during a hard living era for most of mankind. Each character from the story we all know and love is given his and her due treatment of their origins inside the author's mind from interaction, contemplation, thought, down to the written word onto paper. Portrayed here are Dickens own family problems, and his rough childhood growing up poor during the era of "the law of iron wages", which cause him to resent and feel some bitterness toward his elderly father. What had impressed me the most besides the beautifully told story, honestly was actor Christopher Plummer who in his late 80's approaching his 90's, is still hammering away with strength on both the stage, television, and film. For a man to work that much, and act that well of the gold standard of thespianism at his age, all one can state in amazement is the man has to superhuman. It shows us the work ethic, and high quality of professionalism many Canadian, Irish, Australian, and British actors engage in when it comes to their craft. This movie was an absolute "Holiday-Christmas" time joy to watch, and again I will go against the MPAA's, less than taken seriously anymore, rating system and give it my own rating of G, even though officially it's PG. Yet another rare film that both adults, teens, and very young children would like. A huge A-/B+ for "The Man Who Invented Christmas", for it was just as much of a joy seeing the creative process behind this world favorite as it had been reading, & watching adaptations of the story over many years.

history.review_title: Are you down with the League? The film has serious problems
history.text: My review of "Justice League" for the end of 2017: With my two days off I had taken a first look at the Christmas time holiday films, including (at least for me) the highly anticipated DC expansion movie spectacular sequal to Batman Vs Superman, Warner Brothers 2017 "Justice League". This past summer's "Wonder Woman" was a very surprising smash hit and worthy as a member of the "Batman" DC unvirse, but last year's "Suicide Squad" was not so great. Well from what I heard online, and from the noise made by critics Warner Brothers had decided to tone down the darker hard elemental tones and simply just produce a lighter more kid-teen friendly film. DC & Warner Bros were upset about the reaction to the hard lined darker B vs S, & I felt made the wrong decision by making this film lighter instead of what I believed worked perfectly before. This move might have been taken in positively by most comic book movie fans out there (in fact many fans posted happy reviews online via Youtube), but not by me because I really generally only enjoy harder more R rated themed material only rarely on occassion taking the time to see a G or PG movie. One of the reasons I had loved the 2008 - 2012 Christopher Nolan-Bale- Michael Caine trilogy along with waaaay back 1989's Michael Keaton version honestly because they were tougher, more edgy dark adult themed movies. Thus unlike EVERYONE else on planet Earth, maybe lets say ten other human beings who saw the film, I was one of the very few who really enjoyed the Hell out of 2016's "Batman Vs Superman" minus the Doomsday character scene. So yes this movie is lighter, but that does not mean it is not enjoyable because at the end of the day it is still a decent film (but could have been much better). Quick synopsis, a few years after the events of "B Vs S" about half the Earth's population morns Superman. Batman-Bruce Wayne played again by Ben Affleck, has been waiting for the time when his theory of creepy alien invaders will attack Earth. One night in a roof top fist fight with an ugly street thug city robber, his theory is proven correct and he has to get his plan into gear of searching, finding, meeting, and bringing together the world's superheros into one team. We learn that Wonder Woman lives her new life as an art restorer on the other side of the Atlantic ocean in England or France, (across from Bruce Wayne who still fights crooks in Gotham IE we assume Jersey City-New York). When, what I guess are, a crew of well dressed gunmen bank robber-Terrorists attack London, she is called into action as her true superhero self. (If these dudes are bombers then why go to the trouble of robbing the bank with AR-15s? But I guess that does not matter). One thing that I found a bit frustrating, & maybe this was done on purpose, but we still do not know who Wonder Woman romantically will get involved with. We had slight hints that maybe she does find Batman-Bruce Wayne attractive (but they also have heated arguments), but we then noticed scenes where she was very attracted to Superman, and even our new hero Arthur Curry the Atlantian Marine named Aquaman has his own crush on her plus vice versa. Well Gal Godet's character has three masculine handsome studs to pick from. I wanted to see something more than what was given to us. So thus the plot comes together & the team forms to save Earth. The special effects work very well, action stunt sequences are pretty first rate, but the film does have some problems namely, at least in my humble opinion, a very lame and weak villain (ugly blueish very tall guy with an axe & falcon helmut). I felt this villain's origins were weak, cheesy, too cartoonish, & I never once understood how he & his insect like shock troops traveled appearing out of the sky from no where as if he had a cosmic time warp key or a wormhole device. The Cosmic Cube, or the All Spark, box things were also a complete copy of "Transformers" and did not move the plot convincely enough. Nothing is technically explained well enough in regards to this villain nor his technology, & his rationale was not very moving nor intersting. His insect alien soldiers were very video game like, easily shot with a space rifle or punched in the face a few times where they splatter into green goo. At the end I do think Nolan's trilogy (2007-2012), Tim Burton's first 1989 movie, B Vs S of 2016, & this past summer's "Wonder Woman" are much better films, the movie is still watchable. I also personally did not care for in the least the "Flash" character, he is the comic relief & he is popular with fans but he was just not cool enough to be on the equal stage with my boy Batman-Bruce Wayne, or my new homegirl Wonder Woman. He in my view really sucked and brought the film down, but not as much as the loser villain had. These parts of the film could have been written better, but over all the effects are great, the costumes are pretty darn fantastic, the artistic imagery is in the golden age of comic books, and the action sequences do play out nicely enough for me to give this movie a solid C with neither thumbs up nor thumbs down, only yet another so so movie that could have been a thousand times better.

history.text: Roger Ebert wrote a very bad review of this movie. That is one of the reason I like this movie so much. Ebert thought that he could pan this based upon the fact that it could not be understood. In telling us it could not be understood, Ebert's review is exposed as just the reprehensibility critics can stoop to. The movie provides the answers to what is going on as they are revealed by an investigation. Now, anyone who has ever done real criminal investigation knows that it takes a bit of brain power to unravel the mystery, the data that is hidden, twisted data and the lies and irrelevant data that comes one's way during an investigation. So, for Ebert to have said what he said means he didn't apply himself to figuring it out whatsoever. But more than that, Ebert, got lost himself. The movie lays it all out. Those who apply themselves to the mystery know they had to listen, spot the contrary data, the lies, and understand as the movie went on that the plot twists Ebert disliked so much were simply revelation points of usable data, sign posts so to speak, on the way to successfully solving the puzzle. This movie was quite clever, completely sequitur and actually followed all the steps in dialogue and events to allow the movie goers to solve the plot of the movie. Ebert, in my opinion was a joke as a critic and his review of this movie tells us more about Ebert than he would have liked for us to know. I recommend this movie to anyone who likes to exercise his gray matter and be entertained while doing. The movie is actually a very good primer in Basic investigation practice. Every actor in the movie did a fine job; and the direction was flawless as was the writing.

history.title: Double Indemnity
history.text: A superfically perfect noir thriller with flaws that are not immediately noticed by the viewer. The first flaw is that Walter goes for double indemnity on Dietrichson. This is sure to make the insurance company suspicious. The second flaw is that Lola, the daughter, is brought in like a deus ex machina to discredit Phyllis and wise Walter up to her real personality. The third flaw is that Nino Zachetti, Lola's boyfriend is brought in as a fall guy that both Phyllis and Neff want to take the fall for the murder. So the basic characters, Walter, Phyllis and her husband, were not enough to fill out the plot. Wilder and his writers had to bring in more characters whose role is dubious, when we consider that Walter and Phyllis kill Dietrichson, Phyllis shoots Walter, Walter murders Phyllis, and is caught by Barton Keyes. Lola and Zachetti are clumsily brought in to hold the structure together, and the result is the opposite. They make the movie seem contrived. Edward G. Robinson as Barton Keyes is the real glue that holds the movie together. His implacable intelligence, his growing suspicions weave a web around Walter and Phyllis that ultimately destroys them. Finally, I wonder what the censors thought about the fact that Nino Zachetti was having sexual relations with both Lola Dietrichson and her mother. I suspect there was trouble. What redeems the movie is the mood, the great acting, the complexity, which allow us to sit back and enjoy it without thinking about the flaws. It was not a box office success, but it is a classic.

history.title: Alien(Spanish)
history.text: This movie could almost be seen as a comedy. "An alien life form -- let me reach out and touch it!" Then they bring it into the ship with only Sigourney Weaver protesting. It has covered Kane's face and breathing for him. "Let's cut through one of its arms!" The acid penetrates several decks of the ship. Now that they finally realize it's dangerous, "Let's go after it with a butterfly net!" Possibly the stupidest scene is Harry Dean Stanton looking for the cat while the monster stalks him. "Here, kitty kitty kitty.." Unintentionally funny. In the end, of course, they all die. Except Sigourney Weaver, who does an effective strip-tease in the shuttle before realizing the alien is in the shuttle with her. Using clever controls of vents, she blows the monster out into space, and says into the radio, "This is Ripley, the last survivor of the Nostrum, signing off." This one scene is watchable.

history.title: Grand Illusion
history.text: In the Truffaut biography, someone said of Renoir, "He can make an armoire talk." Renoir was very proud of this, and indeed his genius consists in humanizing things we don't usually think of as animate. What I admire most in his best films is that you can feel the air in the room with the characters. The air is alive. There are many riches here, such as the soldiers dressing up as women in a musical comedy and the audience looking on in awe because all the soldiers are celibate. The tenderness and respect shown to Boildieu by the wounded Von Stroheim, burns all over his body, his spine broken, is very touching. Yet Renoir said of the movie, "That damned Grande Illusion ruined my career!" The movie typecast him and he couldn't make the films he wanted to make. Some call this the greatest movie ever made. I don't think so, it's too local, too specific. But it is a great movie, delightful to watch.

history.title: Fast, Cheap and Out of Control
history.text: After much thought, I realized that the subject of this lyrical documentary is behavior: the behavior of the lions, the behavior of the mole rats, the behavior of the robots, the behavior of the trees Ray Mendonça is trimming. But Erroll Morris is making a more subtle point: the behavior always threatens to elude Man's attempts to control it. From this we get the title "Out of Control." The protagonists relish the challenge they face, and are optimistic. Toward the end they begin to reflect on what will happen when they're gone. Will carbon-based life be replaced by silicone-based life? A tender mood ensues. But Caleb Sampson's end-title music is brave, forging into the future, but always with a touch of humor. "Boys and girls, count backward with me!" Says the ringmaster as the man is about to to be shot out of a cannon. To me, nothing Morris ever did compares to this quixotic fantasy.

history.title: Kiss of the Spider Woman
history.text: What hurts this movie is Arreghi's incomprehensible credulity. As a political prisoner he would immediately suspect that his homosexual cellmate is a spy, chosen precisely for his homosexuality. But Arrreghi alternates between spouting political slogans and berating his cellmate for failing to face reality. The pot is calling the kettle black. What saves the movie is that they both die. Arreghi is tortured to death while Molina, in a fine irony, is killed by insurgents because of his love for Arreghi. He is not politicized, he is a man in love with another man.

history.title: Dark Passage (Keepcase)
history.text: This is an underrated, highly symbolic noir classic. Throughout the movie Lauren Bacall functions as Bogart's mother and protector, though she is visibly young enough to be his daughter. This is nowhere more evident than when she removes the bandages from his plastic surgery. She is literally giving birth to him as a new person, a person she can love. Memorable is the metamorphosis engineered by Tom D'Andrea and his plastic surgeon friend. The only flaw in the structure is the 35 minutes that go by without us seeing Bacall at all. Bogart has to overcome his enemies, the most important being the feline, sibillant Agnes Moorhead (the real villain in the plot), before he can reunite with Bacall in another country. Very well made.

history.title: Female Pervert
history.review_title: Spoiler Alert (She Also Has a Theremin)
history.text: This movie is unusual. It's unpredictable. I wish I knew someone who is like the main character and that I was close friends with her. She's great. Why can't I ever meet anyone like that? There's not really a plot with a beginning, middle and an end. It's more of a "slice of life" look at her. We see her hanging out with friends, at meetings with her therapist, at work, and on a couple of dates. She develops a video game involving the removal of men's body hair. She works on a campaign to improve some company's image with the involvement of female refugees from Iraq who have moved to Sweden (because Americans like Sweden). This also somehow involves Japan (because we also like Japan). It's very funny. So far as the DVD is concerned, there are no subtitles in any language, and the only special feature is the trailer.

history.title: The Assassin
history.text: This is not an action movie. It is described as a martial arts movie, but that is misleading. There are only a few action/fight scenes. It's a great movie. This may be Shu Qi's best performance. The cinematography is fantastic. The story is good, but you have to pay attention! The exclamation point is there because this is a subtle, quiet movie. The plot points are not always obvious. Many people have given this poor reviews because it did not meet their expectations. They expected action. No one should ever watch a movie with any expectations, but with an open mind.

history.title: Ab-Normal Beauty
history.text: This movie contains character actions which drive me right up the wall. Only in fiction are people too stupid to call the police when in such situations. The main character receives a videotape of a young woman being beaten to death. She shows it to her best friend/lover. They choose not to call the police! They decide it's just someone playing a joke! I can't stand it. These things happen all the time in bad movies - people making such stupid choices in such situations. The movie is never scary or suspenseful or thrilling as the director says he intended. It's just annoying. The two leads are very good and very good-looking, but they are wasted in a very dumb story. I wish the filmmakers would read this review so they could see how dumb they were when they wrote this.

history.title: Red Pill, The
history.text: This is one of the best documentaries I've ever seen. I was almost scared to watch it because I was a little familiar with the subject matter and worried about the painful issues that are addressed in the movie. The way she tells it and shows it works quite well. The people who appear in the film in support of men's rights know what they're talking about and the naysayers who appear in the film reveal their ignorance and bias. Why don't they want equal rights for everyone? Is it because they honestly believe their own lies? The film should be seen by everyone.

There is an element of mystery as the identity of the man who can become the living embodiment of a long-dead pirate is not revealed until near the end. The cast was good, though I would have liked to have seen Linda Stirling doing more. She does get involved in some of the action: she flies a plane now and then, and is involved in some of the shooting.

history.title: The Bob Newhart Show: The Complete Second Season
history.review_title: A LACKLUSTER 2ND SEASON AFTER THE GREAT 1ST SEASON
history.text: The first season is a hilarious, warm, endearing, and timeless comedy. The chemistry is great and the stories are well done. This 2nd season feels like nothing more than an experimental money grab. Hey, let's try a bunch of things that do not work and coast through on the good will of what came before. The inclusion of Bob's sister Ellen is one of the most gratuitous additions in the history of television. Most of the time, this season has no resemblance to the show we have come to know and love. The tone is different and the characters are only the same at the threadbare basics. If one didn't know better, they could assume they was watching an entirely different show. There are a few diamonds here but you will have to dig past the muck and the slime to get to them. Two episode with his patients The Last Tv Show and the one where Bob raises his rates are wonderful. So is the christmas episode which exudes the warmth of the first season. Most of the rest are a lost cause. A big slump in the series.

history.title: G.I. Joe Series 2: Season 2
history.review_title: Better than the First Season but Not Better than the Dragonfire Special
history.text: The Dragonfire Special gave Cobra Commander some really witty and character based lines. The first season did this as well. This 2nd season does not feature this. Not only do they do away his blue and white snazzy battlesuit but they also butcher his dialogue down to insults and commands, nothing more. He is back to his blue outfit with the hood but is still voiced by the virtuoso Chris Latta. Many of the characters that were absent from the first season return for this season. The Baroness's voice actress does not return for the 2nd season despite always doing the voice before. The best characters this season are General Hawk, Scarlet, Snake Eyes, Storm Shadow, Cobra Commander, and Night Creeper leader. The two best episodes involve Scarlet and the brotherhood of Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow(now a good guy). These standout episodes are The Sword and Shadow of a Doubt. The Sword in particular stands out as flawless. The anti-drug episode The Greatest Evil, also stands out due to its tone and subject matter.

history.title: Glam
history.review_title: The Most Un-Feel Good Feel Good Movie
history.text: William Mcnamara stars as Sonny, a mute who loves to write, stare off into space, and see random visions about things he can't know about yet. Sonny's mother dies and after a spoon forehead test and a warning about the violence of guns, Sonny heads off to LA to visit his cousin played by Frank Whaley. His cousin repeats most of the things he says like ten times in a row. Jon Cryer plays a drug addict while Tony Danza plays a jerk. A retarded guy likes corn dogs. Vulgar profanity is common. Characters repeat lines over and over. After a series of events that make little sense, it all culminates in Sonny giving a heartwarming hug to his cousin at his time of his greatest vulnerability and everyone learns the value of the word her. If this sounds interesting to you, check this movie out.

history.title: 20 Fairy Tales: Scholastic Storybook Treasures: Classic Collection
history.review_title: Great Adaptations of Classic Fairy Tales
history.text: Weston Woods is at it again with 20 animated shorts based on particular storybook versions of classic fairy tales. There are four standout shorts on this set. The Three Little Pigs, Little Red Riding Hood, Goldilocks and the Three Bears, and Doctor De Soto. This version of the Three Little Pigs is written and illustrated by James Marshall and the animation reflects this superbly. This is the english version of the story also used in Richard Scarry that effectively adds suspense by the wolf devising three plans to try and catch the third pig: one involving turnips, another with apples and a third with the county fair. I know some of you remember this reiteration. Little Red and Goldilocks are also faithfully reproduced in animated form in the proud Morton Schindel tradition. Goldilocks has a great script adaptation by Gene Deitch and is directed by Milan Klikar. Academy Award nominee Doctor De Soto features great narration, animation and music. Hansel and Gretel is good as well.

history.title: Where the Wild Things Are...and 5 More Stories by Maurice Sendak
history.text: This DVD contains 5 animated shorts based on the works of maurice Sendak. Contents: Where the Wild Things Are, In the Night Kitchen, Pierre, Chicken Soup with Rice, One was Johnny, Alligators All Around. BONUS FEATURES- Getting to Know Maurice Sendak, optional read-a-long, Where the Wild Things are in alternative languages, and a trailer for Scholastic in general. Gene Deitch does a good job directing WTWTA and ITNK. Gene once said the proudest moment of his career was during the production of WTWTA when Maurice Sendak dropped by the studio and couldn't tell the difference between his drawings and theirs. Three of the other four cartoons were quite good. The weak link being Alligators All Around. I can't get Carole King's compositions for 1 was Johnny and Pierre out of my head. I Read Chicken Soup with Rice in School and was pleasantly suprised by King's unique interpretation. GTK Maurice Sendak is an insightful bonus feature where Sendak explains his writing process how WTWTA and ITNK came about, and more.
