history.title: Scooby-Doo in Arabian Nights (Repackage)
history.review_title: The Second Best Scooby Doo Movie After Boo Brothers
history.text: I received this film in the mail today and watched it. I have wanted to see this film ever since watching a three minute clip from it on youtube. I love the character designs used in this movie. Shaggy and Scooby look radically different in this incarnation but in a good way. They finally found the middle ground: not as superbly designed as Where are You but infinitely better than the nauseatingly amateurish stylings of A Pup Named Scooby Doo. This ties with Boo Brothers concerning great vocal talent. Casey Kasem gives his most enthusiastic and distinctive voiceover for Shaggy during his career. Charlie Adler is even tolerable here as a psychotic captain. The sound effect design is the best of all the franchise and the music is definitely some of the best they have ever used as well. The ink paint team did great with their broad outlines and flat colors. Kudos to the background department for their minimalist UPA inspired designs. The film boasts a witty script despite the first story being too long.

history.title: Friday the 13th, Part V: A New Beginning
history.review_title: The Best in the Friday Series
history.text: John Shepherd stars as an older version of Tommy Jarvis in this fifth installment of the franchise. This time, it's a mystery as to who the killer is. Is it Jason Voorhees back from the grave or is it Junior doing his mother's wishes of getting rid of the whole lot at the halfway house? Could it be Roy, a man seeking vengeance for the death of his son or is it our hero Tommy, finally snapping after years of Jason related Trauma? Director Danny Steinmann does the best he can with the premise and dishes up a plethora of good scenes with some truly great actors. John Shepherd's method acting came to great use in this film and I could truly believe he was this traumatized adolescent. All his mannerisms were spot on. Other great performances were given by Jerry Pavlon as stutterer Jake, Melanie Kinnaman as Pam, and Shavar Ross as Reggie the Reckless. I even liked the hillbilly mother and son duo. The best death involved a tree and a leather strap.

history.title: Penitentiary
history.text: Other reviews have already attested to the Greatness of the original "Penitentiary," and there is little I can add; this movie is so unbelievably well-made, written, edited and acted, that it remains one of the absolute BEST prison movies of ALL TIME. I can't think of a movie that has such a perfect balance of jaw-dropping action/fight scenes, comedy that is truly funny, and even drama that comes across as totally sincere. "Penitentiary" delivers on all levels. i just wanted to comment on the Xenon' dvd; it is the one to get. The print looks great, with a sharp image and bright, saturated colors. Those who are used to their old VHS versions of this title will be very pleased. The picture is presented in it's original 1;85 aspect ratio, so you get the full picture, with nothing missing. The dvd is non-anamorphic, but that is not a big deal. When using the zoom feature on your 16x9 tv's, the picture will fill the screen perfectly. The Xenon dvd even offers a directors commentary track. I can't recommend this edition enough

history.title: Penitentiary 2
history.text: One of the absolute WORST sequels of all time. It's sad, because the original "Penitentiary" from 1979 is one of the finest prison films and boxing films ever made. So what happened here? don't waste your time; just watch the first one and pretend this thing doesn't exist..

history.title: Black Candles / Evil Eye
history.text: In this twin pack you get a demonic double feature, from 2 different decades; the cool, stylish 70's, and the tacky, tasteless 80's. It's sad that most reviewers here have praised the 80's movie, "Black Candles," simply because it is loaded with wall-to-wall sex, nudity and perversion. This is most definitely the weaker title. "Evil Eye," aka "Malocchio" however, is a highly enjoyable, warped giallo from the greatest decade of exploitation/grindhouse cinema; the 1970's. Starring the cult movie icon/sex symbol Jorge Rivero, this is actually the sexier of the two movies, even though the sex in this one is not very graphic, compared to the soft porn "Black Candles," which is an artless mess. "Evil Eye" has not gotten the same remastering treatment here, but it is such a rare and obscure title that I'm happy it has been made available in any shape. Recommended for fans of darker Italian 'giallos' with the supernatural twist, like "All the colors of the Dark." "Black Candles" is a fairly poor film, that resembles a lot of the soft core stuff they used to show on late night cable tv. A good idea would be to buy the set for "Evil Eye," then sell the other disc to some amorous 16 year old boy, whom is the age group that "Black Candles" will mostly appeal to..

history.title: L'amour Dangereux
history.text: Sweet love story, with some beautiful location photography. This was a blind buy for me, meaning i had never seen the film, but like the actor Nicolas Cazale's work in some other French films. The story concerns an Algerian boy who gets in trouble with the law, and goes on the run with the beautiful daughter of his boss. It is a story that has been told before in films like "Guncrazy" with drew Barrymore, but "L'amour Dangereux" re-tells it without any exploitative elements, such as unnecessary graphic violence or sex. This is a very French production, supposedly made for French television, which is surprising, as it looks good enough for the big screen. I am happy to have discovered this film..

history.title: The Brute and the Beast
history.text: The Wild East release of this seminal Italian Western, "The Brute & the Beast," AKA "Massacre Time," is worth the price. It offers a good widescreen print, although not a lot of 'restoration' seems to have been done, as the colors seems a bit washed out. You get a choice of 2 different English dubs, and the updated voice-over is actually an improvement over the standard, original dubbing. But it's nice to have the option of choosing whichever you prefer. The cover art is pretty great as well. This is one of three Westerns director Lucio Fulci did during the 1960's. the others being "Four of the Apocalypse" and "The Silver Saddle." I definitely recommend "Four of the Apocalypse" if you like "The Brute..." but you can skip "Silver Saddle;" it's a huge letdown.

history.title: Cathy's Curse
history.text: This new restoration from 'Severin' offers a stunning new print of a movie that, up until recently had only been available in horrible, washed out, blurry and orange colored copies. Now the bright, saturated colors pop, and the blood is redder, and missing scenes have been restored that give the story a more natural flow. Beware of certain sellers here who are still selling those awful poor quality editions. Make sure you get the version from Severin films. As far as the film itself goes, i do not understand why it is so maligned here. "Cathy's Curse" is a truly creepy, tightly paced and atmospheric "grindhouse" classic. This film manages to achieve that gothic, eerie feel that many horror movies fail to deliver. This is a possession tale, of a little girl who's body and soul are slowly being taken over by another little girl, who was burned alive when the car she was in crashes one night. Every character in this film seems a little off, and there is a frantic, crazy energy from beginning to end. Featuring many "WTF" moments like little children using foul language and bursts of outrageous surreal imagery. I'm sure fans of Italian horror from the 1970's will really appreciate "Cathy's Curse," while those into more traditional Hollywood-style horror will be repelled by this exercise in weird cinema.

history.review_title: A Five Star Movie Ruined Because of Poorly Done Ending - Beware Spoilers
history.text: This remarkable tale was beautifully done and well acted. Some editing of the facts was necessary if the story was to be condensed into a feature length film, so I didn't mind that a lot was left out. But for it all to make sense, the screenplay really did need to follow the story to it's conclusion, because it was Effie's victory against all odds that made this historically important. This movie follows her suffering to the point where she decides to leave her husband, but doesn't show the happiness that came to her in the years that followed. The strange case of Effie Gray and John Ruskin is one of the most heart wrenching true stories I know of. This movie has an interesting take on this tale, and the costumes and scenery are beautifully done. I didn't mind the slow pacing because it is mainly about the silent, claustrophobic suffering of this unfortunate girl who found herself at the mercy of an unloving older husband and unspeakably cruel in-laws. Dakota Fanning's portrayal of a teenaged bride who it trapped in the clutches of Victorian hypocrisy and injustice is riveting. This would have been a 5 star movie for me, except it stopped short of the end. Victorian laws could be utterly unjust to some women and there were those who never found a way out. Effie Gray wasn't alone in her plight because many lives were ruined during this time period. Effie's story is remarkable - not because of her suffering - but because she found the courage to stand up for herself and (against all odds) succeeded in escaping her horrific marriage and experiencing a second marriage that was happy and loving. Doesn't anyone understand how absolutely RARE this outcome was???? Why was most of it left out? I found it frustrating, that after I suffered along with her through the tortures of her union with Ruskin, the movie ends suddenly without ever allowing me to witness her ultimate victory and the happiness that she found. It would have only taken another 10-15 minutes for a satisfying conclusion and I saw no reason to leave the viewers without a some kind of closure that would allow them to leave the theater feeling like this dreadful tale had been resolved - especially when (in real life), that happy ending actually did happen for Effie. Why was it left out? This failure reduced an otherwise wonderful movie to a frustrating waste of time.

history.title: GARBAGE WARRIOR
history.review_title: Earthships are a Great Start to Find Alternative Housing, but This Movie Lacks the Other Side of the Story
history.text: I have always hated waste and so the notion of "Earthships" is intriguing to me. However this movie leaves some things to be desired. It is difficult to watch this without being blood boiling angry at the injustice of "authorities" who abuse their power and squelch people who are trying to explore cheaper and better ways to build housing. The folks in this community have some truly innovative ideas that deserve to be explored and perfected. I am convinced that we haven't even scratched the surface of what is possible in the area of sustainable off-grid living and in this day and age it is unconscionable that this kind of architecture is being suppressed by those who should be supporting it. Having said that, I feel that this movie is very one-sided in the way it presents the story. After watching this, I was thrilled with the amazing and simple ideas that seem to work so great, and there is truly some good ideas here. I was so inspired that I looked further into the possibilities and found out that building homes from garbage has some inherent problems - not the least of which is that discarded tires are made of potentially toxic materials, and when used as the main matrix of a structure, they emit toxic gasses that can make people who live in these buildings very, very sick. It might not be an issue for everyone, but it isn't a healthy environment for those who are sensitive. And for people who are prone to cancer, it can be deadly. Not to mention that many of these homes have failed to live up to their initial promise - some leaking, some too hot, some too cold and others that have been disappointing in a number of other ways. Also, the low cost promise doesn't always pan out as expected. When done right, these houses end up being as costly as their traditional counterparts - and being experimental, the potential loss if it doesn't work out is enormous. So, on the one hand, there are "powers-that-be" who are committed to the status quo and might even have something to lose if better housing can be made more efficiently at a lower cost. There is a huge architectural and building industry that will fight tooth and nail to protect their own special interests. On the other hand these housing pioneers are creating buildings that are far from proven for their long term structural viability and health implications. I do wish we had freedom in this country to proceed with experimental projects like this. The lack of it holds us back in a day and age when this kind of innovation is most needed. However, as in all experimental projects, we need a balanced view and the ability to go into it with eyes wide open.

history.title: POV: Lost Boys of Sudan [DVD]
history.text: This is one of the most heart wrenching stories of the past 100 years and I was surprised at how much of what happened was glossed over or lightly touched upon in this documentary. This particular version is not the whole story and doesn't do justice to what these boys endured. As a "culture shock" story, it is fine, but it starts in the middle - at the refugee camp and doesn't adequately explain why and how they got there why these boys were being sent to the USA in the first place. This is not about Sudanese men emigrating to the USA, but a horror story of genocide and survival against all odds. It is always interesting to see people adjusting to a new culture and a new home, but the brutal truth of THE LOST BOYS OF SUDAN is barely touched upon here. For a more complete story watch the documentary, GOD GREW TIRED OF US: https://amazon.com/God-Grew-Tired-John-Bul/dp/B000R8YC22/ref=sr_1_9?ie=UTF8&qid=1468809495&sr=8-9&keywords=god+grew+tired+of+us+book OR Watch the feature length film based on this story, THE GOOD LIE, starring Actors: Reese Witherspoon, Arnold Oceng, Ger Duany, Emmanuel Jal, Kuoth Wiel: https://amazon.com/Good-Lie-Blu-ray-Reese-Witherspoon/dp/B00K2CI0HG/ref=sr_1_2?ie=UTF8&qid=1468809612&sr=8-2&keywords=The+good+lie As for this documentary, it just isn't a full account of the Lost Boys of Sudan.

history.review_title: This Movie Drug Me Down. I'd Rather Watch Something That is Uplifting and Builds Hope.
history.text: This movie was one of the most boring and pretentious flicks I have ever watched. It had Meryl Streep and I think she is a marvelous actress. But sometimes even the best will choose a dud. I'm not sure what I was supposed to get from this. At first, it seemed to have potential and I kept watching because it looked like an interesting story that was going to resolve in a satisfying manner. But no. It dragged on and on, getting more depressing with every scene, until by the end all the hope was drained away and all we were left with was grief and despair. I guess it was supposed to be "deep" but I just found it to be full of wallowing in the sorrows of life with the final message that there is no way out. This was just too sad for me. I don't watch movies to be mired in sadness and defeat. Real life can be tough and wise people try to find ways to rise above it. When I see a movie, I want something that will uplift my spirits, not something that will drag me down. If you are the "philosophical" type who likes to meditate on human misery, then you might like this. As for me, I think there are better and wiser ways to fill my mind.

It was a real shame when the tv series ended, but happily, periodic Made For TV Movie episodes are still being produced. I’m not sure why TV shows have descended to the level that we all too often see aired, and sometimes programs that are well meaning and wholesome are not always the best quality. SIGNED, SEALED, DELIVERED has the best of both worlds - it is a first rate professionally done series, without the nasty underbelly that gives rise to some shows that dominate mainstream TV programming these days. Highly enjoyable, entertaining and something you wouldn’t be uncomfortable watching with your grandmother, your children or your pastor. EDITED TO ADD: Since another Amazon customer asked about closed captioning, I will add this comment about closed captioning on the DVD that I purchased: Yes, the DVD does have a closed caption option. I don’t know what SDH subtitles are, but the closed captions are large, clear and easy to read. Since I didn’t watch the whole video with closed caption enabled, I am not sure if it is accurate throughout the whole DVD, but what I saw seemed perfect and easy to use. The only thing that bothered me was that the captions are not at the bottom of the picture screen, but plastered in the middle of the screen so that it covers up some of the action of the film and sometimes it even covers the actors’ faces. It isn’t too bad, because the caption boxes are translucent and you can see through them. It is distracting, though.

history.review_title: Lame Plot, Wooden Acting, and the Dumbest Scenery I Have Ever Laid My Eyes On
history.text: This wasn’t my favorite movie. I really wanted to like it but the screenplay, the actors, the director and ESPECIALLY the scenery and cinematography grated on my very last nerve. The acting was lame and the storyline was trite and unbelievable. The only interesting thing about it was getting a close-up look at Meghan Markle. I’ve never seen suits, and this is the first exposure I’ve had to her acting skills. She’s real pretty, but if this is an example of her acting skills, I am not really impressed. I think being a royal duchess will suit her much better than this and I hope it works out for her. PROCEED WITH CAUTION!!! SPOILERS AHEAD!!! I can’t hold Meghan Markle entirely responsible though, because nobody could make this inane character come to life and no actor, no matter how good, could redeem this cheesy and far-fetched movie. The acting was bad, but the whole premise (of a woman who is dumb enough to drop a man she loves in favor of a cold fish that fits a “wish list” in a handbook) just made me cringe. Talk about being out of touch with your feelings!!!! It was like fingernails on a chalkboard. I’d love to see the actress who could make this character sympathetic. Of the two male leads, one was an absolute caricature with not a single attractive thing about him - a dead soul and a creepy persona. How she could have even accepted even a first date with this dud is beyond me. Especially when she had already met Mr. RIGHT. The smug sister made me want to scream. There were two characters that were even remotely likable to me and that was the mother and the second male lead (Mr. Right.) Now, have you noticed that I am not using any of the characters’ names???? There is a reason for that. It is because this movie was so deadly boring that I can’t remember any of the characters’ names! I can barely remember the plot! And I only watched this day before yesterday. But the thing that is really, REALLY so irritating is the setting and scenery. They made a big, BIG deal about this story happening in Denver. And to beef up that illusion, there was a plethora of fake, painted MOUNTAIN scenery, stuck in everywhere there was a place to cram it in. The pictures were beautiful, but they were so obviously fake that it was jarring. The worst part is this: DENVER, COLORADO IS NOT IN THE MOUNTAINS, PEOPLE!!!! I live in Colorado and I have been to Denver. It is a beautiful city with some very distinctive landmarks. However, mountains are not part of the picture unless you look way into the distance where you can see the Rocky Mountains looming from far away. The city of Denver is at an elevation of 5280 feet altitude - 1 mile high. It is an area known as The High Plains. The Rocky Mountains range from 9,000 feet altitude to a staggering high of more than 14,000 feet altitude - almost 3 miles high. The mountain elevations are 2.5 times higher than Denver and to get to them from the city would take a 1 - 4 hour drive - depending on where you are going. If this story had been set in Breckinridge, Vail or Aspen, or EVEN Salt Lake City, Utah, I could have overlooked the obvious painted scenery, and just let my imagination enjoy the illusion. But to set this story in Denver and try to pull of such a fake tale is mind boggling and it makes the folks responsible seem pretty ignorant. The real stinker was not the horrible plot or the wooden acting. It was the dumb, dumb scenery. I just couldn’t believe my eyes. So there you have it. Not a good movie at all. From all the other reviews, I have to realize that I am standing alone in this, but I can’t help it. Hallmark can do so much better than this bomb.

history.title: Anne of Green Gables: A New Beginning
history.review_title: Disturbing false account of Anne's life before Green Gables
history.text: I was extremely disappointed in this movie! Not only is it disturbing, but it is not true to the Anne stories written by Montgomery. The story line just makes your head spin, and you keep waiting for things to be "straightened out".....but they never are. Not only does this story completely deviate from what Montgomery tells us of Anne's past (I suppose the writer of this film just took liberties, and used the Anne fame and the fame of his previous Anne movies, to get away with this writing).....but it even ruins the way you look at Anne. If THIS is what Anne was really like - I want no part of her!!! A very disturbed girl that manages to get away with incredible lies, and to use the lies to get the things she wants......this is a far cry from Montgomery's Anne. When this movie arrived, my whole family could not wait to start watching it - we settled in with popcorn, and prepared to enjoy the evening. Instead, we all sat painfully in stiffness throughout the entire movie - speechless - and hoping we were not seeing what we were - and not understanding what we were seeing.......and then we all left the room agitated, and with sick feelings in the pit of our stomachs ........PLEASE stay away from this movie!!! And at best, rent it if you must see it......but please review it before you let youngsters watch - it has little or no moral value lessons in it, and will leave you confused and angry......and could even convince young children to take up lying as a method of getting what they want - or as a means to drown theirselves in denial!!! "A New Beginning" is an appropriate sub-title for this movie - Sullivan has completely given Anne a "new" beginning (she's teetering on the brink of insanity here folks).....and TOTALLY different from what Montgomery would have given her!!! The original three movies by Sullivan of Anne (Green Gables, Avonlea, Continuing Story) are wonderful six star films - beautifully done, with excellent acting, and heartwarming characters that make you want to live life to the fullest and believe in your dreams - watch them all! Even if they deviate from the books, they are still wonderful family viewing (even my husband enjoys them). But this movie is just terrible.......stay clear of "A New Beginning"!!!!!

history.title: Force Majeure
history.review_title: Pay little or no attention to those who had no ability to understand the film's point.
history.text: It's unfortunate that the average American watched this film and complained as if nothing happened. European cinema puts simple ideas on screen and then asks the characters in the story to deal with them, unlike American films which decided decades ago to use sound and visual effects in place of story and storytelling, asking nothing except reaction from character and audience alike. The central conflict involves a morality play - do you save yourself, or do you save your loved ones in the event of an emergency? Is there a correct answer? Is it unmasculine? Is it unmotherly? Is it inhumane? These are the questions put forth to a family on vacation in the mountains, who must deal with the consequences of choices made by instinct in the moment. Even more, the film doesn't shy away from the uncomfortable humor of the scenario or its aftermath, even as the family tears itself apart. If your far more used to turning your brain off for 2 hours, look elsewhere. If you're opening to questioning yourself and the ones you love, watching with you, enjoy this fascinating dark comedy and discover something about who you are underneath it all, and pity those who tell you to skip this film, inconsolable with rage at what they discover.

history.review_title: Prime doesn't mean it's worth your time, even if it's "free."
history.text: As I wrote for the DVD release, 2 stars is generous for only 2 acceptable shorts out of 7. If this is the best version of "Fun" that Strand and San Francisco Frameline could make, you'd be better off going out to Folsom in only your underwear because that is more fun than these boring sexless shorts! The only "fun" short out of 7 tries is the 1 that has subtitles called "Bald Guy," a musical from Scandinavia, and those subtitles are not even available in this digital version! However, all of the American shorts are tired, tired, and exhausted. I watched "Spooners" last year and while its trying to be charming and had the crowd laughing, the lead actor is a wet fish and the bearded boyfriend bearly saves him from ruining it. The other five films are not entertaining at all. They're shot poorly with standard bad gay acting. 1 short is just 2 guys talking in a beige kitchen and living room and that's it, another short is just 2 guys talking on a bland street corner in LA and that's it, another is supposed to be in Alaska but it may as well have been shot in Nebraska because its mostly indoors. Fun, right? I don't live in San Fran anymore but I wouldn't see the shorts programs there if this is what they liked or played, Outfest is soooo much better for shorts, lots come to mind easily. I'm just very shocked after some good shorts DVD releases in the last couple of years that this was so bad. I sold the DVD I had to recope some of the money I spent on it because 1 amusing musical isn't worth keeping 5 or 6 yawn-inducing ones. There's so much better on YouTube and Vimeo now anyway, way past the crummy gay comedies here.

history.review_title: The hubris of terrible filmmakers asking people to pay to watch an awful short
history.text: I had to laugh when I saw this amongst the options for LGBT films to rent. Not Prime, actually asking for money! This Cali filmmaker may as well be a walking desert because "thirsty" is the only way to describe him. He would play this film in a parking lot if he could, and he'd fly across the country or world if it played in that parking lot, just so he could take credit for making it. All one needs to do is go to the laughable Facebook fan page to see this guy in action! As for the film itself, I have to wonder who broke this poor guy's heart this bad to be thoroughly obsessed with supposedly shaming him for ghosting or dumping him. This drama-free meladrama has some of the worst acting I've ever seen. I'd be surprised if he could direct an actor to West Hollywood, much less how to speak on camera truthfully. The film was poorly edited, made no sense, and at 17 minutes, could be about 11 minutes shorter. The lead's grandma, who never says a word and has less than 10 seconds of screentime, gives him the self-esteem it takes to tell a mean ex off, in the most stilted phone exchange ever, and somehow makes him cry? The sheer stupidity of the screenplay will make anyone with half a brain supremely angry for having your time wasted watching it. It didn't even get into OutFest, where shorts of the highest caliber can't even get distribution, but this guy thinks you should pay to watch such drivel, as you can see from the number of planted friends giving 5-star reviews to fool you. So use the Freudian slip in the poster, which tells you what your answer should be to "Should I rent, or bother to watch, this atrocious short?" Nar. Not even if it's free.

As low budget gay indie films go, there are many, many, many worse than "Best Day Ever." These films must never make any money because it often feels they spent $500 making them. If I would recommend this film to anyone, it's to someone in need of a pick me up. This is yet another wish fulfilmment fantasy where the older guy ends up with a cute young twink, but in this case, the older man looks like handsome Mel England, and the twink looks like dad-bod strawberry ginger Tom Saporito. There is a sweetness and a familiarity by which these two find each other, as the older guy turns 50, worried as all men that age they'll end up alone. There's is a relationship based in friendship and sparks, so by the time these two are giving you the tried and true frontal shots and getting it on in bed, you're aching for them to get it going. It's not a hot scene, but loving and based in affection. This is a film in which many men will see themselves. Why do we wait until we're senior citizens to settle down? I wish the supporting characters were more memorable, and that the production values were stronger, but if this appeared on Logo, I'd probably watch it again on a rainy day. Beyond older men, I don't know if it would translate as well to others.

history.review_title: Don't judge it off of the first two awful minutes
history.text: Actors who make shorts where they play the lead, direct, produce AND Exec Produce are about as fun to think about as actors who write and star in one-man shows. You'll probably want to avoid 4 out of 5 of them. Shawn Ryan, the actor/director/producer/exec producer in question here, probably qualifies among the majority. However, his film "Charlie" indicates there maybe is more to him than just annoying actor tendencies. It would be easy to dismiss this short after 60 seconds given the shrill family we first meet. Ryan, as Charlie, comes off like a rich simpleton but harassed like a idiot criminal. Bizarre and unbelievable circumstances puts Charlie in the backyard of a family at the opposite end of the spectrum, so nice they're all beyond reason or belief, on Christmas Eve. It's here where the films best moments happen, albeit at sporadic moments. Ryan must be connected to the casting of "Parks & Recreation" because Jim O'Heir and Mo Collins play the family's warm and inviting parents. They're involvement outshines everyone involved. Collins displays a maternal instinct that allows her to play more than just her normal outrageous comedic side. She's quite compelling at moments. As for Ryan, there isn't much to praise. Playing a mute character renders him mostly as furniture, though one scene involving a shave gives him a solid expressive moment to play, and he does well there. Perhaps then Ryan would do better to pawn off some of those other roles besides actor if that's what he's trying to be. A real director might have a made short worthy of 5-stars, where the lead is the true focus, not the better known co-stars. As a Prime freebie, gay guys might enjoy a rare holiday-driven treat, even if it's very light on the gay. As a rental though, you might be disappointed.

history.review_title: There ARE subtitles, but you have to watch it on your computer to see them!
history.text: Ignore the 1-star reviews, which are almost exclusively related to Americans who can't be bothered to watch a trailer, or follow instructions, and would rather complain and wreck the movie's rating here for their own failings to figure out a mishandled situation by Amazon... YES, this is a foreign-language film. NO, they don't speak English here. YES, there are subtitles. NO, they are not automatically turned On (like they should be, Amazon). YES, you can watch it with subtitles! NO, I could not turn on the subtitles via my TV, another problem created by Amazon. YES, it will play on your computer with subtitles! NO, not automatically. Just press Play after you rent it, move your mouse over the screen towards the top right corner of the picture, and hover over the revealed icon on the left, which will allow you to choose to watch with subtitles! YES, you can alter the look and size of the subtitles! Just go to the Settings tab on the Home page (also near the top right), and change them there. And now that the users have made easier what Amazon and the distributor should have done in the first place... The movie itself has heart, a few laughs, and a subtle message about the way neighbors (including immigrants with Muslim names) can uplift and revitalize your life. There are dark elements, but smart kids and teens can still watch it with the family. It's not any darker than an animated film.

history.review_title: A pure cinematic experience for all of the senses!
history.text: What can one say about this unexpected delight called "The Handmaiden" without gushing? This is pure cinema and emotion at the highest levels one could hope to find. This twisty affair of lies, lust, greed, obsession, and many other sins begins as a tale of deception and becomes a love story of tenderness and awakening. Along the way there is political intrigue, pastoral scenery, impeccable costumes, gorgeous people, sexual indecency, ghost stories, a killer score, and a screenplay to die for. Had "The Handmaiden" been in the English language, like the director's last film called "Stoker" with Nicole Kidman, it would have been an Oscar contender. The acting from the entire enselmble brings this pulpy story to viseral life, and makes it an unforgettable experience. Yes, it is subtitled but please do not let that dissuade you from buying or renting this modern masterpiece. If you miss it, you'll only have yourself to blame!

history.title: UNDER THE GREENWOOD TREE (FF)(DVD)
history.review_title: Enjoyable Period Rom-Com With Hardy Depth and Charismatic Casting
history.text: A lighthearted, high-spirited, and comically earthy yet not raunchy treat filled with Thomas Hardy's multi-generational life and romantic challenges and catalysts including caste inequities, enjoyably whipped up with olde world fairytale-like Ye Olde Village charm, electric romantic charisma and likeable other characters casting intimately filmed and satisfyingly reverberating with more thought-provoking depth than lighter fare period rom-coms yet surprisingly lighter than Thomas Hardy's usual, though still telescoping his large life macrocosms into small and deceptively simple microcosms. My only critiques the dreadfully painted fake snow drifts (filmed in England, why couldn't this heavily English garbed period piece in four-season setting have used actual winter?) and the director's shift from Hardy's awakening young male hero to the young female's perspective emancipating them from rural into turn-of-the-century industrial Britain but this detour from Hardy's too much the director's proudly admitted copying Bathsheba Everdene and "Far From the Madding Crowd" instead of being true to Hardy's, making me want to read his novella and to look for an older version of the film to experience this idyllic time in England from a coming of age young Hardy's horizon. Still, Hardy could not but be pleased by the beautiful and irrepressibly hopeful expectation of love, joy, and fun of youth and other passions too--surprising how rich the lingering takeaway, though should not be since it is after all a Thomas Hardy.

history.title: The Beverly Hillbillies: The Official Fourth Season
history.review_title: Beautiful, new-looking picture quality; and has English subtitles
history.text: Picture-perfect-- beautiful picture quality, vivid color; an extremely sharp, clean picture, thus BRAND-NEW-looking episodes. Also, they have very accurate English subtitles, unlike Season 2 (which has no subtitles), which I'm currently watching also. The only negative for this Season 4: most of the episodes this season have thin plots and aren't very funny or interesting. The exceptions would be the two about Possum Day/Granny running for Possum Queen, which were quite funny. Beautiful Sharon Tate, tragically a victim of the Manson Family murders in 1969, appears as a bank employee in the first two or three episodes of this season (and was in quite a few episodes in the preceding seasons, mostly in that role but also in others). As to Season 4 plots: on the other hand, they are superior to those in Season 2, which as I'd noted above, I am watching simultaneously, and the acting is more loose and relaxed in Season 4, esp. from Max Baer as Jethro and Irene Ryan as Granny-- resulting in funnier delivery of their lines and overall better episodes, I feel. Highly recommend.

history.title: Commitments, The
history.review_title: Excellent picture quality, even on a high-def TV! (2004 2-disc version)
history.text: Note: this review is for the 2004 2-disc version, which is the best DVD version of this film. Unusual, excellent movie about a 1960s soul music band put together in the 1990s by a young local in Ireland, and the working-class band's ups and downs, along with his own personal travails. The band has more than 10 members, incl. 3 pretty female backup singers (2 of whom occasionally sing lead), so various subplots and tensions play out. Extremely entertaining, constantly funny, and if it weren't for the unnecessary persistent use of foul language and an arguably gratuitous sex scene (where no nudity was shown), this would be a great movie for the entire family. Very funny, quite enjoyable, very musical, keeps your interest the entire time, and lots of great 1960s American soul music is played throughout by very talented people. This is the definitive version of the DVD to purchase, and I own several different versions. This one shows the movie in anamorphic widescreen (unlike some other versions in 4x3), and has been remastered to have an extremely sharp picture, yes, even on a high-definition TV. The Blu-ray is about to be released, and I'm curious if they can get the picture quality appreciably better than is seen here, because this is really an excellent, sharp, colorful picture for DVD, even on a high-definition TV set, which ordinarily makes DVDs look pretty mediocre (I always prefer Blu-rays when available, which are made in Hi-def because they are intended for Hi-def TVs). This 2-disc set has the most extras available for any DVD version of this movie (it has 2 or 3 on the making of the film), and is the definitive DVD version. UPDATE 5/02/2017 - The picture quality of the Blu-ray is essentially identical to the above 2004 2-disc DVD version. As much as I prefer Blu-rays, it's virtually impossible to see any upgrade in picture quality for the BR when comparing both versions on a Hi-Def TV, unfortunately. The bit rate of the Blu-ray is higher, but my eyes don't really see any better picture.

history.title: Billy Jack: The Complete Collection (Born Losers / Billy Jack / The Trial of Billy Jack / Billy Goes to Washington) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Shout Factory's blu-ray set is another weak effort from them.
history.text: Yikes! Yet again, Shout Factory has produced a very sub-par Blu-ray, in this case, a sub-par 4-disc set, just as poor as are so many of their Blu-rays and DVDs. These are people who simply don't know how to do anywhere near as good a job as the major studios do at remastering and producing the best possible Blu-rays and DVDs, and they reveal repeatedly that they do not have access to the best film prints to start with (as to "The Trial of Billy Jack" and "Born Losers"). I should have known this would be another bad Shout Factory experience, especially when I opened the sealed package and saw that one of the four discs was missing! (A friend who lives nearby, who also pre-ordered this set, loaned me that last disc so that I could view it, thus I reviewed that one here along with the others.) ** My review will be a somewhat detailed discussion of the technical aspects of the Blu-ray 4-disc set's picture quality, audio, and extras (or lack thereof), but not addressing the content or story of the four films, which I think has been addressed in great detail by other reviewers over the years. ** First of all, I will compare the new Shout! Factory blu-ray of 1971's "Billy Jack" in this 4-disc set with the previous blu-ray of a few years back from Image Entertainment. And the latter is superior in nearly all ways to this new Shout! Factory version. In this newer version, at the beginning of the closing credits, they suddenly repeat the audio section of "One Tin Soldier" that had been played as the movie was concluding, including the police sirens, yes, even the police sirens are repeated in the closing credits. The problem is, there shouldn't be ANY music in the closing credits, as all previous versions, incl. VHS, show-- just silence. This was somebody's dumb attempt to throw in some more of the famous theme song, but as it doesn't belong, not even one note, in the always-silent closing credits, it makes no sense at all; AND, it also starts abruptly, not at the beginning of the song or at some sensible intermediate point, as if some 4th-grader threw it on there mid-stream . . . it's just ridiculous. The new version-- the Shout! Factory version-- is about 27 seconds shorter in running time, and this is mostly due to the fact that the earlier Blu-ray had the Motion Picture Association rating at the end for a few seconds, as on the original print, whereas that was omitted in this new version and some graphic like "BillyJackRights.com" was thrown on there instead in this new one, thus not being faithful to the original print. And, the most important point to me-- the picture quality-- while solidly good, is simply not quite as good on this newest version, because the color is oversaturated in many places, making faces sometimes oversaturated, and occasionally there are slightly wrongly-tinted fleshtones. Also, somebody decided to retain-- or add in-- additional grain into this version, making the picture granier and less desirable (to me) than the cleaner-looking previous blu-ray version. Some movie aficionados think older movies should show grain even on blu-rays, which, in a blu-ray, I simply cannot understand, as I am looking for the best, sharpest, most hi-def picture quality-- not the worst. The one improvement in the new Shout! Factory blu-ray version of "Billy Jack" is that it contains English subtitles, while the previous Blu-ray version by Image Entertainment has no subtitles. The newer version also has a significantly louder volume to the audio. But, it completely omits any documentaries or trailers, only has a radio spot, whereas the earlier version has TWO different filmmaker commentary tracks, plus a mini-documentary about the making of the movie, as well as several 1973 re-release TV commercials. Even the menu on the earlier Blu-ray is superior, vastly superior, to the menu on the new one. The new menu contains audio of "One Tin Soldier" while the old one only has an irritating drum beat, but the earlier one does have a number of huge still photos from the movie that zoom in and out a bit for a few seconds each, then the photos change. Whereas on the new discs, there is a still artistic rendering of Tom Laughlin as Billy Jack that doesn't change at all (on ALL FOUR discs in this set). All in all, the Shout! Factory version of "Billy Jack" is inferior on all counts to the prior Image Entertainment version except for its louder volume and its inclusion of English subtitles. The new "Born Losers" blu-ray cannot be said to be any sharper than the most recent DVD release, which I also own. Interestingly, it has some grain removed, so it looks like a sort of smoother picture, but it is not sharper than the DVD at all, though I think most people would agree that it is somehow prettier. The problem is, every single defect, artifact, and piece of dirt showing in the DVD's picture exists here in the Blu-ray as well. Nothing was cleaned up. The picture actually jitters mildly in some spots, it's a very slight thing but one can detect it, and in this way, it is identical to the most recent DVD, which, as I recall, was an upgrade in quality compared with previous DVDs of the same film. I would say that the "Born Losers" Blu-ray is a definite disappointment, though it does have this somehow smoother look to it than the DVD and thus is an improvement, however minor. It also contains English subtitles. Oh yeah, at 1m38s into the movie, as Vicky narrates the opening and says that, "All I knew was his name. Billy Jack," the English subtitles show "Bill Jack." Seriously. I don't like (and never have liked) the other two movies, "The Trial of Billy Jack" and "Billy Jack Goes to Washington," so I will leave discussions of possible missing segments and music to two of the previous Blu-ray set reviewers, "kidglov3s" and "blood simple." I CAN say that the new "The Trial of Billy Jack" blu-ray print looks beaten-up, is also a bit unfocused, and shows all kinds of white streaks and artifacts, resulting in a VERY weak-looking, old-looking Blu-ray picture. Really, it's of below-average DVD or VHS quality, even for a 1974 film, and I have lots of DVDs and VHS tapes OF OLDER-THAN-1974 movies whose picture looks better on my high-definition TV set than does this Blu-ray. A very poor job. They obviously started with a weak master print and then decided not to improve it. Wow. "Billy Jack Goes to Washington" is the only one of the four films not shown in 16x9; it is presented in letterbox, at a 2.35:1 aspect ratio. This means there are black bars above and below the picture, not my favorite thing but something which movie aficionados seem to love, because it generally means that the film is being presented the way the director intended, with a very wide screen that includes everything, from left to right, that the director wants to include. Anyway, the picture quality is excellent. Not amazing or gorgeous, but of solid Blu-ray quality for a 1977 film. With fine color and sharpness. I don't see anything to complain about on that front. The other two reviewers I mentioned above complained of "stutters," whose meaning I don't know. But I only noticed any picture jitters, if THAT is the definition, in the brief scenes obviously shot from a moving helicopter, mostly at the opening of the movie, and I wouldn't call that a jitter, anyway; it is no different from other movies which have scenes shot from a moving helicopter. Apart from these scenes, I didn't notice any jitter or instability at all in this BR film, whereas that certainly does exist in the new Blu-ray version in this set of "Born Losers" as I previously noted. Now, I did not watch every scene of "Billy Jack Goes to Washington," nor remember it (or "Trial") much from my theater viewings 40 years ago, so I cannot properly discuss whether any scenes or music were edited out of this film, a complaint of the two reviewers I mentioned above. I have no doubt that they are accurate in their descriptions, however. Overall, this set is a huge disappointment. I well recall that Shout! Factory absolutely butchered Season 7 of the seminal TV show, "All in the Family," after Sony had done a beautiful job on the first six seasons-- Shout! Factory used the wrong video speed (in frames per second), or something like that, and EVERY episode had weird, faulty-looking, film-like video with out-of-sync audio. When I brought this to Shout! Factory's attention via direct communication with them (as did some other Amazon reviewers), and asked them if they were going to correct this and replace the set, they said that they absolutely were not going to do that. THAT is representative of the ACTUAL so-called "love and attention they deserve" that Shout! Factory claims to give their releases. I think they simply do not have the skills, nor desire, nor access to the best film prints, nor perhaps the budget, to make truly excellent Blu-rays and DVDs. Their release of the TV show, "Room 222," has to be one of the worst butcher-jobs ever, as Shout! Factory admittedly didn't have good master prints to work with (they so warn us on the outer packages of the two DVD seasons they offered, and some episodes look like 3rd-generation VHS recordings!). This Billy Jack four-disc Blu-ray set is just VERY DISAPPOINTING overall, if not plain poor, and I cannot recommend this purchase as any sort of upgrade unless English subtitles are crucial to the buyer. Only if a potential buyer has never owned any of these films could I possibly recommend purchase of this Blu-ray set, which, in fairness, would be better than nothing. *** Here's a little tidbit for Billy Jack fans: when I viewed the 1958 Rodgers & Hammerstein film musical SOUTH PACIFIC on blu-ray a few weeks ago, I was shocked to see Tom Laughlin in the opening scene (and a couple of other scenes) as a jaded pilot smoking a cigar. Indeed, he is up in the plane flying the first time we see him. Good for him, I say, but I'd bet he never advertised that when he was a youth-inspiring, anti-establishment rebel in BORN LOSERS, BILLY JACK, etc. I can see the film trailer now: "Billy Jack, starring Tom Laughlin, whom you may remember from the charming Rodgers and Hammerstein musical, South Pacific . . . " NOT!! I saw him on TV a week later in another 1950s film, 1957's THE DELINQUENTS, and a quick trip subsequently to Wikipedia enlightened me as to his film career pre-Born Losers. Interesting stuff. ***

history.title: JFK: 3 Shots That Changed America
history.review_title: Excellent in all respects. DON'T MISS!
history.text: Absolutely riveting compilation, put together perfectly, of the events surrounding the JFK assassination, using real-time news footage of several TV networks and local stations, from a few hours before the assassination through the next few days-- including Ruby's murder of Oswald and Oswald's funeral-- as well as related events occurring many years later, such as the trial of Jack Ruby, the trial of Clay Shaw in 1969, and the 1978 House Subcommittee on Assassinations. I have never seen anything on this subject that is so complete in terms of original TV footage, some of it minute-by-minute, and amazingly, there is no narrator, just some on-screen graphics introducing most of the segments. This is the closest thing to reliving those terrible few days. The picture quality is absolutely perfect regarding most of the clips. With slightly over 3 hours of footage, and clips from so many different sources, I can guarantee that even the most experienced JFK assassination buffs will see plenty of footage that they have never seen before. I had not heard of this production, but I find it to be as good as the one I had previously thought was the absolute best, the double-episode covering the JFK assassination of "The Sixties," the 2014 CNN documentary series. In fact, that one borrows plenty of footage from "JFK: 3 Shots That Changed America"! Get this DVD. If the subject matter interests you at all, then this will probably become your favorite production on this subject.

history.title: Nazis: A Warning from History, The (DVD)
history.review_title: Truly great, fresh documentary on the Nazis
history.text: As someone who has seen most every documentary on the Nazis, as well as having read most of the major books on the subject as well, over several decades, I can say that this documentary--at least to this American viewer-- presented tons of new information, tons of new historical footage, and many new interviews with Germans who were there. It is extremely well put-together by a producer who clearly knows what he is doing, and was a thoroughly compelling, never-boring viewing from beginning to end. Essential to any student of this subject. Highly recommended.

history.title: Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
history.text: This is a nice film that seems to accomplish what it sets out to do, but there are a few flaws. Perhaps it tries to do too much in too little time--the first half of the film feels very fragmented and disjointed. There's very little flow to it, and it sometimes takes a few moments to allow the brain to catch up with sudden shifts in the narrative. I would also agree with other reviewers who are disappointed with what has been left out--there seems to be a fear here of running too long, something that we learned with "Gandhi" isn't a huge problem if you have a truly compelling narrative. And the life of Mandela does provide that. They could easily have given us more details without spoiling the film. That said, it's still a worthwhile film to see.

history.title: Margot At The Wedding
history.text: This was really awful. Like some other reviewers, we kept with it until the end, hoping that something would come of the mess, but it never does. All the reasons for which it's horrible are in the other reviews, so I'll just say that none of the characters are sympathetic, none but Margot and her sister are developed at all (and they're developed poorly), and the cinematography is quite mediocre--some of the scenes are extremely dark and washed out, as if the director and the people on the cameras didn't understand anything about light or lighting while they were filming. All in all, a horrible waste of time.

history.title: Arrested Development: Season 4
history.text: This is an absolute travesty. Everything that made Arrested Development a strong series is gone, and is replaced by weak writing, contrived situations, lame characters, a ridiculous plot, and very weak editing. This last one is probably the biggest disappointment--the editing of the original three seasons was truly inspired, but here it's quite lame and very weak. It's evident from episode one that this is not the AR development of old. The horribly contrived situation of Michael living in his son's dorm and being so completely stupid that he can't see that his son isn't okay with it makes me cringe as a viewer. And when he gets in a public shower with his son when there's a free one right next to it, well, that's just creepy in many, many ways. And the creepy things continue all through the season. We felt dismayed after the first two episodes, but we decided to watch the whole season just to see if things get better. They don't--they actually get worse. This is a complete waste of time and effort and energy and money, and it all leads to one of the most stupid endings that I've ever seen to anything. I think the five-star reviews are from people who were so happy that the show was back that they didn't care about quality, but this is like a long-lost friend coming back into your life, only now he's into drugs and he smells bad and he constantly insults you and calls you names--he's not the same friend you used to have.

history.title: Before I Fall [Blu-ray]
history.text: I was fortunate enough to be able to see this on a plane, so there was no risk of wasting time on a movie I never had heard of before. It starts out a bit slow and seems to be heading in very predictable directions, and for the most part, that's true. In this type of film, the conflicts and opportunities for growth and change are set up very carefully in the first "normal" day, and this film isn't any different from the norm. There are, however, some rather consistent twists and turns that end up making this story different from the norm, and some of the twists work while others do not. The main character's "rebellious" day, for example, plays rather shallowly and annoyingly, though it also provides us with some interesting background that wasn't there before. The main actress (I've forgotten her name) is quite good, and all in all the acting, directing, and camera work are quite strong. The story is good, though again somewhat predictable most of the time. I think the most frustrating thing of the film is that the main character takes a lot of time to catch on to many things, and she seems smarter than that. Perhaps she's not, though. This is a good film and well worth watching.

history.title: Cowboys & Aliens Region Free
history.text: We just watched the Blu-Ray version, and the sound mixing was absolutely horrible--I had to hold the remote the entire movie because when people were talking, I had to turn up the volume, but as soon as any action or music started, it was incredibly loud and I had to turn it down again. While it was a somewhat enjoyable film in many ways and quite entertaining in a mindless way, I probably would go with such a low rating because they've done something that so many others do--they've made the aliens so strong and fast that it's absolutely ridiculous to think that they could be defeated by a ragtag group of outlaws and Apache warriors, along with a guy with a super-weapon on his wrist. It's just silly--you can make aliens strong to make the audience admire the victors for having defeated them, but not so strong that they're practically invincible.

history.title: Gattaca
history.text: This is an extremely slow-moving film that has some interesting moments, but that all in all turns out to be disappointing. It's not a thriller--it's simply a study on how long he can go avoiding detection. There are some plot elements that stretch one's belief far too much, but they've all been mentioned in other reviews. The characters, in general, are flat--there's very little depth to any of them. It ended up being a very long two hours for very little that was enjoyable.

history.title: Moscow on the Hudson
history.text: This is really nothing more than a typical Hollywood formulaic piece of crap, to be honest. There's nothing in the script that's original, and the characters are all horrible stereotypes. It's a shame because there's a lot of talent here, but it's poorly utilized in a very poor film. Robin Williams is always hit or miss--great sometimes, decent in awful films others. This is one of the latter.

history.title: 11:14 (DVD) (WS)
history.text: Horrible--this would be a zero-star movie if I could give it zero. The script is simply awful--the dialogue is stilted and unnatural, the time frames don't add up, the characters are simply stupid people doing stupid things in contrived and unbelievable situations. None of the characters are at all sympathetic, and neither of us watching it cared even the slightest bit for any of them. Simply a bad movie, one to pass on.

history.title: Bandidas
history.text: This was a lot of fun--it's not a great movie, by any means, but everyone involved seems to know that, and they're more interested in making a fun piece of entertainment than trying to create a work of art. And it works. Cruz and Hayek work extremely well together, the plot holds up fairly well, the supporting actors are all decent, and it's a fun way to pass an hour and a half. No one is taking themselves or their roles too seriously, and the result is very enjoyable. So if you want to enjoy the company of two very friendly ladies who are very good actresses, this is a good film to watch.

history.title: Modern Family: Season 9
history.text: Okay, so it's over. The last couple of seasons have demonstrated significantly diminishing quality, but this one is a pretty bad season by any standards. Especially poor are the scripts, which force the characters into some pretty stupid situations, which forces the actors to overcompensate, trying to make something stupid seem realistic. All in all, a huge disappointment--the actors are still good enough that if you were to get some fresh scriptwriters in there, you could make every season as good as the first. But this is Hollywood, I guess, so they'll just let it die a pitiful death several years after it should have been cancelled or improved.

history.title: Exodus [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Confusing Blu-ray compatibility info (Region B Australia)
history.text: What a mess and what confusion on this highly sought after blu-ray. I had the laser version and always wanted HD copy especially given the great on location scenery in Israel and Cypress. Only 3000 of the original blu-ray was printed according to blu-ray experts; the cost thus is very high for these. Thus we are stuck looking for imports from Australia. The code on the disk says region B only and most people say it will not work on US players. Well I took a chance on buying one from Australia when the retailer says it is region free but marked region B. Well it came and it worked. The disk is a better transfer for 90% of the scenes. Some scenes still suffer from video noise when you look at the sky. Unlike the original blu-Ray sound is only in English 2.0 DTS. I suspect because people complained over DTS 5.1. There are no extras or trailers...nothing. So feel confident on region B blu-rays and you do not have to get it from Australia.

history.title: Gloomy Sunday (1999) (Import All Region)
history.review_title: Masterpiece- Korean region free import at great value
history.text: This is a spectacular heart breaking movie with a haunting musical score framing the brutality of German occupied Budapest during WWII and their heinous treatment of the Jewish population. It is one of those movies which can be watched over and over like Inglorious Basterds because it has an appropriate revengeful ending. Unfortunately the theatrical Wide-screen version costs a fortune and has no extras. The Korean import is digitally remastered but is a smaller screen with superb DTS 5.1 sound in German with English subtitles. There are plenty of extras but most only with Korean text or subtitles. It's a trade-off for price sensitive people. I was able to get it direct from Korea for $6 versus buy the WS version for $79. There is also a Korean blu-Ray version with fancy booklet and extras. But I suspect those extras are not translated into English. So if you want a good copy and can live without widescreen this is a great value.

history.title: Donkey Skin
history.review_title: Definite must for fans of Demy musicals
history.text: The only reason I got this DVD was to make sure I had all of Jacque Demy's French musicals. This was after my delightful experience with Umbrellas of Cherbourg and The Young Girls of Rochefort with the fabulous music of Michel LeGrand and the unforgettable beauty Catherine Deneuve. Koch Lorber has done a very decent transfer with soundtrack upgraded to DTS 5.1 and white or yellow subtitles. The extras which include a great psychological panel discussion are fabulous running probably another 90 minutes for this colorful adult fairy tale; yes Demy loves pastels and color....lots of color. The fairy tale is a variation on the story of Cinderella but this one is a little odd being a fairy tale about incest and an adult woman's (no way is she a girl) flight from her father who matter of fact wants to marry her.

history.title: Lost Horizon
history.text: Gorgeous restoration on about 90% of the film, an extra minute of film, plus about six minutes of audio only with stills. The extras are great and show us what we could have had if an original negative had been found not to mention some great background information. Capra wanted the film longer than 132 minutes but it flopped. There are people like me who want the 6 hour version. The packaging is excellent with nice glossy booklet. Well worth the upgrade especially at this unbelievable Amazon price of $12.

history.title: Malena
history.text: This movie is like eating candy only to find it has a bitter center. Understand first for fans of Monica Bellucci that the version shown here is redacted as if it held some horrible dark secret about the assassination of JFK. Censored by 17 minutes; we are all adults so I don’t know why it was so viciously cut. If you want the uncut version wou will need to purchase from Korea or China. I got this version only because it was available for $5.50. Yet it is a lovely story of a boy’s coming of age, masterfully done. I suspect Malena’s beauty was symbolically maimed by the pettiness of the backward towns-people amidst Italian fascism during WWII; these are mean-spirited people, but so was Mussolini. Perhaps that is precisely why fascism flourishes. Her triumphant return to the crappy town which was the source of her abuse is puzzling and never explained in the short making of Malena bonus feature.

history.title: Simon

history.title: Napoleon (1927) ( Napolon vu par Abel Gance ) [ NON-USA FORMAT, Blu-Ray, Reg.B Import - United Kingdom ]
history.text: So sorry there are so many games played regarding this film. Certainly I wanted this Blu-ray 5.5 hour version with all the commentaries. But the version available does not play on standard U.S. players, and I was not about to buy a region free player then pop $75 for this film. Since I had a laser player I got the very decent laser disc with the score of Carmine Coppola; not blu-ray quality but much better than VHS and many DVDs. Well done film and quite innovative given that it is a silent film. But it is disappointing in that it covers Napoleon’s life only through 1797 missing the most important part of his life. it should have been called YOUNG NAPOLEON. Four hours is plenty given it missed the meat of his sordid career.

history.title: Inferno
history.text: Such a valid point to make ... then screw it up with disjointed, annoying flashes. It took forever to get the film started, then even longer to figure out who was chasing who and why. I never read the book, but can't believe it was as hard to absorb as the first 30 minutes of this mess. Overpopulation is a worldwide problem. The poorest and most ignorant people are compounding the problem at an alarming rate. Moonraker was a better example of dealing with the problem. Too bad this show didn't do a better job of condemning people for having too many children...and religions that preach no birth control. I was expecting a good mystery -- seeking clues, while racing against the clock. Here, the locations were spectacular, the clues were lame and by the end, you're not sure you want Hanks to stop the Inferno.

history.text: 2.5/5 stars. This Paul Blart has about 25% of the laughs (if that) of the original. One of the worst things about the movie is that two of the main characters are out of the movie right away (his mom and Amy) and Amy divorcing him just basically undoes everything that he worked to get in the first movie. No spoilers because it happens right in the beginning of the movie. I get that he's a geeky guy that things don't go well for, but couldn't they have written her out of the script in another way, like having her on a business trip or something? Now for the rest of the movie. Most of the jokes fall flat. Paul doesn't give any "fun facts" for anyone which was pretty funny for the first movie. He again shows off his segue skills, and there is a heist or attempted heist going on. You might recognize the main villain from Band of Brothers. Probably the funniest part of the movie was when Paul gets in the fight with the peacock and the piano player just keeps playing. The main fight scene between paul and the security guards and the henchmen is also entertaining if not flat out unbelievable. Let's hope there's not a Paul Blart 3, but I'm sure it made enough on the box office for there to be one. One last thought, the commercialization of this movie was much more obvious than in the first Blart. You could easily count at least 5 items that are blatantly advertised. Sort of reminds me of Minority Report except without the quality movie attached.

history.title: La La Land [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
history.review_title: Fantastic fun, catchy music, memorable and worth owning
history.text: My wife and I saw this at the theater on New Year's Eve last year. What a spectacular movie. While not perfect (Gosling's vocals leave something to be desired), it's such a fun movie with very catchy music that I still find myself listening to the soundtrack. This movie hits all the right notes. It takes place in LA and since I love visiting California it makes it that much better. We visited Los Angeles this year and had a wonderful time. We got a chance to visit the Warner Bros lot for a tour (WELL worth it if you're in the area!) and they had a mock La La Land coffee shop where we had a photo op (see picture). In the movie, Ryan Gosling goes to visit Emma Stone, who works at the WB Lot coffee shop. They showed us on the tour where they were walking when they filmed that scene between two soundstages. Other aspects of the movie include J.K. Simmons as the restaurant owner who fires Ryan Gosling in his trademark style (think Whiplash but not as intense). Emma and Ryan have a fantastic on-screen chemistry and are funny as well as heartfelt and of course the music is great. Gosling's vocals are not as good as Stone's but I can forgive that given how much I enjoy this movie. Some may not like the ending but it is what it is and is a memorable 7 minutes. I bought this in 4K Blu-ray even though I don't have a 4K TV yet because it included the regular blu-ray as well. The soundtrack sounds great on my system, and video is high quality. I would highly recommend this but rent it first as it's a polarizing movie!
