history.text: I was told to watch this by a friend. I thought this movie was really stupid. There is not one character I liked. I’m not sure if the viewer is suppose to root for the main characters at the end but if so that’s completely ridiculous as they are terrible people who do horrific things. They are psychopathic murderers not anti-heroes. I literally didn’t care what happened to any of them. The only good thing I have to say about it is that the movie has some good music. That’s it.

history.title: Cult of Chucky (Unrated)
history.text: The first Child’s Play will always be the scariest. Like the first Nightmare on Elm Street it can’t be outdone by a sequel or remake. I found Seed and Bride to be cheesy and corny. I hated them. Like Nightmare on Elm Steet the franchise of Child’s Play became more comical with each sequel. That said I was pleasantly surprised to watch Curse of Chucky. It brought back the scare so I was looking forward to Cult of Chucky thinking hopefully that the franchise had been revived in a good way. I was wrong. The overt gore and subpar acting by some of the cast was bad. The whole storyline was a letdown. I was excited to see the Andy Barkley character back but he was never utilized to his full potential. He’s in maybe a total of 20 minutes of the movie if that. The plot with the multiple Chuckys and stupid jokes made this movie more like Seed and Bride. Overall I was pretty disappointed. I watched this while I was still riding a binge-buzz having just finished the awesome second season of Stranger Things on Netflix. This movie pretty killed that. I realized quickly I should’ve just started rewatching ST or went to bed. I will say that Jennifer Tilly was great as always and I really enjoyed Fiona Dourif’s acting and character. She looks so much like her dad that at times, especially at the end, I thought I was looking at Brad Dourif.

history.title: Jaws 3
history.text: The first Jaws was the awesome. The sequels of course weren’t as good. I remember watching this as a kid and loving it just because of the underwater tunnel and restaurant scenes. Watching it again as an adult I can definitely see it’s more of a fair movie. It’s pretty unbelievable to me now. It does have a great cast. This is one of those movies you really just watch for a little fun or as a time killer. I’ve definitely seen worse but I’ve also also seen better. My baby cousin who is 20 years younger than me had no idea there was even a Jaws 3 made. He thought they stopped at 2. He’d never even heard of it when I told him and thought I was pulling his leg. Made me feel kinda old ha ha.

history.title: Jaws: The Revenge
history.text: In my opinion this is the worst of the sequels to Jaws. I still don’t understand why Michael Caine and Lorraine Gary chose to be in it.

history.title: Fear, Inc.
history.text: The acting is so bad. The main character is incredibly annoying. I didn’t find it funny or scary, just really stupid. I can’t believe anyone rated this movie 5 Stars. Just watch The Game. It’s soooo much better.

I thought this might be a decent time killer but I hated this movie. The main character is a victim of his own very bad decisions. Watching someone make such stupid choices is hard to watch. It starts to feel ridiculous. There’s a twist but I had it figured out long before the end. Watch Fatal Attraction instead. It’s a much better movie. I feel like I wasted 6.00 on this one.

history.title: The Box
history.text: I couldn’t get past the terrible southern accents. I’m from the Deep South and it’s laughable how bad some southern accents are in movies. Ask other southerners. They will say the same thing. This is supposed to be based in Virginia. The accents portrayed here are way too thick to be believable. I have family in Virginia and they do not have accents like those who live in the Deep South, like those portrayed in this movie. It may be a minor thing but it was off-putting to me and made it hard to even watch or take the movie seriously.

history.title: Flatliners
history.text: It was ok. The original is a really good movie with an amazing cast. I had no real bias going in because I was actually looking forward to the movie since it isn’t a total remake per say. Yet something was missing. The story just didn’t grab me like it’s predecessor did. I didn’t care for the characters like I did the first either. There isn’t really much of a climax here. Especially if you’ve seen the first one. There is a lot of partying and it didn’t really go into as much depth of the characters’ backstories as the previous one did. The first is one I’ve watched again from time to time. This is one I won’t be watching again. I also feel like Keifer Sutherland’s role was wasted here. I don’t understand why they didn’t have him play Nelson like he did in the previous movie. That would've made it more interesting to me. Even a small, little Easter egg would’ve been a nice tip of the hat to the original. Instead he plays just an everyday ordinary doctor/teacher with no real purpose other than maybe putting pressure on medical students. I don’t even remember his name in this film. I feel like that was a bit of wasted potential. Ellen Page was great but why they chose to go the route they did with her character so soon in the film is beyond me. Especially since she is the most well-known actor (other than Sutherland) in the film. She was pretty much the only character I really cared even a little bit about. I feel like the first movie had more of a lesson about forgiveness than this one. The first was about asking forgiveness for the sins you’ve committed against others. This one supposedly is about forgiving oneself but you don’t actually realize it till a small scene which is thrown in near the end. Overall I give it 2 stars instead of 3 because to me it’s more of a meh movie than a good one.

history.title: The Dark Tower
history.text: I thought it was ok. I haven’t read the books yet and even I could tell and wished the story had been more fleshed out. I felt like a lot was left unexplained about the entire story and the Dark Tower world. The good thing is that this has made me want to read the books as I find the story very interesting. I know that this is an entire series of books written by King who is one of my favorite authors. I wished maybe that they would’ve went the route of several sequels like LoTR to give us the entire story instead of trying to explain everything in one film. I can see why book readers would be disappointed here as I find the lack of depth portrayed here disappointing myself and I haven’t even read the books yet. As a stand alone movie I think it is good but definitely not great. It had a lot of potential and could’ve been better. It was rather short and I was surprised at how quickly it was over. I read recently that a Dark Tower series is coming out soon. I’m looking forward to seeing that. In the meantime I plan to start reading the books.

Good but not great. For me it was more of a fun movie than a scary one. There wasn’t as much gore as I’d thought there’d be considering that a lot of movies these days go that route. There is a lot of language though. In my opinion I feel like it didn’t go into enough depth with the relationship of the losers. The bond of the kids wasn’t explored as much as I would’ve liked and it seemed to barely scratch the surface of their fierce loyalty to one another. It left me feeling as though they weren’t that close. The CGI in my opinion also wasn’t that good. There are a couple scenes with the woman and the leper that I thought the CGI was pretty sloppy. There was plenty of source material from King’s book so I have no idea why they chose for Stan to be afraid of a painting. In the book he gets locked in a building with 2 dead boys. That would’ve been much scarier in my opinion. My biggest disappointment was the way Mike’s character was handled. In the book he’s the son of a very kind and loving family who happen to own a farm. The family including Mike experience racism firsthand. His father was one of my favorite characters in the book even though he wasn’t a very big one. It’s from him that Mike gets his love of history and learns how to handle the discrimination he experiences. Mike’s love and knowledge of the town history is taken away and given to Ben in this film which serves no real purpose. Ben is already suppose to be the engineer of the group and Mike the historian. Instead Mike just becomes a stand-in character in this film. The other character change I didn’t like was Bev. She comes across as older than the boys to me. I don’t know if it’s her make up or personality but she certainly seems more like a teenager than a middle schooler. In the book she is also the one whose aim sends Pennywise scurrying back to the sewers. In the film she becomes the damsel in distress which needs to be rescued near the end. It somewhat took away from the independence of her character. I did like how the relationship with Bill and Georgie was more fleshed out. You get a real feeling of how much Bill loved his brother in this film. Overall I think it’s a pretty good movie but not flawless. People online seem to have very strong feelings about this film. If you criticize it whatsoever some people seem to become very upset. I don’t understand why people take the opinions of others so personally these days. Especially over something as trivial as a movie.

history.title: The Jungle Book
history.review_title: Better than I thought it would be.
history.text: I was pleasantly surprised with the retelling of the Jungle Book story. The special effects do justice to the movie. I'm usually critical how CGI is overused in movies today, but it gave the talking animals more of a realistic look. And the jungle scenes looked realistic and natural. My main criticism is with the young actor playing the orphan. He lacked the ability to convey depth or emotion.His performance was passable but I think an Indian actor with the correct dialect would have made it more convincing. Also I didn't care for the songs hijacked from the animated version. It just didn't work for me. And of course the word "cool" uttered by the main character sounded silly. I recommend this version, even with the flubs I mentioned. I usually don't sit thru a whole movie these days, but I it kept me involved.

history.review_title: Awful. Boring. Been done a thousand times before.
history.text: Mindless drivel. Bad acting. Bad directing. Preposterous dialog. I didn't expect Shakespeare, but hoped for more than this trite offering.

history.title: Arrival [Blu-ray]
history.text: Arrival is one of those movies with good production values, competent actors, except for Forrest Whittaker and a new twist to a visit by Aliens. The problem is that I walked away confused and bewildered as to why I stuck it out. It was free, so I suppose that answers the second question. I like the idea that for a change the Aliens are not out to rip us limb from limb or zap us into dust, but I hoping for a more coherent story line. I had to go to Wikipedia to figure out what I had watched. I found myself getting up and doing something around the house and then coming back to watch, and then getting up again and again in order to get thru the movie. Not a good sign. If critics are calling this film the best movie of the year, the movie business is dead. Not financially, but artistically dead. Having a female heroine save the day and humanity seems to be the trend these days, but it's getting a bit overused. I like Amy Adams as an actress, but I think her role in this movie wasn't that great. I didn't relate to any of the characters in this film.

history.title: DOCTOR STRANGE
history.text: I wanted to like this movie basically because I think Benedict Cumberbatch is fine actor, but even his abilities do not save this film. I wish I could put my finger on why films like this don't entertain me. The visuals are well done and the obviously the production values are high. The dialog and plot is predictable and unnecessarily complicated at times. Little or no character development and some of the actors are just there for the sake of a diverse cast. There is no talent displayed by the Director actors or the anyone else associated with the making of this film. The usual CGI effects galore and twists and turns that make little sense. I suppose thats what audiences are used to today and apparently eat it up. I confess to being puzzled as to why films like this make hundreds of millions of dollars. But it is what it is.

history.title: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
history.review_title: Not as good as the previous installment.
history.text: My impressions upon watching this film were partly based partly on the first installment of "Rise of the Planet of the Apes" . I usually rate a movie as to whether I will watch it over and over again, or watch it once and put it away. This is a one time deal for me. I give it three solid stars for production value and acting, specifically by the Ape characters. I found the human actors annoying at times and the human lead, the nice guy, irritating and wimpy. The story was slow and monotonous. Rise of the Planet of the apes was original and held my interest throughout. I've watched it several times and each time enjoyed it." Dawn" sort of moved along slowly and made me wonder if maybe they should have moved in different direction with the story line. Nothing too original. The humans being human and the Apes in turn acting as bad as humans. As with most films made today, they seem to dumb the movies down for the masses. By not making it too complicated they fill the theaters and make their money.

The newest installment of the star trek franchise tries , but fails to capture the Original TV series flavor. Visually of course the CGI is superior to anything the previous TV and early movies did. And the costumes and makeup are excellent, but I just don't relate to the actors. One scene in particular I found annoying. I'll just leave it to ones imagination which scene that was.

Silly idea. In 1869 America, that they would have a black secret service agent, even if it existed back then is preposterous. The film producers should have forgotten political correctness and stay true to the source material. Aside from that it is still a bad movie.

The original Star Trek series is something that has never in my opinion been duplicated. Many movies and TV productions later, make me realize that the original was the best. Except of a few poor offerings, I have watched each and every episode numerous times and have enjoyed them all as though seeing them for the first time. I don't care for the enhanced special effects nor do I like what George Lucas did with the original Star Wars movie. If it's not broke don't fix it. The original series had it's own charm and I have never been a fan of the movies or other incarnations of the series.

In my opinion the fourth season had it's highlights, but was the weakest of the previous three seasons. Episodes 20 and 21 were blatantly obvious references to mutucultrial diversity that is constantly being thrown around , and is something that Hollywood feels compelled to insert into everything we watch today. Scott Bakula is the week link. His acting style just doesn't seem to fit well into the character of Archer. Jolene Blalock showed more depth and ability in the fourth season. When she's in scene it's impossible to take your eyes off her. She has a look that's hypnotizing. The last episode was weak and anticlimatic.

history.title: The Mummy (2017) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Could have been a good movie if it had a story, decent dialog and direction. And John Steinbeck.
history.text: I watched this movie from start to finish. It was free, so I didn't feel ripped off and my time is not that valuable as to wanting 2 hours of life back. Tom Cruise is a competent enough actor when given decent material and the actress playing the Egyptian princess is probably the highlight of the film. She's exotic and beautiful to look at. The other actors, with the exception of Russell Crowe, were substandard. What frustrates me about todays films is how they can be so bad with almost unlimited budgets. The three things that a film should give the movie goer is the story, believable dialog and direction. And a fourth, good Cinematography. Why, I ask myself, is Hollywood pumping out films like these? I know the source material has been done dozens of times, but a good writer can make it somewhat interesting. It's as if the people making movies just don't care, as long as it makes money, or keeps them busy. Maybe creativity and ability are dead in the film industry. Maybe it's political correctness watering down the talent pool. Or maybe it's that all the really talented people are dead. Who knows? I usually judge a movie I enjoy by how many times wish to view it. This was a one time event.

history.title: Jerry Warren Collection Vol. 2 Triple Feature
history.review_title: Not as Enjoyable as Collection 1 but Well Done DVD
history.text: Odds are that if you are even on this page, you know the type of films Jerry Warren is known for. The 4 stars doesn't imply these movies are on par with anything by Michael Powell, George Kukor, or Carol Reed. These are what they are Drive-In B movie and dreadfully low budget (there is good low budget, see Detour). The DVD by Kit Parker Films/VCI Entertainment is extremely well made. The movies are well represented with high quality prints of each. These movies couldn't look or sound better than what you have here and given the nature of these movies, you'd almost never expect this much care to be taken to release these movies on DVD in any form, much less a good form. You can contrast these with the public domain prints of other Jerry Warren movies (Incredible Petrified World, Terror of the Bloodhunters, Teenage Zombies) and you do get something worth your money here (IF you are looking for low budget horror/sci fi from the 50s and 60s). There isn't much in the way of extras here but what is here is enjoyable. It is an audio reenactment of a portion of an interview with Bri Murphy conducted in the early 90's for a horror mag. You get alot of information about Murphy who did a ton of work on Warren's first films and eventually married him. There's alot of talk about Man Beast and the Incredible Petrified World but neither is included on here. As for the movies, only House of the Black Death looks to be a complete Warren film but it isn't. Harold Daniels directed the majority of House of the Black Death and Warren did brief insert scenes. Attack of the Mayan Mummy and Creature of the Walking Dead are made up of parts of movies Warren bought cheap then shot some new footage to tie them together. Turns out Manbeast was the same thing too (Warren made a movie around stock footage of rock climbers, this is on the first collection). This set isn't as entertaining for me personally because these spliced together movies are painfully dull. Recommended DVD if you are interested in these types of movies because you will get your money's worth.

history.title: Doctor Who: Ghost Light (Story 157) [DVD]
history.review_title: DON'T START WATCHING THIS DOCTOR WITH THIS STORY or with the Curse of Fenric
history.text: I came into the tail end of the original series of Doctor Who much like many fans these days (especially those from outside the UK), via DVDs. I remember watching the show off and on until Season 22 ended. I was only 7 at the time. My family had it on mostly to pass the time. When the show returned, none of us even knew about it. I suspect that was common outside of the UK for the casual fans. The Doctor Who DVDs started sprouting up a decade ago and the treatment for each story was phenomenal. They were loaded with commentaries, documentaries, the works. Each release was like a Criterion Collection DVD. They were hard not to collect. I became a Whovian via the novels (Eater of Wasps did it) and went right to these. The release order from the BBC was a mistake. I suspect they put it up to a fan vote because of the reputation this story has among fans. What the BBC should have done was release these in some sort of sequential order because alot is assumed to be understood by this, the third season of Sylvester McCoy's Doctor and the second for his companion Ace. The reason the Doctor and Ace are even in the mysterious house where all the action takes place is because of some trauma in Ace's past. The Doctor takes her there to confront the causes of it. The Doctor does this quite a bit in Season 26 because for the first time (ever?), the Doctor has complete control of where he can stir his TARDIS. He decides to be a child psychologist or a guidance counselor for troubled teens (even resembles a few). If you are new to the 7th Doctor. You don't pick up on much else if Ghost Light and the Curse of Fenric are your introduction to him. The subplot of Ace's demons is meaningless if you start watching any of the 7th Doctor in the last season because you really don't see enough of the character to care. Ace is a departure from the usual companions because she has serious real life personal problems. She's a runaway, with a penchant for chemistry. She accidentally manages to blow herself up and land across the universe where she is marooned. In that story (see Dragonfire) Ace is given a proper introduction. That story was also clever in that additional characters appear different when you reflect them off of Ace's. A little girl on the planet makes you think what Ace was like as a child, the character Belazs makes you wonder where Ace will likely end up in 20 years if the Doctor where not a part of her life(Start there fans). In Ghost Light ,you don't care about Ace being in the house or why the Doctor takes her there without understanding her history. You also don't understand why the Doctor is doing this either. He does come across as an intergalactic psychologist without the background It's the same exactly with another poorly timed DVD release, The Curse of Fenric. While Sophie Aldred conveys the emotions and is given the lines to do so, the character is not weighted enough in the uninitiated's mind for it to carry the meaning implied. The story is complex and that's fine. SPOILER ALERT (assuming I understood what I saw). A creature uses bodies to maintain his life, his constant change reminds the forces of Light (a character) how much he despises the changes that come with time. He seeks to change (ironically enough) all things that have changed over time back to their original form. Then there's the story which is buried beneath something I can't forgive in this release and that is sound design. Dialogue should not be drowned out by incidental music. Trying to appreciate Ghost Light out of the blue is like trying to appreciate John Coltrane's Live in Japan in one full sitting without ever hearing the man play his alto sax before in your life. Having the dialog buried is something I hope the BBC is having corrected while this is out of print. It's no secret that the show was down to a bare minimum budget and production times were slashed. Sometimes shows can get away with that, Doctor Who was known for it ('All these corridors look the same to me Doctor") this story however is sunk by them. Another problem you can likely tie in to the shrunken budget is the fact this complex story is told in only three half hour episodes. Doctor Who used to run 26 half hour episodes a season, by the time it returned, the series was down to only 14 episodes. I wonder if things were unexpectedly altered to so to fit this into the 14 episode season calendar. Mentioning all this now seems moot since Ghost Light and the Curse of Fenric are both out of print (in the US) and better starting points are in print and readily available (Dragonfire, even the Happiness Patrol) but if I can warn just one other person ahead of time, then the time was well spent. The extras are great on this. The documentary fleshes out the script. There is also some sadness conveyed in it since this was the last original series Doctor Who story filmed in studio. The BBC gave us DVDs introducing many, none obsessive Doctor Who fans to it's final original series Doctor with Remembrance of the Daleks, The Curse of Fenric and Ghost Light. The first is justifiably in print in the US. The other two, it's best to weight and let the Seventh Doctor and Ace settle into your mind. Learn how the Seventh Doctor operates a bit, develop feeling for his companion then enjoy. You will like this once you get to know them

history.review_title: Maybe the only mob movie where not a single gun is fired.
history.text: This may be the only mob movie ever made where not a single bullet is fired. It's not giving away too much given the tone in many of the scenes is highly charged with danger. The story is about a shoe shiner who is pegged by the mob to be a patsy for the murder committed by a friend of theirs because of his resemblance to the assailant. They assigned a disgruntled henchman to watch over him over a weekend and in an act of defiance, the henchman takes the shoe shiner on a weekend trip to Lake Tahoe where the shoe shiner is ironically mistaken to be something that he's not. Things carry on from there and there is both slapstick and subtle comedy meshed well into the storyline. The story is cowritten and directed by David Mamet. Cowriter is Shel Silverstein. With that much talent behind the script and the camera, you know the talented actors will have something good to work with. A recommended movie.

history.title: Haunted Honeymoon (1986, Ntsc, All Region, Import)
history.review_title: It's hard for a movie with this great a cast to be bad but....
history.text: This movie was hard to miss on cable in 1987. Cinemax and HBO sometimes played it twice on the same day, especially on weekends. It seemed movies that did poorly at the box office were sold cheap to cable television and cable TV had no problem beating the movies to death. I also saw Police Academy's 5 and 6, Hot to Trot, Short Circuit 2 and The Longshot constantly. When you are 9 years old, it's easy to find things to stare at. That doesn't make any of these movies good. Haunted Honeymoon has a great cast and some great moments but it is one of the worst films any of these actors ever appeared in. The storyline makes no sense and instead of filling in the plot holes (where does the opening premise of "Scaring him 'to death' go?), it ends with a cheap gimmick. A plot hole is when the narrative changes direction with no explained reason. After sitting through a couple of them in the same film, you're wondering more why things changed than what's going to happen next. Good movies don't have plot holes. Finding ways to fill the plot holes in a comedy usually are the funniest scenes in the movie. An example of this is the ending of Monty Python's Holy Grail. How can we end the search for the grail, the charge of the castle AGGHHH and the case involving the mysterious murder of the historian by the man in armor on horseback? Go see it to see how it ends. A plot hole in The Producers would have been omitting the scenes showing how Max Bialystock was raising the million dollars, an extreme plot hole in that would have been not showing the scenes of the musical "Springtime For Hitler" being performed but instead jumping from before the play starts to the court scene. Luckily neither had plot holes like the Haunted Honeymoon. The humor makes no sense at times either. How could anyone mistake Gilda Radner with a portly cross dresser trying to impersonate the portly cross dressing Dom DeLuise (as Larry Abbot's Aunt)? That made the scene in which this happened implausible and that's not good comedy. Wilder extends the scene which makes it even worse. The opening premise of scaring Wilder's character to shock him out of the bizarre problems he has on his radio show could have been an excellent display of Gilda Radner's talent for characterization. Her character is a radio actor so making use of the character's acting talents would have been a way to show her own creativity. Instead, Radner plays just the actress and she doesn't get much opportunity to expand much beyond being an actress. She has a great dancing scene with DeLuise which is the only memorable scene in the movie. Throughout it all, I felt like I was watching a Mel Brooks movie which was waiting for Mel Brook's humor and cohesion to show up. The cast as I said is exceptional and they were all sadly underused. Wilder is the exception. He gives himself plenty of room to be funny by being in the most scenes but why not share the light a little bit??? It seems like each co star has A single good scene in the movie and nothing more. Paul L Smith as Dr Paul Abbot who introduces the premise of scaring Larry, has a great introduction, then he's all but gone in the rest of the movie. Jim Carter plays the magician Montego. He has no real reason for being there except to just look creepy in a few scenes and to add characters to the whodunit? murder mystery (the death of the portly cross dresser in the beginning) He is mysterious but has no reason to be mysterious and we don't figure out why he's being that way and the story never bother's to explain. You don't get enough of these characters in the story to even add them to the list of murder suspects. You don't get scenes of suspicious behavior later explained away. When the murder is revealed, it's no wonder who it is because he's the most seen male character. These are some of the plot holes. The movie does have its moments but it should have been so much more with the cast Wilder had to work with. it's a shame that this is the end result. This was a missed opportunity and it's no wonder Wilder never tried his hand at writing, directing and starring in the same movie again.

history.title: Manos: The Hands Of Fate
history.review_title: If you're blasting the movie with your review, you're 50 years too late.
history.text: It's a bizarre thing. People who know of Manos: The Hands of Fate still feel the need to mention how bad of a movie it is, then give it a 1 star rating as though they're shocked by that. If it weren't 'the worst movie ever made' would it be given such a 5 star restoration and deluxe DVD release? THAT'S WHY THIS IS 5 STARS. The work done on the restoration, the commentaries, the cute puppet show, everything. This is the Criterion Collection version of "the worst film ever made." Consider the low budget bad movies or just bad movies out there that have fallen through the cracks and will never be heard of again. "The Brain Eaters", "Idaho Transfer", "The Last Shark", these movies are lost but Manos is famously bad. Made famous of course by Mystery Science Theater 3000 in the early 1990's. For people who whine about bad movies, MST3K must be a thorn in their side because there's almost 200 movies that have a cult following that say "C.C. and Company" or the "Curse of the Headless Horseman" will never have. It's almost a shame after seeing what has been done with one. The movie and what is behind it is well known. The film was made on a bet. The writer, director, star had to make a movie to win the bet which he did. These are pictures and they are moving. A lot of the, I think excellent artwork by co-star Tom Neyman is on display. The lengthy screen time of the painting featuring the Master and his dog also the sculpture are good indications that the appreciation is shared with the filmmaker as well. The soundtrack is jazzy and works well throughout. As far as I could tell, there doesn't seem to be any of the canned incidental music floating around during the movie. (If you watch enough low budget films you will hear the same music and sound effects popping up often. Incredible Melting Man's music fills up almost half of the music used in Don Doher's Nightbeast is the most recent example I've heard. Others are Bill Rebane's sci fi/horror movies in the '70's. Sync sound filming wasn't happening during this movie. You could call that an Italian approach to filmmaking. Every line of dialogue and every sound effect you hear is dubbed in later. Unlike Italian films though, Manos has maybe four people voicing the acting parts of all the character's seen on the screen. This gives the movie a leg up on some other low budget horror movies who dwell too heavily on narration which makes everything dull. Beast of Yucca Flats, Monstrosity, Creeping Terror, Monster A-Go Go are more dull than just bad. Low budget filmmaking is what it is. The shots aren't well framed, but you can't worry about retakes or reshooting, or complex setups or adequate blocking for the actors. Time is money. The filming is broken up in 30 second blocks as well. An equipment limitation. But the film is in color. I think that adds to this movie retaining an edge over a lot of films in this category. This is a 5 star restoration. I put this release on the same level as [[ASIN:B001PMRBMW The She-Beast]] Both films were released with great care and attention to the quality of the print and presentation. Both also contain audio commentaries which are good. Recommended for fans of cult movies. YES, the movie is considered BAD. Blasting it for being bad in the review is like closing the barn door after the cows have all left, to coin a phrase.

history.title: Doctor Who: The Twin Dilemma (Story 137)
history.review_title: Dull thud of a story following Caves of Androzani.
history.text: Season finale's tended to be the most exciting story of the season. Why finish this season with Twin Dilemma? I can easily imagine fans of the time trying to maintain interested in this story line after what may have been the greatest regeneration story among all of the classic Doctor Who series. I strongly believe the anticlimatic end to this season with Twin Dilemma set up a disadvantage for Colin Baker's portrayal of the 6th Dr. This isn't near the best of the 6th Doctor stories either. I would have preferred a TV version of Slipback to this. The story in itself is ok. I personally would have liked more time spent with the 6th Dr and Peri in the first episode. It could have been like "The Edge of Destruction" from the 1st Doctor era. The story takes place entirely in the TARDIS with the characters periodically shifting from benevolent in nature to malevolent and with no reason to speak of. The volatile, even manic 6th Doctor at the outset could have explored that aspect of his new persona's introduction. The first episodes starts with this somewhat but it doesn't stay with it. The mystery would be more interesting than the abduction of twin brother math geniuses (abducted for any reason, destroy a planet, appear in a theater production of Hamlet where Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are strangely portrayed by lookalikes. The 6th Doctor era has some excellent stories. I rank this not far behind Timelash, well behind Vengeance on Varos, Two Doctors, Revelation of Daleks, Attack of the Cybermen, Mark of the Rani and even some of the disjointed Trial of a Timelord. It does have an excellent DVD but at this point, anyone bother to read these reviews know the classic Doctor Who DVDs have excellent features which make them like Criterion Collections in that regard. While i am an avid fan of the 6th Doctor. He was the last Doctor I saw as a kid. Not being in the UK and not surrounded by fans of the show, I never returned to it after the hiatus because I never knew it came back until it was far too late.Still, I never felt this story was a a good introduction, and for it to be shown immediately after the fast paced, action filled Caves of Androzani was a bad mistake in my view. Let the notion of a new Doctor build during an off season. Then slam them with the volatile regeneration in a better context than this.

history.title: Doctor Who: The Gunfighters
history.review_title: Much maligned but I like it.
history.text: Alot of people loathe this story and it is definitely credited for being the low point rating wise of the Hartnell era. Compared to some of what follows in the span of the next 23 years, this is like high art in the Dr Who canon but in context, it's not much loved. The criticisms. 1. Dodo is probably the most maligned Dr Who companion character of all time. I don't know why, I don't get it, but there it is. Dodo doesn't get much respect and she is in her 3rd story with The Gunfighters. The trio of Steve, Dodo and the Doctor started with The Ark, carried on to the Celestial Toymaker and then to the old west.This is Dodo's only long storyline and maybe that's why so many 'fans' don't like it. 2. The mix of genres. If you want Sci Fi and monsters you'll get that more in the 2nd Doctor stories. If you want history, you'll get that (alot) with the 1st Doctor stories. Venturing into the American west in the late 19th century must have seemed natural for the producers but unlike others, an entire genre of popular television entertainment isn't devoted to other history stories. I never saw a fleet of TV shows made covering the various characters during the French Wars of Religion in the 16th century. This must have rubbed people wrong at the time and I can understand how that continues to be an issue. The other history stories interwoven the Doctor and his companions into the story well, and they did it well again here in my view. Doc Holiday uses the Doctor as a stooge hoping he'd bare the wrath of the Clanton brothers. That sets the stage of events to follow. 3. Maybe the British doing American figures in history works about as well as Americans portraying prominent British figures. I however enjoyed seeing this because I can easily imagine the actors enjoying themselves. Laurence Payne is excellent as Johnny Ringo. He seems to really get into the role. 4. The singing interludes. Lynda Baron has a lovely voice but why does she or anyone have to sing the scenes we just saw? That is something I don't remember seeing in too many western shows. There was usually just cheesy suspense music. What I liked about the Gunfighters was that to me, it was a typical Dr Who story. The basic formula in every Dr Who serial is, the Doctor and his companions land somewhere, they immediately get knee deep into trouble, find themselves separated much of the time as the plot and suspense thickens and ultimately things seem to about to boil over when the Doctor and his companions turn it all around. Granted, there are no great cataclysms threatening the universe in this story but there wasn't in the Celestial Toymaker, or the Savages either. For history, it is not entirely accurate. Johnny Ringo survived the OK Corral and may not have even been involved in it as it turns out. None of the Earp brothers died before the OK Corral. There were other reasons why the gunfight was fated to take place. It wasn't Wyatt Earp out to get revenge. If you know these things and know how the Doctor can't change history, but observe it and if he gets entangled in it, wriggle out without altering it, then these things may bother a serious Whovian. The earliest Doctor stories felt they had to stress this point hard because of the amount of history stories. Alot of fans msut have been wondering why the Doctor didn't prevent disasters instead of watch them unfold as powerless as those who know nothing of their fates. The Gunfighters is certainly not where I would start with the 1st Doctor. It's a tragedy that The Dalek's Master Plan, The Massacre and The Savages are mostly if not entirely lost and this story remains of the Dr and Steven era.In comparison to those, this story is weak, but it is still worth it if only to hear Steven sing under distress for the Clanton's

history.title: Mystery Science Theater 3000: Volume XXXVIII
history.review_title: Three Season 6 Episodes and One from Season 10
history.text: I mention the seasons these are from because the Mike Nelson era changed considerably over time. It's hard to rate the episodes included. I always liked Invasion USA which is a big red scare movie made in the early 50's. Colossus And The Headhunters is sort of like a poor man's Hercules movie. High School Big Shot is another '50's era B movie about a kid who tries to pull off a million dollar heist aided by the actor who brought the Tribbles to the Enterprise in that Star Trek episode. Not too many fans mention these episodes much. They're not the episodes I would chose to introduce a neophyte to the series. The main reason is the movies aren't as fun in their own right as other movies that were riffed on. The type of movie I would try to introduce someone to the series with is Track of the Moon Beast. Fans of the series will appreciate Track of the Moon Beast the most for Johnny Longbow's wonderful stew recipe. This is a stale 70's monster transformation movie which seemed to be really popular during that era of B movies. If it's not a man turning into a lizard, it's women being turned into bees, or a man and his wife turning into bats, or some American in the Philippines turning into the beast of the yellow night. The riffing was excellent by Season 10 too. The cast had it all down pat by then. Because of the cult nature of the show and that much of this series can be viewed online, there needs to be something more for a reason to buy this and all of the sets. What you are buying is the high quality picture/audio and the bonus features and I appreciated both enough to buy these sets. The original version of High School Big Shot (should you dare to watch it) is included, a short interview with Joel Hodgson speaking about Mike, a featurette on producer Albert Zugsmith who produced such classics as Orson Welles last film directed for a Hollywood studio, Touch of Evil to Invasion USA and Girls Town which was also riffed by MST3K, and a short interview with Leigh Drake who played Kathy Nolan in track of the Moon Beast. If you develop an appreciation for low budget movies, then you'll enjoy half these features, if not then you'll probably only relike the Joel interview.

history.title: The Conversation [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A very European film but made in America by Americans
history.text: If you are a fan of American films but wondered why European films seem so different. Compare this movie to other movies released in the US in 1974. This is not a European film but this has a genuine feel of a European film. European movies in the 60's and 70's tended to have very strong, character driven storylines. There's movies with plots centered around events and stories centered around characters. This is about Harry Caul. Caul is a surveillance expert who knows how important it is to keep a private life as private as possible because he knows what can happen when it is not a secret. The first act unpacks all the aspects of Caul's character as he and his associates Stan and Paul wrap up an assignment. The job seems typical to Caul until he begins to wonder about his employer and what he plans to do to the couple who were bugged. The story continues to center around Caul until his world quite literally falls apart around him. The story never veers away from Hackman's portrayal of Harry Caul. This is not unlike Messer im Kopf, Belle De Jour, Alphaville, The Tenant, or almost all of Fassbinder's films in that the main character's journey IS the story. This certainly might not sit well with American audiences because American films don't often do this. I don't know if the way it was shot influences this as well. There's alot of wide angles, alot of grays and, at times, extreme claustrophobia. Again, the setting reflects Caul and his state of mind. The more we learn about Caul's past, the more we can understand his paranoia and obsessions. This, to me, is the kind of movie a director wants to make when he has the leverage to make it. This isn't light entertainment. This is a stark psychological thriller and one of the best I've ever seen and I've seen alot of them. A classic but don't expect anything like The Godfather, Apocalypse Now or even Rumble Fish from this. I wish Coppola made more films in this vain.

history.title: Mystery Science Theater 3000: XXXVII
history.text: Some of these MST3K episodes are....well....challenging and that's because even though there's jokes and comedy all the time, the movies themselves are still there to be seen and attempted to be appreciated even in a subconscious level. There's some MST3K episodes that I just can't sit through because I get a kind of right twitch when I try to see certain movies. It's not great sign and not what you want from entertainment. Some episodes, you can like right away and those are the classics. This set has some episodes that take a little getting used to. The Human Duplicators is the one Joel era episode. It's a mid 60's sci fi/spy type movie filmed in color. It's the other movie that has Dolores Faith and Richard Kiel in it (Phantom Planet being the first). It also starts George Nader whose films earned him a couple more appearance on MST3K in other episodes (Robert Monster and one from the KTMA season). Hugh Beaumont from Lost Continent fame (yse, that's a joke) also costars in this. The Human Duplicators, for me took a little getting used to. It's goofy, but those ceramic looking 'androids'........I'll just end this here. Escape 2000 Is one of the few Season 7 episodes that were made. This was a vague sequel (same main character but that's about it) to the Italian movie called Bronx Warriors.It's a campy early 80's action movie. Italian B movies from this era were trying to borrow alot from Escape From New York/Mad Max/Warriors and this movie is a good example of it. This felt like an instant classic for me. I was laughing off the bat but the jokes aside, these Italian movies are hilarious in their own right. The Horror of Party Beach is a Season 8 episode which I loved when it aired live. This is a black and white mid 60's horror movie with dead pirates(looked like the deck of a pirate ship to me!) being transformed and brought to life by toxic waste and terrorize the nearest beach community. Just saying the plot is hilarious. Invasion of the Neptune Men. Is another Season 8 episode and it, for me was one of the hardest episodes to sit through. This is a early 60' Japanese action movie with "Space Chief" defending the world against, Invaders from Neptune. There's alot of vagueness going on and kids running around in shorts. It was a struggle but I did eventually learn to appreciate it. It's a good thing that Shout Factory mixes the Joel and Mike episodes together even if it may not have been planned. Not that one is better than the other but the episodes have a different feel to them. A comedians' personality affects how a joke is delivered and the same goes with reading scripts. Proof of this is trying to imagine Joel Hodgson trying to do a Mike Nelson impression and Mike Nelson trying to do a Joel Hodgson impression during these episodes .

history.review_title: An action packed film with a touch of humor and romance.
history.text: This was an entertaining film. The chemistry between Dolph and his girlfriend made the film. There were plenty of fight scenes and shootouts. I loved Dolph's funny one liners. There was nonstop action. There were a few odd mistakes. The main female Russian agent wears a terrible wig for the whole movie for no apparent reason. Also at the end of the film an entire sub of men are poisoned and killed. Minutes later not one of those dead men are visible on the sub. Where did they go? Nevertheless, it's a fun action film. The special FX were well done. Dolph kicks major butt and that's what I wanted to see. Recommended for Dolph Lundgren fans.

The only problem that I have is that DL acted like he had a major crush on a cute African American woman but he didn't give her a big sloppy kiss at the end. They chickened out and backed away from making DL clearly choose her over the cute blonde. It was left in the air. Most of the action is in the last twenty minutes. The characters were well developed. This is a film where DL actually acts more than he fights. Recommended for DL fans and fans of post-apocalyptic films. history.title: WKRP in Cincinnati: The Complete Series [DVD]
history.review_title: They Said It Couldn't Be Done..."They" Were Wrong
history.text: A few years ago, the first season of WKRP was released and was quickly panned for being nothing more than the syndicated version with original music removed. I wrote a lengthy review at that time and commented (among other things) that if they were going to replace the music with elevator music then at least they could have put some thought into it. If Arthur says he hears dogs and their is no dogs in the fake music, there is a problem. I also commented how I felt obtaining the original music would sell WKRP DVDs even if the price had to be jacked up to cover the costs. Enter "The Complete Series". I'm thrilled to say that this is the WKRP I remember, and I didn't notice the elevator music that I read still exists in a couple of scenes. I was also thrilled to see some episodes restored with scenes I hadn't seen is years because of syndication chopping. In a nutshell, this is a great release. It isn't perfect, however. The quality of video is good, but not restored in any way. Some scenes (especially in the pilot) appeared too dark on my TV while others seemed slightly out of focus. It was hit and miss on these and doesn't take away from the whole, but boy would it have been nice to have a clean restored copy! The extras disk was interesting, but left me wondering why Sanders and Bonner weren't part of the reunion. While I'm sure there were budget constraints after getting the music rights, it would have been nice to have some more extras as well. If you love WKRP, you will love this set. It still could be better, but the accomplishment of Shout! in getting this out can't be criticized. What was once a series we were told would never make it to DVD is here and it is wonderful to see the shows uncut again. Great job, and thank you for giving back one of the great series from my childhood!

David does an excellent job of showing how tired Poirot is after having done a job where the guilty soldier kills himself, not being able to have his own compartment on the train the first night, when he is suddenly called back to England for another job with no rest. A real jewel of a movie!

history.title: Cafe Society [DVD + Digital]
history.text: Like Allen's film Crimes and Misdemeanors, Café Society revisits the temptation of adultery and also the temptation of murder, when that power will makes ones own life easier. We see each character to a greater or lesser degree troubled by the moral choices they are required to make, but in the end each of the characters does what he/she want and follow their own desires. The main character, who appears to be Allen himself( the words and delivery are classic WA-especially in the early scenes) is a nebbishy young man who at first refuses a prostitute, but later has no trouble working with gangsters and committing adultery. His uncle leaves his wife when he finds someone he "loves" more. In the end the only character who finds true peace is the gangster on death row, who although he displayed no sign of conscience when committing murder,now finds the promise of eternal life through repentance of his sins.

history.title: Passengers
history.review_title: Avalon, Sleeping Beauty, and the "Good LIfe"
history.text: Last year's space survival film "The Martian" will be brought to mind, but this science fiction story is not really about science, but about what makes a full life - a question as old as Socrates. Without giving away the plot, the characters decide to take a journey believing that in the end they will find fulfillment by creating something in a new world, be it a house or a book. The plan is changed and they must reassess what it means to live and to be fulfilled. In the end their choices and attitudes are believable, as their humanity remains unchanged in spite of changes of time and space. ( if there is any criticism of the plot to be made it would be the odds against the second (accidental) awakening being a ship's officer who can explain the problem, act as a mentor character, then leave the scene so that the Adam and Eve characters can go on alone. Also it seems that once the basic problem is fixed, the two characters could have gone back to sleep - the thin reasoning against this that it is "proprietary" is unconvincing)

While this is to a degree true, it is not something about which to be particularly proud. Just one example, the creation of Iraq out of three distinct and incompatible regions around Mosul, Baghdad, and Basra has led to a century of conflict.

history.review_title: Not a charming film but well acted especially by Daniels and Eisenberg. Not fun to watch people wreck their own lives.
history.text: We might learn more about the early life of writer director Noah Baumbach by watching this semi-autobiographical film than we are comfortable with. The characters that he creates -or perhaps remembers- each have interesting quirks but the adults are not attractive personalities and the two sons are harried and damaged to various degrees. Baumbach did get an Oscar nomination for writing the screenplay. The writing is good but the subject simply does not reward us. I watched it only for the acting. Jeff Daniels builds his character of the brilliant author dad bit by bit until we know him quite well and hate him. Simply put, he is an xxx hole. Laura Linney has less screen time as the mom, also an accomplished writer. Her character also has such flaws that we cannot root for her either. Jesse Eisenberg is very very good as the teen age older son, suffering through adolescence while trying to cope with the flayed marriage of his parents. I only watched this movie to see his earlier work, before he became a star. He handles his task well and we can feel some sympathy for his character. William Baldwin and Anna Paquin play lessor roles. Set in Baumbach's home town of Brooklyn NY the film resides in 1986, apparently his teen years. Baumbach also wrote The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou, which some might have seen.

history.title: Ghost in the Shell (2017)
history.review_title: Fast action, serious subject submerged under shoot'um up story, visual delight.
history.text: Ghost in the Shell Part Robocop, part Frankenstein and part Avatar, Ghost in the Shell, a remake of the 1995 Japanese Aname' animated feature, comes at us hard as a 100% rock'em sock'em no holds bared action flick that totally delivers. This $110 million production delights the eye while providing the kind of action thrills that we yearn for. Poor Major, Scarlett Johansson's character, has nothing left of her physical self save for her brain, neatly tucked into a manufactured body by a nefarious defense company in Japan as a new kind of weapon. Things like this never turn out well. Director Rupert Sanders has managed only one other feature film, the quite acceptable and successful Snow White and the Huntsman. Here he brings the most intensely imagined future city spaces since the incomparable Blade Runner. He scatters giant hologram advertisements around his Tokyo to confuse and mesmerize our eyeballs while at the same time rushing us through the non-stop action. For a particular and fortunately very large slice of the movie going public, this kind of flick brings us rushing into the theater. This make the third time Johansson has appeared as a somewhat more than human heroine after the recent Lucy and her continuing roles as The Black Widow in the Marvel films. She has the backing of not famous but skilled actors, including Michael Pitt, lately of Boardwalk Empire. The writing delivers a double surprise, first this movie satisfies us in all respects even if it comes from a Japanese comic book, not a promising lineage. Second, four writers have their names in the credits, often a bad sign. But this time we get just enough of a back story, slowly revealed to us, about the central character, to keep us interested in her fate. Once again the tiny movie lion, New Zealand, provides the place where the film came to be made. A very great deal of the frames in the film are done with movie magic. The vast invented city in all of its complexity could only exist in a computer. It doe look real, it surely does. Ghost in the Shell runs for a solid two hours and carries a mild PG-13. The non-stop mayhem results if a fair body count but no slow motion blood and guts shots like some films. No language or nudity problems arise. I liked Ghost in the a Shell lot better than Lucy. Lucy did very very well at the box office. Ghost in the Shell is a much better film and I expect it to gather a giant audience.

history.review_title: A very worthy film crushed by a sub par ending.
history.text: Life What could be scarier than to be trapped in a tiny space station with some horrible space monster? What could be more fun than to see amazing space pictures flow across the screen? How did the director get all those actors to float around in the space station, seemingly with no gravity? How does the movie come together to please us? Keep reading. Born in Sweden and never mind his name: Director Daniel Espinosa comes with a couple of very solid movies to his credit. He directed Safe House with Daniel Washington, an absolute knock out in the suspense/action genre. He also directed Child 44, a tight as a fiddle tale set in contemporary Russia. Espinosa knows how to keep us on edge. The writing team of Rett Reese and Paul Wernick have worked with each other numerous times before. The co-wrote Zombielandd, arguably the best Zombie film of all time and a great success commercially. They also penned Deadpool, the stupendously successful and vastly entertaining comic book super hero flick. These writers have mastered the art of the quip. The film has two strong male stars to anchor our attention. Jake Gylienhall and Ryan Renolds (Deadpool) are two of the astronauts in the orbiting space station. They are supported by Rebecca Ferguson, also born in Sweden. The busy Ferguson has three films in release in 2017. In a space/horror flick the actors are not heavily taxed in the drama department and all turn in credible efforts. The film has a lot going for it. Espinosa has a keen eye for faces in his camera lens and the space shots are awesome. The monster is creepy and pretty terrifying, so that's good too. But ultimately the film fails to please. In a recent space epic, Gravity, an astronaut sacrifices himself to save another astronaut. In Life, a whole series of astronauts make heroic sacrifices to save not just their crew mates, but at the end the entire human race. We don't like it when heroism of the highest caliber goes for naught. It makes great courage and great character seem pointless and the entire human experience a futile and nihilistic pursuit. Phooey. Cinematography and clever direction cannot overcome a terrible ending. Life runs for one hour and 43 minutes. It carries a strong 'R' rating for the usual language reasons, but not for naked people. They made this space/horror movie for a fairly modest $58 million and it will do reasonably well and never mind the lack of logic and cheap ending. Just relax and watch the action. Two saw blades.

history.review_title: Instantly forgettable summer filler brightened by some very good acting by Pena and Shepard.
history.text: I watched this at the theater. Chips Actor Dax Shepard will seem familiar to TV viewers. He has appeared in a long line of home screen shows. I had no idea that he also wrote screen plays and directed films. Well, he writes his first big screen big movie with "Chips" and ditto with his screen play. But to write, direct and star in a $25 million Hollywood revival of a classic TV series must be a real thrill for him. Co-star Michael Pena can do anything from very serious drama ("World Trade Center") to a brilliant comic role in "Ant Man" that made that otherwise so so film more interesting for me. He as an astonishing 84 acting credits. Other notable actors include Kristen Bell (wife of Director Dax Shepard) in a smaller supporting role and Jessica McNamee (many TV credits) also in support. I loved Vincent D'Onofrio in his role as a mountain man in the recent "Magnificant Seven". Also appearing are Adam Brody and Ben Falcone in cameos, both solid actors and familiar faces. Jane Kuczmarek who played the mom in "Malcome in the Middle" also serves. Fans will want to watch closely for a quick take of Erik Estrada who played Pena's character in the 1977-1983 TV show. This forgettable, hot weather entertainment tries to break some new comedic ground with a recurring sexual reference joke that didn't break a laugh on the first try. Set in LA, the stream of homophobia jokes also seem flat. What excellence writer/director Dax Shepard gives to the audience comes from discrete moments-many of them as it happens-of very nice bits between actor Dax Shepard and his co-star Michael Pena. Dax plays an earnest (LA style earnest) but dim Mr. Nice against Pena's hard driving FBI man with some character quirks. The not convincing story provides a place to put sight gags and jokes in bad taste-but not any more than that. The Motion Picture Association of America quite rightly awarded "Chips" a hard R rating. The film includes frequent objectionable language issues of the worst kind. Not content with drug use, booze and cigarettes the film has total nudity and many examples of lesser degrees of nakedness. Watch out for some graphic injuries also. Please leave the wee ones at home. The film lasts for one hour and 40 minutes. So far "Chips" has brought $25 million to the box office. Pena and Shepard can only bring the movie to an average three saw blades.

history.review_title: Not much here except plenty of naked and half naked girls.
history.text: Director Sean Ellis made a clever little short. He picked up an Academy Award nomination for best short film. Then he expanded the short into an hour and a half feature film. This version is the result. Ellis reportedly made the expansion in a single week. After seeing the film, I believe it. Lots of naked girls make Cashback interesting. The central character, an art student who suffers insomnia, cannot carry the film alone. Ellis gives him the ability to stop time. The artist uses the time stoppage to disrobe customers in his grocery store and sketch them. All the while he morns his breakup with his girlfriend. It makes pretty thin soup. Ellis does have a good eye with his camera and the cast does well with what they are given.

history.title: BFG
history.text: Charming tale told by the Disney masters but not one of their magical best. A little girl becomes friends with a giant who kidnaps her from a London orphanage. There are some very clever giant hiding in plain sight moments that I quite liked and some gorgeous scenes with dream flickering like neon fireflies. A solid Disney film and good for all ages. One heart stabbing thing that wasn't Disney's fault struck me very hard. At the beginning of the film there is a shot of Westminster bridge, a much filmed spot. It is also the spot where a Jihadi murdered and injured a number of people just a short time ago. We live in sad times.

history.review_title: Truly outstanding Zombie movie from Korea.
history.text: I have watched loads of Zombie flicks, some made in out of the way places (please see my book of Zombie movie reviews "A Gross of Zombies _144 reviews of Zombie movies) but never a Korean Zombie flick. Holy smokes, this one has every thing you want in a Zombie movie and more. What we want is good production values-this one is professional level, even if not as slick as Hollywood's best efforts. We want it to be scary (or sometimes to be funny but scary fits here). Imagine being trapped on a train as a Zombie Apocalypse begins. Our protagonists are faced with increasing numbers of Zombies and fight and flee from car to car. It is terrifying. Why? Because director Yeon Sang-ho carefully took the time to introduce us to the characters before feeding them to the un-dead. The main guy is some kind of fund manager, a guy whose marriage has failed because of his devotion to his work. In an early, situation setting scene, he gives his daughter a Wii game system, only to discover that he had given her one previously, on children's day. So, distant dad takes his little daughter on the Train to Busan so she can spend time with divorced mom. We get not just a rip roaring Zombie flick but a good dose of social commentary as well. The young Korean girls are adorable, totally cute. When they turn you can hear hearts breaking in the darkness. We have examples of genuine heroism and genuine swinish selfishness. Korea is a largely Christian country so we are shown people exhibiting the best kind of Christian virtue-laying down one's life for a friend sort of stuff. And because it is an Asian country, we see Karmic Justice dealt out with satisfying rapidity. The Zombies themselves are jerky but and clumsy but fast. People do have some chance to survive. I always like it when there is an avenue to survival for the characters. Some of the Zombie scenes are very well set up and well imagined. These people really thought about every scene and it pays off for the watchers. This was the 6th highest grossing (hee hee) movie in Korean cinema history. Even with subtitles rotten tomatoes gave it a stellar 97% which is huge. It runs for just shy of two hours and has an R rating. This is one of the very best Zombie movies ever made.

history.text: I was afraid to see this movie. I expected some horrible stuff like Bad Santa or Bad Teacher. I was wrong. The bad moms here might have been called 'over whelmed moms' with more truth. The moms in the movie all try to be the best moms they can be, and it is hard as we parents well know. What results is a fairly conventional comedy with good moments,some good jokes and excellent performances from the main players.

history.review_title: Low grade shoot um up, great cast wasted by terrible script.
history.text: Even the stellar cast cannot save this repetitive offering. They took the standard Jason Statham movie and wrung out any of the things that make his best work interesting, fun and even exciting to watch. The all important connections were just left out and what we have left is a long series of well staged fight scenes. He shoots lots and lots of bad guys but the bad guys might have just as well have been clay pots for all the excitement they generated. The Plot was very thin to start with and by the end slipped off into a parody of a lessor Bond film. Jessica Alba, totally cute, had no chemistry with her co-star. But what do I know? The public lapped it up and made it into a very profitable project.

history.title: Becoming Jane
history.text: Women were property and had no rights. A good marriage (money) was a woman's only way to have a comfortable and respectable life. Jane Austen broke the rules. She wanted to marry for love, not for money or comfort. When you break the rules you will be punished by society, because society holds on tooth and nail to the status quo. That hasn't changed but people ignore a lot of it today (sometimes at their own peril). A great love was lost because the lovers had no control over their own lives. In the end Jane never married, he did, of course, but their love was solid all the days of their lives (not that it did either of them any good). Society is a hard task master. This is a politically loaded movie. Depressing for sure...no happy ending. Having the love of your life name his oldest daughter, from another woman, after you, would not be considered a happy ending in the opinion of most people. Jane, however, seemed pleased. Basically, the man she loved was willing to run away with her and give up everything (or at lest try). But Jane, being "responsible," and deciding for both of them based on an ASSUMPTION, felt that he would resent her later if she took him away from caring for his parents. He tried, she just caved and let the love of her life go. No gold medals for Jane. He went on with his life and was a good boy. She wrote and kind of wasted away. At the end of the movie she looks frail and pathetic next to her sister-in-law who is about 10 years older than she is. It's not a beautiful film either. It's dark and dreary. Even the landscape is miserable looking. Drab...drab...drab. If the drabness was meant to show how people actually felt, it worked perfectly...miserable, dark, dreary and drab. Blah.

history.title: Sherlock Holmes: The Complete Granada Television Series
history.text: Brett IS Sherlock Holmes. He is perfect and each episode is wonderful. He's brilliant. His movements and facial expressions are part of the story. Watson, Mrs. Hudson...each and every character is dead on. Best Sherlock series EVER. Don't miss it. An icon brought to life in the best of ways.

Daniel Craig is a great Bond. In Skyfall he looks worn out and tired. He is wounded, out of shape, and living in a lush paradise somewhere, drunk and pretending to be dead. He looks used up and he is. But one morning, while at the bar, he sees something on the news that catches his attention. He gets up and goes home. Because he was "dead" he is forced to go through a series of physical and mental tests, to prove his readiness to take on the bad guys. And the movie takes off from there. He failed all of the tests, of course, but he doesn't know that until much later. There are some great action scenes and the relationship between 007 and M has never been better. There are a couple of slow parts, now and then, but the villain is wonderful and Bond's sidekick, in the opening scenes, turns out to be someone we know and love. The new Q looks like a 12 year-old geek and is very likable. There is a surprise ending, which means there will be some changes in the next film. Craig brings a complex heart and soul to the Bond character. He is interesting to watch. He's tough, guarded, does what has to be done, regardless of the cost, and yet he seems lost and conflicted. M tells him that "orphans" make the best agents...and maybe she's right. Craig is far less superficial than the other Bonds (although I love Sean). The villain garners our sympathy on some level. He has been severely damaged and abused by the Agency. The torture and abuse made him what he is. All in all it's a great film and Daniel Craig is an exceptional Bond.

history.title: 84 Charing Cross Road
history.text: This is a great film. It is true to the book in every way but one. I do not understand the first and last shots. They were not in the book and kind of take away from the story but they only last a few minutes. The letters are the dialogue and Bancroft and Hopkins are perfect in their roles. I would read the book first, if you are going to do both...but the movie stands alone. The film is a copy of the book and it's wonderful. I highly recommend it.

history.title: Paris: The Luminous Years - Toward the Making of the Modern
history.text: I highly recommend this brilliant film to anyone interested in the artistic and literary geniuses who lived in Paris from 1905 to 1930. No one is left out. Poets, artists, all wonderfully presented. The film shows how poetry influenced the work of painters and vice versa. Too many names to mention but I cannot stress enough how enjoyable, educational and amazing this film is. Black and white, interviews, a lot of original film. Poets, artists and their relationships, as well as how they dealt with the artistic environment that fought against change. I plan on watching this film again and again, just so I don't miss anything. Some subtitles, translations from French speakers to English.

history.title: Aloha [DVD]
history.text: I hadn't heard any of the advance criticism. But I'm a big fan of Cameron Crowe, Bradley Cooper, and Hawaii! Great combination, along with some other fine names: McAdams, Stone, Murray. A complete mess. I couldn't figure out what the plot line was. The Hawaiian location seemed only secondary to the premise of the movie. The performances were awful: is Cooper sincere? is Murray sincere? What is McAdams doing in this movie? Why is Stone so hyper and shrill? Couldn't Crowe have told Stone to turn it down a few notches? Is the movie a love story? An espionage film? A political independence story? A nature vs nuture saga? Unfortunately, it's all of these things. And yet it's none of these things. What a waste of a great cast and location.

history.title: Die Walkure
history.text: I attended the matinee performance that was used for this DVD. Excellent all around! Top honors go to James Levine, Jonas Kaufmann, Eva Marie Westbroek, Bryn Terfel, Stephanie Blythe, and Deborah Voigt. There were many criticisms going around at that time. First, that The Machine was a terrible concept - I thought it was wonderful and evocative. And it created an extraordinary acoustic so that singing at all volumes could be easily heard. Second, that Voigt wasn't up to the task of Brunnhilde. She was certainly better in previous seasons as Sieglinde (a part she nearly owned), but she sang very well in this performance. Kaufmann and Westbroek sang beautifully, looked great, and were ultimately heartbreaking. Terfel and Blythe brought to life their scene together - a scene that is usually a crashing bore. My only quibble is that the final scene between Wotan and Brunnhilde was woefully misguided - it was more about acrobatics than colossal heartbreak. Brunnhilde was perched high atop The Machine, and it wasn't even Voigt, but a double. It could've been so much better. For the best Wotan-Brunnhilde scene, you have to watch James Levine's previous endeavor with James Morris and Hildegard Behrens.

history.title: Verdi: Otello
history.text: I attended one of these Vickers/Scotto performances, but before I knew much about opera. This is a great performance. Vickers is truly terrifying as the towering leader brought low by malice. Scotto is a riveting Desdemona. She doesn't take her destiny lying down. MacNeil however overacts the villainous Iago. Why would Otello believe him? As for the singing, Vickers gives everything he has, but I prefer Domingo (his voice is far more beautiful, and he's a more wounded hero than a ferocious one). Scotto sings a beautiful Verdi line, especially her famous pianissimo, and she makes you believe it's really happening before your eyes. Fleming and Te Kanawa, on other DVDs, sing far more beautifully, but they're very simple characterizations (although Verdi said that's what he wanted). I highly recommend this DVD, but I'd buy Domingo/Fleming or Domingo/Te Kanawa as my first choice.

history.title: Bette Midler: The Showgirl Must Go On
history.text: I saw this show in Las Vegas. I'm not a 'Vegas' kind of guy. I don't like gambling, casinos, or splashy shows. But I was very pleasantly surprised by Bette Midler. She sang, danced, told jokes, did some dramatic scenes, and was overall astonishing. I don't know where she got the energy to pack all that entertainment into one performance! I bought this DVD to replay that great experience.

history.title: Son of Saul
history.text: Although there have been fine movies about the Holocaust (Schindler's List, Sophie's Choice, Judgement at Nuremberg), Son of Saul is on a different level altogether. It brings you right into the gas chambers and ovens. Almost too much to bear, but an important viewpoint. Some of the comments here are odd -- they didn't like the ending. Well, millions of people were being murdered, it's not The Sound of Music!

history.title: Eugene Onegin
history.text: The Met's beautiful production, which I just saw again a few days ago with Peter Mattei as Onegin. There is already a fantastic DVD available from the Met with Dmitri Hvorostovsky and Renee Fleming, an excellent portrayal of the opera. But this one might be even better with the great Russian diva Anna Netrebko and Kwiecien, along with a great Lenski, Beczala. When I saw this performance in the theater, we all gasped at the end -- Tatyana gives Onegin a big luscious kiss -- and we all thought, 'are they changing the ending? Will Tatyana leave Gremin after all?' No, of course not. She was showing Onegin what he was going to miss in his life. Unfortunately, Gremin is sung poorly. It's a small role, but important. If the role is sung well, you realize that Tatyana has a real struggle. Both DVDs are very worthy and should be in your collection as a first choice. The only drawback is that Onegin was sung and acted even better by Mattei in the recent revival. Kwiecien, in comparison, almost fades into the scenery.

history.title: Strauss: Elektra - James Levine Metropolitan Opera Exclusive DVD
history.text: A landmark recording, not only of this opera, but perhaps all operas on DVD. During the 1990s, the two greatest Elektras were arguably Hildegard Behrens (whose portrayal is that of a wounded animal) and Gwyneth Jones (who portrayed a tigress, ready for the kill). Very different, both valid. Here we have Behrens who inhabits the vocal/acting role so completely, it's like watching history unfold before you. She is partnered by Deborah Voigt, who was perhaps at the peak of her vocal powers. James Levine conducts the score as if he's writing the music anew; remarkable. The staging is perfectly suited to the story -- a lopsided world of black, white, and shadows. The only weak link for me is the Klytemnestra of Brigitte Fassbender. She is a notable concert artist, but here she alternately screams, staggers, and foams at the mouth. I don't know how Elektra doesn't burst out laughing at her behavior. A dignified queen would give Elektra a substantial battle. But anyway, this performance is the real deal. If you can find it at a decent price, grab it.

history.title: Hello Dolly!
history.text: I actually saw the original film release in 1969. Wonderful movie, but so utterly out of place during the Vietnam/Nixon/Hard Rock era. The passage of time has been good. Now it can be seen as a step back in time to a long-ago era, like an old operetta. Streisand reportedly never cared for the film, but she's actually fantastic. Yes, she's incongruously young, but she looks great, dances like a pro, tosses off her lines with the appropriate comedy or poignancy. AND THAT VOICE! She just soars like a comet. The BlueRay is quite an improvement over the original, and also fine, DVD.

history.title: Moonlight
history.text: I was looking forward to seeing this highly awarded movie. And now I'm completely baffled. A fill-in-the-numbers collection of ethnic grievances. Self-conscious and irritating camera work. Paper-thin plot. Over the top performances. I wanted to turn it off, but felt obligated to watch it till the end. And this won the Oscar for best picture? Well, that's proof that Hollywood has been cowed into the latest politically correct mineshaft. I will never watch it again and wouldn't dream of recommending it to anyone I like.
