history.text: The movie that answers the question for the ages: "What if Robin Sparkles had taken time off from cheesy music videos and sexually suggestive kids shows to make a movie!?" If you're of the "so bad it's good" philosophy, then this is a prime candidate. Otherwise it's just bad. Very, very bad. If you get the "How I Met Your Mother" reference, you might actually get a laugh out of this movie. After watching this movie (in fast forward obviously) I can only assume that Robin Sparkles and Jessica Glitter were based on Dru-Anne Perry and Gina Calabrese.

history.title: Passengers
history.text: I loved this movie because it is a sci-fi movie with high production values, two main actors that I really like, and two supporting actors that I really like, and because it was (sort of) romantic without being too over the top. But what really intrigued me about the movie was the underlying question of the morality of what the male lead did. Obviously it was bad, but just HOW bad. Where does it fall on the scale between really bad practical joke and murder?

history.title: Arrival [Blu-ray]
history.text: Amy Adams did a fantastic job as did Jeremy Renner. The story is very thought provoking. I confess I didn't actually figure out what was going on with the weird flashbacks until close to the end of the movie, but I loved it once I figured it out. I don't really buy the "aliens existing outside of the constraints of time" thing, but maybe that's because, as a Christian, that's essentially how we think of God. (Having created time, He exists outside of time.) But the exploration of the concept is certainly more entertaining in this setting. I also ABSOLUTELY LOVE the alien design. Virtually every creature on earth exhibits (external) bilateral or radial symmetry. I keep waiting for some adventurous designer to think outside the box and make a sentient life form without bilateral (or radial) symmetry. This one doesn't quite go outside the box, but it certainly gets close to the wall. I personally would have enjoyed a little more exploration of how they figured out the linguistics, but I suspect they would have lost a lot of the audience in so doing.

history.title: Live Die Repeat: Edge of Tomorrow
history.review_title: This Movie Didn't Get Nearly Enough Attention [Mild SPOILERS]
history.text: Great movie. I'm a big Sci-Fi fan and Tom Cruise fan (the actor, not the Scientologist) so maybe I'm a little biased. Like Oblivion, I always appreciate a high production value Sci-Fi movie, and Tom Cruise as the lead is icing on the cake. Usually, I'm not a big fan of time travel - time shifting - sort of movies, but this one (along with Arrival) is a definite exception to that rule. I also really appreciated the humor involved in his predicament, particularly when Emily Blunt's character almost shoots him in the head (for the umpteenth time) AFTER he has lost his reset button. EDIT: Sorry. I think she actually tries to STAB him, not shoot him.

history.title: Jack Reacher: Never Go Back
history.review_title: Um.... The First Jack Reacher Movie Was Great!
history.text: The producers should have taken their own advice from the title. This movie was pretty disappointing compared to the first one. Of course that statement applies to the vast majority of sequels. Even so, it wasn't awful, it was just... forgettable. UPDATE: I think one of the things that just kills this movie is the casting of Cobie Smulders as the female lead. Don't get me wrong, I loved her in the series "How I Met Your Mother", but that's part of the problem. I don't know if it's her acting or just my perspective, but in just about every scene I kept expecting her to deliver one of those priceless, unintended punch lines. Unfortunately, Jack Reacher being decidedly NOT that kind of movie, it makes every scene she's in kind of uncomfortable to watch. Add to that the fact that her counterpart in the first Reacher movie was Rosamund Pike and Cobie Smulders just never really had a chance.

history.title: The Magnificent Seven
history.text: Answers the age old question: "Can you really take a bunch of good actors and make a crappy movie?" Yep. Yes you can. Okay, crappy is a bit harsh. But when you start out with a budget busting cast, and some of the best source material around, you better make one heck of a good remake.

history.title: The Imitation Game (Blu-ray + Ultraviolet)
history.review_title: Watched a Movie, Fell Asleep, Woke Up to a Sermon About Not Being Evil to Gay People
history.text: Pretty interesting plot, but it does run on a bit. And then they just couldn't resist the ten minute sermon about how history has been so mean to gays... even the really smart ones! To be fair, it was pretty abominable at times, but I tend to watch movies for their entertainment value rather than their persuasive value. Maybe I'm just weird that way.

history.title: The Martian
history.text: Loved this movie... mostly because of Matt Damon (since he gets about 80% to 90% of the screen time), not because I'm some huge Matt Damon fan, but because his acting was just excellent in this movie in particular. And to be honest, the whole cast was excellent. Kudos to the director. One thing I really love about the movie is that, while the run time is not at all what I'd consider excessive, the story line is pretty epic, as in, it covers a lot of ground with great economy of time and yet doesn't feel rushed. This is just a beautifully made film and at least seems pretty realistic. It isn't one of those films which paints an overly rosy picture of Mars being made habitable. Side note: Personally, I don't think terraforming Mars is physically possible unless we figure out some way of partially melting part of its core. Without a partially fluid metallic core, there's very little magnetosphere to guard from solar winds. Without a fairly decent magnetosphere, most of the atmosphere that is present gets blasted away. So you can make atmospheric gases 'til the cows come home and you're not going to get an atmosphere that hangs around long enough to sustain much of anything. One might argue that you could create an underground ecosystem, but why go 34 million miles to do that when you could do that on the moon (with fairly epic advances in technology at least,) or for that matter, right here on Earth. But I digress. In other words, I like this movie because it has a gripping story line, is a high production value sci-fi movie (which are much too few and far between for my taste), and because, despite it being sci-fi, it doesn't overtax my suspension of disbelief for the most part. And especially because the acting is so darn good.

history.title: Hacksaw Ridge [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital]
history.review_title: My War Film Gore-o-Meter Just Got a New Number.
history.text: Pretty inspiring story. But WOW! They really turned the gore factor up a notch from level 10 (Saving Private Ryan) to 11. Made it actually kind of difficult to watch. Of course I grew up in the late John Wayne era, where many a brave actor fought and died though nary a drop of fake blood was spilled... 'cept maybe a little dribble from the corner of the mouth for the close-ups.

history.review_title: How This Movie is Like Going to a Prostitute
history.text: I suppose it could have been worse. I could be like some of these poor souls who actually read the books and so were somewhat emotionally invested. Stars the perennially meh Brad Johnson and discount Laura Dern (Emily Lloyd). The only actual halfway passable acting in it was Jonathan Cake as Nero. Each of the main characters except for Brad Johnson is some famous historical figure: Alice Liddell (Alice in Wonderland); Nero; Samuel Clemens. Not sure about the African Princess woman, (producers walkin' that fine line between cultural appropriation and full blown racism in that character) or the Nazi death camp NOT survivor (can we fit any more stereotypes in here?) Of particular note, acting-wise is Brian Moore as the alien Monat: His performance is particularly awful for a main character. I want to know why all the people come back with essentially perfect bodies, but the alien gets a perpetual head spasm for no apparent reason. It seems unlikely to be an evolutionary advantage, universal among his species. Whatever. Maybe he was just trying to distract us from the really lame make-up. He's probably one guy who was glad the movie didn't get picked up as a series. Could you imagine going to work every day having to pretend to have Parkinson's disease? That's what he was in for. Pretty much all the other characters just get grunts and grrrs or whimpers and screams depending on whose side they were on. I just watched this movie. It was bad enough that I had managed to block out the fact that I had already seen it a few years ago and didn't remember that fact until about two-thirds of the way through it. The story line actually does seem decent; I might even consider checking out the book series (although I suspect I'll just take a shower and try to block out the whole sad incident from my memory again.) The director has to feel a sense of accomplishment for this made for TV movie though - it seems like he managed to squeeze in every cliche from his list of cheesy movie cliches. Don't watch this movie unless you are craving the loss of two hours of your life followed by a deep sense of regret.

history.title: Psychic School Wars: Movie [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A Pretty Trainwreck of a Film
history.text: I'll start with saying this: this movie is pretty. The colors and visuals are great to look at. But just looking pretty doesn't make this a great or even good movie. The plot is a mess. Characters do things for reasons that aren't explained very well. The movie also doesn't seem to know what it wants to be. A light slice of life? A school romance? A mystery that the heroes have to solve? It has all these things yet when one scene is light and comedic then immediately followed by drama it gets jarring to say the least. The movie also expects to just already know things about the characters and backstory. Does some elements of the plot need to be further explained? Yes. Does the film explain why or how? Of course not. You should already know, duh. The film is based on a book to my knowledge and it has been adapted before, so maybe those other iterations have the answers this telling ommits? Maybe, but this story should stand on its own without the need to look into previous established lore in alternate versions. I should at least try to summarize the plot, too. There are a trio of friends, the generic male lead, his female childhood friend that is obviously in love with him yet he never notices, and her big breasted friend whom the male lead is in love with for reasons that aren't established. Then a mysterious transfer studint, who is totally not Kaworu from Eva, shows up and weird things start happening to their friends and other classmates. There is also some plot device about cell phones that goes no where. The characters are bland. Like really bland. The main lead has no interesting personality or any uniqueness. The childhood friend is a run of the mill tsundere trope, getting angry at lead boy but pine for him in secret. The big breasted girl, well has big breasts. And is, like, totes nice. And Kaworu is there too. Oh, wait, no I forgot, he's totes NOT Kaworu. Should you buy this film? No, I don't think so. It's worth a rent, I'll give it that, mostly for its pretty visuals.

history.title: Engaged to the Unidentified [Blu-ray]
history.text: Might have minor spoilers. If you're scrolling through Crunchyroll and are in the mood for a totally bland, boring series, then you've hit the jackpot! Engaged to the Unidentified is a bad series. It's boring, unfunny, not romantic and after finishing the series you're unlikely to remember any scenes or moments from this monitinous drag of an anime. The story centers around a generic 16 year old high schooler, like countless other anime heroines, who is to marry a mysterious person from her past. I'll just spoil the twist since it doesn't really matter and the series never uses the premise in any interesting manners. So the person that anime girl is engaged to is like a dog person. Or something like that. Cool, right? Not really, since this character is beyond boring and hardly ever speaks. If you think you're going to get a charming anime romcom; look elsewhere. The two leads have zero chemistry. There are of course, the whacky side characters such as dog person's annoying little sister (Who is clearly there to be the OMG Kawai! character) and anime girl's older sister, who has a little sister... fetish? And is the best character in the show; although she does get tedious at times. There are other characters as well, but none are particularly important nor memorable. The show tries to add some supernatural elements to the standard slice of life romcom anime but does so poorly. The fact that anime girl is engaged to a shapeshifting dog person is never explored in detail. Nor does the anime use that for comedic purposes. If the show never utilizes the bizarre nature of the situation, then what's the point? It just becomes an anime about a girl and a boy who can also shapshift, but never does. That's extreamly entertaining. Throughout the series the two leads never bond aside from dog person constantly saying he loves anime girl, but that's just lazy writing. I don't think this the worst anime of all time or anything but it certainly is not good. The show is just so generic and run of the mill without any outstanding personality that I can not in good faith recommend this anime. If you are looking for a similar anime that does a romcom far better than this, then I'd recommend School Rumble.

history.title: Plastic Little - The Adventures of Captain Tita (Essential Anime Collection) [DVD]
history.text: Plastic Little, an anime film that knows it's bad and relishes in that fact. The 'plot' follows Captain Tita, a 'pet shop hunter', as she comes across a girl, Elysse, on the run from some shady people and desides to help her out. The plot doesnt really matter in this anime as its main draw is its fan service (And there is a good amount!). The animation is good and fluid; looking like old school anime, or at least mid-90s anime. The characters aside from Tita and Elysse get very little to do, but with a run time of about an hour, I don't mind. There isn't much substance in Plastic Little and I doubt anyone involved with the project thought they were making the next Akira, but they did succeed in making a short, fun adventure anime. So if you're looking for something to watch and willing to turn your brain off for an hour, then Plastic Little won't let you down. The nudity is an added bonus..

history.title: Princess Jellyfish - Complete Series - S.A.V.E.
history.text: Princess Jellyfish is an enjoyable yet short anime that follows the daily lives of a group of nerdy, geeky women (Dubbed the Sisterhood) who live in the same apartment complex. Their lives get turned upside down when one member of the sisterhood befriends a charismatic male crossdresser who then decides to visit her complex. I would recommend this anime to anyone that enjoys whacky comedy as well as some romantic moments. The characters are all unique and have their own identity, be it loud and boisterous to quiet and timid. Princess Jellyfish is a very unique show and my summarization doesn't give the show justice. The animation is great, the characters are interesting, the general plot is good and the show has a very fun atmosphere. The only real issue I have with the show is that it leaves things very open ended. Like Berserk, one would have to pick up the manga to continue the story. That aside, I highly recommend this anime.

history.title: Love Chunibyo & Other Delusions - Heart Throb
history.text: The sequel to Love Chunibyo and Other Delusions, Heart Throb does not add new plot twists to the previous story and it continues along with the same slice of life formula of its predecessor. There is one new character, a girl that Yuuta knew in the past and may harbor feelings for him. There is a love triangle thing that occurs in this season, a few one off episodes dealing with the other main characters and that's about it. The relationship between Rikka and Yuuta is still trotting along slowly (A bit too slowly, but hey, they're new to this) there aren't any big romantic moments between them but they are still pretty cute together. Heart Throb is more episodic than the previous series but doesn't have such a confused vision of what it wants to be or what its message is. At its heart this is just a cute romcom anime with quirky characters and is a good watch for a quick pick me up. If you liked the first Chunibyo then you'd likely enjoy this as well. Just don't expect too much.

history.title: Shiki: The Complete Series [Blu-ray]
history.text: In Shiki residents of a small secluded village in Japan people begin dying off mysteriously after the arrival of a suspicious family. The village doctor Toshio Okazi tries to find the cause of these deaths and put an end to them even if he has to do some shady things in the process. Shiki is a slow show. Like really, really slow. I almost dropped the show multiple times but I convinced myself it would get better. It does get better in the second half as the story kicks in and the slow build pays off. The towns people start to fight back against the Shiki, vampire like creatures that were the cause of the random deaths. The show tries, however, to make the viewer sympathetic towards the Shiki by going over their own inner monologs and povs. It is hard to feel sympathy for them when they were the ones who attacked first. The show tries to make the viewers question the morality of both sides, human and Shiki. I don't think it works if you paint one side as villainous and evil only to then flip flop and say otherwise. The show's pace is slow and may be a turn off for some viewers and I completely understand. I would say watch a few episodes before you judge but you'd have to watch a lot to do so. I hesitantly recommend Shiki, but maybe read the summaries of the first few episodes as the show takes a while to get going. If you like these kinds of shows, and don't mind the snail's pace the show starts at, then by all means pick it up.

Unless you really want to watch Goku fight Beerus again (Only now with cheaper animation) along with a lot of filler, then go ahead and pick up this set. You're better off waiting for when the US releases finally get to the Universe 6 arc, or even better, the Goku Black arc. Super starts rather slow and it takes a while for it to pick up steam, but the show does get better and is now almost on par with the original DBZ in terms of action.

This is by far the best season of Pokemon since the original Kanto days. The animation is more stylized and doesn't look as generic as the previous seasons of the show. This series also has a more laid back tone, taking a more slice of life approach rather than having one continuous arc. I've watched episodes both in the original Japanese and the dubbed English and both are fine. There are some more mature episodes as well that surprised me and the drama wasn't put aside for unnecessary jokes. This a fun show and is the first Pokemon series to actually feel like an anime.

history.title: Boys Be... Box Set
history.text: This anime is a mess. Boys Be... is a romantic/comedy anime that follows 3 boys as they enter the world of dating. There are a variety of girls that the boys interact with, some resulting in romance, some in heartbreak. That so far is fine, but the issue is that there are far too many side characters that the main trio are overshadowed and left underdeveloped. For the first few episodes it's like a new girl every episode that simply disappears in the next with no mention of said character. The animation itself is poor at best and frequently the characters are off model. The ending too is not an ending, rather the series just stops. There are no resolutions or any real feeling of growth for the characters (Two in particular are especially infuriating). The show would have benefited with more episodes and less side characters. I don't particularly think this is an anime that absolutely deserves a purchase, but if you want a series that builds then abruptly stops, then you may like this anime.

history.title: MARTIAL CLUB - Hong Kong Shaw Brothers 1981 movie DVD (Region 3 / R3)(Full Restored From The Original Film) Gordon Liu, Kara Hui, directed by Liu Chia Liang (English subtitled)
history.text: One of the better Shaw Brothers films, with intense competition and deception between martial groups in South China. A northern expert comes to find the best club in town. Of course courtesy and honor are the requisite traits of true masters!

The 3 stars are just for the fight scenes, which are pretty well done. The movie itself is an example of Hong Kong comedy, circa 1980, which I admit to having a strong aversion to due to its silly, slapstick character. The young "hero" is not actually a eunuch, but gets involved in a myriad of palace intrigues, including conspiracy, theft, betrayal and even murder. It's all a little ridiculous because the hero is a bit of a dopey sap, and sometimes seems to engage in extreme risks merely on impulse. There are several strong sexual references in the movie but they are distinctly adolescent and more annoying than funny or provocative. The only nudity involves the bare backsides of old men, also annoying though intended to be humorous. After thinking about these criticisms maybe I should have given it 2 stars! And the soundtrack was left in the original Cantonese not translated into Mandarin or English.

history.title: Boogie Nights [Blu-ray]
history.text: This is such a great film. You actually feel invested in the characters and care about what they go through being in an industry that's frowned upon (not by most people, but by a lot). The plot goes in directions that you don't expect, and there's a surprising amount of bloody violence that actually feels necessary and not just thrown in for violence's sake. Paul Thomas Anderson is one of the greatest directors working today, and I consider this to be his second best movie ("There Will Be Blood" is first). Plus, if this movie can make me take Mark Wahlberg seriously, it must be good.

history.title: Punch-Drunk Love (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Hate It or Love It -- I Hated It Then Loved It
history.text: When I first saw this movie, I hated it. I didn't know what the hell was going on. The main character was uncomfortable to watch because I didn't get what his problem was. Things just happened. But then I revisited it. And it was different. It became a beautiful and odd tale of a depressed man with repressed anger who meets the love of his life and must fight for her protection when a phone sex worker he calls begins threatening him with physical violence if he doesn't give up all his cash. It's a bizarre movie that can and will definitely put people off, I can definitely say that. But for someone who's willing to sit down and watch a cinema genius' first attempt at a love story, with very humorous moments, artsy transitions and a great soundtrack, as well as a really good performance by Adam Sandler, this is worth a look.

history.title: The Place Beyond the Pines [Blu-ray]
history.text: I like Derek Cianfrance's films. I'll never forget the impact "Blue Valentine" left on me. I had seen films involving failing relationships, but that film was an autopsy of a failed relationship, and it was absolutely heartbreaking the whole way through. I loved it so much that I had to see Cianfrance's take on a bank robbery film. And man, is this film just as amazing, if not more than his previous outing. Not only are the performances stellar in this, but the directions the story goes blew my mind. This is a very ambitious film and it pulls all the right stops, in my personal opinion. It was a beautiful drama that spans two generations and had unexpected moments that stayed with me long after the movie ended. I love it.

history.title: Stranger Things Season 1 4-disc DVD / Blu-Ray Collectors Edition Box Set (Exclusive VHS Box Style Packaging)
history.review_title: One of the Best Shows I've Ever Seen
history.text: This is one of the best original shows from the "LMAO ROFLMAO IM DYING WHO DID THIS STAY WOKE I GENUINELY FIND LELE PONS FUNNY" generation. It has scenes of really well-built tension, humor and moments that deserved to be ranked as some of the greatest scenes in TV history (there's a scene involving Winona Ryder and some strung up Christmas lights that will blow your mind when you realize how creative and visually beautiful it is at the same time). I highly recommend this for anyone who's in need of a "binge-worthy show" fix.

history.title: Kingsman 2: The Golden Circle
history.review_title: It Sucks. Never Watch It. Please.
history.text: This is one of the worst movies I have ever seen, and I have seen way too many films to distinguish which ones are good and which ones are bad. I think the first "Kingsman" film is one of the best and most fun comic book-based films I've ever seen (yes, it's based off a comic book). It has character arcs, genuinely funny lines and moments, great visuals and frenetic actions sequences that have been analyzed and studied by numerous critics and DIY filmmakers like myself. The sequel is the biggest piece of sh*t I have ever had the misfortune of watching. I hated this movie so much that I felt personally insulted by Matthew Vaughn and everyone involved for wasting my time with this extremely disappointing, low-effort pustule of a movie. The humor is gone, the characters you met and loved in the first film are played by bored actors in this one, the villain is not even close to being as interesting as the first film's villain (and this film's villain has the stupidest, most nonsensical motive), the action isn't engaging or feels like it has any weight/consequence, and even the music is ear-piercingly awful. There is one good fight scene near the end that is ruined by a COUNTRY cover of Cameo's "Word Up." I despise this movie with all my being. The death of my excitement for a third film is more tragic than Elton John's overlong cameo in this movie. Please save your money and time. Never watch this. Don't even rent it from a library for free. I cannot think of a worse moviegoing experience I've had this year. And I saw "The Book of Henry."

history.title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer [Blu-ray]
history.text: This is a very polarizing film. The director himself is a very polarizing person because he doesn't make easily accessible films. "The Lobster," which is his best known film so far, was more enjoyed by viewers than hated, but some didn't understand the stilted delivery of the strange dialogue, the repetitive use of classical songs or just the overall bizarre universe the film takes place in, "The Killing of a Sacred Deer" takes the things most judged in "The Lobster," and cranks it up to 11. The disturbing content here rivals Lanthimos' own "Dogtooth," a film I highly recommend. To avoid spoiling the main plot, the basic story is about a surgeon who occasionally takes care of a teenaged boy, but the boy begins to show his true, disturbed colors and threatens to destroy the surgeon's life and family. Not everyone will enjoy it. The pacing can be slow for some, the dialogue/performances might make viewers angry over how nonsensical and emotionless it all is, and the payoff might not feel worth the wait. But for anyone willing to accept the world Lanthimos gives to us, the movie proves to be a Kubrickian-styled thriller based off Greek mythology with every aspect being vital to the overall experience. There is no other way this film could have been portrayed as effectively as how Lanthimos tells this story. The tension is effectively built, the emotionless dialogue makes the viewer feel the frustration they wish the characters would show, and long after it's over, you will want to discuss the metaphors, symbolism and motives of certain characters because this movie doesn't spoon feed the viewer whatsoever. It's definitely not for everyone, but it's also not the worst two hours you'll spend watching something. I know it was a great use of my time.

history.title: Dear Zachary: A Letter to a Son About His Father
history.review_title: The One Documentary That Broke Me
history.text: This is a documentary that will break you emotionally. I cannot describe how hard I cried watching this. While some of the editing choices were out of place, it does not take away from the impact of what you're watching. This is a must see, but not one you'd want to watch multiple times. It will leave you shaken, sad, angry and you'll want to call everyone you know after it's done. The proceeds made from this film go to a great cause that I implore you to support. This is a very important movie to watch. And it's not all sad; there are very funny and charming moments and great footage that'll immediately make you feel close to the subject of the film. It's a shocking emotional rollercoaster of a documentary that deserves to be watched at least once. One time is all you need.

history.title: It's Such a Beautiful Day
history.text: One of the most interesting animated films I've ever seen. Don Hertzfeldt is an artist who should not be overlooked. While he's known for his comedic short films, "It's Such a Beautiful Day" successfully blends comedy with tragedy and can even leave you reevaluating how you live your life. You can tell a lot of painstaking work went into it and it pays off unbelievably well. The bluray also contains "World of Tomorrow," another great short film, and other works by Hertzfeldt that are worthy of multiple viewings if you're ever in need of a pick-me-up.

history.review_title: Brilliant Portrayal of the Life and Times of Hugh Hefner
history.text: Once I started watching the first episode, I was hooked; couldn't stop watching until there was no more to watch. Although in many places I find it to be quite irritating, it remains as truthful and accurate as I can imagine a documentary series ever will be. This is a fast-paced, entertaining documentary about the life of Hugh Hefner and the story of the Playboy empire, with a great deal of its folly, some of its tragedy, all of its beauty, and most of its ugliness laid out with incredible frankness and honesty for all of us to learn from. There are a lot of very beautiful, naked women and even some R-rated sex, but nothing gratuitous there; the story of Hugh Hefner's life simply cannot be accurately depicted without those elements. Observations about the influence that Playboy had on the culture of the time might seem to be overly self-congratulatory, but within my experience, they are spot on. While it's tragic that rabid support for corrupt power-mad totalitarian politicians became inextricably entangled with Hefner's original quest for personal freedom, it's nevertheless true that Playboy was instrumental in communicating that odd mixture of philosophies to an entire generation of people who became the media moguls of today. I was there to watch these things happen. When Hefner started Playboy magazine, I was just 3 years old. I grew up as Playboy grew, so to a great extent, the events depicted in this documentary are the story of my life. In the voice-over at the beginning, Hef tells us that this the story of Playboy, "at least as I remember it." I can honestly say that, for good or for ill, the events are described are accurate as well as I remember, too. When I was 10 years, old, my family moved to Hef's home state of Illinois. I even graduated from the same school, the University of Illinois, albeit 23 years after he did. The continuing tragedy is that even to this day, Hefner has never realized that he actively supports the very things that he detests. His "women's movement" encounter should have taught Hefner that these politicos have no interest in the welfare of anyone but themselves--their only paradigm is their own personal power and their only tool is hate--and today you just need to turn on the television to see them still at work with the same one paradigm and the same one tool. Amusement for Hefner fans: I actually ran into Hef and his then-girlfriend Barbie Benton while I was at the University of Illinois. My first hint was in the morning. I'd been out flying at the Willard Field, the university's airport, and as I landed my little Piper airplane I saw that iconic black DC-9 aircraft with the bunny on the tail parked on the apron. The actual Hef sighting was a little later. Hef and Barbie were on their way into a bar called Stan's Gridiron while I was on my way out. Would it be unseemly for me to turn around and follow them back in, just for a bit of a gawk? Aw heck, nobody noticed me anyhow. Golly; Barbie Benton in the flesh. Oskee-wow-wow. I learned later that they were in town so that Barbie could pose for a local sculptor. Bumped into them again a few years later at the Johnson Space Center, where I was working and they were touring. Barbie was wearing a stretchy tube top when she tried on a space suit. To get into the top, you have to stretch your arms over your head, so... well... America's space program is mostly memories these days; some of those memories are more pleasant than others. We always remember close encounters with celebrities; that's one of the things that really distinguishes them as celebrities. Dick Gregory's description of the Chicago Playboy Club is spot on--the drinks were stiff and the food was great. I got my Playboy Card when I was 21 years old, and that place was a must-do on frequent visits to the Windy City. I don't even remember the menu on the buffet, but I do remember that it was mind-boggling. Ditto for the St. Louis Playboy club. Those were the days!

history.review_title: Low-budget portrayal of a long worn-out theme
history.text: A handful of quite good actors muddle their way through an unrealistic drama where the stereotypical British officer stereotypically orders his troops to commit suicide by attacking the German trenches, just like in movies about Gallipoli. It would be a wonder that the Brits could win the war with such incompetent officers, but the stereotypical German solders seem to be even more nuts. Meanwhile it's tragedy and angst all around when the pregnant wife back homes dies while trying to get an illegal abortion of some other man's baby. War is unpleasant, and WWI was especially nasty and pointless.

history.review_title: So bad it's an insult to the audience
history.text: "The Temple of Doom" is the movie that put me off Indiana Jones movies--so bad that I never again when to see one of the films in the theater. I watched it again in Amazon Prime to make sure and, yup, my memory serves me well. Despite its high budget and top-notch star, this is one of the worst movies ever made. We spent the entire time just wanting it to be over with. After it was released in theaters, we were not surprised to see that critics universally panned it. Yet, we see incredibly high ratings on Amazon. Easy to explain. At least now, based on the ratings and assuming they pay full price for the Amazon Prime accounts for their sock puppets, we can see that Disney spends at least $100, 000 per year for accounts to game the ratings, plus whatever they pay their writers for gushy reviews of movies they own. That's not a bad marketing investment considering that it's worth hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue.

"Moontrap Target Earth" was written by the same fellows who wrote the 1989 film, "Moontrap," Robert Dyke and Ted Ragsdale, and it shares the same basic idea of an advanced, ancient civilization that left dangerous robots behind. Beyond that, though, it's a far more cerebral treatment of the story (read: "low budget") and leaves a lot of open plot lines and unanswered questions. Nevertheless, even with its slow pace and unnecessary side shows, the film kept me interested and watching to the very end and proved to be thought-provoking enough to keep my mind going on it well afterward. [SPOILER] One scientific item of note: In the ending, the gizmo on the moon uses some super-duper science fictiony technology to terraform the moon. This is, in fact, quite reasonable if you can get enough atmospheric gasses to the moon in the first place. The moon's gravity is not sufficient to retain an atmosphere indefinitely, but if we were to somehow bring in enough oxygen and nitrogen to get Earth-normal pressure at the surface of the moon, and then do nothing to maintain it, it would take 10,000 years for the pressure to leak down by 1%. So, it's safe to conclude that if we had the ability to release that much gas the moon's surface, we would be able to maintain the atmosphere by slowly replenishing it. Water in the atmosphere would stabilize the surface temperature, and being a real "greenhouse gas" would probably trap enough heat to raise the mean temperature from -9F to something people can live in.

He's engaged, and on vacation in Goa with his fiancé. She's married to a drug dealer. Some of the actors are very good, others are wooden text-recital machines. Logically this film might get a PG rating for cartoonish gangster violence and adultish themes.
