history.review_title: Rob Zombie’s Halloween tries too hard and ends up terrible!
history.text: The film cannot hold a candle to John Carpenters original movie. It seems to me that the remake is trying too hard to be scary causing a reverse effect. For one thing Michael Myers is much scarier as a normal sized male 6ft and skinny, not 6 foot 8, 290 lbs. The blonde kid portraying Michael didn’t look like Andre the giant as a grade schooler, so no way would he grow up to be that big. Having Michael Myers be that huge makes him less scary. Like Frankenstein’s monster people would spot him coming from a mile away. He wouldn’t be able to hide anywhere. It was a problem for Halloween 4 as well having Linebacker Michael is less scary than your average person. The original film’s version of Michael as a child prodigy from a normal average suburban loving home is a much more interesting premise than Michael coming from a white trash family. The original film builds a lot of tension and left a lot of his back-story up to the viewer’s imagination. In the remake Michael is bullied, but not to the tipping point where he would commit homicidal murder. The psychiatric hospital breakout was utterly ridiculous. Since when does Michael Myers have super human strength like Jason Vorhees in the later Friday the 13th movies? That whole scene came off as comical nothing more. Michael kills the guard’s and just happens to slowly walks out of the whole maximum security complex like a Sunday stroll in the park. Another thing about the film that really bothers me is Michael not killing his sister Laurie onsite. Since when would he just gather her up in his arms take her for a stroll around the block, Ludicrous Speed GO!!!!! The Michael Myers from the original would have killed her instantly in a millisecond. The body count is much higher in this film and you never really care about these characters in general. It cheapens death in a way making it feel less final. I think network TV shows are doing this far to often nowadays as well. The original Halloween did not have a lot of blood, guts or gore, it was far more about the suspense with much better storytelling. In this movie the gore is overboard as well once again giving us the opposite effect of scary. I saw this film in the movie theater on its original run and when the movie finished walking out of the theater I thought man that sucked. Now I am a fan of Rob Zombie. I like Rob’s music and saw him in concert a few times and he puts on a great show. I thought House of 1000 Corpses was not bad just a little above average. I hated The Devil’s Rejects and thought it was stupid. So let’s hold the praise for calling Rob Zombie some great director. He is not in the same league as John Carpenter, Wes Craven, Alfred Hitchcock etc etc. I would rate this film 1 to 1 ½ stars. It is definitely not worth your time or money. It does nothing but tarnish the original Halloween’s legacy. Rob needs to learn that sometime less is more when it comes to horror movies. The movie needed more suspense and less outright gore and a normal sized Michael Myers not Kane from the WWE.

history.review_title: “IT” is the best horror movie I have seen in years. The kids and story are worth your time.
history.text: After just seeing the movie in the theater, "IT" is the best horror movie I have seen in a long time. The film is not really that scary but the suspense and creepy factor definitely hit home. The acting and story pacing is excellent. You end up caring about these kids and they all seem realistic and talk and act their age. Richie is hilarious, while the film mostly focuses on Bill and Beverly, all the kids get screen time. I am a sucker for the nostalgia as well. Crazy to think how 1989 was so long ago but to me it feels like last week in a way. The movie definitely gets the psychological terror right, which is much more interesting than a high body count. The film will keep your glued to your seat and that is the sign of a good movie. Pennywise the clown reminded me a lot of Freddy Krueger from the Nightmare on Elm Street series. Because IT terrorizes the children with their worst fears before it kills them. Tenderizes the meat from what I read somewhere. I have not read the book which seems longer than the Holy Bible. I did know a little about the story from the old ABC miniseries. But let’s be honest made for TV movies almost always suck no matter how good the acting by Tim Curry. You can’t get away with anything near an R rated film on network TV. So right off the bat I knew the production was going to be much better. I liked how this film stuck with just 1 of the books focusing on the children’s story and the sequel will follow the kids as adults. Great move by the filmmaker’s part and it’ll pay huge dividends at the box office for them. IT is a recent horror movie worth watching it isn’t 4 hours long, it does have some very chilling moments. The bully’s are all believable Gretta is a real bitch, and the Bower’s kid is just nuts. After awhile I was rooting for IT to find and eat Gretta. Maybe IT does in the sequel? One can always hope right. I was also hoping Ben eventually ends up with Beverly. Excited to see the next film to see what happens next. I read somewhere that the only part of the movie that didn’t seem realistic was the kids bicycles no BMX or 10 speeds. The bikes would have fit more in a 1970’s time period. But besides that slight oversight the film is excellent.

history.title: High Noon
history.review_title: High Noon is a thrilling western with a great cast and a good story but kind of a dull climax.
history.text: High Noon is a classic western movie coming out in the golden age of Hollywood. I recently viewed it on Hulu Classics and thought it was good. It is a pretty basic story of a small town marshal Will Kane on his last day on the job, who gets married and then finds out a man he put behind bars is once again free looking for revenge and coming in on the noon train that day. The characters are all pretty interesting and you can see a lot of different points of view from all the towns’ people. Gary Cooper and the whole cast do an excellent job. With the way the word spread around this tiny western town of the outlaws return in less than an hour’s worth of time you would think everyone had society media like Twitter, Facebook or Instagram back then. The film is good and I liked the feeling of impending dread and fear the townspeople display. The clocks are in nearly every scene in the film as it gets closer to 12 O’clock. The marshal repeatedly fails to get together a pose to take on the outlaws. Eventually abandoned by everyone he takes on 4 outlaws by himself. Now each minute in the film feels like 20 minutes gone by, it is hard to believe the Marshal would have time to get into a fistfight and get fixed up by the local barber, let alone make it to a tavern, a church and several house calls all in the short amount of time before the train arrives. The marshal had maybe an hour tops once he found out the news. I liked how his wife shot one of the bandits and didn’t act like a helpless damsel in distress and actually took matters in her own hands. I would have liked it even more if she would have shot at Frank Miller as he attempted to abduct her leading to the finale. I recognized Lee Van Cleef right away at the beginning and I thought he was the main villain and the train would be coming with more goons or bandits. Another thing that I thought about was how much one of the outlaws was drinking before the shootout, I would of thought the film would have made a point of showing him stumble or bumble his weapon because of all the liquor he drank up til that point but nothing really becomes of it. If anything the only thing I found a bit lacking was the final confrontation with the lead villain Frank Miller. The film seemed to end very abruptly without the Marshal shaming the townsfolk for their cowardice or at least have Will Kane slowly look around at all the people and let them know they were wrong to abandon him during his time of need. That is the only reason why I would not give this 5 stars. Overall I think this is a 4 star film. The plot is good with an interesting cast of characters. The running out of time aspect is well done and you can feel the tension in the air, but ultimately the shootout was not as good as the buildup.

history.title: Blade Runner 2049 (Blu-ray) (BD)
history.review_title: Blade Runner 2049 has an original story, lots of similarities to the first film and leaves a lot up to the viewer’s imagination.
history.text: This is an incredibly deep film like its predecessor. I thought it was a good solid film but not as good as the original movie. You see lots of scenes that are very similar in style and substance. The breaking through the wall, the girl with the frizzy orange/pink hair looking homeless, the Blade Runner getting the hell beat out of him, a main character committing a selfless act of sacrifice etc etc. Similar to the first film, lots of plot lines are left open to the viewer’s imagination. I thought Jared Leto character Wallace was actually a pretty good mastermind villain in the movie and it is a shame we don’t really find out what happens to his character, similar to Tyrell from the first movie but far more ruthless. Luv was also a very good female villain character echoing how difficult it is to kill a combat Replicant like Roy Batty (Rutger Hauer.) Blade Runner is one of those Sci Fi films where the future is not all bright warm and fuzzy. More bleak and full of despair a dystopian future gone bad. The premise from the 1st film is loosely based on the Replicants who were made by man to be slave labor and colonize other planets in the solar system. The whole Blade Runner theme is about a detective unit design and constructed to retire or destroy any rogue Replicants that makes it’s way back to Earth. The new film explores a world where the replicants coexist with humans in just about every manner of life. The new film opens up a lot of new ideas kind of like opening pandora’s box in a way. I thought the scenes with K and Joi were kind of dull and lifeless whereas I think the relationship with Mariette the pleasure replicant could have been very intriguing. What if agent K happened to get her pregnant how deep would that rabbit hole go and could a cool sequel be made out of that movie? A lot can be made out of a hologram wanting a host body to make love to a non human. I rather like the idea of Rachel having twins and thought that could have been very unique as well. Alas these are just ideas the film does not really explore. If anything the film is not as strong as the original movie because there wasn’t a group of Replicants to chase after and hunt down. In this film there is only 1 Replicant K retires. You never get the feeling that he is tracking a group of outlaw Replicants returning to Earth seeking more life like the Nexus 8’s from the original movie, which seemed like a noble cause. I always imagined the Replicants working in space like the Sean Connery movie “Outland”, and in many ways like the movie “Logan’s Run” but Blade Runners instead of Sandmen, both Sci Fi films that have mild similarities to Blade Runner but not as deep plots more straightforward. Blade Runner 2049 doesn’t really touch on either of those subjects. We don’t see any of the Replicants in space or the hunting down of the rogue Replicants. I also thought K would have found Deckard much earlier in the movie instead of the last 3rd of the film. So much time seemed to be devoted to Joi and K’s relationship it seemed to hurt the rest of the movie. Although robot sex might be interesting it is not the reason I came to see this movie. I was expecting more of a detective story set in a future world. The Gaff scene I thought would carry more weight as well. Gaff seemed to be ok with letting Rachel and Deckard live showing us his own humanity to do the right thing. The film doesn’t really roll with that dimension either. Was he ordered to hunt them down? Did he have any choice words about K being a Replicant Blade Runner? Maybe something to ponder when they release the deleted scenes on the extended DVD. Blade Runner 2049 is one of those films you really need to see a couple of times to make sure you didn’t miss anything. There is a lot going on and it is like a puzzle you are trying to solve. Many people will find the movie too long or not enough action for our ADD society that can’t think outside of an action scene every few second of the movie mentality.

history.title: Happy Death Day [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Ultimately an interesting idea ruined by the PG-13 rating and dumb moves by the main character.
history.text: Those of you familiar with Bill Murray’s “Groundhog Day” and The newer Tom Cruise film “Edge of Tomorrow” will feel right at home with this plot. It is basically a woman stuck in the same days set of events trying to figure out who keeps killing her resetting each day. It seems to me there would be an easier way to break the chain in this movie. The movie borrows heavily from just about every other slasher film in existence. I did like the mask the killer used and the film does have some decent scenes. While the film is interesting for the most part what pisses me off is the lack of an R rating. Seriously why tease us with a possible nudity scene walking naked through campus and not show any skin. I get why the studio’s stay away from the R rating to make more money and have more of an audience view the film but it hurts the overall film. If the lead actress Jessica Rothe was that sensitive about showing her body I am sure the studio could have rounded up another good looking blonde body double. Also with all the new computer technology they can practically photo shop her in any way she would like. That is why Happy Death Day is like “I know What You Did Last Summer” a minor weak horror film instead of something more you'll remember. Nobody goes to a horror movie expecting to see a made for TV movie. Seriously I paid $15 to see this movie in the theater I don’t want it to skimp out on anything sex, gore, violence, suspense I want to see it all. As in the famous words of Booger from Revenge of the Nerds, “I want to see bush pan down.” There didn’t even seem to be any chemistry between the Jessica Rothe and Israel Broussard. You don’t get the feeling that they are going to be rolling on the carpet or bed anytime soon. Also for young college girls all the sorority girls look to be in their early to mid 30’s not early 20’s. And you don’t get any scenes of them naked either. What kind of horror movie/sorority house is this, pathetic. Overall I would rate the film 3½ stars. The movie had potential but the weak PG-13 rating and no smart thinking by the main character hurt the movie.

history.review_title: Unforgiven is an authentic version of the Wild Wild West
history.text: Unforgiven is the best western movie I have ever seen. It rings true shot for shot, scene for scene. I love just about everything in this film. The hero is sometimes the villain Sheriff Little Bill (Gene Hackman) and the villain is sometimes the hero William Money (Clint Eastwood) depending on your point of view. The characters are so rich and deep. Little Bill maybe the big boss man sheriff but he is a horrible carpenter. The same can be said of William Money being a terrible hog farmer, but also an outlaw to be feared. Some things in life god intended for us to do more than others. Even hired guns like English Bob have their faults lying to his own biographer to make himself look better. The movie is full of characters with realistic human faults which makes the movie so believable. You sympathize with the whores in this film who are treated as little more than meat. When some drunken cowboy carves up the face of a young girl, for a tiny slight. No justice was done and the poor girl received nothing while the tavern owner received all the compensation which was horses in this case. The movie is unflinching in its brutality and authenticity of how the west really was. This is the first film in ages to depicted what it is like to kill a man. It is not something glorious that you see in the standard action movies but something you have to live with. When William Money tells his young outlaw partner “it’s a hell of thing killing a man” you believe it down to your core. Yet even deep down with all Will’s faults he does right by his partners and ends up being a just human being and a good father to his children. His story is one of sadness but also redemption and a hope that one day he will find salvation. This isn’t your modern day country music theme of celebrating the almighty pickup truck, being true to your first love, your dog and lovin your mumma. Far from it. There were brothels and whore houses. Cowboys were more ruffian and scoundrels than good Christian folk. Life wasn’t easy for anyone on the frontier. Clint Eastwood’s acting and directing are superb in this film. Whenever I hear a list of top 10 movies of all time if this movie isn’t on the list then it is hogwash. I have seen the movie well over 20 times and yet when I see it on TV no matter where it is at in the movie I stop to finish watching the film. That is the sign of a great movie. This is a 5 star movie and probably the best western ever made. This is one of those rare movies where the casting seems perfect for every character. The final shootout is gripping and it glues you to the screen.

history.review_title: Cabin Fever is a terrible movie. It is so bad it’s almost a guilty pleasure to watch!
history.text: Oh where to begin with this turkey. The movie has just about every bad horror movie cliché within the film except the obvious masked killer. Instead you get a virus and “Cujo” combined. Now the acting is god awful and the stupidity of the characters will make you chuckle. While watching the movie I was thinking no one can be this dumb. Then I realize that we elected Donald Trump. The thing is this movie is so damn bad it is actually worth watching. Like Battlefield Earth bad, but it is worth your time to soldier on to the end. Back to the movie. You do get cussing, nudity and violence so kudos to the director for making an “R” rated horror movie. God Bless him for that, so sick and tired of watered down PG-13 horror movies tempting us with skin and cutting the camera away for possible death scenes not showing you anything. You basically have 2 couples and the stoner tagalong going on a spring break trip to a remote cabin in the woods. Now right off the bat the plot of “Evil Dead” comes to mind. No way was this movie going to touch that masterpiece. I was a little surprised they didn’t try and cram in a third woman for Bert’s character which is the stupidest human being on the planet in this movie. You get cliché after cliché over and over again. Marcy rowing solo in the lake in a canoe is your “Friday the 13th”moment. Several things in this movie just seem out and out goofy. The cop obsessed with underage drinking and riding a bicycle similar to the goofball cop in “Scream”. I was thinking what was the director smoking that day? The blonde kid biting people just seemed oddball crazy right out of something like the kid from “Deliverance”. The saving grace in this film is actually the beautiful Cerina Vincent who plays Marcy. For her nude scenes alone I would give this film an additional star. Don’t know why some actresses are afraid of nudity. Never hurt Jamie Lee Curtis or Sharon Stone’s career. Overall this is a 1 star quality film, but because of the R rating and nudity I have to at least give this 2 stars. Several parts still don’t make a lot of sense but if you are in the mood to see a bad movie as a guilty pleasure this should be your go to film.

history.title: Swingers (Collector's Edition)
history.review_title: Swingers is a wonderful movie about friendship and moving on with life.
history.text: Swingers is a very different kind of film. It is a guy flick but women can easily relate. I saw the film years ago and just thought it was kind of average, nothing special. However seeing it again recently in my mid to late 30’s I have grown a new appreciation for the film. The heart of the movie is really about how your friends help you through the toughest times in life and are there for you when you need them. It reminded me a little bit of the Entourage show years before that show was ever created. This movie could have been a blue print for that show years later. Who hasn’t been in a position like Mike’s in the film where he is trying to move on and get past his old girlfriend. Or meeting someone new and looking at the phone wondering should you call or wait a day or two. Mike has a group of pals who keep him motivated to hit the town and meet new women and move on with his life. Dorothy looked pretty hot to me in the movie. Vince Vaughn who plays “Trent” in the movie is excellent and really steals the best scenes in the movie. But at the same time that Trent is a showman and a ladies’ man, he is most fulfilled when his best friend Mike is happy. I love the way the guys talk in the film I thought it was funny and interesting throughout. So funny when Mike's buddy says “I was playing Hamlet 2 months ago and now can’t even play Goofy at Disneyland” just kills me, hilarious scene. The movie is a little bit hard to watch at times because in many ways I was like Mike’s character, when I was single in my 20’s I couldn’t get a date to save my life. Felt like I had the black plague or leprosy when it came to meeting single women. Yet when I found a girlfriend every hot girl in the world wanted to get to know me. It’s like where the hell were they when I was single? Such is life. The movie is strongest in these scenes where you know Mike is going to make a mistake or come off as too desperate but you are constantly rooting for him to succeed. The film doesn’t really explore his actual job and you wonder where all the guys get money to go out on the town every night. You would think that being a standup comedian would make you a very big extrovert providing lots of people to meet and get to know. Mike could make fun of his failures in the dating world like Woody Allen and meet women that way. The title is a bit misleading when I saw the title I didn’t think they were referring to the swing dance music scene. By the end of the movie I felt the film had a positive message about taking a chance on someone new. Mike’s friends are over the moon for him and you wish you had buddies like that in real life. Overall I think Swingers is a very good movie I would rate it 4 1/2 stars. Be ready for a lot of cussing and “baby, you’re in the money”. This is the type of movie I want my own kids to watch when they get older and start the dating process. I know they will get hurt and make mistakes but I want them to see how having such a good group of friends can help you get through the toughest obstacles in life.

history.title: Hired Gun: Out of the Shadows, into the Spotlight
history.review_title: I loved the content, but many of the Hired Guns had long successful music careers which makes the title kind of misleading.
history.text: Hired Guns is a film that had me at hello. The film mainly focuses on rock musicians who were hired at the last minute to replace permanent band members on short notice. I loved watching this documentary. It could easily have been a whole series or several hours longer. It is a very broad subject and really only focuses on the 1970’s- present day. Watching the Billy Joel band behind the scenes was fascinating how those classic albums were formed and the people behind the scenes. But it wasn’t a case of hiring a studio musician at the last minute. The film does have a lot of focus on pop and glam rock musicians and doesn’t focus much at all on R&B and other genres of music. The documentary earns creditability by interviewing real rock stars Jason Newsted, Rob Zombie, Rudy Sarzo, Alice Cooper, Eric Singer, David Ellefson. I kind of wish the director would have reached out to Aerosmith, KISS, and Dave Mustaine from Megadeth to get there points of view as well. Because all of those bands have had revolving musicians come and go in their bands as well. Some of the films highlights include Jason Newsted’s interview about taking over Cliff Burton from Metallica, Brad Gillis with the impossible job of replacing Randy Roads to finish off the Diary of a Madman tour with Ozzy Osbourne’s band in 1982. Rob Zombie talking about replacing a bandmate with a better player but screwing up the chemistry in the band by losing the glue or personality of that person that made the band function. Alice Cooper listening to his take on what they are looking for in replacement musicians if a band mate is sick or up and leaves the group for a better opportunity. These are all high quality great interviews. Alice Cooper seemed to have a revolving door of great musicians that came and went in his band. I knew that Derek St Holmes was the singer for the Ted Nugent band and never really got the credit he deserved. Likewise I didn’t know Ray Parker Jr. was a long time studio musician before he became famous with the Ghostbusters one hit wonder song. I had also heard that the singer from Filter was greedy and kind of destroyed his own group. There were no interviews from Trent Reznor so we don’t get his point of view either on how that went down or what went down with his former guitarist for Nine Inch Nails. That is the thing with this documentary it shows Billy Joel in a bad light but really if you look at it from Billy’s point of view He probably had his reasons. Not everyone has been swindled out of 100 million dollars. That would make you mistrust everyone in your group no matter how honest they were. Some of the Hired Guns in the story started out as studio musicians then became full time replacement band members so the title is a little bit misleading. I also thought it was interesting for all these real rocker guitar players playing pop songs just to earn a living and get there foot in the door for music they really want to play. I actually really admire that, I am sure your street credit would probably go to crap if you were playing for Madonna, Mandy Moore, Katy Perry or Pink but for these struggling musicians just trying to make a living that was probably the big break they were looking for. I also liked how one of the musicians said it wasn’t an easy life, one minute you could be playing a European rock festival in front of 100,000 people then the next unemployed making peanuts. I would rate this 5 stars but it easily could have been longer with more substance. Focusing on some other genres of music like R & B, Jazz, Blues but had good content for what it is.

history.title: King of the Underdogs
history.review_title: Captivating documentary about a great director rarely recognised outside of Hollywood.
history.text: It is a very interesting documentary on the films of John G Avildsen's primarily his 2 biggest ROCKY and The Karate Kid movies. The documentary film is very honest and open with all the actors and people he worked with. The interviews from the actors are all fascinating. I especially found the movies John passed on or was fired from incredibly interesting. Unlike Steven Spielberg John didn't kiss Studio heads butts and winded up being passed over from several large films that he could have had. Seeing raw footage of John Travolta in Saturday Night Fever was pretty cool, one of those films John wanted to do but didn't get the chance to or the film Serpico which helped cement Al Pacino as a major movie star. Politics do come into play in the film industry just like regular society when John was dating an actress who's old boyfriend had studio ties and he was fired from doing a movie. Also the film features early casting calls with Sigourney Weaver before she was a well known actress along with Mathew Mcconaughy and a few other actors,That would later become huge movie stars like Daniel Craig who was the villain in The Power of One, John seemed so happy that his actor has gone on to great success as James Bond. The documentary touches on some of John's other powerful films such as "Joe", "Save the Tiger", "Lean On Me", "The Power of One". Not all of these films were massively successful but they are all memorable and captivating films you won't forget. I loved the scene where John meets Frank Capra his idol and asks him how he was able to do all the films he wanted and he tells him you have to make the bosses or the studio heads "make them think it was there idea" That seems so true in real life. Some times you have to know who to impress/kiss ass or do a favor for to get ahead. Of course the bulk of the film is dedicated to ROCKY and The Karate Kid his most famous films focusing on underdog characters. The director is correct when anyone talks about ROCKY it almost always centers around Sylvester Stallone and not on the director John Avildsen. I really enjoyed seeing John's Oscar acceptance speech I wish the movie would have played the whole speech and not just a snippet of it. Mr. Magi's character is as iconic as Darth Vader is to the movie business. Both ROCKY and The Karate Kid stand the test of time and are great movies to this day. I actually believe that The Karate Kid 2 never really receives its due for being such a great sequel. One of the best sequels in movie history in my book. The film also cannot be understate how powerful Bill Conti's musical score was to both movies. The music is dramatically powerful and instantly recognizable for both pictures just a few bars and you know exactly what film it came from. I would easily rate this film 5 stars I could have watched another hour or more easily about John's other films. I thought more of the film would have been strictly about ROCKY and The Karate Kid but found the film interesting non the less. If anything some parts of the film seemed rushed and I would have liked to have seen more about the impact these 2 specific films had on Hollywood. It seemed like there were countless duplicates and clone films of these films that were never done with the effort and style of John's movies.

history.title: When a Stranger Calls
history.review_title: when a stranger calls don't answer! but watch this movie.
history.text: As a kid I loved the old suspense mystery TV and horror movies. I don't remember seeing this one but I had seen it a few times and thought it was one of those newer graphic blood gore horror movies. I got this at a discount store when I saw who was in it and when it was made. It is one of the better suspense mystery movies. The beginning of the movie is done very well with the baby sister getting phone calls and then find out the person is in the house and the kids are dead. But then it drags a little with Durning chasing after the escaped mental patient with some scenes that just seem like a waste of time that have nothing to do with the story. It gets back on track and the ending is very good. I won't ruin the ending. If you live 70's tv movies and horror you will like this. and there's no blood and gore to ruin the movie.

history.title: Man on the Moon
history.review_title: Man on the Moon is a wonderful trip into the life of the brilliant mind of Andy Kaufman.
history.text: As a kid I saw Kaufman do all his famous routines and thought he was hilarious but my dad and family didn't get it at all. I thought he was great on Taxi too. Not a fan of Carrey but I went see this movie when it first came out and thought it was good. Now I think it's great. I have had it on VHS yes still have it and dusted it off and it gets better with each viewing. The entire movie is incredible from the writing to directing to the acting by everybody. DeVito is great as the manager. I had forgot he was on Taxi with Kaufman. Hollyweird could not make a movie like this today. It would have to have all their leftist propaganda added. Those who say this is boring or bad need CGI special effects and blood and gore and sex and violence to get their attention span activated. This movie is for those who have a attention span and sense of humor.

history.title: Madhouse
history.review_title: Dr Death is in the Madhouse! A lost horror Classic!
history.text: A Horror Classic! Those who wrote negative reviews obviously don't like movies with great acting and story and without CGI graphic blood and gore even though this one does have some gore. Vincent Price and Peter Cushing are great in this together. Price plays it perfect as the horror star who has a nervous breakdown after his girlfriend is murdered and he was the main suspect but can't remember if he did it or not. Cushing plays his former writer of Dr Death series who brings him back to restart the series for the BBC but Price is not thrilled with reviving Dr Death from the Dead. The story has twist and turns and it's obvious the movie points the finger at Price as the killer but ? is he? The ending is especially good and done very well. A masterpiece of horror for Price and Cushing. A must see for all classic horror fans.

history.title: The Monster Club (remastered widescreen edition)

history.text: Another lost gem! It's the way horror movies should be made! Great story telling and acting with humor and little graphic blood and gore. Price is a horror writer who gets bite by a vampire Carradine who brings him to The MOnster Club and gives him a history lesson in monsters and tales of terror. The stories are so good and fun to watch. If you like Thrillers and Suspense you'll love this movie. This was made in 80''s when new wave and punk was starting to get popular so there is music in the MOnster Club but it's actually pretty good and doesn't ruin the movie. A must have for Price fans.

history.title: Ranma ½ - Set 1 (Special Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I have been a fan of Ranma 1/2 since the days when I could only find the odd VHS tape in my local movie stores. Mostly it was the dub, but sometimes I was lucky enough to find a tape in the original Japanese. Those were very different times for anime fans in America. Now, 20 years in the future we have the sets that we never could have imagined, but that the series always deserved. The show has never looked better, and I doubt it is possible to improve on what we have been given. Not only does it look beautiful and pristine, however, but the masters have not been tampered with. Gone are the American title cards of the old DVD sets, and they are replaced with the original Japanese shots with soft subtitles. I may be mistaken, but this set doesn't seem to have a single hard subtitle in it.. and for a fan of animation and the purity of the original material, that is a dream come true. This is a set that will please both the hardcore anime fans, and the casual viewer who isn't necessarily interested in the minute details. The extras are nothing to sneeze at as well. They are very well represented with this set, and a welcome addition for the animation historian. Finally, the packaging is absolutely gorgeous. It goes for that strong Chinese theme that is prevalent throughout the series. It fits and looks great on my shelf. Highly, highly recommended.

history.review_title: Great potential, but falls very short
history.text: I was disappointed in this movie. I thought it was going to be dark, creepy, and scary, but this had none of that. This movie turned out to be just weird and seemed to go on forever, even though it's only 100 minutes. You can figure out what is going on before one of the main character's does. I wouldn't suggest this movie unless you like stupid, long, and boring movies.

history.title: I Really Hate My Job
history.review_title: Neve Campbell is one of my all time favorites, but...
history.text: This movie turned out differently than I expected. I thought there would be more to it instead of it just taking place in a restaurant. I love Neve Campbell, but sadly the other girls were hard to understand at times because they have accents and whisper a lot. In order to like this movie, you really need to be in the mood to hear about several stories at once and how they go back and forth between the characters. In case you were wondering about seeing Neve Campbell naked, yes, you do get to see her completely naked, but the camera doesn't show her naked the entire time that she is. That's probably the only reason why I didn't give this movie 1 star. I didn't hate it, but didn't love it either. I think I'll watch this movie a couple more times to see if I can like it better the 2nd or 3rd time around. I suggest you rent before you buy, but the choice is yours.

history.title: Detroit
history.review_title: Can't we all just get along?
history.text: This was one of the best movies I've seen all year! This true story will definitely effect you in several different ways, especially emotionally. I think Kathryn Bigelow is one of the best women in Hollywood to write and direct the movie's she does. This movie might not be The Hurt Locker, but the acting by everyone in this movie is absolutely amazing! You can just feel the pain and emotions for these men and women. These things alone made me give it 5 stars. I highly recommend this movie to everybody, even if it's just one time. I think this is an important part of history people should know about. I'm really glad things are better today, but we still have a long way to go. Whether you buy or rent this, I can promise you won't be disappointed. I really hope this gets an Oscar nomination.

history.title: Kingsman 2: The Golden Circle
history.text: This movie was absolutely a fun one to watch! It's not going to win any awards or anything, but that's the point. This is just a really good mindless action movie. The reason I only gave it 3 stars is because there were a couple things that just bothered me. #1. There's a famous musician in this movie and I thought it was funny at first, but then it became an annoying on going joke that they beat to death. #2. Julianne Moore's character Poppy Adams really got on my nerves. It seemed like she was trying to do a Harley Quinn impression, but tried too hard and went overboard with it. I really hope they make more of these movies like they have with James Bond. I love these kinds of movies where it's filled with an insane amount of action and cool gadgets. I do highly suggest this movie if you don't care about some little annoying things.. I know I will definitely watch this again, if not several times. Sit back, relax and let this fun action packed movie take care of your long day or for a good weekend movie night.

history.title: Dunkirk (Blu-ray) (BD)
history.review_title: You need to be a history buff to like and follow this movie
history.text: What a horribly made movie! This incredible true story deserves SO much better. This movie starts out quiet and sort of confusing about who is who, but you figure it out. The three most incredibly annoying things are. #1. This movie jumps all over the place and expects you to know what's going on without knowing someone's name(s) and then will jump around to another place and so on. I don't want to guess what's going on and get lost, or why people are doing what they're doing without explanation. There's not much dialogue throughout this movie. That also makes it really hard to follow. You'll be watching a scene with talking and that might last a minute or so and then it'll jump to another couple scenes without any talking and then it'll start again. #2. Your eyes will go crazy and so will your brain. The 16:9 ratio goes from widescreen to full screen every couple seconds or so and that drove me crazy while jumping all over the place. #3. They play this intense music to make you think something really big is about to happen, but doesn't. I sadly don't recommend this movie. I don't think I'll watch another war movie unless it's done by Mel Gibson, Clint Eastwood, or Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks. Those guys are the absolute best at doing war movies. Rent before you buy and then decide. You'll be very happy you did. I guarantee it!

history.title: mother!
history.text: This movie started out really intriguing and suspenseful, but after about 30 minutes in, it gets CRAZY and WEIRD! I really don't know how to express how weird and crazy this movie is without spoiling it and I don't want to do that, but I will say watch at your own risk and suggest you rent before you buy. This movie is pretty disturbing and unnerving in spots. You will hate yourself if you spend your money on it because you will hate this movie unless you like this kind of stuff. Darren Aronofsky wrote and directed this movie. The only movie of his I have liked so far is The Wrestler. I think I will stay away from his stuff from now on unless I hear good things about a new movie that my friends or family suggest. I love Jennifer Lawrence, but I hope she sticks to the roles she has been doing. Sorry this review is so short, but I don't like spoiling anything. Don't waste your time and money on this one!

history.title: Stronger
history.review_title: One of the best films of the year that didn't get enough recognition
history.text: This movie is absolutely spectacular alongside Jake Gyllenhaal. This true, emotional, real life story of Jeff Bauman (Survivor of the Boston marathon bombing) is sure to inspire many people about how not to give up on life after your life gets turned upside down. I had to give this movie 5 stars due to the acting by everybody, especially Jake Gyllenhaal portraying Jeff Bauman. I would have to suggest this movie to everyone, even if you watch it just once. I would like to say more, but don't want to ruin anything. Whether you decide to rent or buy, I guarantee you won't be disappointed in this movie!

history.title: Mountain Between Us, The
history.text: This movie is fair. I could only give it 3 stars though. I thought this was going to be a little more suspenseful and dramatic, but wasn't. There were a couple times where it was suspenseful, but not enough to keep me on the edge of my seat wondering what's going to happen next. I heard the book is much better, so, I guess I'll have to read that and compare the differences. I suggest you rent before you buy. I wish I had.

history.title: Flatliners [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: When remakes make the original even better
history.text: This remake is absolutely horrible! I would give this zero stars if I could. This remake is a little more on the actual medical side of things, but I still love the original MUCH better! The one thing I did like, but was ruined, was seeing Kiefer Sutherland reprise his role, but the thing that ruined that was him going by Dr. Barry Wolfson instead of Dr. Nelson Wright. If they would've gone by his original name/character, I would've liked that a whole lot more because of the things he says to his new med students. I think it also would've been good to go by his original character because it would make this feel more like a sequel and tie things together a lot better and make it a little more interesting. There were a couple scenes that made me jump, but that was the only thing that this movie made me feel. As for the acting in this movie, it's absolutely terrible! I used to think Ellen Page was a good actress, but the last few things I've seen her in including this shows that she's really a one dimensional type of actress. I don't recommend this movie to anybody unless you're like me and need to see for yourself. I suggest you rent before you buy and then decide if you want to waste your time and money on this.

history.title: Brawl In Cell Block 99
history.review_title: HELL NO! Don't waste your time and money on this!
history.text: I was looking forward to seeing this movie and see Vince Vaughn do something else for a change. Sometimes comedians can play a really good serious role, but unfortunately that wasn't the case here. I kept waiting for this movie to get good, but it never did and it seemed like the longer I waited, the worse it got and by the time it was over, I really hated this movie. The acting is really terrible alongside a weak plot. The one thing that made me laugh like crazy were the fight scenes. Those scenes are like watching WWF or really bad sparring in slow motion and are very far fetched, but they will make you laugh! I don't recommend this movie to anybody unless you're like me and need to see for yourself, but consider yourself warned! I hope Vince Vaughn goes back to doing comedies or creepy guys like in Domestic Disturbance or Psycho. He's very good at those type of roles. If you are looking for a really good movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat the entire time, I highly recommend [[ASIN:B0752HBQMY Shot Caller [Blu-ray]]].

history.title: Curse of the Pink Panther
history.text: We were pleasantly surprised, both seeing this movie for the first time. Huge Peter Sellers fans and in particular the Blake Edwards Pink Panther creations, we thoroughly enjoyed this movie even though the master himself was not in it. There are scenes that are side splitting, including the blow up doll, the really outstanding car chase and many others. Herbert Lom like Sellers was himself fantastic and continues to be so in this movie.

history.title: The Jewel in the Crown (25th Anniversary Edition)
history.text: It was fantastic to watch this again after some twenty years. We've never read the Raj Quartet so cannot compare the books with screen adaptation, but this series is stellar in every way. As with all stories, there are people to sympathize with and love, those we love to hate and those who disgust. The "forbidden love" aspect is a regular theme in any story that deals with the ruling colonists and their racist overlord sentiments. We see this in Passage to India and Indian Summers which is another very good series.

history.title: Shirley Temple: America's Sweetheart Collection, Vol. 2, Baby Take a Bow / Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm / Bright Eyes
history.text: Bright Eyes, Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm and Baby Take a Bow are packaged here in their own individual discs in a box pack. What a remarkable child star Shirley Temple was. I first saw a movie of hers in the early 1960's as a child myself and thought she was amazing. There were two movie firsts with Shirley Temple movies. She was the world's first child star and she was the first to dance with a great African American star of vaudeville and then screen, 'Bojangles" Johnson. Their duets are not only memorable but a delight to watch. Temple was truly a child prodigy, with an IQ of around 155 and she never fluffed her lines. She also memorized everyone else's lines and was quick to remind them when they fluffed. President Roosevelt thought highly of Shirley Temple since her movies were a temporary escape for so many during the pain of the Great Depression. Baby Take a Bow was rather controversial at the time, since it featured the child (played of course by Temple) living in a perceived criminal environment. These movies will always be a joy to watch and Temple will always hold her own as the most amazing and gifted young child in early movie history. We bow to Shirley!

history.title: Carry On Collection Vol 1
history.text: Oh how we adore these movies! I grew up on the Carry On series although didn't get to see them all! Kenneth Williams was always my firm favorite and wished he appeared in all of them (although he appears in most). This collection contains; Carry On Camel, Don't Lose Your Head (a hilarious take on the French Revolution), Up The Khyber (a great humorous take at the British Khyber Pass era), Doctor, Camping, Again Doctor, Jungle and Carry On Loving. All are excellent with Carry on Follow That Camel being a hilarious take on The Four Feathers. Many regulars who appeared in most if not all the Carry On films are favorites such as Kenneth Williams, Kenneth Connor, Charles Hawtrey (a real life character), Sid James (always a lovable favorite and quite the ladies man in films and out), Frankie Howard, Joan Sims, Hattie Jacques, Jim Dale, Angela Douglas, Liz Fraser (who also appeared in a Rumpole episode), Barbara Windsor (an adorable blond who in real life had a long term relationship with Sid James), Bernard Bresslaw (a most talented comic who was lost to us far too soon). Perhaps three of the Carry On series were less than stellar with Carry On Columbus easily being the worst. Carry On England has its merits and is enjoyable albeit it lacking in creativity and storyline. Carry On Emmanuele wasn't quite as bad as critics' remarks about it. Each one of course is loaded with double entendres with almost every sentence containing at least one sexual reference some not so vague as well as creatively funny observances and uses of the English language. They don't make 'em like this anymore!

history.title: This Time I'll Make You Rich [VHS]
history.text: A truly awful movie from start to its highly predictable finish. A sad commentary that it was made with the rough copy in mind of the Trinity movies. Bud Spencer and Terence Hill (Carlo Pedersoli and Mario Girotti), appeared in numerous excellent movies with both engaging storylines and action. This movie has none of the components that made the "Trinity" movies so successful and that remain so popular today.

history.title: Carry on Sergeant
history.text: We were expecting this movie plus Carry On Nurse to come on the same disc, but sometimes, strange things happen with orders. In any case, this was the first film in the Carry On series, 1958. As to be expected, it was not quite developed, nor was it nearly as polished and smooth as the others that followed. Interesting therefore to see many of the characters that would become regulars on the wonderful Carry On series.

history.title: Shirley Temple: America's Sweetheart Collection, Vol. 3 (Dimples / The Little Colonel / The Littlest Rebel) [DVD]
history.text: Delightful as always! The Little Colonel and The Littlest Rebel are really interesting from a storyline perspective considering the times. Both are set during the civil war. The aspect of slavery and how African Americans were depicted, not only for civil war times, but even during the making of these movies is a consideration for the viewer. The now famous stairwell dance sequence in The Little Colonel that Temple did with Bill "Bojangles" Robinson was the first interracial scene on screen and magnificent. "Bojangles" in this viewers opinion was the scene stealer and its a real shame he wasn't filmed more. At the time, he was 57 and Temple was a mere 6 years of age. "Bojangles" appears again with Temple as Uncle Billy in The Littlest Rebel and their dance routines as just as fantastic. All the supporting actors depicting slaves and their children were so outstanding that the movies would fail completely without them. Temple as always is adorably delightful and without her movies we may have never been treated to the genius and wonderful presence of Bill Robinson.

history.title: The Far Pavilions [DVD]
history.text: What a disappointment in every way. After having been wonderfully spoiled by productions such as The Jewel in the Crown, the movie Passage to India, and more recent ones such as Indian Summers, Far Pavilions was simply put, awful. It seems that plenty of empty space was filled with overly drawn out battle scenes and the wedding ceremony was short of painful. The syrupy dialogue between the two main characters was hard to bear along with an unnecessarily limited storyline so highly predictable one is tempted to fast forward to get the whole thing over with. The casting of Amy Irving was a complete failure as she appears wooden and certainly dull. A waste of money.

history.title: Before the Rains
history.text: This is a good "movie" to watch. It does however repeat the same theme as do so many others of this genre. It is understood that colonists took full advantage of the locals over which they enjoyed playing master. The women were in particular poorly treated by their white male overlords considering the British well understood Indian women be doubly punished in their own society (for falling in love, or rather, believing their white overlords loved them). Nonetheless, a well crafted movie albeit a repeated theme.

history.title: Rake: Season 2
history.text: After watching the first series at least three times, we are now re-repeating watching series 2. Roxburgh is really a fine artist and its impossible not to enjoy and like the character he plays. He does so with great subtlety, aplomb and polish. The character itself (Cleaver Greene) lacks all the aplomb, subtlety and polish one could possibly find in a character like Greene, but Roxburgh somehow endears the viewer to this character. The character of Greene has a high, full throttle life libido and is completely unwilling and unreservedly pedal to the metal, full steam ahead without much care for consequences for himself or those closest to him. The supporting cast is truly fantastic. There isn't one weak cast member and without this stellar cast, the series may not be a potent as it is. Its fantastic and too bad we can't find anything like it here in the US. So far, the story lines are good and as yet have not strayed into the ridiculous as we've seen (sadly) with the Dr. Blake series.

history.review_title: Alec Guiness At His Best (And Long Before Obi Wan Kenobi)
history.text: Nifty Brit movie on the trial and tribulations of a vacuum cleaner salesman who is "chosen" to serve his homeland by posing as a secret service agent (the same governmental body used by 007). With the advice of his friendly doctor (Burl Ives) he gets in over his head by "pulling the wool over his superiors eyes" when he begins recruiting other agents "that are never quite recruited." Not knowing the first thing about the dangers of being a secret agent he bumbles along until things take a serious tone and he fears for his life, following the murderous death of his doctor friend, his fellow agents try to poison him and he gets the hint to take his daughter and return to England. Better than your average 3 star movies so 4 stars.for Our Man In Havana.

history.title: The Silver Fleet
history.review_title: ANYONE FOR A NICE BOAT RIDE?-- NAZIS ONLY PLEASE!
history.text: Nicely done WWII movie about a Dutch boat builder who becomes part of the Dutch resistance when his community boat company is taken over by the Nazis. Good suspense and action as we watch him slyly becoming a friend of the Nazis, to the point that his friends and employees believe he is a "quisling" or Nazi collaborator. But don't believe it for a moment. He is secretly the head of the resistance and realizes that he must cooperate or watch his loved ones suffer under Nazi rule. But as he cooperates "his" way, we soon realize that it is not important that he builds boats for the Nazis, but it is important, "how he builds them" The last scene is indicative of just how much courage and determination it took to defeat the Nazis.
One of the best war movies I have seen. Originally shot in Black and White it seems more like you are actually involved in some of the horrific naval battles of the time period.

This actual strip was similar in many ways to Bloom County by Berk Breathed but was totally unique to its author, Brett Merhar with the characters taken from his friends and relatives. Perhaps the most endearing character was Angus the caffeine addicted ferret who it seems everyone loved. The other characters Brett actually knew, especially Johnny Jenkins, his best childhood friend and Paula Wisconsin, modeled after his sister. This collection of episodes, first aired on Showtime goes deeper into Bretts life experiences, again using and exaggerating members of his own family. I always looked forward to reading the nationally syndicated strip and while the show is definitely more like South Park than Bloom County it still retains cutting edge humor. Recommended!

history.title: Air Force
history.review_title: Long Lost Gem Reconstructed on DVD
history.text: Excellent WWII movie showing the trials and tribulations of a bomber crew as they are ordered to fly across the Pacific just after the Japanese attack Pearl Harbor. The script is tight and does a good job of character development, The acting, especially by Harry Carey who steals the show, is what acting should be, and the story line is believable and realistic. Directed by one of the all time great, war- time directors, Howard Hawks, this is truly a gem from the past. Exciting action right to the end makes this one of the best wartime movies of the 40's.

history.text: After the original picture, which was very well done and had excellent special effects and very good acting, the following two are real stinkers. Apparently done with a non-existent budget (they are shot almost entirely on one set, a room or a building) using close ups. The acting is atrocious and the script written by and for morons. The special effects amount to costumes with moving parts including head masks like the kind used in New Orleans during mardi-gras. The only thing good I can say about this "collection" is it includes the directors cut of the original Mimic in Blu ray and for the price it makes it a good deal. So buy the trilogy and toss the disc with the second and third movies and enjoy the four star original..

history.title: Witches of East End: Season 1
history.text: I REALLY wanted to love this show. As an avid CHARMED fan who owns the whole series and all books related to the show, I wanted to experience something magical and female power centered. This is NOTHING LIKE Charmed. Sure its about witches but so is BEWITCHED & THE WITCHES OF EASTWICK. Get my drift? THAT SAID, I found it was a bit like PRACTICAL MAGIC yet far inferior! Witches of East End is about two sets of sisters, the elder sisters Aunt Wendy & Mother Joanna and the youngsters Ingrid & Freya. I was attracted to the elder sisters more. Their story has MORE history and mystery, depth and suspense. My favorite is Wendy, the wayward well-meaning flighty witch who is misunderstood but who clearly loves her family and is willing to "do bad" for the sake of greater good and for self-preservation. She's sexy, playful, knowledgeable of her craft, weird & brave enough to be different. I find Joanna to look & behave as ANCIENT & IMMORTAL as she claims. She seems a bit scattered/bipolar as one minute she wants nothing to do with magic (which seems really ridiculous considering HER LIFE) and the next admitting that magic is a part of her family's legacy. I disliked Freya the Divalicious buxom vamp who (poor girl) is torn between marrying a rich stud doctor and running away with her Bad Boy Black Sheep cute future brother-in-law. Then there's Ingrid, the supposed bookworm shy academic librarian who seems to lose all sense and performs a screwed up spell every damn episode while other people suffer the consequences. The treatment of the Black characters was cruel yet typical. I was disappointed but not surprised by what happened to them. Maybe the books are better? It seems that the episodes are RUSHED with plot points and flashbacks that titillate yet go no where, usually confirming Bad Guys that I had already figured out 20 minutes into a show. And some issues that could take a whole season get resolved in 40 minutes. WHAT'S THAT ABOUT? Everyone lives well, looks great and is consumed with love affairs or keeping secrets. Maybe if there were more connections between the main characters then I would care. But unlike Charmed, most of THESE SISTER WITCHES WORK ALONE. As a result, the conflicts are inevitable because nobody has any idea what their friends, family, lovers, mother, sister, aunt or enemy is doing. And for characters who have lived so many lives, you'd think they'd acquire some kind of wisdom or common sense. I think what really made me NOT like the show is that these witches are all about personal gain and appear self-centered. On CHARMED, the witches are saving the world or helping others as well as themselves. In later seasons when it became more about just them, it was okay because viewers had watched them sacrifice and do A LOT OF GOOD so the Halliwells had earned the right to focus on their own lives. You watched and cheered! I don't know the Beauchamps and the storytelling seems to act as if the viewer already does. I can't forgive accidental deaths or excuse loss of life orchestrated by the MAIN CHARACTERS until I have really grown to love them. My favorite Immortal is STILL the Highlander. My favorite Witches are STILL the Charmed Ones. My favorite fantasy is STILL Buffy the Vampire Slayer. My favorite Kick-Ass Woman is STILL Xena the Warrior Princess. And as for soap opera deliciousness, there are SO MANY OTHER BETTER CHOICES. Hell, I am way more invested in the relationship between Leonard & Penny on the Big Bang Theory than any of the couples on this show, LOL! What also freaked me out, that the Beauchamp Sisters Freya & Ingrid, seem to share a weird (phoenix like) quality with animated characters Hank & Dean from The Venture Brothers show. LMAO Anybody who watched that cartoon should know what I mean. Its NOT the same BUT they have a way of STAYING AROUND................................. It's okay. I just didn't care about the characters. I probably won't buy the 2nd season though.

history.title: 3 Days to Kill
history.text: I like Kevin Costner. I like badass tough guy movies. I wasn't expecting Shakespeare or even Clint Eastwood. But I just turned it off after about 30 minutes in. I didn't like any of the characters (NOT Costner, his daughter, his fellow spies/hitmen, even the Villain was boring). I thought the action was very disjointed. The tone of the film was odd, not tongue in cheek or satire or black comedy.................. it just seemed awkward and stilted. the cool tough women seemed superficial and irksome. The living situation for Costner's character REALLY bothered me. The soundtrack was forgettable. I did not like this film.

history.title: Annie
history.review_title: Oh Hell No!!!!!! Just plain AWFUL
history.text: I wanted to like this movie. I saw ANNIE on Broadway when I was a girl around 10yrs old. I also saw the WIZ, which is a funky "Black" version of the Wizard of Oz. Quincy Jones did the music and it was fabulous, the musical theater production with Stephanie Mills- NOT Diana Ross movie fiasco. ANYWAY...... I also saw & LOVED the film version of ANNIE from the 1980s and as a teacher I screened the film often with students plus played the soundtrack. Loved JAY Z's sampling of Hard Knocks Life- BUT the 2014 movie is awful. NO ONE can sing. The staging (NOT ACTUAL DANCING) is stilted and awkward. No one is LIKABLE or CUTE. And the extra issue given to Annie, I found demeaning and RACIST. The original Annie didn't suffer from (SPOILER ALERT!!!),illiteracy!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!?!!!! WHY oh WHY did anybody think this waste of celluloid was entertaining is beyond me. YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED. I immediately threw the DVD in the trash after viewing. I felt ashamed & duped. As a theater buff, musical lover, movie addict, proud African American, mother and an educator- I find this movie to be a dud.
