history.title: Four Christmases
history.text: I'm not sure how to explain all the things wrong with this movie. I agree with the reviewer who said this was a huge step back for Reese Witherspoon. This is a Christmas movie that starts out with a couple who live together but to spice up their love life, they cruise bars and pretend they don't know each other. In the first five minutes there is a word I wouldn't want my kids to hear and I didn't care for it in a Christmas movie either. The big line in this movie is "you can't spell families without lies. That nearly says it all. This couple plans a trip for the holidays telling their family they can't visit but are caught on a TV camera at the airport which blows their "lie" about why they can't visit. They have to visit four families as both their parents are divorced. There is not a redeeming quaility here. If you want a feel good, truly Chrismas movie, this isn't it. One person said she would put this as one of the 25 worst films she had seen. I would take that down to ten. To each their own, but we won't be watching this again.

history.title: A Star For Christmas
history.text: The person who wrote if you watch about half of the movie you might decide you want to own. I watched a little over half and said the heck with it. I love Christmas movies but this fall so short. It have very little to make it feel like a Christmas movie. The actress getting so turned on by watching the guy eat a cupcake and then drooling over his behind, every time he did something was a bit much. He dead head brother was totally unbelievable. Very poor excuse for a Christmas movie or any movie for that matter. Just proves that Hollywood people have run out of ideas but know there are many of us who love Christmas movies so they try anything. I gave this to my daughter (loves, loves, loves Christmas movies) but told her that I doubted she'd like it. I asked her to give it back to me if she didn't and I'll donate it. That's the only thing I can see that it's good for.

history.title: Christmas Mix
history.text: This one had possibilities but fell short. The Pepper guy was supposed to play off the super nice Dr. Love but he fell under her spell almost immediately. All of us baby boomers are having trouble seeing Maureen McCormick as the mother but truth be told she's old enough to be a mother and grandmother. Apparently she's had a face lift or botox because there are no lines on her face. To compensate, they keep her hair pulled back with stringy pieces falling down. In one seen venetian blinds are in front of her so there's not clear view of her face. It's shadows, that apparently the directors though we'd see as lines. And the ending is so interesting. (Not) There's never any questions that the guy is going to go back and get her. There was never any chemistry and very little interaction between her and her so-called boyfriend. The most exciting part of the movie was wondering how many transmissions he messed up to get it to move (if he did). It's on my shelf but if it "walked away" I wouldn't be disappointed.

history.title: Merry Ex-Mas
history.text: I thought this would be good because it had Dean Cain in it. However, we only watched a little of it and my husband and I said we were both so lost. We couldn't tell who was who; who was supposed to be the bad guy or good guy. It was just confusing. Another one we passed along to our daughter because she not only love Christmas movies, she loves Dean Cain. Again, I told her that if she didn't like it to give it back and I'd donate it. It's almost hard to donate such back movies to unsuspecting people.
Apparently I mixed up my reviews of Christmas mix and naughtier and nice. Hard to tell the difference. I hope Amazon doesn't post the review of Christmas mix.

history.title: Defending Santa
history.text: I was totally disgusted with this movie. Just to talk about the quality of the movie; I agree with the people who've said it wasn't great. The acting was poor. I too, expected Jodie Sweeten to have a more prominent role in the movie. We only saw her a few times. The "Santa Claus" didn't look like the typical Santa Claus. I also got a little confused about him talking about going into hibernation until Thanksgiving but then mentioning that Mrs. Claus would be worried. Words fail me, when it comes to the little horse. (If he was alive why was he in a box with no air holes?") That was just a small amount of the junk. But the biggest disappointment of all was Dean Cain participating in this movie. It was, as one reviewer said, a remake of A Miracle on 34th Street but the really strange part was that it also had a touch of God's Not Dead, in which Dean Cain also had a part. Instead of a class room of people standing and saying God's Not Dead, this had a court room of people saying, "I believe in Santa Claus" or some such bunk. As a Christian I was very offended. I wasn't going to watch it all but I felt I needed to, just to see if there was any redeeming quality to this movie. Is Dean Cain playing in faith based movies for the money or in Santa Claus movies for the money. Does his convictions go to the highest bidder? I was going to donate this to Good Will, it was only watched once but I will not help spread this bunk. It's going in the trash where it belongs. It is trash and should never had been made. It was much more entertaining, hearing my 6 year old granddaughter, on Christmas Eve, singing, "He's not making a list; he's not checking it twice. He doesn't know who's naughty or nice because Santa Claus is not coming to town - because he's not real."

history.title: Ice Sculpture Christmas
history.text: This has been the month of Hallmark Christmas movies. I usually like all of them, but occasionally find one I just can't watch. I'd already ordered this movie before he was shown on TV. I bought it based on the description. I won't make that mistake again. I donating this one. If you want to learn the fine art of ice sculpturing, perhaps you'll like it. I know it started off with the guy and the girl totally disliking each other. I'm sure they were in love by the end of the movie but as you can tell from what I've written, I couldn't stick around long enough to watch it all. A blemish in the ice???? Really? Who cares? Some people may love this movie but for me it was definitely not worth what I paid for it - especially since I couldn't even watch it on TV.

history.title: Christmas in the Smokies
history.review_title: Can't go wrong in the Smokies
history.text: This is another one I bought before I saw it on TV. I'm not sorry I bought it, thank goodness. I bought it because it was set in the Smokies-one of my favorite places. We visit there twice a year and could have bought a place for the money we've spent. We have the problem of getting the whole family to join us and all finding a way to make a living. This movie didn't give me much hope that it could ever happen. Being raised on a farm in the "hills of Kentucky" not mountains, I loved the farm scenes. People from out of state have called the area around here mountains but they are just hills; the mountains are in the eastern part of the state. I understood the fight of the protagonist wanting to save her farm. Our whole area tried to do that when the TN Army Corps of Engineers, decided to take acres of farmland and turn it into a lake. Therefore, I love it when someone wins against the big guys. We couldn't save our home; I can never show my kids where I grew up; it's all underwater - so maybe I loved the fight this girl had in her and her winning more than some. I won't say the acting was great or that anything was unpredictable but it's great when the farmer wins and you just can't go wrong in the Smokies. I do say I agree with the people who've said they don't understand her holding on to the anger against a boyfriend for so long, but they had to make a movie. I enjoy these type of movies; trying to save the farm, etc. I have a city born and bred husband and my children were also. They only visited the grandparents on the farm after their grandparents had retired. They know nothing of that world and I love watching something that takes me back for a while. It's a nice relaxing movie. I'll watch it several times, I'm sure.

history.title: Christmas Under Wraps
history.text: I've seen this movie about three or four times; on TV and because I own it. I one of those saps who loves Christmas movies. As we've come to learn, there always has to be a Christmas movie with Candace Cameron Bure. I'm always surprised by the super Christian lady acting in some of these movies but none as much as this one. We've all seen her kissing every man except her husband but this time, she's believing in elves and Santa. It was interesting to see Candace with almost red hair (strawberry blonde perhaps). She has to wear colored contacts because her eye color changes in each movie. This movie is about the privileged daughter, who did work hard to get her medical degree, but planned to ride on her father's coat-tails. She ends up in Alaska when that doesn't happen where the part with they guy is very predictable. If you get past all of that, I shocked at how fast her internet service was, alter it was plugged in and even more strange - Candace has a LIVING MOTHER!

history.title: Crown for Christmas
history.review_title: Not in the Majority - we didn't like it
history.text: Every year, Hallmark comes out with new Christmas movies. We all know how they're going to end because no one has had a fresh idea in ages. However, this is always one or two surprises and I try to by those in case they aren't shown again. (Three Days, for example) However, I will not be purchasing this one. I didn't like the same old story and honestly, I didn't like the actors. I seem to be in the minority here, but I couldn't stand this movie. It was on so many times this year and my husband and I would say, "not again". Then we'd watch one of our DVD's from previous years. If you're not surprised that a prince falls in love with a commoner and every commoner wants to be a princess, apparently, then you'll like this movie. We're all different and that's what makes the world go around. So my husband and I are different. We hated this movie, the plot and the actors. Do they have to do this every year?

history.title: Hot Fuzz (Combo HD DVD and Standard DVD)
history.text: This might be the funniest of director Edgar Wright's 3 English comedies since actor/comedien Simon Pegg is in it as well as Nick Frost, who appeared in the first one as well. It's also a fitting farewell to 2 actors who would pass shortly after this film was released, Billie Whitelaw (The Omen) and Edward Woodward (The Equalizer). It's a funny sendoff of such action films like "Beverly Hills Cop" and "Lethal Weapon". I'm looking forward to seeing Wright's "Baby Driver" in theatres soon.

history.title: Dune
history.review_title: Lynch's cult classic is worth seeing
history.text: I bought this at a bargain price in HD DVD so I don't what the price of it is now. Anyway despite the reviews, this is still an interesting albeit flawed version of the classic tale. Plus it's got a great cast of Patrick Stewart, Jose Ferrer, Max Von Sydow and Jurgen Prochow (Das Boot) plus a young looking Kyle McLachland as Paul. it's still worth seeing.

history.title: Night Moves [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A neglected film noir from the '70's
history.text: This neglected film noir from the '70s deserves another look since I believe it's the last decent collaboration between Gene Hackman and director Arthur Penn (their last film together in the '80's was unsatisfactory). Like his wiretapper in "The Conversation" Gene plays another isolated character whose marriage to Susan Clark is falling apart when he gets an assignment to find a missing teenager (Melanie Griffith) and deliver her to her alcoholic mother. But all is not what it seems in this thriller which after a meandering middle resolves into a dynamic finale. Hackman is excellent and the supporting cast particularly Griffith in her debut and Jennifer Warren as a mystery woman are fine also. Compared to the classic "The Conversation", this is a good but not great film noir.

history.title: Barry Lyndon (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Stanley Kubrick's lush period drama and O'Neal's best performance to date.
history.text: This was one of Kubrick's few failures yet it was named along with "Nashville" by the NBR as one of the best fiilms of the year. I saw this in a theatre and I knew that it was at least 3 hours yet the slow pacing plus the cinematography and Ryan O'Neal's performance kept me awake and riveted me to my seat (I didn't even go out for popcorn or take a restroom break). Since it's release it's grown in stature and Martin Scorsese has listed it as one of Kubrick's masterworks. So if you're not tired or in the mood for a period piece, by all means check this out. I plan to get the Blu-Ray soon.

history.title: Rio Bravo (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: Hawk's last masterpiece with Wayne and Dean Martin
history.text: Howard Hawks is generally passed over in the Great Director's category usually occupied by Hitchcock, Lean, Welles and John Ford possibly because he has managed not to be pigeonholed as a director of one genre but a master of many (the westerns, screw ball comedy, film noir and even sci-fi horror). In his return to the Western genre, he has managed to make both an entertaining film and yet also an artful one as well. He's also managed to carve out a masterful performance from Dean Martin and introduce a newcomer by the name of Angie Dickinson. If you're not yet a fan of him, do check this out but also his other films as well like "Bringing Up Baby", "To Have And Have Not" & "The Big Sleep" both with Bogart, "Sgt York" with Gary Cooper, "His Girl Friday' , "Only Angels Have Wings" both with Cary Grant and the original "Thing".

history.review_title: A stab at a young man's love affair fails
history.text: I wanted to like this movie because of the cast but unfortunately it didn't register as much as an earlier film, "The Graduate". I think a large part of the problem lies in the performance of British actor, Callum Turner. He's okay with his American accent but his performance seems too self centered and not vulnerable enough for us to really care for him. On the other hand, the young actress who plays Mimi, his off and on girlfriend for some reason we do care. I sat through watching this film and seeming very detached from the main characters with the exception of the wonderful Jeff Bridges who at least brings some color to his role as the wise mentor and Beckinsale is always easy to watch but even her character is somewhat cold. So if you're expecting another "Graduate"---forget it! By the end of the movie, I was glad that it was over.

history.title: The Beguiled (2017) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Coppola misses with this remake of a gothic tale.
history.text: I viewed this remake out of curiosity since I'm very familiar with the 1971 version starring Clint Eastwood and Geraldine Page. Unfortunately director Sofia Coppola's vision and direction can't even hold a candle to director Don Siegel's take on this gothic tale. Almost devoid of psychological tension particularly in the near climatic scene when Burney chooses one young female over another with dire results, we only see him caught in bed with her but there's no lead up to that scene. Also Coppola has eliminated the black maid from the story which actually to the tensions in the original--and of course every Southern household in those days did have slaves. And as much as I like Kidman and Colin Farrell as actors, they cannot match the intensity and charisma of the original leads of Eastwood and Page. Even the normally excellent Kirsten Dunst lacks the pathos and empathy of the late Elizabeth Hartman as Edwina plus her scene with Farrell ends not in an embrace of love but in a near rape. The only positive thing I can say about this remake is that it's beautifully shot but overall rent or buy the original. I do hope someday either Universal or Twilight Time releases the original in Blu-Ray.

history.title: The Beguiled (1971) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Clint deviates from the action mode
history.text: I’ve already ordered this in Blu Ray and despite the period setting—it’s still timely due to the recent sexual allegations against prominent figures. Also the recent remake can’t even hold a candle to this cult classic since in the remake a character has been removed and secrets about the main character are not shown. This film and “Play Misty For Me” showed that Clint could do more than play an action hero. I doubt if John Wayne could ever do a movie like this.

history.title: Total Recall (Blu-ray + DVD)
history.review_title: Nifty remake of Dick's short story
history.text: I bought this on sale at Best Buy for only $9.95 and that was a bargain. I have mixed feelings about this film, on the one hand Colin Farrell is a better actor than Arnold was in the original but the direction by Len Wiseman lacked the irony and wit of Paul Verhoeven but the visual effects were fantastic and well shot yet the film is somewhat over long---like almost 2 hours or more. The ladies of course are a treat to watch since we have Kate Beckingsale , always great in tights or underwear and the lovely Jessica Biel. Anyway at that bargain price I can't complain and it's in Blu-Ray as well.

history.title: Inferno (3D / 2D)
history.review_title: Ryan fights the elements to survive in the desert in 3D.
history.text: In an interview just a few year before he died, Robert Ryan was asked how he felt about some of the films he's done in Hollywood and he replied, "Most of them were really dogs, but I did think "Inferno" was pretty good." I agree with him on this since I've seen the film on TV years ago but never knew it was in 3D until I saw it at a 3D festival in Berkeley. It's a stunning film shot by Lucien Ballard who also lensed "The Wild Bunch" another film that Ryan professed to be one of the better films though that was a tough shoot for him and William Holden since Peckingpah demanded they work long hours in the grueling heat. The story was so good that Fox remade it as a TV movie with Arthur Hill in Ryan's part and Diana Muldaur in Fleming's part as the scheming wife. I bought this originally as an import from Scotland but now it's available domestically. You won't go wrong or disappointed with it--it's one of the best films along with "House Of Wax" to showcase 3D.

history.text: Play Misty for Me is terrorizing, the original Fatal Attraction. I loved it. All the others are very good also. ' The Eiger Sanction', has many raw scenes of mountain climbing but to me ends strangely. In Coogan's Bluff he plays a western deputy sheriff who comes to NYC to pick up prisoner to bring back to Arizona. It was good non Dirty Harry but typical Eastwood role. I found 'The Beguiled' to be very different then the other films. He is a wounded Yankee soldier found and taking in by girls and woman school mistress of all girls school. He is a little unscrupulous and takes advantage of 2 of the girls, one only 17 and even makes it with the head mistress as they protect him from capture. Needless to say this leads to complications for Clint as he is double dealing them. It doesn't end good for him, to say the least. Rare bad ending for Clint. But I enjoyed it none the less. Good packaging, storing of discs and very good remastering make for a very highly recommended collection.

history.title: Henry & Anne: The Lovers Who Changed History
history.text: The other reviewer mentions most of the surface and background of their love for each other. But this should have been expanded to include important names involved, especially in the second half it was a real let down. Lets see now, oh yes, Where is Thomas More, Thomas Cromwell and several others not even mentioned here. Not even in passing, nothing. Aren't they important enough in relation to what happened to Anne?? Even if there were time restraints, how can you leave out all the major players involved in this story of Anne and Henry?? My goodness, it was fine to see and hear passages from their love letters to each other. But and I repeat but their was to much left out at the end to be able to understand what was happening to Queen Anne. For goodness sake Henry was at Wolf Hall making planes with Jane Seymour and did in fact marry her 11 days after Anne's beheading. ( The fact that he married Seymour 11 days later is all that mentioned here by Lipscomb) So, to me this was a big,big disappointment. Was expecting a lot more.

targets.title: The Matrix Triple Feature (The Matrix / The Matrix Reloaded / The Matrix Revolutions) [Blu-ray]

history.text: I wanted to like this movie. I really tried to like this movie. Unfortunately this film has not aged well, and leaves one feeling like they just ate a bag of candy when they really wanted steak and potatoes! Most of the acting is weak, although Rip Torn and Cornel Wilde hold their own. But the use of lousy still photos to show flashback memories, and some wretched music detract from the message wow this film. Worse yet, what was considered in its time to be editing worthy a Academy Award nomination just looks abysmal in today's film environment, showing that we have come along way, baby, in regards to editing. Listening to poorly recorded voice overs while looking at still photo images that Grandma could have shot better, really gets old fast. There are very few portions of this film that hold up all these years later, and I say that as a huge fan of 60's films. While there may have been a story in there somewhere, it gets lost in the poor production work.

history.review_title: Solid Fun and Guns in Aussie Land
history.text: Tom Selleck has never thrilled me in movies or TV, and he still doesn't in Quigley Down Under. However, I found this to be a solid flick, with a good story, and elements of classic '60s and '70s westerns that I love. A bit "spaghetti", a bit traditional, but a lot different due to the overall subject matter, Quigley entertains well. Even though this film is a bit long, it never gets boring. The blend of the Aussie aspects, (aboriginals, Australian scenery, music touches), makes for an enjoyable cinema experience.

history.title: The Wanderers [Blu-ray]
history.text: Much more than I expected. Being a fan of vintage "gang" films, this one satisfied and surprised. Some good acting, good script and dialogue, and decent production. Not an award winner in my opinion, but plenty of fun to watch and fits with the timeframe of the story. I give it five stars because I would indeed watch this again, and more than once.

history.title: Vigilante Force
history.review_title: Not the Best of Two Actors I Usually Enjoy!
history.text: I remembered this as a much better flick...but this DVD let me down. Kinda poor quality, especially image quality lacking. I know this is a 70's film, and I keep that in mind...and in fact, I liked this in the cinema when I first saw it....but this has to be Kristofferson's worst acting job of his career. (I typically love to watch him, as well as Jan Michael Vincent...but wooden acting here and lousy direction combined with low film imagery forces me to only give it a 3 star rating. I like it for the collection value mainly.

history.title: Drive-In
history.review_title: Something To Savor If You Love(d) Drive-Ins!
history.text: Love this little treasure that allows me to enjoy my own memories of the drive-ins I grew up with. Just a completely fun flick overall. Will watch this many times in coming years...

history.title: Cracking Up (a/k/a Smorgasbord)
history.text: Terrible film, and I say that as a great Jerry Lewis fan. I bought this as a collection item, not expecting much. And not much is what I got. Disjointed with terrible skits that reek of ancient vaudeville schmaltz and no rhyme or reason to most of this mess. I believe I laughed once or twice...or it may have been a burp. I love Jerry, but not this particular flick.

history.title: The Geisha Boy [Blu-ray]
history.text: Fine Jerry Lewis effort here. Fun little storyline, plenty of laughs, and some heartfelt effort. I viewed this many years back, and I think I enjoyed it just as much watching the DVD. Decent production value too.

history.title: Who's Minding the Store?
history.review_title: The Laugh Master Minds The Store.
history.text: Jerry, Jerry, Jerry...you are splitting my sides! Funny flick for sure with some great setups and executions that deliver plenty of laughs. One of my favorite Jerry films. Not the greatest production value...but with these laughs I don't care!

history.title: Sorcerer (1977) (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Blows You Away While Grinding Through a Jungle of Hell
history.text: This film blew me away when it first came out in theaters. The tension, suspense, soundtrack...a powder keg of action that grinds away and seems to meld Hitchcock, Tarantino, and a bit of Peckinpah into a delightful blast!

history.title: Catch-22
history.text: A great effort at capturing a terrific book that is a satirical winner. So many great performances and so many actors who would soon be well known, or were already well known when this was produced. I love this film. Not in my top rated flicks, but near that portion of goodies. You will be surprised at how many people you recognize in these roles. But be ready for a very different tale.
